  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
\]
such that
\[
  \sum_{j>J+H}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{I_j}(K)}{\chiBar_p}
  \ge \frac{c}{2}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant from
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-window-incidence-alternative}.  Since \(G\) has
bounded degree, \(V(I_j)<\infty\) for \(J\le j\le J+H\).  Choose \(p_1<\pc\)
so that, for every \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\),
\[
  \chiBar_p
  >
  \frac{16(H+1)}{c^2}
  \sum_{j=J}^{J+H}2^{2\alpha(j-J)}V(I_j).
\]
This is possible because \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\).

Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-window-incidence-alternative} with any
\(p_0\in[p_1,\pc)\), and take the resulting \(p\) and \(K\).  If the tail
alternative \eqref{eq:finite-window-tail-alt} holds, we are done.  Suppose
instead that the incidence alternative \eqref{eq:finite-window-incidence-alt}
holds.  For its thresholds
\[
  \lambda_j=\frac{c}{4(H+1)}2^{-\alpha(j-J)},
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:incidence-layer-volume-bound} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \sum_{j=J}^{J+H}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \frac{|\mathcal N^{I_j}(K,\lambda_j\chiBar_p)|}{|K|}
  &\le
  \sum_{j=J}^{J+H}
  2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \frac{V(I_j)}{\lambda_j\chiBar_p}  \\
  &=
  \frac{4(H+1)}{c\chiBar_p}
  \sum_{j=J}^{J+H}2^{2\alpha(j-J)}V(I_j)
  <\frac{c}{4},
\end{aligned}
\]
contradicting \eqref{eq:finite-window-incidence-alt}.  Hence the tail
alternative must hold.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Single remote annulus obstruction]
\label{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}
Let \(G\) have bounded degree, and suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as
\(p\uparrow\pc\).  If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0,
\]
then there is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that the following holds.  For every
\(\alpha,\gamma>0\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), and an integer \(j>J+H\) such that
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p
\]
and, with \(I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}]\),
\[
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{I_j}(K)}{\chiBar_p}
  \ge
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}
  (1-2^{-\alpha})(1-2^{-\gamma})
  2^{-(\alpha+\gamma)(j-J)} .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant from
Proposition~\ref{prop:fixed-window-obstruction-escapes}.  Put
\[
  c=(1-2^{-\alpha})\epsilon .
\]
For \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\),
Proposition~\ref{prop:fixed-window-obstruction-escapes} gives
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) and a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), with
\(|K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p\), such that
\[
  \sum_{j>J+H}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{I_j}(K)}{\chiBar_p}
  \ge \frac{c}{2}.
\]
If the desired lower bound failed for every \(j>J+H\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \sum_{j>J+H}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{I_j}(K)}{\chiBar_p}
  &<
  \frac{c}{2}(1-2^{-\gamma})
  \sum_{j>J+H}2^{-\gamma(j-J)}  \\
  &\le
  \frac{c}{2}(1-2^{-\gamma})
  \sum_{k\ge1}2^{-\gamma k}
  <\frac{c}{2},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the inequality \(j>J+H\) implies \(j-J\ge1\).  This contradiction
proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single remote annulus has root and incidence layers]
\label{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, there is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\alpha,\gamma>0\), every pair of
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there
are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), and an integer
\(j>J+H\) such that \(|K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p\) and, with
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}
  (1-2^{-\alpha})(1-2^{-\gamma})
  2^{-(\alpha+\gamma)(j-J)},
  \qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
we have
\[
  |Z_p^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j/2)|\ge\frac{\sigma_j}{2}|K|
\]
and
\[
  |\mathcal N^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j\chiBar_p/2)|
  \ge\frac{\sigma_j}{2}|K|.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j\) by Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}.
Lemma~\ref{lem:annular-root-layer-extraction}, applied with
\(\lambda=\sigma_j/2\), gives the root-layer lower bound.  The incidence
lower bound follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:root-layer-incidence}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Escaping annuli have susceptibility-scale volume]
\label{cor:escaping-annulus-volume}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, there is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\alpha,\gamma>0\), every pair of
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there
are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) and an integer \(j>J+H\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  V(I_j)=\sup_{x\in V}|\{z\in V:d(x,z)\in I_j\}|,
\]
we have
\[
  V(I_j)
  \ge
  \frac{\epsilon^2}{16}
  (1-2^{-\alpha})^2(1-2^{-\gamma})^2
  2^{-2(\alpha+\gamma)(j-J)}
  \chiBar_p .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j\) by Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, and
let
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}
  (1-2^{-\alpha})(1-2^{-\gamma})
  2^{-(\alpha+\gamma)(j-J)} .
\]
That corollary gives
\[
  \frac{|\mathcal N^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j\chiBar_p/2)|}{|K|}
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:incidence-layer-volume-bound} gives the opposite bound
\[
  \frac{|\mathcal N^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j\chiBar_p/2)|}{|K|}
  \le
  \frac{2V(I_j)}{\sigma_j\chiBar_p}.
\]
Thus \(V(I_j)\ge\sigma_j^2\chiBar_p/4\), which is the displayed inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Penalized volume obstruction]
\label{cor:subexponential-volume-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, there is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every pair of integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) and an integer \(j>J+H\) such that
\[
  V((2^j,2^{j+1}])
  \ge
  \frac{\epsilon^2}{16}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^4
  2^{-2\eta(j-J)}\chiBar_p .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:escaping-annulus-volume} with
\(\alpha=\gamma=\eta/2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Logarithmic radius obstruction]
\label{cor:logarithmic-radius-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every pair of integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) and an integer \(j>J+H\) such that
\[
  V((2^j,2^{j+1}])
  \ge
  \frac{\epsilon^2}{16}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^4
  2^{-2\eta(j-J)}\chiBar_p
\]
and
\[
  2^j\ge \frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let
\[
  c=\frac{\epsilon^2}{16}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^4,
\]
where \(\epsilon\) is supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:subexponential-volume-obstruction}.  Since
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), we may choose \(p_*<\pc\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:subexponential-volume-obstruction} applies to every
\(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and every \(p\in[p_*,\pc)\) satisfies
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  >
  \Delta \chiBar_p^{1/2}
  \left(\frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right)^{2\eta}
\]
and \(\log_\Delta\chiBar_p>4\).  Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose \(p,j\)
by Corollary~\ref{cor:subexponential-volume-obstruction}.
Put \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).  If \(2^j<L/4\), then
\[
  V((2^j,2^{j+1}])
  \le \sup_{x\in V}|B(x,2^{j+1})|
  \le \Delta^{2^{j+1}+1}
  < \Delta \chiBar_p^{1/2}
\]
uniformly in the center \(x\), while
\[
  2^{2\eta(j-J)}\le 2^{2\eta j}<\left(\frac L4\right)^{2\eta}.
\]
The volume lower bound would then imply
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  \le
  V((2^j,2^{j+1}])\,2^{2\eta(j-J)}
  <
  \Delta \chiBar_p^{1/2}
  \left(\frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right)^{2\eta},
\]
contradicting the choice of \(p_*\).  Hence
\(2^j\ge L/4\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Logarithmic backscatter fan]
\label{cor:logarithmic-backscatter-fan}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every pair of integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer
\(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a set \(Z\subset V\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
\]
we have
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  2^j\ge \frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  |Z|\ge \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z),
\]
and every \(z\in Z\) satisfies
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p .
\]
In particular,
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,z)\in I_j\}|
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p
  \qquad(z\in Z).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, and put
\[
  c=\frac{\epsilon^2}{16}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^4.
\]
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, with
\(\alpha=\gamma=\eta/2\), applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and every
\(p\in[p_*,\pc)\) satisfies
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  >
  \Delta \chiBar_p^{1/2}
  \left(\frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right)^{2\eta}
\]
and \(\log_\Delta\chiBar_p>4\).

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose \(p,K,j\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}.  Let
\[
  Z_0=Z_p^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j/2).
\]
That corollary gives
\[
  |Z_0|\ge\frac{\sigma_j}{2}|K|
\]
and, by Lemma~\ref{lem:root-layer-incidence},
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,z)\in I_j\}|
  \ge\frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p
  \qquad(z\in Z_0).
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \sum_{x\in K}|\{z\in Z_0:d(x,z)\in I_j\}|
  &=
  \sum_{z\in Z_0}|\{x\in K:d(x,z)\in I_j\}|  \\
  &\ge
  \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p |Z_0|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p |K|.
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose \(x\in K\) for which the corresponding summand is at least the
average, and define
\[
  Z=\{z\in Z_0:d(x,z)\in I_j\}.
\]
This proves the lower bound on \(|Z|\), the annular relation
\(d(x,z)\in I_j\), and the two displayed lower bounds for each \(z\in Z\).

It remains only to force the logarithmic lower bound on \(2^j\).  Since
\(|Z|\le V(I_j)\), the preceding lower bound gives
\[
  V(I_j)\ge c\,2^{-2\eta(j-J)}\chiBar_p .
\]
Put \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).  If \(2^j<L/4\), then
\[
  V(I_j)\le \sup_{v\in V}|B(v,2^{j+1})|
  \le \Delta^{2^{j+1}+1}
  < \Delta \chiBar_p^{1/2},
\]
while
\[
  2^{2\eta(j-J)}\le 2^{2\eta j}<\left(\frac L4\right)^{2\eta}.
\]
Thus
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  \le V(I_j)2^{2\eta(j-J)}
  <
  \Delta\chiBar_p^{1/2}
  \left(\frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right)^{2\eta},
\]
contradicting the choice of \(p_*\).  Therefore \(2^j\ge L/4\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive logarithmic backscatter fan]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-backscatter-fan}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a set \(Z\subset V\) such that,
with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
and
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
\]
we have
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  2^j>BL,
\]
\[
  |Z|\ge \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z),
\]
and every \(z\in Z\) satisfies
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p .
\]
In particular,
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,z)\in I_j\}|
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p
  \qquad(z\in Z).
\]
If \(\Delta\ge3\), one may take \(\omega=\Delta-1\), so the admissible range
includes every
\[
  B<\frac{1}{2\log_\Delta(\Delta-1)} .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, and put
\[
  c=\frac{\epsilon^2}{16}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^4 .
\]
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, with
\(\alpha=\gamma=\eta/2\), applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and every
\(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), satisfies \(BL>1\) and
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  >
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2B\log_\Delta\omega}(BL)^{2\eta}.
\]
This is possible because \(2B\log_\Delta\omega<1\) and
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\).

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose \(p,K,j\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}.  Let
\[
  Z_0=Z_p^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j/2).
\]
Exactly as in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:logarithmic-backscatter-fan}, choose \(x\in K\) and
\[
  Z=\{z\in Z_0:d(x,z)\in I_j\}
\]
so that
\[
  |Z|\ge \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p,
  \qquad d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z),
\]
and every \(z\in Z\) has the displayed backscatter and incidence lower bounds.

It remains to prove \(2^j>BL\).  Suppose instead that \(2^j\le BL\).  Since
\(|Z|\le V(I_j)\), the volume-growth assumption gives
\[
  |Z|
  \le
  \sup_{u\in V}|B(u,2^{j+1})|
  \le
  C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+1}}
  \le
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2B\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
Also \(2^{2\eta(j-J)}\le2^{2\eta j}\le(BL)^{2\eta}\).  Therefore
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  \le
  |Z|2^{2\eta(j-J)}
  \le
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2B\log_\Delta\omega}(BL)^{2\eta},
\]
contradicting the choice of \(p_*\).  Thus \(2^j>BL\).

The final assertion follows from the same tree-volume estimate as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-scale-amplification}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Separated subfan extraction]
\label{lem:separated-subfan-extraction}
Let \(G\) be locally finite, let \(Z\subset V\) be finite, and let
\(r\ge0\) be an integer.  Put
\[
  V_{2r}=\sup_{v\in V}|B(v,2r)|.
\]
Then there is a set \(Z_r\subseteq Z\) such that
\[
  d(z,z')>2r\qquad(z,z'\in Z_r,\ z\ne z')
\]
and
\[
  |Z_r|\ge \frac{|Z|}{V_{2r}},
\]
with the convention that the assertion is trivial if \(V_{2r}=\infty\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(Z_r\) be maximal subject to the separation condition.  Maximality
implies that the balls \(B(z,2r)\), \(z\in Z_r\), cover \(Z\).  Hence
\[
  |Z|
  \le \sum_{z\in Z_r}|B(z,2r)|
  \le |Z_r|V_{2r}.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted separated subfan extraction]
\label{lem:weighted-separated-subfan-extraction}
Let \(G\) be locally finite, let \(Z\subset V\) be finite, let
\(a_z\ge0\) for \(z\in Z\), and let \(r\ge0\) be an integer.  Put
\[
  V_{2r}=\sup_{v\in V}|B(v,2r)|.
\]
Then there is a set \(Z_r\subseteq Z\) such that
\[
  d(z,z')>2r\qquad(z,z'\in Z_r,\ z\ne z')
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z_r}a_z
  \ge
  \frac{1}{V_{2r}}\sum_{z\in Z}a_z,
\]
with the convention that the assertion is trivial if \(V_{2r}=\infty\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Greedily choose vertices as follows.  While unchosen vertices remain, choose a
remaining vertex \(z\) of maximal weight \(a_z\), add it to \(Z_r\), and
delete all remaining vertices in \(B(z,2r)\).  The chosen vertices are
\(2r\)-separated.  If \(C_z\) is the set deleted when \(z\) is chosen, then
\(|C_z|\le V_{2r}\) and \(a_y\le a_z\) for every \(y\in C_z\).  Thus
\[
  \sum_{y\in C_z}a_y\le V_{2r}a_z .
\]
Summing over the disjoint deleted clusters gives
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z}a_z\le V_{2r}\sum_{z\in Z_r}a_z .
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive separated backscatter fan]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-separated-backscatter-fan}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
we have
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  2^j>BL,
\]
\[
  |Z_\theta|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4C_{\rm vol}}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
  \qquad
  d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z_\theta),
\]
\[
  d(z,z')>2r_p
  \qquad(z,z'\in Z_\theta,\ z\ne z'),
\]
and every \(z\in Z_\theta\) satisfies
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p .
\]
Consequently, the balls \(B(z,r_p)\), \(z\in Z_\theta\), are pairwise
disjoint.  If \(\Delta\ge3\), one may take \(\omega=\Delta-1\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j,x,Z\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-backscatter-fan}, and set
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor .
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:separated-subfan-extraction} to \(Z\) and \(r_p\).  The
resulting set \(Z_\theta\) inherits \(d(x,z)\in I_j\), the lower bound
\(2^j>BL\), and the pointwise backscatter lower bound from \(Z\).  Moreover,
\[
  |Z_\theta|\ge \frac{|Z|}{V_{2r_p}}.
\]
The volume-growth assumption gives
\[
  V_{2r_p}\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2r_p}
  \le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
Combining this with
\[
  |Z|\ge\frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p
\]
from Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-backscatter-fan} gives the
displayed lower bound on \(|Z_\theta|\).  The separation
\(d(z,z')>2r_p\) implies that the balls \(B(z,r_p)\) are pairwise disjoint.
The final assertion follows from the tree-volume estimate in
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-scale-amplification}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Separated backscatter fan]
\label{cor:separated-logarithmic-backscatter-fan}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/2\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a
set \(Z_\theta\subset V\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
we have
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  2^j\ge \frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  |Z_\theta|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4\Delta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta},
  \qquad
  d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z_\theta),
\]
\[
  d(z,z')>2r_p
  \qquad(z,z'\in Z_\theta,\ z\ne z'),
\]
and every \(z\in Z_\theta\) satisfies
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p .
\]
Consequently, the balls \(B(z,r_p)\), \(z\in Z_\theta\), are pairwise
disjoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j,x,Z\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:logarithmic-backscatter-fan}, and set
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor .
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:separated-subfan-extraction} to \(Z\) and \(r_p\).  If
\(Z_\theta\) is the resulting separated subset, it inherits the annular
relation and the pointwise mass lower bound from \(Z\).  Since \(G\) has
maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\),
\[
  V_{2r_p}\le \Delta^{2r_p+1}\le \Delta\chiBar_p^{2\theta}.
\]
Combining this estimate with
\[
  |Z|\ge\frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p
\]
from Corollary~\ref{cor:logarithmic-backscatter-fan} gives the displayed lower
bound on \(|Z_\theta|\).  The separation \(d(z,z')>2r_p\) implies that the
balls \(B(z,r_p)\) are pairwise disjoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Rooted fan energy]
\label{def:rooted-fan-energy}
For \(p<\pc\), \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), \(x\in V\), finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), and \(Z\subset V\), define
\[
  \mathcal W_p^I(x,K,Z)
  =
  \sum_{z\in Z}\tau_p(x,z)
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,z).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gated fan energy]
\label{def:gated-fan-energy}
For \(p<\pc\), \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), \(x\in V\), finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), \(Z\subset V\), and an integer \(r\ge0\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal G_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z)
  =
  \sum_{z\in Z}
  &\left[
    \sum_{a:d(a,z)=r}\tau_p(x,a)\tau_p(a,z)
  \right]  \\
  &\cdot
  \left[
    \sum_{b:d(b,z)=r}\tau_p(b,z)
    \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,b)
  \right].
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Point-gated fan energy]
\label{def:point-gated-fan-energy}
Let \(p<\pc\), \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), \(x\in V\), let \(K\subset V\)
and \(Z\subset V\) be finite non-empty sets, and let \(r\ge0\).  If
\(a,b:Z\to V\) satisfy
\[
  d(a_z,z)=d(b_z,z)=r\qquad(z\in Z),
\]
define
\[
  \mathcal H_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z,a,b)
  =
  \sum_{z\in Z}
  \tau_p(x,a_z)\tau_p(a_z,z)\tau_p(b_z,z)
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,b_z).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coalesced gate energy]
\label{def:coalesced-gate-energy}
Let \(p<\pc\), \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), \(x\in V\), let \(K\subset V\)
and \(Z\subset V\) be finite non-empty sets, and let \(r\ge0\).  If
\(a:Z\to V\) satisfies
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r\qquad(z\in Z),
\]
define
\[
  \mathcal J_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z,a)
  =
  \sum_{z\in Z}
  \tau_p(x,a_z)
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,a_z).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Gate decomposition]
\label{lem:gate-decomposition}
Let \(G\) be locally finite, let \(p<\pc\), let \(r\ge1\), and let
\(I\subseteq(r,\infty)\).  If \(x\in V\), \(K\subset V\) is finite
non-empty, \(Z\subset V\), and \(d(x,z)\in I\) for every \(z\in Z\), then
\[
  \mathcal W_p^I(x,K,Z)\le\mathcal G_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(z\in Z\).  Since \(d(x,z)>r\), every open path from \(x\) to \(z\)
has a first vertex \(a\) on the sphere \(\{v:d(v,z)=r\}\).  The initial
segment from \(x\) to \(a\) and the terminal segment from \(a\) to \(z\) are
edge-disjoint, so the BK inequality gives
\[
  \tau_p(x,z)
  \le
  \sum_{a:d(a,z)=r}\tau_p(x,a)\tau_p(a,z).
\]
Similarly, if \(y\in K\) and \(d(y,z)\in I\), then \(d(y,z)>r\), and
\[
  \tau_p(y,z)
  \le
  \sum_{b:d(b,z)=r}\tau_p(y,b)\tau_p(b,z).
\]
Summing the second inequality over such \(y\), multiplying by the first
inequality, and then summing over \(z\in Z\) gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Gate-pair selection]
\label{lem:gate-pair-selection}
Let \(G\) be locally finite, let \(p<\pc\), let \(r\ge0\), and put
\[
  M_r=\sup_{z\in V}|\{v:d(v,z)=r\}| .
\]
Let \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), \(x\in V\), let \(K\subset V\) and
\(Z\subset V\) be finite non-empty sets, and suppose that the sphere
\(\{v:d(v,z)=r\}\) is non-empty for every \(z\in Z\).  Then there are maps
\(a,b:Z\to V\), with \(d(a_z,z)=d(b_z,z)=r\), such that
\[
  \mathcal H_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z,a,b)
  \ge
  M_r^{-2}\mathcal G_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For each \(z\in Z\), write the \(z\)-summand of
\(\mathcal G_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z)\) as
\[
  \sum_{\substack{a:d(a,z)=r\\ b:d(b,z)=r}}
  \tau_p(x,a)\tau_p(a,z)\tau_p(b,z)
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,b).
\]
There are at most \(M_r^2\) non-negative summands.  Choose
\((a_z,b_z)\) to maximize the displayed quantity.  The chosen term is at
least \(M_r^{-2}\) times the whole \(z\)-summand.  Summing over \(z\) proves
the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Gate coalescence]
\label{lem:gate-coalescence}
Let \(G\) be locally finite, let \(p<\pc\), let \(r\ge0\), let
\(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), \(x\in V\), and let \(K,Z\subset V\) be finite
non-empty sets.  If \(a,b:Z\to V\) satisfy
\[
  d(a_z,z)=d(b_z,z)=r\qquad(z\in Z),
\]
then
\[
  \mathcal J_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z,a)
  \ge
  p^{2r}\mathcal H_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z,a,b).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(z\in Z\), and let \(\pi_z\) be a geodesic from \(b_z\) to \(a_z\).
Since \(d(a_z,b_z)\le2r\), the probability that every edge of \(\pi_z\) is
open is at least \(p^{2r}\).  For every \(y\in K\), the events
\(\{y\leftrightarrow b_z\}\) and \(\{\pi_z\text{ is open}\}\) are increasing,
and their intersection implies \(\{y\leftrightarrow a_z\}\).  Hence FKG gives
\[
  \tau_p(y,a_z)\ge p^{2r}\tau_p(y,b_z).
\]
After summing over \(y\) with \(d(y,z)\in I\) and using
\(\tau_p(a_z,z)\tau_p(b_z,z)\le1\), we obtain
\[
  \tau_p(x,a_z)
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge
  p^{2r}\tau_p(x,a_z)\tau_p(a_z,z)\tau_p(b_z,z)
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,b_z).
\]
Summing over \(z\) proves the lemma.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[High one-gate layer extraction]
\label{lem:high-one-gate-layer-extraction}
Let \(p<\pc\), let \(r\ge0\), let \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), let \(x\in V\), let
\(K,Z\subset V\) be finite non-empty sets, and let \(a:Z\to V\).  Suppose that
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z}\tau_p(x,a_z)\le\chiBar_p
\]
and that
\[
  \mathcal J_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z,a)\ge L .
\]
Put
\[
  Z^\sharp
  =
  \left\{
    z\in Z:
    \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
    \ge \frac{L}{2\chiBar_p}
  \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge \frac{L}{2\chiBar_p}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For \(z\notin Z^\sharp\), the \(K\)-to-gate mass is less than
\(L/(2\chiBar_p)\), while for every \(z\) it is at most \(\chiBar_p\).
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
  L
  &\le
  \mathcal J_{p,r}^I(x,K,Z,a)  \\
  &\le
  \frac{L}{2\chiBar_p}
  \sum_{z\in Z}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  +
  \chiBar_p\sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)  \\
  &\le
  \frac L2+
  \chiBar_p\sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z).
\end{aligned}
\]
Rearranging gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted separated fan]
\label{cor:weighted-separated-fan}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/2\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a
set \(Z_\theta\subset V\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
we have
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  2^j\ge \frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z_\theta),
  \qquad
  d(z,z')>2r_p\quad(z,z'\in Z_\theta,\ z\ne z'),
\]
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z_\theta}\tau_p(x,z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4\Delta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta},
\]
and every \(z\in Z_\theta\) satisfies
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p .
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta}\chiBar_p^{2-2\theta}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  |Z_\theta|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4\Delta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta},
\]
and the balls \(B(z,r_p)\), \(z\in Z_\theta\), are pairwise disjoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, and put
\[
  c=\frac{\epsilon^2}{16}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^4.
\]
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, with
\(\alpha=\gamma=\eta/2\), applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and every
\(p\in[p_*,\pc)\) satisfies
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  >
  \Delta \chiBar_p^{1/2}
  \left(\frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right)^{2\eta}
\]
and \(\log_\Delta\chiBar_p>4\).

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose \(p,K,j\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}.  Let
\[
  Z_0=Z_p^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j/2).
\]
Then \(|Z_0|\ge(\sigma_j/2)|K|\), and every \(z\in Z_0\) satisfies
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p .
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \sum_{x\in K}\sum_{\substack{z\in Z_0\\d(x,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(x,z)
  &=
  \sum_{z\in Z_0}
  \sum_{\substack{x\in K\\d(x,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(x,z)  \\
  &\ge
  \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p |Z_0|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p |K|.
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose \(x\in K\) for which the corresponding inner sum is at least the
average, and set
\[
  Z=\{z\in Z_0:d(x,z)\in I_j\}.
\]
Then
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z}\tau_p(x,z)\ge\frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p.
\]
Since \(\tau_p(x,z)\le1\), this gives
\[
  V(I_j)\ge |Z|\ge \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p
  =c\,2^{-2\eta(j-J)}\chiBar_p .
\]
The same bounded-degree comparison as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:logarithmic-backscatter-fan} gives
\(2^j\ge(1/4)\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).

Now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted-separated-subfan-extraction} to \(Z\), with
weights \(a_z=\tau_p(x,z)\), and with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor .
\]
The resulting \(Z_\theta\) is \(2r_p\)-separated and inherits the annular
relation and the pointwise backscatter lower bound from \(Z\).  Since
\[
  V_{2r_p}\le \Delta^{2r_p+1}\le \Delta\chiBar_p^{2\theta},
\]
the weighted extraction gives
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z_\theta}\tau_p(x,z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4\Delta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta}.
\]
Multiplying this by the pointwise lower bound
\((\sigma_j/2)\chiBar_p\) for the backscatter from \(K\) gives the displayed
lower bound on \(\mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)\).
The cardinality bound follows from \(\tau_p(x,z)\le1\), and the ball
disjointness follows from the separation.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive weighted separated fan]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
we have
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  2^j>BL,
\]
\[
  d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z_\theta),
  \qquad
  d(z,z')>2r_p\quad(z,z'\in Z_\theta,\ z\ne z'),
\]
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z_\theta}\tau_p(x,z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4C_{\rm vol}}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
and every \(z\in Z_\theta\) satisfies
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p .
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8C_{\rm vol}}
  \chiBar_p^{2-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  |Z_\theta|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4C_{\rm vol}}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
and the balls \(B(z,r_p)\), \(z\in Z_\theta\), are pairwise disjoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, and put
\[
  c=\frac{\epsilon^2}{16}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^4 .
\]
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}, with
\(\alpha=\gamma=\eta/2\), applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and every
\(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), satisfies \(BL>1\) and
\[
  c\chiBar_p
  >
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2B\log_\Delta\omega}(BL)^{2\eta}.
\]

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose \(p,K,j\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:single-annulus-root-incidence}.  Let
\[
  Z_0=Z_p^{I_j}(K,\sigma_j/2).
\]
As in the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:weighted-separated-fan}, there are
\(x\in K\) and
\[
  Z=\{z\in Z_0:d(x,z)\in I_j\}
\]
such that every \(z\in Z\) has the displayed backscatter lower bound and
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z}\tau_p(x,z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4}\chiBar_p.
\]
Since \(\tau_p(x,z)\le1\), this also gives
\[
  |Z|\ge c\,2^{-2\eta(j-J)}\chiBar_p.
\]
If \(2^j\le BL\), then the volume-growth bound gives
\[
  |Z|
  \le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+1}}
  \le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2B\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
and \(2^{2\eta(j-J)}\le(BL)^{2\eta}\).  This contradicts the choice of
\(p_*\).  Hence \(2^j>BL\).

Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted-separated-subfan-extraction} to \(Z\), with
weights \(a_z=\tau_p(x,z)\), and with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor .
\]
The resulting set \(Z_\theta\) is \(2r_p\)-separated and inherits the annular
relation, the scale bound \(2^j>BL\), and the pointwise backscatter lower bound
from \(Z\).  Since
\[
  V_{2r_p}\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2r_p}
  \le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
the weighted extraction gives
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z_\theta}\tau_p(x,z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4C_{\rm vol}}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
Multiplying by the pointwise lower bound
\((\sigma_j/2)\chiBar_p\) for the backscatter from \(K\) gives the displayed
lower bound on \(\mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)\).  The cardinality bound
follows from \(\tau_p(x,z)\le1\), and ball disjointness follows from
separation.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Separated fans]
\label{def:separated-fans}
Assume \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  Fix
\(0<\epsilon\le1\), \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/2\), and integers \(J,H\ge0\).
For \(p<\pc\), an \((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\) is a
quadruple \((K,x,j,Z)\) such that \(K\subset V\) is finite non-empty,
\(x\in K\), \(j>J+H\), \(Z\subset V\) is finite non-empty, and, writing
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
the following conditions hold:
\[
  |K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  2^j\ge \frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  |Z|\ge \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4\Delta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta},
  \qquad
  d(x,z)\in I_j\quad(z\in Z),
\]
\[
  d(z,z')>2r_p
  \qquad(z,z'\in Z,\ z\ne z'),
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,z)
  \ge \frac{\sigma_j}{2}\chiBar_p
  \qquad(z\in Z).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Root-weighted separated fans]
\label{def:root-weighted-separated-fans}
An \((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan \((K,x,j,Z)\) at \(p\) is
root-weighted if, with \(\sigma_j\) as in
Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans},
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z}\tau_p(x,z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^2}{4\Delta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Fan exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:fan-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/2\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\) exists for any
\(p\in[p_1,\pc)\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We prove the first claim by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0.
\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:separated-logarithmic-backscatter-fan}.  Fix arbitrary
\(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/2\), and integers \(J,H\ge0\).  That corollary says
that for every \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there is
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) and an \((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at
\(p\).  Hence this \(\epsilon\) violates the asserted fan-exclusion property.
The contrapositive proves
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

Under the additional quasi-transitivity and mean-field susceptibility
assumptions, the \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Weighted fan exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:weighted-fan-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/2\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no root-weighted
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\) exists for any
\(p\in[p_1,\pc)\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The proof is the same contrapositive argument as for
Proposition~\ref{prop:fan-exclusion-criterion}, using
Corollary~\ref{cor:weighted-separated-fan} in place of
Corollary~\ref{cor:separated-logarithmic-backscatter-fan}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Fan energy exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:fan-energy-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/2\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan \((K,x,j,Z)\) at \(p\) satisfies
\[
  \mathcal W_p^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}(x,K,Z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta}\chiBar_p^{2-2\theta}
\]
for any \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), where \(\sigma_j\) is the parameter in
Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Again argue by contraposition.  If
\(\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p>0\), then
Corollary~\ref{cor:weighted-separated-fan} supplies an \(\epsilon>0\) such
that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/2\), and every \(J,H\),
near-critical parameters contain a separated fan with the displayed fan-energy
lower bound.  This contradicts the asserted exclusion property for that
\(\epsilon\).  The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gated fan obstruction]
\label{cor:gated-fan-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/4\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a
set \(Z_\theta\subset V\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\), and
\[
  \mathcal G_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta}\chiBar_p^{2-2\theta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:weighted-separated-fan} applies to every
\(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and
\[
  \left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor\ge1
  \qquad(p\in[p_*,\pc)).
\]
Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\).
Let \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta\) be supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:weighted-separated-fan}.  Since
\(2^j\ge(1/4)\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\) and \(\theta<1/4\), we have
\[
  r_p<2^j.
\]
Thus \(I_j\subseteq(r_p,\infty)\), and Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-decomposition}
applies.  Combining
\[
  \mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta}\chiBar_p^{2-2\theta}
\]
with
\[
  \mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \le
  \mathcal G_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
\]
gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive gated fan obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-gated-fan-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), and a set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
the data satisfy the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan}, and
\[
  \mathcal G_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8C_{\rm vol}}
  \chiBar_p^{2-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan} applies to every
\(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and
\[
  \left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor\ge1
  \qquad(p\in[p_*,\pc)).
\]
Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan}.  Since
\[
  2^j>B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  r_p\le\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p<B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
we have \(r_p<2^j\).  Thus \(I_j\subseteq(r_p,\infty)\), and
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-decomposition} applies.  Combining
\[
  \mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8C_{\rm vol}}
  \chiBar_p^{2-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega}
\]
with
\[
  \mathcal W_p^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
  \le
  \mathcal G_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta)
\]
gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive point-gated fan obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-point-gated-fan-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a finite non-empty set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\), and maps \(a,b:Z_\theta\to V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
the data satisfy the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan},
\[
  d(a_z,z)=d(b_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z_\theta),
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal H_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a,b)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{2-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gated-fan-obstruction}.  Since
\(d(x,z)\in I_j\) for every \(z\in Z_\theta\) and \(r_p<2^j\), each sphere
\(\{v:d(v,z)=r_p\}\) is non-empty.  Let
\[
  M_{r_p}=\sup_{z\in V}|\{v:d(v,z)=r_p\}|.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-pair-selection} gives maps \(a,b:Z_\theta\to V\) with
\[
  \mathcal H_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a,b)
  \ge
  M_{r_p}^{-2}\mathcal G_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta).
\]
The volume-growth bound gives
\[
  M_{r_p}\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{r_p}
  \le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
Combining this with
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gated-fan-obstruction} gives the displayed
point-gated lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive one-gate fan obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-one-gate-fan-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-2\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a finite non-empty set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\), and a map \(a:Z_\theta\to V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
the data satisfy the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan},
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z_\theta),
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal J_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a)
  \ge
  p^{2r_p}
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{2-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta,a,b\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-point-gated-fan-obstruction}.  The
gate-coalescence lemma gives
\[
  \mathcal J_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a)
  \ge
  p^{2r_p}
  \mathcal H_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a,b),
\]
and the point-gated lower bound gives the displayed one-gate lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive high one-gate obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-high-one-gate-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a finite non-empty set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset \(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a
map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
the tuple \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) satisfies the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan},
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
and, putting
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
we have
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The condition \(1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0\) implies the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-one-gate-fan-obstruction}.  Thus we may
choose \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta\) and a map \(a_0:Z_\theta\to V\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-one-gate-fan-obstruction}.  Set
\[
  \Lambda=
  p^{2r_p}
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{2-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
Since \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) satisfies the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan}, the balls
\(B(z,r_p)\), \(z\in Z_\theta\), are pairwise disjoint.  Since
\(d(a_{0,z},z)=r_p\), the vertices \(a_{0,z}\) are distinct, and hence
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z_\theta}\tau_p(x,a_{0,z})\le\chiBar_p .
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:high-one-gate-layer-extraction} to \(a_0\) with
\(L=\Lambda\), and let \(Z^\sharp\) be the resulting set.  Restrict \(a_0\) to
\(Z^\sharp\), and call the restriction \(a\).  Since
\[
  \frac{\Lambda}{2\chiBar_p}
  =
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
\]
the two displayed lower bounds follow.  The root lower bound makes
\(Z^\sharp\) non-empty.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive expanded gate-annulus obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a finite non-empty set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset \(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a
map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
the tuple \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) satisfies the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan},
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
\[
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the data by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-high-one-gate-obstruction}.  If
\(z\in Z^\sharp\), then \(d(a_z,z)=r_p\), while the weighted separated-fan
conclusions give \(d(x,z)\in I_j\).  The triangle inequality gives
\[
  d(x,a_z)\in(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p]=I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}.
\]
Similarly, every \(y\in K\) with \(d(y,z)\in I_j\) satisfies
\[
  d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}.
\]
Thus the pointwise \(K\)-mass lower bound from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-high-one-gate-obstruction} remains valid
when the summation is enlarged to \(d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\).  The
remaining displayed properties are inherited.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Capped anchor-count feasibility]
\label{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\) and
\[
  \rho(\theta,U,\omega)
  =
  1-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega-2U\alpha_\omega .
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\),
every \(U>B\), every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), either
\[
  2^j>UL,
\]
or
\[
  A_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{\rho(\theta,U,\omega)}
  \le 1,
\]
where
\[
  A_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{16C_{\rm vol}^4}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}U^{-3\eta}.
\]
Consequently, for fixed admissible parameters, a capped branch occurring
arbitrarily close to criticality forces \(\rho(\theta,U,\omega)\le0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Take
\(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that the expanded gate-annulus obstruction
applies, every selected \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\), and
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\ge1\).  Choose the expanded gate-annulus data.  If
\(2^j>UL\), the first alternative holds, so assume \(2^j\le UL\).

Let
\[
  A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}.
\]
The separated-fan conclusion gives disjointness of the balls \(B(z,r_p)\),
and since \(d(a_z,z)=r_p\), the map \(z\mapsto a_z\) is injective on
\(Z^\sharp\).  The root-mass lower bound and \(\tau_p\le1\) therefore give
\[
  |A|
  \ge
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
The metric conclusions also give \(A\subseteq B(x,2^{j+1}+r_p)\).  Under the
cap \(2^j\le UL\),
\[
  |A|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+1}+r_p}
  \le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(2U+\theta)\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Since \(p\ge1/\Delta\), \(r_p\le\theta L\), and \(j\le\log_2(UL)\), we have
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \ge
  \frac{1}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}U^{-3\eta}L^{-3\eta}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Combining the last three displays gives the stated feasibility inequality.

If the capped branch occurs for a sequence \(p\uparrow\pc\), then the displayed
inequality holds along that sequence.  Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) and
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), this is impossible when
\(\rho(\theta,U,\omega)>0\).  Hence \(\rho(\theta,U,\omega)\le0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Optimized anchor-count gate escape]
\label{cor:optimized-anchor-count-gate-escape}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, put
\[
  \alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega .
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that the following holds.  If
\(\alpha_\omega>0\), then for every
\[
  0<U<\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega},
\]
every \(\eta>0\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), the same conclusion holds for every finite \(U>0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}.  First suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega>0\) and \(0<U<1/(2\alpha_\omega)\).  Choose \(B=U/2\), and
then choose \(\theta>0\) so small that
\[
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
and
\[
  1-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega-2U\alpha_\omega>0 .
\]
Also \(2B\alpha_\omega=U\alpha_\omega<1/2<1\).  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, for all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\) there are expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
either the desired inequality \(2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), or the capped
anchor-count feasibility inequality with a positive exponent.  Taking \(p_0\)
still closer to \(\pc\) makes the latter inequality impossible, so the desired
escape holds.

If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), fix finite \(U>0\), choose \(B=U/2\), and then choose
\(0<\theta<\min\{B,1/2\}\).  The same argument applies because
\(\rho(\theta,U,\omega)=1-2\theta>0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Half-logarithmic expanded gate obstruction]
\label{cor:half-log-expanded-gate-obstruction}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, put
\[
  \alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega .
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that the following holds.  If
\(\alpha_\omega>0\), then for every \(\delta>0\), every \(\eta>0\), every
pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\),
there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-\delta\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), the same conclusion holds with the right-hand side
replaced by \(U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\) for every finite \(U>0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(\alpha_\omega>0\), choose
\[
  0<U<\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}
  \quad\text{with}\quad
  U>\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-\delta .
\]
The first part follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:optimized-anchor-count-gate-escape} with this \(U\).  The
case \(\alpha_\omega=0\) is exactly the second part of that corollary.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Corollary~\ref{cor:optimized-anchor-count-gate-escape} is the strongest pure
scale amplification available from the present volume-counting inputs.  It
uses only the number of selected anchors \(A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}\).  The
support-profile arguments below are therefore not needed to force logarithmic
escape up to \(1/(2\alpha_\omega)\); their role is to expose the additional
two-replica support geometry of the remaining live branch.

The scale hierarchy is as follows.  The normalized square-profile argument
forces capped escape only up to \(U<1/(4\alpha_\omega)\), the Schur and
support-profile arguments reach \(U<1/(3\alpha_\omega)\), and the anchor count
reaches \(U<1/(2\alpha_\omega)\).  These thresholds refer to different
objects, so the weaker support-profile range below should be read as a
diagnostic for \(Y\) and \(\Theta_p\), not as the best available pure scale
bound.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Anchor-count large-scale criterion]
\label{prop:anchor-count-large-scale-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\), \(U>B\), \(\theta>0\),
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
\[
  \rho(\theta,U,\omega)
  =
  1-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega-2U\alpha_\omega
  >0,
\]
and no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}, with
these parameters, and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We prove the first claim by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0 .
\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, and choose
\(\eta,B,U,\theta,J,H,p_1\) from the assumed criterion for this \(\epsilon\).
Put \(\rho=\rho(\theta,U,\omega)>0\), and
\[
  A_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{16C_{\rm vol}^4}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}U^{-3\eta}.
\]
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
\(p_*\ge p_1\), the capped anchor-count feasibility corollary applies to every
\(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and whenever \(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  A_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^\rho>1 .
\]
This is possible because \(\rho>0\) and \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\).

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\).  Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}
gives expanded gate-annulus data.  Its large-scale alternative contradicts
the assumed exclusion.  Its capped feasibility alternative contradicts the
choice of \(p_*\).  This contradiction proves
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Half-logarithmic expanded-gate exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:half-log-expanded-gate-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  If \(\alpha_\omega>0\), suppose
that for every \(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\[
  0<\delta<\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega},
  \qquad
  \eta>0,
  \qquad
  J,H\ge0,
  \qquad
  p_1<\pc
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-\delta\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), the same conclusion holds if for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist a finite \(U>0\), \(\eta>0\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits data
satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
In either case, if \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We argue by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0 .
\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:half-log-expanded-gate-obstruction}.

First suppose \(\alpha_\omega>0\), and choose
\(\delta,\eta,J,H,p_1\) from the assumed exclusion for this \(\epsilon\).  Take
\(p_0\ge p_1\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:half-log-expanded-gate-obstruction} applies.  It gives
expanded gate-annulus data satisfying the displayed half-logarithmic lower
bound, contradicting the exclusion.

If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), choose \(U,\eta,J,H,p_1\) from the assumed exclusion
for this \(\epsilon\), take \(p_0\ge p_1\) close enough to \(\pc\), and apply
the second part of Corollary~\ref{cor:half-log-expanded-gate-obstruction}.
This again contradicts the exclusion.  Hence
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

The final assertion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-half-logarithmic anchor-density obstruction]
\label{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega>0\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that
for every \(\lambda>0\), every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\), every
\(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  U_\lambda=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda,
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
and with
\[
  A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\},
  \qquad
  R_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=2^{j+1}+r_p,
\]
at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>U_\lambda L,
\]
or
\[
  \frac{|A|}{|B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})|}
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where
\[
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}
  =
  \frac{1}{16C_{\rm vol}^4}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)^{-3\eta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Take
\(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that the expanded gate-annulus obstruction
applies, every selected \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\), and
\(L\ge1\).  Choose the expanded gate-annulus data.  If
\(2^j>U_\lambda L\), the first alternative holds, so assume
\(2^j\le U_\lambda L\).

As in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, the map
\(z\mapsto a_z\) is injective on \(Z^\sharp\), and
\[
  |A|
  \ge
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
Since \(p\ge1/\Delta\), \(r_p\le\theta L\), and \(2^j\le U_\lambda L\), we
have
\[
  |A|
  \ge
  \frac{1}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}
  U_\lambda^{-3\eta}
  L^{-3\eta}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
The metric conclusions give \(A\subseteq B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})\), while the
volume bound and the cap give
\[
  |B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})|
  \le
  C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+1}+r_p}
  \le
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(2U_\lambda+\theta)\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Dividing the last two displays and using
\[
  1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha_\omega
  -(2U_\lambda+\theta)\alpha_\omega
  =
  -2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega
\]
gives the stated density lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Near-half-logarithmic density-exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:near-half-log-density-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1<\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\lambda>0\), \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\),
\(\theta>0\), integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying all
conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
either of the following two conditions:
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p ,
\]
or, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  2^j\le
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)L
\]
and
\[
  \frac{|A|}{|B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})|}
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where
\[
  A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\},
  \qquad
  R_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  =
  2^{j+1}+\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
and \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We argue by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0 .
\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}, and choose the
parameters from the assumed exclusion for this \(\epsilon\).  Take
\(p_0\ge p_1\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction} applies.  The
corollary gives expanded gate-annulus data satisfying either the displayed
super-half-logarithmic scale condition or the capped density condition.  Both
are excluded by assumption, a contradiction.  Hence
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-half-logarithmic root-ball mass obstruction]
\label{cor:near-half-log-root-ball-mass-obstruction}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega>0\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that
for every \(\lambda>0\), every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\), every
\(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  U_\lambda=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda,
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  R_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=2^{j+1}+r_p,
\]
at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>U_\lambda L,
\]
or
\[
  \frac{1}{|B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})|}
  \sum_{a\in B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})}\tau_p(x,a)
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the same data as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  If
\(2^j>U_\lambda L\), there is nothing to prove, so assume
\(2^j\le U_\lambda L\).  Put \(A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}\).  The expanded
gate-annulus obstruction gives \(A\subseteq B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})\).  As in
the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, the map
\(z\mapsto a_z\) is injective on \(Z^\sharp\), and hence
\[
  \sum_{a\in A}\tau_p(x,a)
  =
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
The lower bound on \(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\) and the upper bound on
\(|B(x,R_{j,p}^{\rm gate})|\) from the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction} therefore give
the displayed average-mass lower bound.
\end{proof}

  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .

then

\begin{proof}

\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-ball-mass-obstruction}, and choose the
parameters from the assumed criterion for this \(\epsilon\).  Take
\(p_0\ge p_1\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-ball-mass-obstruction} applies.  The
corollary gives expanded gate-annulus data satisfying either the
super-half-logarithmic scale condition, contradicting the first exclusion, or
the displayed root-ball mass lower bound.  In the latter case the inherited
weighted separated-fan conclusion gives \(2^j>B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), so the
second exclusion applies and gives the contradiction.  Hence
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-half-logarithmic root-annulus mass obstruction]
\label{cor:near-half-log-root-annulus-mass-obstruction}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega>0\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that
for every \(\lambda>0\), every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\), every
\(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  U_\lambda=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda,
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>U_\lambda L,
\]
or
\[
  \frac{
    \sum_{\substack{a\in V\\ d(x,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(x,a)
  }{
    |\{a\in V:d(x,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  }
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the same data as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-ball-mass-obstruction}.  If
\(2^j>U_\lambda L\), there is nothing to prove, so assume
\(2^j\le U_\lambda L\).  Put
\[
  S_{j,p}(x)=\{a\in V:d(x,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}.
\]
The expanded gate-annulus obstruction gives
\(A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}\subseteq S_{j,p}(x)\), and the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-ball-mass-obstruction} gives
\[
  \sum_{a\in A}\tau_p(x,a)\ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
Hence \(S_{j,p}(x)\) is non-empty and
\[
  \sum_{a\in S_{j,p}(x)}\tau_p(x,a)\ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
Since \(S_{j,p}(x)\subseteq B(x,2^{j+1}+r_p)\), the same volume bound used in
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-ball-mass-obstruction} gives
\[
  |S_{j,p}(x)|
  \le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(2U_\lambda+\theta)\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Dividing by this upper bound and using the lower bound on
\(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\) from the capped case gives the displayed annular
average lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-half-logarithmic root-sphere mass obstruction]
\label{cor:near-half-log-root-sphere-mass-obstruction}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega>0\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that
for every \(\lambda>0\), every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\), every
\(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  U_\lambda=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda,
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>U_\lambda L,
\]
or there is an integer \(n\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\cap\mathbb N\) such that
\[
  \{a\in V:d(x,a)=n\}\ne\varnothing
\]
and
\[
  \frac{
    \sum_{\substack{a\in V\\d(x,a)=n}}\tau_p(x,a)
  }{
    |\{a\in V:d(x,a)=n\}|
  }
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-annulus-mass-obstruction}.  If the
super-half-logarithmic scale alternative fails, put
\[
  S_n(x)=\{a\in V:d(x,a)=n\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal N=I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\cap\mathbb N .
\]
The annulus \(\{a:d(x,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}\) is a disjoint union of the
non-empty sets \(S_n(x)\), \(n\in\mathcal N\).  Its average root mass is the
corresponding size-weighted average of the exact-sphere averages.  Since the
annular average is at least the displayed threshold, one exact sphere must
have average at least the same threshold.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Spherical-average two-point profile]
\label{def:spherical-average-two-point-profile}
For \(n\ge0\), define
\[
  \bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n)
  =
  \sup_{\substack{x\in V\\ S_n(x)\ne\varnothing}}
  \frac{1}{|S_n(x)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_n(x)}\tau_p(x,a),
  \qquad
  S_n(x)=\{a\in V:d(x,a)=n\}.
\]
If \(S_n(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\in V\), we set
\(\bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n)=0\).
\end{definition}

  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is an immediate consequence of
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-sphere-mass-obstruction} and
Definition~\ref{def:spherical-average-two-point-profile}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Near-half-logarithmic spherical-profile criterion]
\label{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1<\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\lambda>0\), \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\),
\(\theta>0\), integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
such that the following two exclusions hold.  First, no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\)
admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Second, for every \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) and every integer \(j>J+H\) satisfying
\[
  B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p
  <
  2^j\le
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
put
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  =
  \left(2^j-\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
        2^{j+1}+\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor\right].
\]
Then, for every \(n\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\cap\mathbb N\),
\[
  \bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n)
  <
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We argue by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0 .
\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-spherical-profile-obstruction}, and choose
the parameters from the assumed criterion for this \(\epsilon\).  Take
\(p_0\ge p_1\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-spherical-profile-obstruction} applies.  The
corollary gives expanded gate-annulus data satisfying either the
super-half-logarithmic scale condition, contradicting the first exclusion, or
a spherical-profile lower bound.  In the latter case the inherited weighted
separated-fan conclusion gives \(2^j>B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), so the second
