exclusion applies and gives the contradiction.  Hence
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic-free near-half-logarithmic spherical-profile criterion]
\label{cor:dyadic-free-near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}
Let \(G\), \(\Delta\), \(\omega\), \(C_{\rm vol}\), and
\(\alpha_\omega\) satisfy the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}.  Suppose
that for every \(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\(\lambda>0\), \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\), \(\theta>0\), integers \(J,H\ge0\), and
\(p_1<\pc\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Assume also that, for every \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  A_{\lambda,\theta}
  =
  2\lambda\alpha_\omega+2\theta+5\theta\alpha_\omega,
\]
every integer \(n\) satisfying
\[
  (B-\theta)L<n\le
  \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+2\lambda+\theta\right)L
\]
obeys
\[
  \bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n)
  <
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-A_{\lambda,\theta}},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
It suffices to verify the second exclusion in
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}.  Let
\[
  B L<2^j\le
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)L
\]
and let \(n\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\cap\mathbb N\).  Since
\(r_p=\lfloor\theta L\rfloor\le\theta L\), the lower endpoint gives
\[
  n>2^j-r_p>(B-\theta)L.
\]
The upper endpoint gives
\[
  n\le 2^{j+1}+r_p
  \le
  \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+2\lambda+\theta\right)L.
\]
Thus the dyadic-free profile assumption implies the second exclusion in
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}.  The
conclusion follows from that proposition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Remote spherical-profile exponent criterion]
\label{cor:remote-spherical-profile-exponent-criterion}
Let \(G\), \(\Delta\), \(\omega\), \(C_{\rm vol}\), and
\(\alpha_\omega\) satisfy the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}.  Suppose
that for every \(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\(\lambda>0\), \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\), \(\theta>0\), integers \(J,H\ge0\), and
\(p_1<\pc\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
For \(p<\pc\), put \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  A_{\lambda,\theta}
  =
  2\lambda\alpha_\omega+2\theta+5\theta\alpha_\omega,
\]
and
\[
  \Phi_p(B,\lambda,\theta)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n):
    n\in\mathbb N,\ 
    (B-\theta)L<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+2\lambda+\theta\right)L
  \right\},
\]
with the convention that the supremum over an empty set is \(0\).  Assume
that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta \Phi_p(B,\lambda,\theta)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -A_{\lambda,\theta},
\]
where \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(D=D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) be the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  The strict
limsup hypothesis gives \(\delta>0\) and, after increasing \(p_1\), the bound
\[
  \Phi_p(B,\lambda,\theta)
  \le
  \chiBar_p^{-A_{\lambda,\theta}-\delta}
  \qquad(p\in[p_1,\pc)).
\]
Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\), we may increase \(p_1\) again so that
\[
  \chiBar_p^{-\delta}
  <
  D L^{-3\eta}
  \qquad(p\in[p_1,\pc)).
\]
Thus the dyadic-free profile bound required by
Corollary~\ref{cor:dyadic-free-near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}
holds.  Applying that corollary gives the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Half-to-full logarithmic spherical-profile criterion]
\label{cor:half-to-full-log-spherical-profile-criterion}
Let \(G\), \(\Delta\), \(\omega\), \(C_{\rm vol}\), and
\(\alpha_\omega\) satisfy the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}.  Suppose
that for every \(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\[
  0<s<\frac{1}{6\alpha_\omega},
  \qquad
  \eta>0,
  \qquad
  J,H\ge0,
  \qquad
  0<p_1<\pc,
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+s\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Assume also that, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  \Psi_p(s)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n):
    n\in\mathbb N,\ 
    \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s\right)L<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
where the empty supremum is \(0\), satisfies
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\Psi_p(s)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
with \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:remote-spherical-profile-exponent-criterion} with
\[
  \lambda=s,\qquad
  \theta=s,\qquad
  B=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-2s .
\]
The restriction \(s<1/(6\alpha_\omega)\) gives \(B>0\), \(\theta<B\),
\(2B\alpha_\omega<1\), and \(1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0\).  The remote interval
in Corollary~\ref{cor:remote-spherical-profile-exponent-criterion} becomes
\[
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s\right)L<n\le
  \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L,
\]
and its exponent is
\[
  2s\alpha_\omega+2s+5s\alpha_\omega
  =
  (2+7\alpha_\omega)s.
\]
Thus the hypotheses are exactly those of the remote exponent criterion with
this parameter choice.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Geodesic baseline for the half-to-full profile target]
\label{rem:half-to-full-profile-geodesic-baseline}
Assume that \(G\) is connected and infinite.  For every \(p<\pc\), every
root \(x\), and every \(a\in S_n(x)\), the event that one fixed geodesic from
\(x\) to \(a\) is open gives
\[
  \tau_p(x,a)\ge p^n .
\]
Consequently
\[
  \bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n)\ge p^n
  \qquad(n\ge0),
\]
and the half-to-full window in
Corollary~\ref{cor:half-to-full-log-spherical-profile-criterion} necessarily
satisfies
\[
  \liminf_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\Psi_p(s)}{\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  \ge
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s\right)\log_\Delta\pc .
\]
Thus the exponent target in that corollary is not ruled out by the geodesic
baseline whenever
\[
  (2+7\alpha_\omega)s
  <
  -\left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s\right)\log_\Delta\pc .
\]
Since \(\pc<1\) on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs, this compatibility
condition holds for all sufficiently small positive \(s\), for instance for
\[
  s<
  \frac{-\log_\Delta\pc}
       {2\alpha_\omega\left(2+7\alpha_\omega-3\log_\Delta\pc\right)}.
\]
This does not prove the required upper bound; it only records that the
spherical-average formulation avoids the immediate geodesic obstruction that
afflicts strict pointwise-supremum criteria.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Geodesic-normalized half-to-full profile criterion]
\label{cor:geodesic-normalized-half-to-full-profile-criterion}
Let \(G\), \(\Delta\), \(\omega\), \(C_{\rm vol}\), and
\(\alpha_\omega\) satisfy the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}, and suppose
that \(G\) is connected and infinite.  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\[
  0<s<\frac{1}{6\alpha_\omega},
  \qquad
  \eta>0,
  \qquad
  J,H\ge0,
  \qquad
  0<p_1<\pc,
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+s\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
With \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), put
\[
  c_s=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak E_p^{\rm sph}(s)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \frac{\bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n)}{p^n}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\ 
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
with the convention that the empty supremum is \(0\).  Assume that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak E_p^{\rm sph}(s)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is locally finite and quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For every \(n\) in the defining window of \(\Psi_p(s)\), we have
\(n>c_sL\).  Since \(p<1\),
\[
  p^n\le p^{c_sL},
\]
and hence
\[
  \Psi_p(s)\le p^{c_sL}\mathfrak E_p^{\rm sph}(s).
\]
Taking logarithms, using \(p\uparrow\pc\), and applying the assumed strict
excess bound gives
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\Psi_p(s)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -(2+7\alpha_\omega)s.
\]
The conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:half-to-full-log-spherical-profile-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Spherical averaged self-avoiding envelope]
\label{def:spherical-averaged-saw-envelope}
For \(0<p\le1\) and \(n\ge0\), define
\[
  \mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw,sph}(n)
  =
  \sup_{\substack{x\in V\\S_n(x)\ne\varnothing}}
  \frac{1}{|S_n(x)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_n(x)}
  \sum_{\gamma:x\to a\ {\rm SAW}} p^{|\gamma|-n},
\]
where the inner sum is over finite self-avoiding paths from \(x\) to \(a\),
including the trivial path when \(x=a\), and may take the value \(+\infty\).
If \(S_n(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\), we set
\(\mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw,sph}(n)=0\).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Self-avoiding envelope controls the normalized spherical profile]
\label{lem:saw-envelope-controls-normalized-spherical-profile}
Let \(G\) be connected, and let \(0<p\le1\).  For every \(n\ge0\),
\[
  \frac{\bar\tau_p^{\rm sph}(n)}{p^n}
  \le
  \mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw,sph}(n).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(x\) with \(S_n(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(a\in S_n(x)\).  On the event
\(\{x\leftrightarrow a\}\), the open cluster contains an open self-avoiding
path from \(x\) to \(a\).  The union bound gives
\[
  \tau_p(x,a)
  \le
  \sum_{\gamma:x\to a\ {\rm SAW}} p^{|\gamma|}.
\]
Divide by \(p^n\), average over \(a\in S_n(x)\), and take the supremum over
\(x\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Self-avoiding half-to-full envelope criterion]
\label{cor:saw-half-to-full-envelope-criterion}
Let \(G\), \(\Delta\), \(\omega\), \(C_{\rm vol}\), and
\(\alpha_\omega\) satisfy the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}, and suppose
that \(G\) is connected and infinite.  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\[
  0<s<\frac{1}{6\alpha_\omega},
  \qquad
  \eta>0,
  \qquad
  J,H\ge0,
  \qquad
  0<p_1<\pc,
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+s\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
With \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), put
\[
  c_s=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw}(s)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw,sph}(n):
    n\in\mathbb N,\ 
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
where the empty supremum is \(0\).  Assume that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw}(s)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is locally finite and quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:saw-envelope-controls-normalized-spherical-profile}, the
quantity \(\mathfrak E_p^{\rm sph}(s)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:geodesic-normalized-half-to-full-profile-criterion} is at
most \(\mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw}(s)\).  The stated exponent hypothesis
therefore implies the exponent hypothesis of that corollary.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Spherical excess-length self-avoiding counts]
\label{def:spherical-excess-length-saw-counts}
For \(n,k\ge0\), define
\[
  \mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  =
  \sup_{\substack{x\in V\\S_n(x)\ne\varnothing}}
  \frac{1}{|S_n(x)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_n(x)}
  \#\{\gamma:x\to a\ {\rm SAW}:|\gamma|=n+k\},
\]
with value \(0\) if \(S_n(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Excess-length upper bound for the spherical SAW envelope]
\label{lem:spherical-saw-excess-length-decomposition}
For every \(0<p\le1\) and \(n\ge0\),
\[
  \mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw,sph}(n)
  \le
  \sum_{k\ge0} p^k\,\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph},
\]
where both sides may be \(+\infty\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If \(d(x,a)=n\), every self-avoiding path from \(x\) to \(a\) has length
\(n+k\) for some \(k\ge0\).  For fixed \(x\), grouping the inner sum in
Definition~\ref{def:spherical-averaged-saw-envelope} by this excess length
gives
\[
  \frac{1}{|S_n(x)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_n(x)}
  \sum_{\gamma:x\to a\ {\rm SAW}}p^{|\gamma|-n}
  =
  \sum_{k\ge0}p^k
  \frac{1}{|S_n(x)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_n(x)}
  \#\{\gamma:x\to a\ {\rm SAW}:|\gamma|=n+k\}.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(x\) on the left and then bounding each summand by
the corresponding supremum gives the stated upper bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[\(q\)-weighted excess-length SAW criterion]
\label{cor:q-weighted-excess-length-saw-criterion}
Let \(G\), \(\Delta\), \(\omega\), \(C_{\rm vol}\), and
\(\alpha_\omega\) satisfy the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}, and suppose
that \(G\) is connected and infinite.  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\[
  0<s<\frac{1}{6\alpha_\omega},
  \qquad
  \eta>0,
  \qquad
  J,H\ge0,
  \qquad
  0<p_1<\pc,
  \qquad
  q\in(\pc,1),
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+s\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
With \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), put
\[
  c_s=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak Q_q^{\rm saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{k\ge0}q^k\,\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\ 
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
where the empty supremum is \(0\).  Assume that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak Q_q^{\rm saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is locally finite and quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Since \(p<\pc<q\), Lemma~\ref{lem:spherical-saw-excess-length-decomposition}
gives
\[
  \mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw,sph}(n)
  \le
  \sum_{k\ge0}q^k\,\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}.
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak S_p^{\rm saw}(s)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:saw-half-to-full-envelope-criterion} is at most
\(\mathfrak Q_q^{\rm saw}(s,p)\), and the result follows from that
corollary.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-excess/tail SAW criterion]
\label{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}
Let \(G\), \(\Delta\), \(\omega\), \(C_{\rm vol}\), and
\(\alpha_\omega\) satisfy the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion}, and suppose
that \(G\) is connected and infinite.  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist
\[
  0<s<\frac{1}{6\alpha_\omega},
  \qquad
  \eta>0,
  \qquad
  J,H\ge0,
  \qquad
  0<p_1<\pc,
  \qquad
  q\in(\pc,1),
  \qquad
  \rho>0,
\]
such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying
all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+s\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
With \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), put
\[
  c_s=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s,
  \qquad
  K_{\rho,p}=\lfloor\rho L\rfloor .
\]
Define
\[
  \mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    q^k\,\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L,\
    0\le k\le K_{\rho,p}
  \right\}
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{k>K_{\rho,p}}q^k\,\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
where empty suprema and empty sums are \(0\).  Assume that both
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s
\]
and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s
\]
hold, with \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is locally finite and quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For every \(n\) in the half-to-full logarithmic window,
\[
  \sum_{k\ge0}q^k\,\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  \le
  (K_{\rho,p}+1)\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)
  +\mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p).
\]
The assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-spherical-profile-criterion} include
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), so \(L\to\infty\) and
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\log_\Delta(K_{\rho,p}+1)}{L}=0.
\]
The two displayed exponent assumptions therefore imply the exponent
hypothesis of
Corollary~\ref{cor:q-weighted-excess-length-saw-criterion}.  Applying that
corollary gives the conclusion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Binned finite-excess SAW criterion]
\label{cor:binned-finite-excess-saw-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}, the exponent hypothesis
on \(\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) may be replaced by the following
finite family of sufficient hypotheses.  Let \(\delta>0\), set
\[
  m_{\rho,\delta}=\left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{\delta}\right\rfloor+1,
\]
and, for \(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}\), define
\[
  \mathfrak B_{i,\delta}^{\rm saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L,\
    i\delta L\le k<(i+1)\delta L
  \right\},
\]
with empty supremum equal to \(0\).  If the long-excess hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} holds and, for every
\(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak B_{i,\delta}^{\rm saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  +i\delta\log_\Delta q
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
then the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(i\delta L\le k<(i+1)\delta L\), then \(q^k\le q^{i\delta L}\), since
\(q<1\).  Hence
\[
  \mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)
  \le
  \max_{0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}}
  q^{i\delta L}\mathfrak B_{i,\delta}^{\rm saw}(s,p).
\]
The number \(m_{\rho,\delta}\) is independent of \(p\).  The displayed binned
exponent inequalities therefore imply the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) in
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}; the long-excess
hypothesis is assumed.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Degree counting cannot control the long-excess tail]
\label{rem:degree-counting-long-excess-tail}
The long-excess term in
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} cannot be verified by
the raw bounded-degree count of self-avoiding paths.  Indeed, for
\(n+k\ge1\),
\[
  \mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  \le
  \Delta(\Delta-1)^{n+k-1}.
\]
Using this estimate in the \(q\)-weighted tail would require
\[
  q(\Delta-1)<1
\]
to obtain a geometric summation in \(k\).  But the standard tree-counting
susceptibility bound gives \(\pc(G)\ge1/(\Delta-1)\), and the criterion uses
\(q>\pc\).  Hence \(q(\Delta-1)>1\) in the relevant regime.  Any proof of the
long-excess hypothesis must therefore use the fixed exact sphere, endpoint
constraints, averaging over \(S_n(x)\), or additional geometry; ambient
degree growth alone is too coarse.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Radial-defect spherical SAW counts]
\label{def:radial-defect-spherical-saw-counts}
Let \(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_m)\) be a path with \(v_0=x\).  Define
\[
  I_x(\gamma)
  =
  \#\{1\le i\le m:d(x,v_i)=d(x,v_{i-1})-1\}
\]
and
\[
  H_x(\gamma)
  =
  \#\{1\le i\le m:d(x,v_i)=d(x,v_{i-1})\}.
\]
For \(n,b,h\ge0\), set
\[
  \mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}
  =
  \sup_{\substack{x\in V\\S_n(x)\ne\varnothing}}
  \frac{1}{|S_n(x)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_n(x)}
  \#\{\gamma:x\to a\ {\rm SAW}:I_x(\gamma)=b,\ H_x(\gamma)=h\},
\]
with value \(0\) if \(S_n(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Radial-defect decomposition of excess length]
\label{lem:radial-defect-excess-decomposition}
For every \(n,k\ge0\),
\[
  \mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  \le
  \sum_{\substack{b,h\ge0\\2b+h=k}}
  \mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(x\) with \(S_n(x)\ne\varnothing\), and let
\(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_m)\) be a self-avoiding path from \(x\) to
\(a\in S_n(x)\).  Let \(O_x(\gamma)\) be the number of steps increasing the
distance from \(x\) by one.  Since adjacent vertices have distances from \(x\)
that differ by at most one,
\[
  m=O_x(\gamma)+I_x(\gamma)+H_x(\gamma)
\]
and, because \(d(x,a)=n\),
\[
  n=O_x(\gamma)-I_x(\gamma).
\]
Thus
\[
  m-n=2I_x(\gamma)+H_x(\gamma).
\]
Consequently every length-\(n+k\) self-avoiding path from \(x\) to
\(S_n(x)\) contributes to exactly one pair \((b,h)\) with \(2b+h=k\).  After
averaging over \(S_n(x)\), taking the supremum over \(x\), and bounding the
supremum of the sum by the sum of suprema, the displayed inequality follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Radial-defect weighted SAW criterion]
\label{cor:radial-defect-weighted-saw-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:q-weighted-excess-length-saw-criterion}, the exponent
hypothesis on \(\mathfrak Q_q^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) may be replaced by the
following radial-defect hypothesis.  With \(L\) and \(c_s\) as in that
corollary, define
\[
  \mathfrak U_q^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{b,h\ge0}q^{2b+h}
    \mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
where the empty supremum is \(0\).  If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak U_q^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
with \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\), then the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:q-weighted-excess-length-saw-criterion} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-defect-excess-decomposition} gives, for each admissible
\(n\),
\[
  \sum_{k\ge0}q^k\,\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  \le
  \sum_{b,h\ge0}q^{2b+h}\,
  \mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}.
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak Q_q^{\rm saw}(s,p)\le
\mathfrak U_q^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)\), and the stated hypothesis implies the
hypothesis of
Corollary~\ref{cor:q-weighted-excess-length-saw-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inward-restricted horizontal radial tail split]
\label{cor:inward-horizontal-radial-tail-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}, the exponent hypothesis
on \(\mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) may be replaced by an inward tail
and a low-inward horizontal tail.  With \(L\), \(c_s\), and \(K_{\rho,p}\) as
in that corollary, define
\[
  \mathfrak I_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{b>K_{\rho,p}/4\\h\ge0}}
    q^{2b+h}\mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\}
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak H_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{0\le b\le K_{\rho,p}/4\\h>K_{\rho,p}/2}}
    q^{2b+h}\mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
where empty suprema and empty sums are \(0\).  If the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} holds and both
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak I_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s
\]
and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak H_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s
\]
hold, with \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\), then the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(K=K_{\rho,p}\).  For every admissible \(n\),
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-defect-excess-decomposition} gives
\[
  \sum_{k>K}q^k\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  \le
  \sum_{\substack{b,h\ge0\\2b+h>K}}
  q^{2b+h}\mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}.
\]
If \(2b+h>K\), then either \(b>K/4\), or else \(b\le K/4\) and
\(h>K/2\).  Therefore
\[
  \mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak I_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak H_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p).
\]
The two displayed exponent hypotheses imply the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) in
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}.  The finite-excess
hypothesis is assumed, so that corollary applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[No horizontal radial steps in bipartite graphs]
\label{lem:bipartite-no-horizontal-radial-steps}
If \(G\) is bipartite, then \(H_x(\gamma)=0\) for every path \(\gamma\) and
every starting vertex \(x\).  Consequently
\[
  \mathfrak M_{n,b,h}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}=0
  \qquad(h\ge1).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(V=V_0\cup V_1\) be a bipartition, and fix \(x\).  After interchanging
the colour classes if necessary, assume \(x\in V_0\).  Every vertex at even
distance from \(x\) lies in \(V_0\), and every vertex at odd distance from
\(x\) lies in \(V_1\).  Adjacent vertices have opposite colours, so their
distances from \(x\) have opposite parity.  Since adjacent distances from
\(x\) differ by at most one, they cannot be equal.  Hence no step of any path
keeps the distance from \(x\) fixed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bipartite inward-tail criterion]
\label{cor:bipartite-inward-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}, assume in addition that
\(G\) is bipartite.  If the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) from that corollary holds and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak I_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
with \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\), then the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:bipartite-no-horizontal-radial-steps},
\(\mathfrak H_{q,\rho}^{\rm rad,saw}(s,p)=0\).  Thus the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:inward-horizontal-radial-tail-split} hold.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact bipartite inward-tail criterion]
\label{cor:exact-bipartite-inward-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}, assume in addition that
\(G\) is bipartite.  With \(L\), \(c_s\), and \(K_{\rho,p}\) as in that
corollary, define
\[
  \mathfrak L_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{b>K_{\rho,p}/2}q^{2b}
    \mathfrak M_{n,b,0}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L
  \right\},
\]
where empty suprema and empty sums are \(0\).  If the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} holds and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak L_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
with \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\), then the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:bipartite-no-horizontal-radial-steps}, only the terms with
\(h=0\) can contribute.  Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-defect-excess-decomposition}
therefore gives, for every admissible \(n\),
\[
  \sum_{k>K_{\rho,p}}q^k\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  \le
  \sum_{b>K_{\rho,p}/2}q^{2b}
  \mathfrak M_{n,b,0}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}.
\]
Thus the displayed exponent hypothesis implies the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak T_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}(s,p)\) in
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}.  The finite-excess
hypothesis is assumed, so that corollary applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-parameter bipartite inward criterion]
\label{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion}, assume in addition that
\(G\) is bipartite.  With \(L\), \(c_s\), and \(K_{\rho,p}\) as in that
corollary, define
\[
  \mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    q^{2b}\mathfrak M_{n,b,0}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L,\
    0\le b\le K_{\rho,p}/2
  \right\}
\]
where empty suprema are \(0\), and let
\(\mathfrak L_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)\) be the tail profile from
Corollary~\ref{cor:exact-bipartite-inward-tail-criterion}.  If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s
\]
and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak L_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s
\]
hold, with \(\log_\Delta0=-\infty\), then the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:bipartite-no-horizontal-radial-steps}, only \(h=0\) can
occur.  Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-defect-excess-decomposition} gives, for each
admissible \(n\) and each \(0\le k\le K_{\rho,p}\),
\[
  q^k\mathfrak N_{n,k}^{\rm saw,sph}
  \le
  \sum_{\substack{b\ge0\\2b=k}}
  q^{2b}\mathfrak M_{n,b,0}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}
  \le
  \mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p).
\]
Thus the displayed exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}\) implies the finite-excess hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak A_{q,\rho}^{\rm saw}\).  The displayed exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}\) implies the tail hypothesis by
Corollary~\ref{cor:exact-bipartite-inward-tail-criterion}'s proof.  Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} gives the conclusion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Binned bipartite finite inward criterion]
\label{cor:binned-bipartite-finite-inward-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion}, the exponent
hypothesis on \(\mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)\) may be replaced by
the following finite family of sufficient hypotheses.  Let \(\delta>0\), set
\[
  m_{\rho,\delta}^{\rm in}
  =
  \left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{2\delta}\right\rfloor+1,
\]
and, for \(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{\rm in}\), define
\[
  \mathfrak C_{i,\delta}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \mathfrak M_{n,b,0}^{\rm rad,saw,sph}:
    n\in\mathbb N,\
    c_sL<n\le
    \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L,\
    i\delta L\le b<(i+1)\delta L
  \right\},
\]
with empty suprema equal to \(0\).  If the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion} holds and, for
every \(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{\rm in}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\log_\Delta\mathfrak C_{i,\delta}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)}
       {\log_\Delta\chiBar_p}
  +2i\delta\log_\Delta q
  <
  -c_s\log_\Delta\pc-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
then the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-excess-tail-saw-criterion} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(0\le b\le K_{\rho,p}/2\), then \(b\le \rho L/2\), so \(b\) belongs to
one of the bins \(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{\rm in}\).  In the \(i\)th bin,
\(q^{2b}\le q^{2i\delta L}\), since \(q<1\).  Hence
\[
  \mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)
  \le
  \max_{0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{\rm in}}
  q^{2i\delta L}\mathfrak C_{i,\delta}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p).
\]
The number \(m_{\rho,\delta}^{\rm in}\) is independent of \(p\).  The
displayed binned exponent hypotheses therefore imply the exponent hypothesis
on \(\mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{\rm in,saw}(s,p)\).  The tail hypothesis is
assumed, so Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion}
applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Subdivision reduction to bipartite graphs]
\label{prop:subdivision-bipartite-reduction}
Let \(G\) be a connected locally finite graph of maximum degree at most
\(\Delta<\infty\), and suppose that \(G\) is infinite.  Let
\(\operatorname{Sub}(G)\) be the graph obtained by subdividing every edge of
\(G\) once.  Then
\[
  \pc(\operatorname{Sub}(G))=\sqrt{\pc(G)}
\]
and
\[
  p_{2\to2}(\operatorname{Sub}(G))=\sqrt{p_{2\to2}(G)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \pc(\operatorname{Sub}(G))<p_{2\to2}(\operatorname{Sub}(G)).
\]
Moreover, if \(G\) is quasi-transitive and nonamenable, then
\(\operatorname{Sub}(G)\) is bipartite, quasi-transitive, and nonamenable.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\).  Its vertex set is \(V(G)\cup E(G)\), where
an edge-vertex \(e\in E(G)\) is adjacent in \(H\) to the two endpoints of
\(e\).  In Bernoulli-\(p\) percolation on \(H\), an original edge
\(e=\{u,v\}\) is open as a two-step connection between \(u\) and \(v\) exactly
when both subdivided edges incident to \(e\) are open.  These events are
independent over \(e\in E(G)\) and have probability \(p^2\).  Thus the open
clusters of old vertices in \(H[p]\) have the same law as the open clusters
of \(G[p^2]\).  Since every infinite cluster of \(H[p]\) contains infinitely
many old vertices, this proves
\[
  \pc(H)=\sqrt{\pc(G)}.
\]

It remains to compare the \(L^2\) thresholds.  Let \(q=p^2\), and let
\(T_G(q)\) and \(T_H(p)\) be the two-point operators on \(G\) and \(H\).
For old vertices \(x,y\in V(G)\),
\[
  \tau_p^H(x,y)=\tau_q^G(x,y).
\]
Let \(R:\ell^2(E(G))\to\ell^2(V(G))\) be the incidence operator
\[
  (Rf)(v)=\sum_{e\ni v}f(e).
\]
Since \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\) and each edge has two
endpoints, \(R\) is bounded.  If \(e\in E(G)\) is viewed as a midpoint, then
\[
  \tau_p^H(x,e)
  \le
  p\sum_{z\in e}\tau_q^G(x,z)
\]
and, for midpoints \(e,f\),
\[
  \tau_p^H(e,f)
  \le
  \mathbf 1_{\{e=f\}}
  +
  p^2\sum_{\substack{z\in e\\w\in f}}\tau_q^G(z,w).
\]
These inequalities give the block domination
\[
  T_H(p)
  \preceq
  \begin{pmatrix}
    T_G(q) & pT_G(q)R\\
    pR^*T_G(q) & I+p^2R^*T_G(q)R
  \end{pmatrix}
\]
in the sense of positive kernels.  Hence \(T_G(q)\) bounded on
\(\ell^2(V(G))\) implies \(T_H(p)\) bounded on
\(\ell^2(V(H))\).  Conversely, if \(T_H(p)\) is bounded, then restricting it
to functions supported on old vertices and then projecting back to old
vertices gives \(T_G(q)\), so \(T_G(q)\) is bounded.  Therefore
\[
  p<p_{2\to2}(H)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  p^2<p_{2\to2}(G),
\]
which proves the claimed identity for \(p_{2\to2}\).

The graph \(H\) is bipartite with parts \(V(G)\) and \(E(G)\).  If \(G\) is
quasi-transitive, then \(H\) is quasi-transitive because a locally finite
quasi-transitive graph has finitely many edge orbits.  Finally, \(G\) and
\(H\) are bounded-degree quasi-isometric graphs, so nonamenability is
preserved.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Subdivision susceptibility comparison]
\label{lem:subdivision-susceptibility-comparison}
Let \(G\) be a connected infinite graph of maximum degree at most
\(\Delta<\infty\), let \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\), and put \(q=p^2\).  There
is a constant \(C_\Delta<\infty\) such that, for every \(0\le p<1\),
\[
  \chiBar_q^G\le \chiBar_p^H
  \le C_\Delta\bigl(1+\chiBar_q^G\bigr).
\]
Consequently, if
\[
  \limsup_{q\uparrow\pc(G)}(\pc(G)-q)\chiBar_q^G<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}(\pc(H)-p)\chiBar_p^H<\infty.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The lower bound follows by restricting the susceptibility in \(H\) to old
vertices and using \(\tau_p^H(x,y)=\tau_q^G(x,y)\) for old vertices
\(x,y\).

For the upper bound, first let \(x\) be an old vertex.  The old-vertex
contribution to \(\chi_p^H(x)\) is \(\chi_q^G(x)\).  For a midpoint
\(e\in E(G)\),
\[
  \tau_p^H(x,e)\le p\sum_{z\in e}\tau_q^G(x,z),
\]
so the midpoint contribution is at most
\[
  p\sum_{e\in E(G)}\sum_{z\in e}\tau_q^G(x,z)
  \le p\Delta\,\chi_q^G(x).
\]
Thus \(\chi_p^H(x)\le(1+\Delta)\chiBar_q^G\).

Now let \(e\in E(G)\) be a midpoint.  For old vertices \(y\),
\[
  \tau_p^H(e,y)\le p\sum_{z\in e}\tau_q^G(z,y),
\]
so the old-vertex contribution is at most \(2p\chiBar_q^G\).  For midpoint
vertices \(f\),
\[
  \tau_p^H(e,f)
  \le
  \mathbf 1_{\{e=f\}}+
  p^2\sum_{\substack{z\in e\\w\in f}}\tau_q^G(z,w),
\]
and summing over \(f\in E(G)\) gives at most
\[
  1+p^2\Delta\sum_{z\in e}\chi_q^G(z)
  \le 1+2\Delta\chiBar_q^G.
\]
Combining the two cases gives the comparison.

Since \(\pc(H)=\sqrt{\pc(G)}\) by
Proposition~\ref{prop:subdivision-bipartite-reduction}, the final implication
follows from
\[
  \pc(G)-p^2=(\pc(H)-p)(\pc(H)+p)
\]
and the fact that \(\pc(H)>0\) for bounded-degree graphs.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Even-sphere subdivision radial identity]
\label{lem:even-sphere-subdivision-radial-identity}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite, let \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\),
and let \(x\in V(G)\).  For every self-avoiding path
\(\pi=(x_0,\ldots,x_\ell)\) in \(G\) with \(x_0=x\), let \(\widehat\pi\) be
its canonical lift to \(H\).  Then
\[
  I_x^H(\widehat\pi)
  =
  2I_x^G(\pi)+H_x^G(\pi).
\]
Consequently, for every \(n,B\ge0\) such that \(S_n^G(x)\ne\varnothing\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{1}{|S_{2n}^H(x)|}
  \sum_{y\in S_{2n}^H(x)}
  \#\{\gamma:x\to y\ {\rm SAW\ in\ }H:I_x^H(\gamma)=B\}
\\
&\qquad =
\frac{1}{|S_n^G(x)|}
  \sum_{y\in S_n^G(x)}
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}}
  \#\{\pi:x\to y\ {\rm SAW\ in\ }G:
      I_x^G(\pi)=i,\ H_x^G(\pi)=h\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, if the supremum defining
\(\mathfrak M_{2n,B,0}^{H,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}\) is restricted to old roots,
then the resulting even-sphere quantity is at most
\[
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}}
  \mathfrak M_{n,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}} .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every path in \(H\) from an old vertex to an old vertex has even length and
alternates old vertices and midpoints.  Projecting such a path to its old
vertices gives a path in \(G\), and self-avoidance in \(H\) implies
self-avoidance of the projected old-vertex path.  Conversely, every
self-avoiding path in \(G\) has a unique canonical lift to a self-avoiding
path in \(H\).  Thus canonical lift is a bijection between self-avoiding
paths in \(G\) from \(x\) to \(y\) and self-avoiding paths in \(H\) from the
old vertex \(x\) to the old vertex \(y\).

For an old vertex \(z\in V(G)\),
\[
  d_H(x,z)=2d_G(x,z).
\]
If \(e=\{u,v\}\) is a midpoint of \(H\), then
\[
  d_H(x,e)=2\min\{d_G(x,u),d_G(x,v)\}+1.
\]
Consider one step \(u\to v\) of \(\pi\), and write
\(r=d_G(x,u)\).  If \(d_G(x,v)=r+1\), its lifted two-step segment has no
inward step in \(H\).  If \(d_G(x,v)=r\), the lifted segment first moves
outward to the midpoint and then inward to \(v\), contributing one inward
step.  If \(d_G(x,v)=r-1\), both lifted half-steps are inward, contributing
two inward steps.  Summing over the steps of \(\pi\) gives
\[
  I_x^H(\widehat\pi)=2I_x^G(\pi)+H_x^G(\pi).
\]

Finally, \(S_{2n}^H(x)=S_n^G(x)\) as sets of old vertices, while
Lemma~\ref{lem:bipartite-no-horizontal-radial-steps} gives no horizontal
radial steps in \(H\).  The displayed average identity follows from the
bijection and the inward-count identity.  Taking the supremum over old roots
and then bounding the supremum of the sum by the sum of suprema gives the
final inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Odd-sphere old-root subdivision bound]
\label{lem:odd-sphere-old-root-subdivision-bound}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\), let
\(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\), fix \(x\in V(G)\), and define
\[
  A_{m,i,h}^G(x)
  =
  \frac{1}{|S_m^G(x)|}
  \sum_{y\in S_m^G(x)}
  \#\{\pi:x\to y\ {\rm SAW\ in\ }G:
      I_x^G(\pi)=i,\ H_x^G(\pi)=h\}.
\]
Suppose that every vertex in \(S_n^G(x)\) has a neighbour in
\(S_{n+1}^G(x)\).  Then, for every \(B\ge0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{1}{|S_{2n+1}^H(x)|}
  \sum_{e\in S_{2n+1}^H(x)}
  \#\{\gamma:x\to e\ {\rm SAW\ in\ }H:I_x^H(\gamma)=B\}
\\
&\qquad\le
  \Delta\sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}} A_{n,i,h}^G(x)
  +
  \Delta\sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B-1}} A_{n+1,i,h}^G(x),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second sum is \(0\) when \(B=0\).  In particular, under the same
local no-dead-end assumption, the old-root odd-sphere quantity is at most
\[
  \Delta\sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}}
  \mathfrak M_{n,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  +
  \Delta\sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B-1}}
  \mathfrak M_{n+1,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}} .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let
\[
  E_n(x)=\{e=\{u,v\}\in E(G):
  \min(d_G(x,u),d_G(x,v))=n\}.
\]
The midpoint vertices \(E_n(x)\) are exactly \(S_{2n+1}^H(x)\).  Since every
vertex of \(S_n^G(x)\) has an edge to \(S_{n+1}^G(x)\), choosing one such edge
for each vertex gives \(|E_n(x)|\ge |S_n^G(x)|\).  Also every vertex of
\(S_{n+1}^G(x)\) has an edge to \(S_n^G(x)\) along a geodesic to \(x\), so
\(|E_n(x)|\ge |S_{n+1}^G(x)|\).

Let \(\gamma\) be a self-avoiding path in \(H\) from \(x\) to a midpoint
\(e\in S_{2n+1}^H(x)\), and let \(z\) be the old vertex immediately preceding
\(e\).  Removing the final half-edge and projecting the remaining old-to-old
path gives a self-avoiding path \(\pi\) in \(G\) from \(x\) to \(z\).  Since
\(e\in S_{2n+1}^H(x)\), the vertex \(z\) lies either in \(S_n^G(x)\) or in
\(S_{n+1}^G(x)\).  In the first case the final half-edge is outward and
\[
  I_x^H(\gamma)=2I_x^G(\pi)+H_x^G(\pi).
\]
In the second case the final half-edge is inward and
\[
  I_x^H(\gamma)=2I_x^G(\pi)+H_x^G(\pi)+1.
\]
For each fixed projected path \(\pi\), there are at most \(\Delta\) choices
for the final midpoint \(e\).  Therefore the odd-sphere numerator is bounded
by
\[
  \Delta
  \sum_{z\in S_n^G(x)}
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}}
  \#\{\pi:x\to z:I_x^G(\pi)=i,\ H_x^G(\pi)=h\}
\]
\[
  \quad+
  \Delta
  \sum_{z\in S_{n+1}^G(x)}
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B-1}}
  \#\{\pi:x\to z:I_x^G(\pi)=i,\ H_x^G(\pi)=h\}.
\]
Dividing the first term by \(|E_n(x)|\ge |S_n^G(x)|\) and the second by
\(|E_n(x)|\ge |S_{n+1}^G(x)|\) gives the displayed bound.  The final
inequality follows by taking the appropriate suprema in the definition of
\(\mathfrak M^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Nonamenable old-root odd-sphere subdivision bound]
\label{cor:nonamenable-old-root-odd-sphere-subdivision-bound}
In Lemma~\ref{lem:odd-sphere-old-root-subdivision-bound}, the local
no-dead-end assumption may be replaced by \(h(G)>0\).  More precisely, if
\(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\) and \(h(G)>0\), then, for every
old root \(x\in V(G)\) and every \(n,B\ge0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{1}{|S_{2n+1}^H(x)|}
  \sum_{e\in S_{2n+1}^H(x)}
  \#\{\gamma:x\to e\ {\rm SAW\ in\ }H:I_x^H(\gamma)=B\}
\\
&\qquad\le
  \frac{\Delta}{h(G)}
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}}
  \mathfrak M_{n,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  +
  \Delta
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B-1}}
  \mathfrak M_{n+1,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second sum is \(0\) when \(B=0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the notation \(E_n(x)\) from the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:odd-sphere-old-root-subdivision-bound}.  The numerator bound
from that proof does not use the local no-dead-end assumption.  Since
\(E_n(x)\) contains the edge boundary of the ball \(B_n^G(x)\),
nonamenability gives
\[
  |E_n(x)|
  \ge |\partial_E B_n^G(x)|
  \ge h(G)\sum_{z\in B_n^G(x)}\deg(z)
  \ge h(G)|S_n^G(x)|.
\]
Also \(|E_n(x)|\ge |S_{n+1}^G(x)|\), because each vertex in
\(S_{n+1}^G(x)\) has an edge to \(S_n^G(x)\) along a geodesic to \(x\).
Dividing the two terms in the numerator bound by these two lower bounds gives
the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Midpoint-root subdivision bound under shifted sphere comparison]
\label{lem:midpoint-root-subdivision-shifted-sphere-bound}
Let \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\), let \(r\in E(G)\) be a midpoint of \(H\),
and let \(u_0,u_1\in V(G)\) be its two neighbouring old vertices.  Fix
\(m\ge1\) and \(C\ge1\), and suppose that
\[
  |S_{m-1}^H(u_j)|\le C|S_m^H(r)|
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  |S_{m+1}^H(u_j)|\le C|S_m^H(r)|
  \qquad(j=0,1).
\]
Then, for every \(B\ge0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{1}{|S_m^H(r)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_m^H(r)}
  \#\{\gamma:r\to a\ {\rm SAW\ in\ }H:I_r^H(\gamma)=B\}
\\
&\qquad\le
  C\sum_{j=0}^1
  \left(
    \mathfrak M_{m-1,B,0}^{H,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
    +
    \mathfrak M_{m+1,B-1,0}^{H,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  \right),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the term with \(B-1\) is interpreted as \(0\) when \(B=0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\gamma\) be a self-avoiding path in \(H\) from \(r\) to
\(a\in S_m^H(r)\), and suppose its first step is to \(u_j\).  Delete this
first half-edge to obtain a self-avoiding path \(\gamma'\) from \(u_j\) to
\(a\).  Since \(d_H(r,u_j)=1\), the distance \(d_H(u_j,a)\) is either
\(m-1\) or \(m+1\).  Writing \(|\gamma|\) for the length of \(\gamma\), and
using that \(H\) is bipartite, we have
\[
  I_r^H(\gamma)=\frac{|\gamma|-m}{2}
\]
and
\[
  I_{u_j}^H(\gamma')
  =
  \frac{|\gamma|-1-d_H(u_j,a)}{2}.
\]
Thus \(I_{u_j}^H(\gamma')=I_r^H(\gamma)\) when \(d_H(u_j,a)=m-1\), and
\(I_{u_j}^H(\gamma')=I_r^H(\gamma)-1\) when \(d_H(u_j,a)=m+1\).

The map \(\gamma\mapsto(j,\gamma')\) is injective after recording the first
old vertex \(u_j\).  Therefore the numerator in the displayed average is at
most the sum, over \(j=0,1\), of the old-root counts from \(u_j\) to
\(S_{m-1}^H(u_j)\) with inward count \(B\), plus the old-root counts from
\(u_j\) to \(S_{m+1}^H(u_j)\) with inward count \(B-1\).  Dividing by
\(|S_m^H(r)|\), using the shifted sphere comparisons, and bounding the
old-root averages by the corresponding global \(\mathfrak M^H\) profiles gives
the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Cheeger shifted-sphere comparison]
\label{lem:cheeger-shifted-sphere-comparison}
Let \(X\) be a connected locally finite graph of maximum degree at most
\(D<\infty\), and suppose that \(h(X)>0\).  If \(a\sim b\), then, for every
\(m\ge1\),
\[
  |S_{m-1}^X(a)|
  \le
  \frac{D^4}{h(X)}|S_m^X(b)|
\]
and
\[
  |S_{m+1}^X(a)|
  \le
  \frac{D^4}{h(X)}|S_m^X(b)|.
\]
Consequently, Lemma~\ref{lem:midpoint-root-subdivision-shifted-sphere-bound}
applies in every bounded-degree nonamenable subdivision graph \(H\), with
\[
  C=\frac{D_H^4}{h(H)}
\]
where \(D_H\) is the maximum degree of \(H\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For every \(r\ge0\) and \(v\in V(X)\), nonamenability applied to the finite
ball \(B_r^X(v)\) gives
\[
  h(X)|B_r^X(v)|
  \le
  |\partial_E B_r^X(v)|
  \le
  D|S_{r+1}^X(v)|.
\]
Thus
\[
  |B_r^X(v)|\le \frac{D}{h(X)}|S_{r+1}^X(v)|.
\]
Since \(a\sim b\),
\[
  S_{m-1}^X(a)\subseteq B_m^X(b)
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  S_{m+1}^X(a)\subseteq B_{m+2}^X(b).
\]
Also, for \(k\ge0\), each vertex of \(S_{k+1}^X(b)\) has a geodesic
predecessor in \(S_k^X(b)\), and each vertex has at most \(D\) neighbours, so
\[
  |S_{k+1}^X(b)|\le D|S_k^X(b)|.
\]
Combining these estimates gives
\[
  |S_{m-1}^X(a)|
  \le |B_m^X(b)|
  \le \frac{D}{h(X)}|S_{m+1}^X(b)|
  \le \frac{D^2}{h(X)}|S_m^X(b)|
\]
and
\[
  |S_{m+1}^X(a)|
  \le |B_{m+2}^X(b)|
  \le \frac{D}{h(X)}|S_{m+3}^X(b)|
  \le \frac{D^4}{h(X)}|S_m^X(b)|.
\]
The common constant \(D^4/h(X)\) proves the two displayed inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Restricted subdivision radial-profile comparison]
\label{cor:restricted-subdivision-radial-profile-comparison}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta<\infty\), let \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\), and suppose that
\(h(G)>0\) and \(h(H)>0\).  Put
\[
  C_H=\frac{D_H^4}{h(H)},
\]
where \(D_H\) is the maximum degree of \(H\).  For \(\ell,B\ge0\), let
\(\mathfrak M_{\ell,B}^{H,{\rm old}}\) and
\(\mathfrak M_{\ell,B}^{H,{\rm mid}}\) denote the quantities obtained from
\(\mathfrak M_{\ell,B,0}^{H,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}\) by restricting the root
supremum to old vertices and midpoint vertices, respectively.  Set these
quantities equal to \(0\) when \(B<0\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak M_{\ell,B,0}^{H,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  =
  \max\{\mathfrak M_{\ell,B}^{H,{\rm old}},
        \mathfrak M_{\ell,B}^{H,{\rm mid}}\}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(n,B\ge0\),
\[
  \mathfrak M_{2n,B}^{H,{\rm old}}
  \le
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}}
  \mathfrak M_{n,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}},
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak M_{2n+1,B}^{H,{\rm old}}
  \le
  \frac{\Delta}{h(G)}
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B}}
  \mathfrak M_{n,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  +
  \Delta
  \sum_{\substack{i,h\ge0\\2i+h=B-1}}
  \mathfrak M_{n+1,i,h}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}.
\]
Finally, for every \(m\ge1\) and \(B\ge0\),
\[
  \mathfrak M_{m,B}^{H,{\rm mid}}
  \le
  2C_H\left(
    \mathfrak M_{m-1,B}^{H,{\rm old}}
    +
    \mathfrak M_{m+1,B-1}^{H,{\rm old}}
  \right).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Since \(H\) is bipartite with parts \(V(G)\) and \(E(G)\), every root is
either old or a midpoint, and Lemma~\ref{lem:bipartite-no-horizontal-radial-steps}
gives \(h=0\) for the radial profile on \(H\).  This proves the displayed
maximum identity.

The even old-root bound is the final inequality of
Lemma~\ref{lem:even-sphere-subdivision-radial-identity}.  The odd old-root
bound is Corollary~\ref{cor:nonamenable-old-root-odd-sphere-subdivision-bound}.
For midpoint roots, Lemma~\ref{lem:cheeger-shifted-sphere-comparison} verifies
the shifted sphere hypothesis in
Lemma~\ref{lem:midpoint-root-subdivision-shifted-sphere-bound} with
\(C=C_H\).  Restricting the old-root averages appearing in its proof by the
old-root supremum gives
\[
  \mathfrak M_{m,B}^{H,{\rm mid}}
  \le
  C_H\sum_{j=0}^1
  \left(
    \mathfrak M_{m-1,B}^{H,{\rm old}}
    +
    \mathfrak M_{m+1,B-1}^{H,{\rm old}}
  \right),
\]
which is the claimed bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Collapsed radial-defect profiles]
\label{def:collapsed-radial-defect-profiles}
For \(n\ge0\) and \(d\in\mathbb Z\), define
\[
  \mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  =
  0
  \qquad(d<0),
\]
and, for \(d\ge0\), define
\[
  \mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  =
  \sum_{\substack{i,j\ge0\\2i+j=d}}
  \mathfrak M_{n,i,j}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}},
\]
Thus \(d\) is the original excess defect \(2I+H\), with the two radial
coordinates summed out.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Property-restricted collapsed radial profiles]
\label{def:property-restricted-collapsed-radial-profiles}
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a property of rooted paths.  For \(n\ge0\) and
\(d\in\mathbb Z\), define
\[
  \mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,\mathcal P}
  =
  0
  \qquad(d<0),
\]
and, for \(d\ge0\), define
\[
  \mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,\mathcal P}
  =
  \sup_{\substack{x\in V\\S_n(x)\ne\varnothing}}
  \frac{1}{|S_n(x)|}
  \sum_{a\in S_n(x)}
  \#\{\gamma:x\to a\ {\rm SAW}:2I_x(\gamma)+H_x(\gamma)=d,\
      \mathcal P(x,\gamma)\}.
\]
The unrestricted profile
\(\mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}\) corresponds to the always-true
property.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted subdivision-to-original profile comparison]
\label{cor:weighted-subdivision-original-profile-comparison}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:restricted-subdivision-radial-profile-comparison}, let
\(0<q<1\), put \(Q=q^2\), and set
\[
  C_\star
  =
  \max\left\{1,\frac{\Delta}{h(G)},\Delta\right\}
  \left(1+2C_H\right).
\]
Then, for every \(m,B\ge0\),
\[
  q^{2B}\mathfrak M_{m,B,0}^{H,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}
  \le
  C_\star
  \sum_{\substack{r\ge0\\ |2r-m|\le2}}
  \sum_{a=0}^2
  Q^{B-a}\mathfrak R_{r,B-a}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}} .
\]
Here and below, every term with a negative defect \(B-a<0\) is interpreted as
\(0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let
\[
  C_0=\max\left\{1,\frac{\Delta}{h(G)},\Delta\right\}.
\]
The even and odd old-root bounds in
Corollary~\ref{cor:restricted-subdivision-radial-profile-comparison}, together
with \(q^{2B}\le Q^{B-a}\) when \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and the defect is \(B-a\),
give
\[
  q^{2B}\mathfrak M_{m,B}^{H,{\rm old}}
  \le
  C_0
  \sum_{\substack{r\ge0\\ |2r-m|\le1}}
  \sum_{a=0}^1
  Q^{B-a}\mathfrak R_{r,B-a}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}} .
\]
For midpoint roots,
Corollary~\ref{cor:restricted-subdivision-radial-profile-comparison} gives
\[
  \mathfrak M_{m,B}^{H,{\rm mid}}
  \le
  2C_H\left(
    \mathfrak M_{m-1,B}^{H,{\rm old}}
    +
    \mathfrak M_{m+1,B-1}^{H,{\rm old}}
  \right).
\]
Multiplying by \(q^{2B}\), using
\[
  q^{2B}\le q^{2(B-1)}
\]
for the second term when \(B\ge1\), and applying the old-root estimate to the
two shifted radii yields the same right-hand side with \(|2r-m|\le2\) and
\(a\in\{0,1,2\}\), multiplied by \(2C_HC_0\).  The \(B=0\) second term is
zero by convention.  Since the full \(H\)-profile is the maximum of the old
and midpoint restricted profiles, the displayed bound follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Subdivision inward profiles from original radial profiles]
\label{cor:subdivision-inward-profiles-from-original-radial-profiles}
Let \(G\), \(H\), \(q\), \(Q\), and \(C_\star\) be as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:weighted-subdivision-original-profile-comparison}.  Let
\(D_H\) be the maximum degree of \(H\), let \(\alpha_\omega\) be the
volume-growth parameter used when applying the bipartite inward criterion to
\(H\), and for \(p<\pc(H)\) put
\[
  L_H=\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H,\qquad
  K_{\rho,p}^H=\lfloor\rho L_H\rfloor,\qquad
  c_s=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}-3s .
\]
Define the shifted original finite profile
\[
  \mathfrak F_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}:
    \begin{array}{l}
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H,\\
    r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2,\ 0\le d\le K_{\rho,p}^H/2
    \end{array}
  \right\}
\]
and the shifted original tail profile
\[
  \mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>K_{\rho,p}^H/2-2}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\]
with empty suprema and sums equal to \(0\).  Then the bipartite inward
profiles of Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion},
computed in \(H\), satisfy
\[
  \mathfrak F_{q,\rho}^{H,{\rm in,saw}}(s,p)
  \le
  9C_\star\,\mathfrak F_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak L_{q,\rho}^{H,{\rm in,saw}}(s,p)
  \le
  3C_\star\,\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion} for \(H\) follow
from the same exponent hypotheses on
\(\mathfrak F_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) and
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For the finite profile, apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:weighted-subdivision-original-profile-comparison} with
\(0\le B\le K_{\rho,p}^H/2\).  Then every defect \(d=B-a\) appearing on the
right-hand side satisfies \(d\le K_{\rho,p}^H/2\).  There are at most three
choices of \(a\) and at most three integers \(r\) with \(|2r-m|\le2\), giving
the factor \(9C_\star\).

For the tail profile, sum the same comparison over \(B>K_{\rho,p}^H/2\).  For
each \(a\in\{0,1,2\}\), the defect \(d=B-a\) satisfies
\[
  d>K_{\rho,p}^H/2-2,
\]
and each fixed \(d\) is produced by at most one \(B=d+a\) for that \(a\).
Summing over \(a\) gives the factor \(3C_\star\).  Multiplicative constants do
not affect the displayed logarithmic exponent hypotheses because
\(\chiBar_p^H\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc(H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Subdivision inward weights match original radial weights]
\label{rem:subdivision-inward-weight-matching}
Let \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\), let \(0<q<1\), and put \(Q=q^2\).  The
weights in the bipartite inward profiles on \(H\) are compatible with the
two-coordinate radial weights on \(G\).  Indeed, in the even-sphere identity
of Lemma~\ref{lem:even-sphere-subdivision-radial-identity}, the relation
\[
  B=2i+h
\]
gives
\[
  q^{2B}=Q^{2i+h}.
\]
In the old-root odd-sphere comparison of
Lemma~\ref{lem:odd-sphere-old-root-subdivision-bound}, the two alternatives
are \(B=2i+h\) and \(B=2i+h+1\), and hence
\[
  q^{2B}\le Q^{2i+h}.
\]
Similarly, in Lemma~\ref{lem:midpoint-root-subdivision-shifted-sphere-bound},
deleting the first half-edge either preserves the inward count or lowers it
by one, and the factor \(q^{2B}\) is no larger than the corresponding
old-root weight.  Thus the subdivision radius shifts introduce constants and
neighbouring radii, but no adverse power of \(q\).
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Subdivision one-parameter inward criterion]
\label{cor:subdivision-inward-tail-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and nonamenable,
with bounded degree, and let \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\).  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(G)}(\pc(G)-p)\chiBar_p^G<\infty.
\]
If the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion}
are satisfied for \(H\), then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By Proposition~\ref{prop:subdivision-bipartite-reduction}, \(H\) is
bipartite, quasi-transitive, and nonamenable, and
\(\pc(H)=\sqrt{\pc(G)}\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:subdivision-susceptibility-comparison}
transfers the mean-field susceptibility input from \(G\) to \(H\).  Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion} to \(H\) gives
\[
  \pc(H)<p_{2\to2}(H).
\]
The equivalence in Proposition~\ref{prop:subdivision-bipartite-reduction}
then yields \(\pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Original radial-profile subdivision criterion]
\label{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}
Let \(G\) and \(H=\operatorname{Sub}(G)\) be as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:subdivision-inward-tail-criterion}.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(G)}(\pc(G)-p)\chiBar_p^G<\infty.
\]
Assume that the non-profile hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion} are satisfied
for \(H\) with some \(q\in(\pc(H),1)\), and put \(Q=q^2\).  If the two
logarithmic exponent hypotheses in that corollary, for the inward profiles on
\(H\), hold instead for the shifted original profiles
\[
  \mathfrak F_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\]
from
Corollary~\ref{cor:subdivision-inward-profiles-from-original-radial-profiles},
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:subdivision-inward-profiles-from-original-radial-profiles}
shows that the shifted original radial-profile exponent hypotheses imply the
corresponding exponent hypotheses on the one-parameter bipartite inward
profiles of \(H\).  Thus the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-parameter-bipartite-inward-criterion} hold for \(H\).
Applying Corollary~\ref{cor:subdivision-inward-tail-criterion} gives the
claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Binned shifted original finite radial criterion]
\label{cor:binned-shifted-original-finite-radial-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}, use the
notation \(D_H,L_H,c_s,\alpha_\omega,Q\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:subdivision-inward-profiles-from-original-radial-profiles}.
The exponent hypothesis on \(\mathfrak F_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\)
may be replaced by the following finite family of sufficient hypotheses.  Let
\(\delta>0\), set
\[
  m_{\rho,\delta}^{G\to H}
  =
  \left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{2\delta}\right\rfloor+1,
\]
and define, for \(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{G\to H}\),
\[
  \mathfrak D_{i,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}:
    \begin{array}{l}
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H,\\
    r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2,\ i\delta L_H\le d<(i+1)\delta L_H
    \end{array}
  \right\},
\]
where empty suprema are \(0\).  If the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion} holds and,
for every \(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{G\to H}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak D_{i,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +i\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(0\le d\le K_{\rho,p}^H/2\), then \(d\le\rho L_H/2\), so \(d\) lies in
one of the bins \(0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{G\to H}\).  In the \(i\)th bin,
\[
  Q^d\le Q^{i\delta L_H},
\]
since \(Q<1\).  Hence
\[
  \mathfrak F_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \le
  \max_{0\le i<m_{\rho,\delta}^{G\to H}}
  Q^{i\delta L_H}\mathfrak D_{i,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
The number of bins is independent of \(p\).  The displayed binned exponent
hypotheses therefore imply the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak F_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  The tail exponent
hypothesis is assumed, so
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Binned shifted original radial tail criterion]
\label{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}, use the
notation \(D_H,L_H,c_s,\alpha_\omega,Q\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:subdivision-inward-profiles-from-original-radial-profiles}.
The exponent hypothesis on \(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\)
may be replaced by the following finite-bin plus far-tail hypotheses.  Let
\(\lambda>\rho/2\) and \(\delta>0\), and set
\[
  m_{\lambda,\delta}^{G\to H}
  =
  \left\lfloor\frac{\lambda}{\delta}\right\rfloor+1.
\]
For \(0\le i<m_{\lambda,\delta}^{G\to H}\), define
\[
  \mathfrak E_{i,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}:
    \begin{array}{l}
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H,\\
    r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2,\ i\delta L_H\le d<(i+1)\delta L_H
    \end{array}
  \right\},
\]
and define the far-tail profile
\[
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\}.
\]
Assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\(0\le i<m_{\lambda,\delta}^{G\to H}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak E_{i,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +i\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
and that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s.
\]
Then the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) holds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Fix an admissible \(m\).  Split the sum defining
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) into terms with
\[
  d\le \lambda L_H
\]
and terms with \(d>\lambda L_H\).  The second part is bounded by
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  The first part is
covered by the finitely many bins
\[
  0\le i<m_{\lambda,\delta}^{G\to H}.
\]
For each bin, \(Q^d\le Q^{i\delta L_H}\), and there are at most
\(\lfloor\delta L_H\rfloor+2\) integer values of \(d\) in the bin and at most
three integers \(r\) with \(|2r-m|\le2\).  Hence the finite part is bounded by
\[
  3(\lfloor\delta L_H\rfloor+2)
  \sum_{0\le i<m_{\lambda,\delta}^{G\to H}}
  Q^{i\delta L_H}\mathfrak E_{i,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
The number of bins is independent of \(p\), and
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}(\lfloor\delta L_H\rfloor+2)}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)).
\]
The displayed assumptions therefore imply the desired logarithmic exponent
bound for the shifted tail profile.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Overshoot and slab localization of the shifted far tail]
\label{cor:overshoot-slab-localization-shifted-far-tail}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, fix
\(\sigma,\beta>0\).  Put
\[
  W_{\beta,p}=\max\{1,\lfloor\beta L_H\rfloor\},
  \qquad
  J_{\sigma,\beta}
  =
  \left\lfloor
    \frac{\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\frac{3s}{2}+\sigma+2}{\beta}
  \right\rfloor+2,
\]
and
\[
  \theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}
  =
  \frac{\lambda}{J_{\sigma,\beta}}.
\]
For a rooted path \(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\), write
\[
  M_x(\gamma)=\max_{0\le t\le\ell}d(x,v_t)
\]
and, for an interval \(A\subseteq\mathbb N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  D_x(\gamma;A)
  &=
  \sum_{u\in A}
  2\#\{1\le t\le\ell:d(x,v_{t-1})=u,\ d(x,v_t)=u-1\}
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{u\in A}
  \#\{1\le t\le\ell:d(x,v_{t-1})=u,\ d(x,v_t)=u\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Define the overshoot profile
\[
  \mathfrak O_{Q,\lambda,\sigma}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal O_{r,\sigma,p}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal O_{r,\sigma,p}(x,\gamma)\) is the property
\[
  M_x(\gamma)>r+\sigma L_H.
\]
For \(0\le j<J_{\sigma,\beta}\), define the heavy-slab profile
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal V_{j,p}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal V_{j,p}(x,\gamma)\) is the property
\[
  D_x\bigl(\gamma;[jW_{\beta,p},(j+1)W_{\beta,p})\bigr)
  >
  \theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H .
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak O_{Q,\lambda,\sigma}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  +
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma,\beta}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) follows from the same exponent
hypothesis on the overshoot profile and on each of the finitely many
heavy-slab profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(m,r,d\) be in the range defining
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\), and let \(\gamma\) be a path
counted by \(\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,{\rm rad,saw,sph}}\).  If
\(M_x(\gamma)>r+\sigma L_H\), then \(\gamma\) is counted by the overshoot
profile.  Otherwise,
\[
  M_x(\gamma)\le r+\sigma L_H.
\]
Since \(|2r-m|\le2\) and
\[
  m\le\left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H,
\]
all radial levels visited by \(\gamma\) are contained, for \(p\) close enough
to \(\pc(H)\), in the union of the slabs
\[
  [jW_{\beta,p},(j+1)W_{\beta,p}),
  \qquad 0\le j<J_{\sigma,\beta}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma,\beta}-1}
  D_x\bigl(\gamma;[jW_{\beta,p},(j+1)W_{\beta,p})\bigr)
  =
  2I_x(\gamma)+H_x(\gamma)
  =
  d.
\]
Since \(d>\lambda L_H\), one of the \(J_{\sigma,\beta}\) slabs has
\[
  D_x\bigl(\gamma;[jW_{\beta,p},(j+1)W_{\beta,p})\bigr)
  >
  \theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H.
\]
Thus every non-overshooting path counted by the far tail is counted by at
least one heavy-slab profile.  Taking the union bound after averaging over
spheres and then taking the displayed suprema gives the claimed inequality.
The final assertion follows because \(J_{\sigma,\beta}\) is independent of
\(p\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Overshoot forces inward defect]
\label{lem:overshoot-forces-inward-defect}
Let \(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) be a path started at \(x\), ending at a
vertex \(a\in S_r(x)\), and let
\[
  M_x(\gamma)=\max_{0\le t\le\ell}d(x,v_t).
\]
Then
\[
  I_x(\gamma)\ge M_x(\gamma)-r.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  2I_x(\gamma)+H_x(\gamma)
  \ge 2\bigl(M_x(\gamma)-r\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(t_0\) be a time at which \(d(x,v_{t_0})=M_x(\gamma)\).  Along the
suffix \((v_{t_0},\ldots,v_\ell)\), the distance from \(x\) drops from
\(M_x(\gamma)\) to \(r\).  The number of inward steps in this suffix minus
the number of outward steps in this suffix is therefore \(M_x(\gamma)-r\).
In particular, the suffix has at least \(M_x(\gamma)-r\) inward steps, and so
does the whole path.  The second inequality follows from \(H_x(\gamma)\ge0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Overshoot tail amplification]
\label{cor:overshoot-tail-amplification}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:overshoot-slab-localization-shifted-far-tail}, put
\[
  \lambda'=\max\{\lambda,2\sigma\}.
\]
Let \(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda'}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) denote the far-tail
profile from
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} with
\(\lambda\) replaced by \(\lambda'\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak O_{Q,\lambda,\sigma}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda'}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
In particular, if \(\sigma>\lambda/2\), then the overshoot term is controlled
by a strictly deeper shifted far tail.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every path counted by
\(\mathfrak O_{Q,\lambda,\sigma}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) ends at radius
\(r\), has defect \(d>\lambda L_H\), and satisfies
\[
  M_x(\gamma)>r+\sigma L_H.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:overshoot-forces-inward-defect},
\[
  d=2I_x(\gamma)+H_x(\gamma)>2\sigma L_H.
\]
Thus \(d>\lambda' L_H\).  Removing the overshoot restriction can only increase
the corresponding weighted sum, which gives the displayed inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, let
\[
  \lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N
\]
with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\), and let \(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\).  For
each \(0\le i<N\), put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}{2}.
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  +
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) follows from the same
exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) and on each of the finitely
many heavy-slab profiles in the displayed sum.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:overshoot-slab-localization-shifted-far-tail} with
\((\lambda,\sigma,\beta)=(\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i)\).  Since
\(\lambda_{i+1}>\lambda_i\) and \(\sigma_i=\lambda_{i+1}/2\),
Corollary~\ref{cor:overshoot-tail-amplification} gives
\[
  \mathfrak O_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_{i+1}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
Thus
\[
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_{i+1}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  +
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p).
\]
Iterating this inequality for \(0\le i<N\) gives the displayed ladder bound.
The exponent conclusion follows because all sums are finite and independent
of \(p\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Heavy-slab token dichotomy]
\label{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:overshoot-slab-localization-shifted-far-tail}, fix
\(\sigma,\beta>0\), \(0\le j<J_{\sigma,\beta}\), and put
\[
  A_{j,p}=[jW_{\beta,p},(j+1)W_{\beta,p}).
\]
For a rooted path \(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\), define
\[
  I_x(\gamma;A)
  =
  \sum_{u\in A}
  \#\{1\le t\le\ell:d(x,v_{t-1})=u,\ d(x,v_t)=u-1\}
\]
and
\[
  H_x(\gamma;A)
  =
  \sum_{u\in A}
  \#\{1\le t\le\ell:d(x,v_{t-1})=u,\ d(x,v_t)=u\}.
\]
Thus \(D_x(\gamma;A)=2I_x(\gamma;A)+H_x(\gamma;A)\).
Let \(\mathcal V^{\rm in}_{j,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  I_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4}L_H
\]
and let \(\mathcal V^{\rm hor}_{j,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  H_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2}L_H .
\]
Define the corresponding inward-token and horizontal-token profiles by
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal V^{\rm in}_{j,p}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal V^{\rm hor}_{j,p}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the heavy-slab profile follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on its inward-token and horizontal-token
subprofiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If a path satisfies \(\mathcal V_{j,p}\), then
\[
  2I_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})+H_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  >
  \theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H .
\]
If neither \(\mathcal V^{\rm in}_{j,p}\) nor
\(\mathcal V^{\rm hor}_{j,p}\) held, then
\[
  2I_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})+H_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  \le
  2\cdot\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4}L_H
  +
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2}L_H
  =
  \theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H,
\]
a contradiction.  Thus each path counted by the heavy-slab profile is counted
by at least one of the two token profiles.  Taking the union bound inside each
weighted sum and then taking the supremum gives the displayed inequality.
Finite sums and fixed multiplicative constants do not affect the logarithmic
exponent condition.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Inward level tokens give exterior returns]
\label{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns}
Let \(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) be a path with \(v_0=x\), and fix
\(u\ge1\).  For every time \(t\) such that
\[
  d(x,v_{t-1})=u,\qquad d(x,v_t)=u-1,
\]
there is a time \(s<t\) such that
\[
  d(x,v_s)=u-1,\qquad d(x,v_{s+1})=u,
\]
and
\[
  d(x,v_a)\ge u
  \qquad(s<a<t).
\]
Moreover, for fixed \(u\), the intervals \([s,t]\) obtained by choosing
\(s\) maximal have disjoint interiors as \(t\) ranges over all inward
level-\(u\) tokens.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since \(v_0=x\) has distance \(0<u\), the path must visit level \(u-1\)
before the time \(t-1\) at which it is at level \(u\).  Let \(s<t\) be the
last time before \(t\) at which \(d(x,v_s)=u-1\).  Then \(v_{s+1}\) cannot
have distance \(u-1\), by maximality of \(s\), and it cannot have distance
less than \(u-1\), since the path later reaches level \(u\) before time \(t\)
and would then have to visit level \(u-1\) again.  Hence
\(d(x,v_{s+1})=u\).  The same maximality argument gives
\(d(x,v_a)\ge u\) for every \(s<a<t\).

If \(t_1<t_2\) are two inward level-\(u\) tokens and \(s_i\) is chosen
maximal for \(t_i\), then after time \(t_1\) the path is back at level
\(u-1\).  To have another inward level-\(u\) token at time \(t_2\), it must
cross from level \(u-1\) to level \(u\) at some time after or at \(t_1\).
Thus \(s_2\ge t_1\), proving the disjoint-interior assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inward-heavy slabs: spread or congestion]
\label{cor:inward-heavy-slab-spread-congestion}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix an integer \(K\ge1\).
Let \(\mathcal V^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}: I_x(\gamma;\{u\})>0\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
and let \(\mathcal V^{\rm con}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \max_{u\in A_{j,p}} I_x(\gamma;\{u\})>K .
\]
Define
\(\mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,spr}}(s,p)\)
and
\(\mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,con}}(s,p)\)
from the same formula as
\(\mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in}}(s,p)\), with
\(\mathcal V^{\rm in}_{j,p}\) replaced by
\(\mathcal V^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}\) and
\(\mathcal V^{\rm con}_{j,K,p}\), respectively.  Then
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,spr}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,con}}(s,p).
\]
In the congested alternative, Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns}
produces more than \(K\) exterior return segments through a single level of
the slab.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Write
\[
  N_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  =
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}: I_x(\gamma;\{u\})>0\}.
\]
If a path satisfies \(\mathcal V^{\rm in}_{j,p}\), then
\[
  \sum_{u\in A_{j,p}}I_x(\gamma;\{u\})
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4}L_H.
\]
If neither the spread nor the congestion property held, then
\[
  \sum_{u\in A_{j,p}}I_x(\gamma;\{u\})
  \le
  K\,N_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  \le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4}L_H,
\]
contradicting the previous display.  Hence every inward-token path is counted
by at least one of the two subprofiles.  The displayed profile inequality
follows by the same union-bound argument as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}.  The final sentence is
exactly Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tokenized finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:tokenized-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, let
\[
  \lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N
\]
with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\).  Let
\(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\), let \(K_0,\ldots,K_{N-1}\ge1\) be
integers, and put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}{2}
  \qquad(0\le i<N).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
