  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,con}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) follows from the same
exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail and on each tokenized slab
profile appearing on the right-hand side.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-far-tail-ladder}.  For each heavy-slab term
in its right-hand side, apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy} and then
Corollary~\ref{cor:inward-heavy-slab-spread-congestion} with \(K=K_i\).  The
displayed inequality follows after summing the resulting bounds over
\(i\) and \(j\).  All sums are finite and independent of \(p\), so the
logarithmic exponent conclusion follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Exact-level exterior-return profiles]
\label{def:exact-level-exterior-return-profiles}
Let \(u\ge1\) and \(K\ge0\).  For a rooted path
\(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\), let
\(\mathcal X_{u,K}(x,\gamma)\) be the property that \(\gamma\) contains more
than \(K\) subpaths
\[
  (v_{s_a},v_{s_a+1},\ldots,v_{t_a}),
  \qquad a=1,\ldots,K+1,
\]
with pairwise disjoint open time intervals \((s_a,t_a)\), such that
\[
  d(x,v_{s_a})=d(x,v_{t_a})=u-1,
  \qquad
  d(x,v_{s_a+1})=d(x,v_{t_a-1})=u,
\]
and
\[
  d(x,v_b)\ge u
  \qquad(s_a<b<t_a).
\]
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for every integer \(j\ge0\)
write
\[
  A_{j,p}=[jW_{\beta,p},(j+1)W_{\beta,p})
\]
and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup_{\substack{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\\u\ge1}}
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal X_{u,K}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
with the value \(0\) if \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\cap[1,\infty)\) is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Spread exterior-return profiles]
\label{def:spread-exterior-return-profiles}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:inward-heavy-slab-spread-congestion}, for every
integer \(j\ge0\) let
\(\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:u\ge1,\ \mathcal X_{u,0}(x,\gamma)\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Spread-inward slabs localize to spread-return levels]
\label{cor:spread-inward-slabs-localize}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:inward-heavy-slab-spread-congestion},
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,spr}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the spread-inward slab profile
follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the spread exterior-return
profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(I_x(\gamma;\{u\})>0\), then \(u\ge1\).  Applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns} to one inward
level-\(u\) token gives an exterior return through level \(u\), i.e.
\(\mathcal X_{u,0}(x,\gamma)\).  Hence
\[
  \mathcal V^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma).
\]
The displayed profile inequality follows immediately from monotonicity of the
property-restricted profiles.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Level-congested slabs localize to exterior-return levels]
\label{cor:level-congested-slabs-localize}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:inward-heavy-slab-spread-congestion},
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,con}}(s,p)
  \le
  W_{\beta,p}\,
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the level-congested inward profile
follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the exact-level exterior-return
profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(\gamma\) satisfies
\(\mathcal V^{\rm con}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\), then for some
\[
  u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N,\qquad u\ge1,
\]
we have \(I_x(\gamma;\{u\})>K\).  Applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns} to each inward
level-\(u\) token and choosing the last preceding outward crossing gives more
than \(K\) exterior return subpaths with disjoint open time intervals.  Hence
\(\mathcal X_{u,K}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Therefore, for each \(r,d\),
\[
  \mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal V^{\rm con}_{j,K,p}}
  \le
  \sum_{\substack{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\\u\ge1}}
  \mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal X_{u,K}}.
\]
After multiplying by \(Q^d\), summing over the same \(r,d\) range, and taking
the supremum in \(m\), the right-hand side is bounded by
\[
  |A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N|\,
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p)
  \le
  W_{\beta,p}\,
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p).
\]
Finally,
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)),
\]
so the extra factor \(W_{\beta,p}\) does not affect logarithmic exponent
criteria.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exterior-return finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:exterior-return-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:tokenized-finite-far-tail-ladder}, write
\[
  X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p)
\]
for \(0\le i<N\) and \(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\).  Then, for all
\(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,in,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, on the horizontal-heavy
and spread-inward slab profiles, and on the exact-level exterior-return
profiles \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:tokenized-finite-far-tail-ladder}.  Each
level-congested inward term in its right-hand side is bounded by
Corollary~\ref{cor:level-congested-slabs-localize}, with
\((\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)=(\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,K_i)\).  This gives
the displayed inequality.  The number of indices \(i,j\) is independent of
\(p\), and
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta_i,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H))
\]
for each fixed \(i\).  Thus the slab-width factors do not affect the
logarithmic exponent hypothesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Return-spread exterior-return far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:return-spread-exterior-return-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:exterior-return-finite-far-tail-ladder}, write
\[
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
\]
and
\[
  X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, on the horizontal-heavy
slab profiles, on the spread exterior-return profiles \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\),
and on the exact-level exterior-return profiles \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:exterior-return-finite-far-tail-ladder}.  Each
spread-inward term is bounded by
Corollary~\ref{cor:spread-inward-slabs-localize}, with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)=(\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,K_i).
\]
The displayed inequality follows.  The exponent conclusion is unchanged because the sums
are finite and independent of \(p\), and the only nonconstant multiplicative
losses are the already exponent-negligible factors \(W_{\beta_i,p}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Exact-level same-sphere profiles]
\label{def:exact-level-same-sphere-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, let \(u,K\ge0\).  Let
\(\mathcal Z_{u,K}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  H_x(\gamma;\{u\})>K.
\]
For \(K\ge1\), let \(\mathcal Z^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:H_x(\gamma;\{u\})>0\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor,lev}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal Z_{u,K}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
with value \(0\) if \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) is empty, and
\[
  \mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor,spr}}(s,p)
  =
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal Z^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Horizontal-heavy slabs: spread or same-sphere congestion]
\label{cor:horizontal-heavy-slab-spread-congestion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak V_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor,spr}}(s,p)
  +
  W_{\beta,p}\,
  \mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor,lev}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the horizontal-heavy slab profile
follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the same-sphere spread and
exact-level same-sphere congestion profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If a path satisfies \(\mathcal V^{\rm hor}_{j,p}\), then
\[
  \sum_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}H_x(\gamma;\{u\})
  =
  H_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2}L_H .
\]
Let
\[
  N_x^{\rm hor}(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  =
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:H_x(\gamma;\{u\})>0\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal Z^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}\) fails and no level in
\(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) satisfies \(\mathcal Z_{u,K}\), then
\[
  H_x(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  \le
  K\,N_x^{\rm hor}(\gamma;A_{j,p})
  \le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2}L_H,
\]
a contradiction.  Hence every horizontal-heavy path is counted either by the
spread same-sphere profile or by \(\mathcal Z_{u,K}\) for at least one exact
level \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\).  Taking the union bound over such levels
gives the displayed inequality, since
\[
  |A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N|\le W_{\beta,p}.
\]
The exponent conclusion follows because
\(\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Tangential run profiles]
\label{def:tangential-run-profiles}
Let \(u\ge0\).  A level-\(u\) tangential run of a rooted path
\(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) is a maximal interval of times
\([a,b]\subseteq[0,\ell]\) such that \(b>a\) and
\[
  d(x,v_t)=u\qquad(a\le t\le b).
\]
Its length is \(b-a\).  Let \(R_x^u(\gamma)\) be the number of level-\(u\)
tangential runs, and let
\[
  T_x^u(\gamma)
  =
  \max\{b-a:[a,b]\text{ is a level-}u\text{ tangential run of }\gamma\},
\]
with \(T_x^u(\gamma)=0\) if there is no such run.  For \(L\ge1\) and
\(R\ge0\), let
\(\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u,L}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  T_x^u(\gamma)>L
\]
and let \(\mathcal T^{\rm many}_{u,R}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  R_x^u(\gamma)>R.
\]
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u,L}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,R}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,tan,many}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal T^{\rm many}_{u,R}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
with value \(0\) if \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Adjacent-level crossing tangential profiles]
\label{def:adjacent-crossing-tangential-profiles}
Let \(u\ge0\), and let \(\eta,\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}\).  A level-\(u\)
tangential run \([a,b]\) of
\(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) is an
\((\eta,\zeta)\)-crossing run if
\[
  a>0,\qquad b<\ell,\qquad
  d(x,v_{a-1})=u+\eta,\qquad d(x,v_{b+1})=u+\zeta .
\]
Let \(R_{x,\eta,\zeta}^u(\gamma)\) be the number of such runs.  If either
\(u+\eta<0\) or \(u+\zeta<0\), this number is understood to be zero.  For
\(R\ge0\), let
\(\mathcal C^{\eta,\zeta}_{u,R}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  R_{x,\eta,\zeta}^u(\gamma)>R.
\]
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak C_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,R,\eta,\zeta}^{G\to H,
     {\rm rad,tan,cross}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal C^{\eta,\zeta}_{u,R}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
with value \(0\) if \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Outward-through tangential spread profiles]
\label{def:outward-through-tangential-spread-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K\ge1\) let
\(\mathcal U^{\rm out}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      R_{x,-1,+1}^u(\gamma)>0\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,spr}}(s,p)
  &=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal U^{\rm out}_{j,K,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{4em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Same-sphere spread: returns or outward-through spread]
\label{cor:same-sphere-spread-returns-or-outward-through}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:horizontal-heavy-slab-spread-congestion}, fix \(K\ge1\).
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,hor,spr}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,8K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j+1,8K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the same-sphere spread exponent hypothesis follows from the
same exponent hypothesis on the outward-through tangential spread profile and
on the same and next spread exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(N\) be the number of levels \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) with
\(H_x(\gamma;\{u\})>0\).  If
\(\mathcal Z^{\rm spr}_{j,K,p}\) holds, then
\[
  N>\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2K}L_H .
\]
For every such level except possibly the initial level of the whole path and
the terminal level of the whole path, there is a two-sided level-\(u\)
tangential run.  Thus at least \(N-2\) of these levels have a two-sided
tangential run.

If more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
\]
levels have an outward-through \((-1,+1)\)-run, then
\(\mathcal U^{\rm out}_{j,K,p}\) holds.  Otherwise, for \(p\) close enough
that
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H>2,
\]
more than \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(8K)\) levels have a two-sided
tangential run of one of the other three types.

Each of these other three types gives an exterior return through level \(u\)
or through level \(u+1\): the two types with exit to \(S_{u-1}(x)\) give an
inward level-\(u\) token, while type \((+1,+1)\) gives an inward
level-\(u+1\) token.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns}, each such token gives
the corresponding \(\mathcal X_{\cdot,0}\) event.  The map from a
same-sphere level \(u\) to the resulting return level has at most two
preimages, so more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H
\]
distinct return levels occur in \(A_{j,p}\cup A_{j+1,p}\).  One of the two
slabs therefore contains more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(8K)}L_H
\]
return levels, which is exactly the spread-return property with parameter
\(8K\) in slab \(j\) or \(j+1\).  This proves the property inclusion behind
the displayed profile inequality.  Taking the union bound inside the
restricted profiles gives the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Record outward-through tangential spread profiles]
\label{def:record-outward-through-tangential-spread-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, say that a level
\(u\ge1\) is record outward-through for \((x,\gamma)\) if there is a
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing level-\(u\) tangential run \([a,b]\) such that
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u
  \qquad(0\le t<a).
\]
For \(K\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal U^{\rm rec}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      u\ge1,\ u\text{ is record outward-through for }(x,\gamma)\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,rec}}(s,p)
  &=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal U^{\rm rec}_{j,K,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{4em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Outward-through spread: record or return]
\label{cor:outward-through-spread-record-or-return}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,spr}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,rec}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\le
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,rec}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,8K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on outward-through spread follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on record outward-through spread and on the
spread exterior-return profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that \(\mathcal U^{\rm out}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds, and let
\[
  N_{\rm out}
  =
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      R_{x,-1,+1}^u(\gamma)>0\}.
\]
If more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
\]
of these levels are record outward-through, then
\(\mathcal U^{\rm rec}_{j,2K,p}\) holds.  Otherwise, more than the same number
of levels admit a \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([a,b]\) that is not the first
visit to level \(u\).

For such a non-record level \(u\), choose a time \(t_0<a\) with
\(d(x,v_{t_0})=u\).  Since the chosen run is entered from level \(u-1\), we
have \(d(x,v_{a-1})=u-1\).  Let \(t\) be the first time after \(t_0\) at which
the path is at level \(u-1\).  Then \(d(x,v_{t-1})=u\) and
\(d(x,v_t)=u-1\), so \(t\) is an inward level-\(u\) token.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns},
\(\mathcal X_{u,0}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Therefore the non-record alternative
implies \(\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,2K,p}(x,\gamma)\).

This proves the first property inclusion, and hence the first displayed
profile inequality.  The second inequality follows from monotonicity in the
spread threshold, since
\[
  \mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,2K,p}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,8K,p}.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Subterminal record outward-through profiles]
\label{def:subterminal-record-outward-through-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for a rooted path
\(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) write
\[
  e_x(\gamma)=d(x,v_\ell).
\]
For \(K\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal U^{\rm sub}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      u\ge1,\ u<e_x(\gamma),\
      u\text{ is record outward-through for }(x,\gamma)\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,sub}}(s,p)
  &=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal U^{\rm sub}_{j,K,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{4em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Record outward-through: subterminal or return]
\label{cor:record-outward-subterminal-or-return}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,rec}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,sub}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,4K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j+1,4K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on record outward-through spread
follows from the same exponent hypothesis on subterminal record
outward-through spread and on the same and next spread exterior-return
profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that \(\mathcal U^{\rm rec}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  If more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
\]
of the record outward-through levels in \(A_{j,p}\) are subterminal, then
\(\mathcal U^{\rm sub}_{j,2K,p}\) holds.  Otherwise, more than the same number
of record outward-through levels \(u\in A_{j,p}\) satisfy
\[
  u\ge e_x(\gamma).
\]

For such a level, choose a record \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([a,b]\).  Since
\(d(x,v_{b+1})=u+1\) and the endpoint has distance at most \(u\), there is a
first time \(t>b+1\) at which \(d(x,v_t)=u\).  By the choice of \(t\),
\(d(x,v_{t-1})=u+1\), so \(t\) is an inward level-\(u+1\) token.  Lemma
\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns} gives
\(\mathcal X_{u+1,0}(x,\gamma)\).

The map \(u\mapsto u+1\) is injective, and if \(u\in A_{j,p}\) then
\[
  u+1\in A_{j,p}\cup A_{j+1,p}.
\]
Thus more than \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(8K)\) terminal or
post-terminal record levels give the same number of return levels in the
union of the two slabs.  One of the two slabs contains more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(4K)}L_H
\]
such return levels, which is precisely the spread-return property with
parameter \(4K\) in slab \(j\) or \(j+1\).  This gives the property inclusion
and hence the displayed profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Persistent subterminal record profiles]
\label{def:persistent-subterminal-record-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, let
\[
  \tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)
  =
  \min\{t:d(x,v_t)=e_x(\gamma)\}.
\]
A subterminal record outward-through level \(u\) is persistent for
\((x,\gamma)\) if its record \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([a,b]\) satisfies
\[
  d(x,v_t)>u
  \qquad(b<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)).
\]
For \(K\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal U^{\rm per}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      u\text{ is persistent subterminal record for }(x,\gamma)\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,per}}(s,p)
  &=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal U^{\rm per}_{j,K,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{4em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Subterminal record: persistent or return]
\label{cor:subterminal-record-persistent-or-return}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,sub}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,per}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,4K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j+1,4K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on subterminal record spread follows
from the same exponent hypothesis on persistent subterminal record spread and
on the same and next spread exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that \(\mathcal U^{\rm sub}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  If more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
\]
of the subterminal record levels in \(A_{j,p}\) are persistent, then
\(\mathcal U^{\rm per}_{j,2K,p}\) holds.  Otherwise, more than the same number
of subterminal record levels \(u\in A_{j,p}\) have a record run \([a,b]\)
after which the path returns to level \(u\) before the first hit of the
endpoint sphere.

For each such nonpersistent level, let \(t>b+1\) be the first time with
\(d(x,v_t)=u\).  Since \(d(x,v_{b+1})=u+1\), the first-return choice gives
\(d(x,v_{t-1})=u+1\), so \(t\) is an inward level-\(u+1\) token.  Lemma
\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns} gives
\(\mathcal X_{u+1,0}(x,\gamma)\).

As in Corollary~\ref{cor:record-outward-subterminal-or-return}, the map
\(u\mapsto u+1\) is injective and sends \(A_{j,p}\) into
\(A_{j,p}\cup A_{j+1,p}\).  Hence one of these two slabs contains more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(4K)}L_H
\]
return levels, giving the spread-return property with parameter \(4K\) in
slab \(j\) or \(j+1\).  The displayed profile inequality follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Deep persistent subterminal profiles]
\label{def:deep-persistent-subterminal-record-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K\ge1\) let
\(\mathcal U^{\rm deep}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\left\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      \begin{array}{l}
      u\text{ is persistent subterminal record for }(x,\gamma),\\
      e_x(\gamma)-u>\dfrac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
      \end{array}
    \right\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,deep}}(s,p)
  &=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal U^{\rm deep}_{j,K,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{4em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Persistent levels are deeply persistent]
\label{cor:persistent-levels-are-deeply-persistent}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,per}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,deep}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on persistent subterminal record spread
follows from the same exponent hypothesis on deep persistent subterminal
record spread.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that \(\mathcal U^{\rm per}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds and put
\[
  B=\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H .
\]
There are at most \(B\) integers \(u\) satisfying
\[
  0<e_x(\gamma)-u\le B .
\]
Since the persistent event gives more than \(2B\) persistent subterminal
record levels in \(A_{j,p}\), more than \(B\) of them satisfy
\[
  e_x(\gamma)-u>B .
\]
This is exactly \(\mathcal U^{\rm deep}_{j,2K,p}(x,\gamma)\).  The displayed
profile inequality follows by monotonicity of property-restricted profiles.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Endpoint-prefix spread profiles]
\label{def:endpoint-prefix-deep-horizontal-spread-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for a rooted path
\(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) let
\[
  \tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)
  =
  \min\{t:d(x,v_t)=e_x(\gamma)\}.
\]
For \(K\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\left\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      \begin{array}{l}
      \text{\(\gamma\) has a level-\(u\) tangential run \([a,b]\) with }
      b<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma),\\
      e_x(\gamma)-u>\dfrac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
      \end{array}
    \right\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,deep}}(s,p)
  &=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{4em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Deep persistent levels are prefix-horizontal]
\label{cor:deep-persistent-levels-are-prefix-horizontal}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,deep}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,deep}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on deep persistent subterminal record
spread follows from the same exponent hypothesis on endpoint-prefix deep
horizontal spread.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every level counted in \(\mathcal U^{\rm deep}_{j,K,p}\) is persistent
subterminal record, hence has a record \((-1,+1)\)-crossing tangential run
\([a,b]\).  Since the level is subterminal, the endpoint sphere has radius
strictly larger than \(u\); after the run exits to level \(u+1\), the path
first reaches the endpoint sphere at a time strictly after \(b\).  Thus
\([a,b]\) is a level-\(u\) tangential run with
\[
  b<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma).
\]
The depth condition in \(\mathcal U^{\rm deep}_{j,K,p}\) is exactly the depth
condition in \(\mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}\).  Hence
\[
  \mathcal U^{\rm deep}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)
  \Longrightarrow
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma),
\]
and the property-restricted profile inequality follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Short endpoint-prefix spread profiles]
\label{def:short-endpoint-prefix-deep-horizontal-spread-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K,L\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\left\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      \begin{array}{l}
      \text{\(\gamma\) has a level-\(u\) tangential run \([a,b]\),}\\
      b<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)\text{ and }b-a\le L,\\
      e_x(\gamma)-u>\dfrac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
      \end{array}
    \right\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,deep,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Endpoint-prefix spread is long or short]
\label{cor:endpoint-prefix-spread-long-short-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,deep}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  W_{\beta,p}\,
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,deep,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on endpoint-prefix deep horizontal
spread follows from the same exponent hypothesis on long tangential runs and
short endpoint-prefix deep horizontal spread.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(\mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds but
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) fails, then among the
levels counted by \(\mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}\) there is at least one
level \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) that is not counted by the short
endpoint-prefix property.  This level has a prefix tangential run witnessing
its membership in \(\mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}\), and no such witnessing
run has length at most \(L\).  Hence \(T_x^u(\gamma)>L\), so
\(\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u,L}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Thus
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre}_{j,K,p}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,short}_{j,K,L,p}
  \cup
  \bigcup_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u,L}.
\]
Taking the weighted property-restricted union bound and then the supremum in
the definition of the profiles gives the displayed inequality, since
\(|A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N|\le W_{\beta,p}\).  The exponent conclusion follows
because \(\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Short endpoint-prefix outward profiles]
\label{def:short-endpoint-prefix-outward-spread-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K,L\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,out,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\left\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      \begin{array}{l}
      \text{\(\gamma\) has a level-\(u\) \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run
      \([a,b]\),}\\
      b<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)\text{ and }b-a\le L,\\
      e_x(\gamma)-u>\dfrac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
      \end{array}
    \right\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,out,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Short prefix spread is outward or returning]
\label{cor:short-endpoint-prefix-spread-outward-return-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then, for
all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,deep,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,16K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j+1,16K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on short endpoint-prefix deep
horizontal spread follows from the same exponent hypothesis on short
endpoint-prefix outward-through spread and on the same and next spread
exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(N\) be the number of levels counted by
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\).  If this property holds,
then
\[
  N>\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
If \(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,out,short}_{j,2K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) also fails, fewer
than or equal to \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(8K)\) of these counted
levels have a witnessing \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run.  Thus more than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(8K)\) counted levels have a short
endpoint-prefix tangential run that is not of type \((-1,+1)\).

For \(p\) close enough, \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(16K)>1\).  After
discarding the possible initial level \(u=0\), more than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(16K)\) such levels remain.  Each remaining
run is two-sided.  If it exits to level \(u-1\), its last step gives an
inward level-\(u\) token; if it enters from level \(u+1\), its first step
gives an inward level-\(u+1\) token.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns}, each token yields an
exterior return through level \(u\) or \(u+1\).

The map from the original level \(u\) to the resulting return level has at
most two preimages.  Hence more than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(32K)\) distinct return levels occur in
\(A_{j,p}\cup A_{j+1,p}\), provided \(p\) is close enough that
\(W_{\beta,p}>1\).  One of the two slabs therefore contains more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{64K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(16K)}L_H
\]
return levels.  This is exactly
\(\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,16K,p}(x,\gamma)\) or
\(\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j+1,16K,p}(x,\gamma)\).  Therefore, for all \(p\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,short}_{j,K,L,p}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,out,short}_{j,2K,L,p}
  \cup
  \mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,16K,p}
  \cup
  \mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j+1,16K,p}.
\]
Taking the corresponding property-restricted union bound gives the displayed
profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Short prefix-record outward profiles]
\label{def:short-prefix-record-outward-spread-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K,L\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,rec,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\left\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      \begin{array}{l}
      \text{\(\gamma\) has a level-\(u\) \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run
      \([a,b]\),}\\
      d(x,v_t)\ne u\ (0\le t<a),\\
      b<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)\text{ and }b-a\le L,\\
      e_x(\gamma)-u>\dfrac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
      \end{array}
    \right\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,rec,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Short outward-prefix spread is record or returning]
\label{cor:short-outward-prefix-spread-record-return-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on short outward-prefix spread follows
from the same exponent hypothesis on short prefix-record outward spread and
on the spread exterior-return profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that \(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,out,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds,
and let \(N\) be the number of levels counted by it.  If more than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(8K)\) of these levels have a witnessing
run that is record, then
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,rec,short}_{j,2K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Otherwise,
more than the same number of counted levels admit a short endpoint-prefix
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([a,b]\) that is not the first visit to level
\(u\).

For each such non-record level \(u\), choose a time \(t_0<a\) with
\(d(x,v_{t_0})=u\).  Since the chosen run is entered from level \(u-1\), let
\(t\) be the first time after \(t_0\) at which \(d(x,v_t)=u-1\).  Then
\(t<a\), and
\[
  d(x,v_{t-1})=u,\qquad d(x,v_t)=u-1.
\]
Thus \(t\) is an inward level-\(u\) token.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns},
\(\mathcal X_{u,0}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Therefore the non-record alternative
implies \(\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,2K,p}(x,\gamma)\).  Taking the
property-restricted union bound gives the displayed profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Short persistent prefix-record profiles]
\label{def:short-persistent-prefix-record-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K,L\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
\[
  \#\left\{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N:
      \begin{array}{l}
      \text{\(\gamma\) has a level-\(u\) \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run
      \([a,b]\),}\\
      d(x,v_t)\ne u\ (0\le t<a),\\
      d(x,v_t)>u\ (b<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),\\
      b<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)\text{ and }b-a\le L,\\
      e_x(\gamma)-u>\dfrac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
      \end{array}
    \right\}
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Short prefix-record spread is persistent or returning]
\label{cor:short-prefix-record-spread-persistent-return-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then, for
all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,4K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j+1,4K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on short prefix-record spread follows
from the same exponent hypothesis on short persistent prefix-record spread
and on the same and next spread exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that \(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,rec,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds,
and let \(N\) be the number of levels counted by it.  If more than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(8K)\) of these levels have a witnessing
record run that stays strictly above level \(u\) until
\(\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)\), then
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,short}_{j,2K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Otherwise,
more than the same number of counted levels have a witnessing record run
\([a,b]\) for which the path returns to level \(u\) before or at
\(\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)\).

For each such nonpersistent level, let \(t>b+1\) be the first time with
\(d(x,v_t)=u\).  Since \(d(x,v_{b+1})=u+1\), the first-return choice gives
\[
  d(x,v_{t-1})=u+1,\qquad d(x,v_t)=u.
\]
Thus \(t\) is an inward level-\(u+1\) token.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns},
\(\mathcal X_{u+1,0}(x,\gamma)\) holds.

The map \(u\mapsto u+1\) is injective and sends \(A_{j,p}\) into
\(A_{j,p}\cup A_{j+1,p}\), for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\).
Thus one of the two slabs contains more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(4K)}L_H
\]
return levels.  This gives
\(\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j,4K,p}(x,\gamma)\) or
\(\mathcal X^{\rm spr}_{j+1,4K,p}(x,\gamma)\).  The displayed profile
inequality follows by taking the property-restricted union bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Ordered prefix-ladder profiles]
\label{def:ordered-short-persistent-prefix-ladder-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K,L\ge1\), let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,lad,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
that there are an integer \(N_\star\ge1\), levels
\[
  u_1<\cdots<u_{N_\star}
  \qquad(u_q\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N),
\]
and level-\(u_q\) \((-1,+1)\)-crossing runs \([a_q,b_q]\) such that
\[
  N_\star>\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
and, for every \(1\le q\le N_\star\),
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u_q\quad(0\le t<a_q),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u_q\quad(b_q<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
\[
  b_q<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma),
  \qquad
  b_q-a_q\le L,
  \qquad
  e_x(\gamma)-u_q>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
and the witnessing runs are chronologically ordered:
\[
  b_q<a_{q+1}\qquad(1\le q<N_\star).
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,lad,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,lad,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Persistent prefix levels form ordered ladders]
\label{cor:persistent-prefix-levels-form-ordered-ladders}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,lad,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on short persistent prefix-record
spread follows from the same exponent hypothesis on ordered short persistent
prefix ladders.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Sort the
counted levels increasingly and write them as
\(u_1<\cdots<u_{N_\star}\).  For each \(q\), choose a witnessing record
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([a_q,b_q]\).  All displayed conditions in
Definition~\ref{def:ordered-short-persistent-prefix-ladder-profiles} except
the chronological ordering are exactly the defining conditions of
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,short}_{j,K,L,p}\).

It remains to check the order.  Let \(u_q<u_{q+1}\).  Since
\([a_q,b_q]\) is record, \(a_q\) is the first time that the path visits level
\(u_q\).  Before the path can first visit level \(u_{q+1}\), its radial
distance sequence must visit level \(u_q\).  Hence \(a_q<a_{q+1}\).  The
time \(a_{q+1}\) is not inside the level-\(u_q\) run, because
\(d(x,v_{a_{q+1}})=u_{q+1}>u_q\).  Therefore \(b_q<a_{q+1}\).  Thus the
sorted witnesses form an ordered prefix ladder, proving the property
inclusion and hence the profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Prefix-pair profiles]
\label{def:bounded-gap-prefix-pair-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,B\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,pair,short}_{j,K,L,B,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) for which there exist
\(v\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) and level-\(u\), level-\(v\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing runs \([a,b]\), \([a',b']\) satisfying
\[
  u<v\le u+B,\qquad b<a',
\]
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u\quad(0\le t<a),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u\quad(b<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne v\quad(0\le t<a'),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>v\quad(b'<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
and
\[
  b,b'<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma),
  \qquad
  b-a\le L,\quad b'-a'\le L,
\]
\[
  e_x(\gamma)-u>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
  \qquad
  e_x(\gamma)-v>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,B}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,pair,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,pair,short}_{j,K,L,B,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Ordered ladders have many bounded successor gaps]
\label{cor:ordered-ladders-have-bounded-successor-gaps}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\), and put
\[
  B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1 .
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,lad,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L,B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,pair,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on ordered short persistent prefix
ladders follows from the same exponent hypothesis on bounded-gap short
persistent prefix-pair profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,lad,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds, and choose
witnesses \(u_1<\cdots<u_{N_\star}\) and \([a_q,b_q]\) as in
Definition~\ref{def:ordered-short-persistent-prefix-ladder-profiles}.  Let
\(B=B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\).  Since all levels lie in the same slab,
\[
  \sum_{q=1}^{N_\star-1}(u_{q+1}-u_q)
  \le W_{\beta,p}.
\]
For \(p\) close enough to \(\pc(H)\), \(W_{\beta,p}\le\beta L_H\), and hence
the number of indices \(q\) with \(u_{q+1}-u_q>B\) is at most
\[
  \frac{\beta}{B}L_H
  <
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H .
\]
Since
\[
  N_\star>\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
and \(p\) may be taken close enough that
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(16K)>1\), more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(2K)}L_H
\]
indices \(q\) satisfy \(u_{q+1}-u_q\le B\).  For every such \(q\), the pair
\((u_q,u_{q+1})\), together with the witnessing runs
\([a_q,b_q]\), \([a_{q+1},b_{q+1}]\), satisfies the bounded-gap prefix-pair
conditions with parameter \(2K\).  The depth requirements are inherited
because
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
  >
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(2K)}L_H .
\]
The lower levels \(u_q\) are distinct, so
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,pair,short}_{j,2K,L,B,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  This
property inclusion gives the displayed profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-gap prefix-pair profiles]
\label{def:fixed-gap-prefix-pair-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,gap,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) such that
\(u+h\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) and there are level-\(u\), level-\(u+h\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing runs \([a,b]\), \([a',b']\) satisfying
\[
  b<a',
\]
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u\quad(0\le t<a),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u\quad(b<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u+h\quad(0\le t<a'),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u+h\quad(b'<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
and
\[
  b,b'<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma),
  \qquad
  b-a\le L,\quad b'-a'\le L,
\]
\[
  e_x(\gamma)-u>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
  \qquad
  e_x(\gamma)-(u+h)>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,gap,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,gap,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded-gap pairs have a fixed gap]
\label{cor:bounded-gap-pairs-have-fixed-gap}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,B\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,B}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,pair,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,KB,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,gap,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on bounded-gap short persistent
prefix-pair profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the finite
family of fixed-gap short persistent prefix-pair profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,pair,short}_{j,K,L,B,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  For
\(1\le h\le B\), let \(N_h\) be the number of levels \(u\) for which the
fixed gap \(h\) has witnesses satisfying the conditions in
Definition~\ref{def:fixed-gap-prefix-pair-profiles}, except with the stronger
depth threshold \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\).  Every level
counted by the bounded-gap pair property contributes to at least one \(N_h\),
so
\[
  \sum_{h=1}^B N_h>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Thus some \(h\) has
\[
  N_h>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4KB}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(KB)}L_H .
\]
The depth assumptions with parameter \(K\) imply those with parameter \(KB\).
Hence, for this \(h\),
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,gap,short}_{j,KB,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
holds.  Taking the property-restricted union bound over \(1\le h\le B\) gives
the displayed profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Confined fixed-gap bridge profiles]
\label{def:confined-fixed-gap-bridge-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the
property that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) satisfying the
fixed-gap conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:fixed-gap-prefix-pair-profiles}, with witnesses
\([a,b]\) at level \(u\) and \([a',b']\) at level \(u+h\), and such that
\[
  u<d(x,v_t)<u+h
  \qquad(b<t<a')
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-gap pairs have confined bridges]
\label{cor:fixed-gap-pairs-have-confined-bridges}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,gap,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on fixed-gap short persistent
prefix-pair profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on confined
fixed-gap bridge profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,gap,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds, and take
a counted level \(u\) with witnesses \([a,b]\) at level \(u\) and
\([a',b']\) at level \(u+h\).  For \(b<t<a'\), lower persistence gives
\[
  d(x,v_t)>u.
\]
The upper run is record at level \(u+h\), so
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u+h
  \qquad(0\le t<a').
\]
Since \(d(x,v_b)=u\) and \(d(x,v_{b+1})=u+1\), the radial distance sequence
cannot exceed \(u+h\) before first visiting \(u+h\).  Hence
\[
  d(x,v_t)<u+h
  \qquad(b<t<a').
\]
Thus every fixed-gap witness is a confined bridge witness.  The profile
inequality follows by monotonicity of property-restricted profiles.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Large fixed gaps do not have enough slab starts]
\label{lem:large-fixed-gaps-do-not-have-enough-slab-starts}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\).  If
\[
  W_{\beta,p}-h\le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
then
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
is false for every rooted path \((x,\gamma)\).  Consequently,
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p)=0 .
\]
In particular, the profile is zero whenever \(h\ge W_{\beta,p}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The only possible counted lower levels \(u\) are those for which both
\[
  u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  u+h\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N .
\]
The slab \(A_{j,p}\) contains at most \(W_{\beta,p}\) integer levels, so there
are at most \(\max\{W_{\beta,p}-h,0\}\) such lower levels.  If the displayed
assumption holds, this maximum is at most
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\).  The bridge property requires
strictly more than this many counted levels, which is impossible.  The final
assertion follows because \(h\ge W_{\beta,p}\) makes the maximum equal to
zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Inward-free confined fixed-gap bridge profiles]
\label{def:inward-free-confined-fixed-gap-bridge-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,free,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the
property that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) satisfying the
confined fixed-gap bridge conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:confined-fixed-gap-bridge-profiles}, with witnesses
\([a,b]\) at level \(u\) and \([a',b']\) at level \(u+h\), and such that
\[
  d(x,v_{t+1})\ge d(x,v_t)
  \qquad(b\le t<a')
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,free,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,free,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Confined bridges are inward-free or returning]
\label{cor:confined-bridges-inward-free-or-returning}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(h\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,free,short}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K\max\{h-1,1\}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on confined fixed-gap bridge profiles
follows from the same exponent hypothesis on inward-free confined bridge
profiles and on the corresponding spread exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds, and
let \(N\) be the number of counted lower levels \(u\).  If more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(2K)}L_H
\]
of these starts admit inward-free bridge witnesses, then the inward-free
bridge property with parameter \(2K\) holds.

Otherwise, more than \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(8K)\) counted starts
have no inward-free bridge witness.  For such a start, choose a confined
bridge witness \([a,b]\), \([a',b']\).  Since it is not inward-free, there is
some \(t\) with \(b\le t<a'\) such that
\[
  d(x,v_{t+1})=d(x,v_t)-1 .
\]
The confinement condition rules out a step down to level \(u\) before
\(a'\), and the upper run is record at level \(u+h\).  Thus this is an inward
token at some level
\[
  w\in\{u+1,\ldots,u+h-1\}.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns},
\(\mathcal X_{w,0}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Since \(u\) and \(u+h\) both lie in
the slab, so does every such intermediate \(w\).

For a fixed return level \(w\), the possible lower starts \(u\) that can map
to it satisfy \(u<w<u+h\), so there are at most \(\max\{h-1,1\}\) of them.
Hence the number of distinct return levels in \(A_{j,p}\) is larger than
\[
  \frac{1}{\max\{h-1,1\}}
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
       {4(2K\max\{h-1,1\})}L_H .
\]
This is the spread-return property with parameter
\(2K\max\{h-1,1\}\).  The displayed profile inequality follows from the
property-restricted union bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Adjacent fixed gaps are immediate]
\label{rem:adjacent-fixed-gaps-are-immediate}
When \(h=1\), the confinement condition
\[
  u<d(x,v_t)<u+1
\]
has no integer solution.  Hence every confined fixed-gap bridge with
\(h=1\) satisfies \(a'=b+1\): the upper record run starts immediately after
the lower run exits upward.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Adjacent stacked prefix-pair profiles]
\label{def:adjacent-stacked-prefix-pair-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,adj,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) satisfying the fixed-gap
conditions from Definition~\ref{def:fixed-gap-prefix-pair-profiles} with
\(h=1\), with witnesses \([a,b]\) at level \(u\) and \([a',b']\) at level
\(u+1\), and such that
\[
  a'=b+1
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,adj,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,adj,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Adjacent confined bridges are stacked]
\label{cor:adjacent-confined-bridges-are-stacked}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,adj,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on adjacent confined fixed-gap bridge
profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on adjacent stacked
prefix-pair profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For \(h=1\), Remark~\ref{rem:adjacent-fixed-gaps-are-immediate} shows that
every confined fixed-gap bridge witness has \(a'=b+1\).  Thus every level
counted by
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,1,p}(x,\gamma)\) is counted by
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,adj,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\).  The profile
inequality follows by monotonicity of property-restricted profiles.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Two-level outward-staircase profiles]
\label{def:two-level-outward-staircase-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the property
that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) such that
\(u+1\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) and there are a level-\(u\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([a,b]\) and a level-\(u+1\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([b+1,b']\) satisfying
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u\quad(0\le t<a),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u\quad(b<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u+1\quad(0\le t<b+1),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u+1\quad(b'<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
\[
  b,b'<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma),
  \qquad
  b'-a\le L,
\]
and
\[
  e_x(\gamma)-u>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
  \qquad
  e_x(\gamma)-(u+1)>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Locally short two-level staircase profiles]
\label{def:locally-short-two-level-staircase-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) be the
property that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) such that
\(u+1\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) and there are a level-\(u\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([a,b]\) and a level-\(u+1\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run \([b+1,b']\) satisfying
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u\quad(0\le t<a),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u\quad(b<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u+1\quad(0\le t<b+1),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u+1\quad(b'<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma)),
\]
\[
  b,b'<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma),
  \qquad
  b-a\le L,\quad b'-(b+1)\le L,
\]
and
\[
  e_x(\gamma)-u>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
  \qquad
  e_x(\gamma)-(u+1)>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,short}_{j,K,L,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Adjacent stacks are outward staircases]
\label{cor:adjacent-stacks-are-outward-staircases}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,adj,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,2L+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on adjacent stacked prefix-pair
profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on two-level outward
staircase profiles with the length cutoff \(2L+1\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every adjacent stacked witness has \(a'=b+1\).  The two witnessing runs have
lengths at most \(L\), so the combined staircase interval satisfies
\[
  b'-a=(b-a)+1+(b'-a')\le 2L+1 .
\]
All record, persistence, and endpoint-clearance conditions are the same as in
the adjacent stacked definition, with \(u+1\) in place of the upper fixed-gap
level.  Hence
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,adj,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)
  \Longrightarrow
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,short}_{j,K,2L+1,p}(x,\gamma).
\]
The profile inequality follows by monotonicity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Staircases are locally short or long]
\label{cor:staircases-locally-short-or-long}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,2L+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  W_{\beta,p}\,
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on two-level outward-staircase profiles
with cutoff \(2L+1\) follows from the same exponent hypothesis on long
tangential runs and locally short two-level staircase profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,short}_{j,K,2L+1,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds but
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) fails, then
some counted staircase level \(u\) is not locally short.  For its witnessing
runs, either
\[
  b-a>L
  \qquad\text{or}\qquad
  b'-(b+1)>L .
\]
In the first case \(\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u,L}(x,\gamma)\) holds; in the
second case \(\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u+1,L}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Since the
staircase definition requires both \(u\) and \(u+1\) to lie in
\(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\), we have
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,short}_{j,K,2L+1,p}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,short}_{j,K,L,p}
  \cup
  \bigcup_{w\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{w,L}.
\]
Taking the weighted property-restricted union bound and then the supremum in
the profile definitions gives the displayed inequality, because
\(|A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N|\le W_{\beta,p}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-gap locally short staircase-pair profiles]
\label{def:bounded-gap-locally-short-staircase-pair-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,B\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,pair,short}_{j,K,L,B,p}(x,\gamma)\) be
the property that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) for which
there is a level \(v\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) with
\[
  u<v\le u+B
\]
such that the locally short two-level staircase conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-two-level-staircase-profiles} hold at
lower levels \(u\) and \(v\), with the same parameters \(K,L\), is larger
than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,B}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,pair,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,pair,short}_{j,K,L,B,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Locally short staircases have bounded successor gaps]
\label{cor:locally-short-staircases-have-bounded-successor-gaps}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\), and put
\[
  B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1 .
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L,B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,pair,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on locally short two-level staircase
profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on bounded-gap locally
short staircase-pair profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds, and
sort the counted lower levels as
\[
  u_1<\cdots<u_{N_\star}.
\]
Let \(B=B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\).  Since all lower levels lie in the
same slab,
\[
  \sum_{q=1}^{N_\star-1}(u_{q+1}-u_q)\le W_{\beta,p}.
\]
For \(p\) close enough to \(\pc(H)\), \(W_{\beta,p}\le\beta L_H\), and hence
the number of indices \(q\) with \(u_{q+1}-u_q>B\) is at most
\[
  \frac{\beta}{B}L_H
  <
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H .
\]
As in Corollary~\ref{cor:ordered-ladders-have-bounded-successor-gaps}, more
than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(2K)}L_H
\]
successor pairs have gap at most \(B\).  For each such pair, the two locally
short staircase witnesses satisfy the bounded-gap staircase-pair conditions
with parameter \(2K\); the endpoint-clearance assumptions are inherited
because replacing \(K\) by \(2K\) weakens the required depth.  Thus the
bounded-gap staircase-pair property holds, giving the displayed profile
inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-gap locally short staircase-pair profiles]
\label{def:fixed-gap-locally-short-staircase-pair-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,gap,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\) be
the property that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) such that
\(u+h\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) and the locally short two-level staircase
conditions from Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-two-level-staircase-profiles}
hold at lower levels \(u\) and \(u+h\), with the same parameters \(K,L\), is
larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,gap,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,gap,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded-gap staircase pairs have a fixed gap]
\label{cor:bounded-gap-staircase-pairs-have-fixed-gap}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,B\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,B}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,pair,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,KB,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,gap,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on bounded-gap locally short
staircase-pair profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the
finite family of fixed-gap locally short staircase-pair profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,pair,short}_{j,K,L,B,p}(x,\gamma)\)
holds.  For \(1\le h\le B\), let \(N_h\) be the number of levels \(u\) for
which the fixed gap \(h\) has locally short staircase witnesses at lower
levels \(u\) and \(u+h\), except with the stronger depth threshold
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\).  Every level counted by the
bounded-gap staircase-pair property contributes to at least one \(N_h\), so
\[
  \sum_{h=1}^B N_h>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Thus some \(h\) has
\[
  N_h>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4KB}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(KB)}L_H .
\]
The depth assumptions with parameter \(K\) imply those with parameter \(KB\).
For this \(h\),
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,gap,short}_{j,KB,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
holds.  Taking the property-restricted union bound over \(1\le h\le B\)
gives the displayed profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Locally short outward staircase-chain profiles]
\label{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,p}(x,\gamma)\)
be the property that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) such that
\(u+r\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) for every \(0\le r<\ell\), and such that
there are level-\(u+r\) \((-1,+1)\)-crossing runs
\([a_r,b_r]\), \(0\le r<\ell\), satisfying
\[
  a_{r+1}=b_r+1
  \qquad(0\le r<\ell-1),
\]
\[
  d(x,v_t)\ne u+r\quad(0\le t<a_r),
  \qquad
  d(x,v_t)>u+r\quad(b_r<t\le\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma))
  \qquad(0\le r<\ell),
\]
\[
  b_r<\tau_x^{\rm end}(\gamma),
  \qquad
  b_r-a_r\le L
  \qquad(0\le r<\ell),
\]
and
\[
  e_x(\gamma)-(u+r)>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
  \qquad(0\le r<\ell)
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{n\ge0,\ |2n-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Inward-free bridges are chains or long runs]
\label{cor:inward-free-bridges-are-chains-or-long-runs}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,free,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
  +
  W_{\beta,p}\,
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on inward-free confined bridge
profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on locally short
staircase-chain profiles of length \(h+1\) and on the long-run profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,free,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds,
and take a counted level \(u\) with inward-free bridge witnesses \([a,b]\)
at level \(u\) and \([a',b']\) at level \(u+h\).  If \(h=1\), the confinement
condition has no intermediate integer level and the bridge is adjacent, so
the two witnesses form a locally short chain of length \(2=h+1\).

Assume \(h\ge2\).  Since the radial distance is nondecreasing on
\([b,a']\), starts at level \(u\), and first reaches level \(u+h\) at
\(a'\), for every \(1\le r<h\) there is a unique maximal interval
\([a_r,b_r]\subseteq[b+1,a'-1]\) on which
\[
  d(x,v_t)=u+r .
\]
Moreover these intervals are consecutive and are \((-1,+1)\)-crossing runs:
if \([a_0,b_0]=[a,b]\) and \([a_h,b_h]=[a',b']\), then
\[
  a_{r+1}=b_r+1\qquad(0\le r<h).
\]
The lower bridge run is record at level \(u\).  Hence no level
\(u+r\), \(1\le r<h\), can have been visited before \(a_r\), since any such
