visit would force an earlier visit to level \(u\).  Thus the intermediate
runs are record runs.  Persistence after each intermediate run follows from
monotonicity until \(a'\) and from the upper-run persistence after \(b'\).
The endpoint-clearance inequalities for intermediate levels follow from the
upper endpoint-clearance inequality.

Therefore, if all intermediate runs have length at most \(L\), the counted
start \(u\) also witnesses the locally short staircase-chain property of
length \(h+1\).  If not, then for some
\[
  w\in\{u+1,\ldots,u+h-1\}\subseteq A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N
\]
the long-run event \(\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{w,L}(x,\gamma)\) holds.

Consequently,
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,bridge,free,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K,L,h+1,p}
  \cup
  \bigcup_{w\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{w,L}.
\]
Taking the property-restricted union bound in the weighted sums and then the
supremum in the profile definitions gives the displayed inequality, since
\(|A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N|\le W_{\beta,p}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Confined fixed-gap locally short staircase-bridge profiles]
\label{def:confined-fixed-gap-locally-short-staircase-bridge-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(h\ge3\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}(x,\gamma)\)
be the property that the number of \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) satisfying
the fixed-gap locally short staircase-pair conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:fixed-gap-locally-short-staircase-pair-profiles}, with
lower staircase witnesses \([a,b]\), \([b+1,b']\) at levels \(u,u+1\) and
upper staircase witnesses \([c,d]\), \([d+1,d']\) at levels \(u+h,u+h+1\),
and such that
\[
  u+1<d(x,v_t)<u+h
  \qquad(b'<t<c)
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,bridge,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,h,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-gap staircase pairs split into chains and bridges]
\label{cor:fixed-gap-staircase-pairs-split-into-chains-and-bridges}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,gap,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,3}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p),
\]
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,2}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,gap,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,4}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p),
\]
and, for every \(h\ge3\),
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,gap,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on fixed-gap locally short
staircase-pair profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the
three-level and four-level locally short staircase-chain profiles and the
confined fixed-gap locally short staircase-bridge profiles with \(h\ge3\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
First suppose \(h=1\), and take a counted level \(u\) in
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,gap,short}_{j,K,L,1,p}(x,\gamma)\).
Let the lower staircase witnesses be
\([a_0,b_0]\), \([a_1,b_1]\) at levels \(u,u+1\), where
\(a_1=b_0+1\).  Let the upper staircase witnesses be
\([c,d]\), \([d+1,d']\) at levels \(u+1,u+2\).  Both
\([a_1,b_1]\) and \([c,d]\) are record level-\(u+1\) tangential runs, so
their initial times are the first visit to level \(u+1\).  Hence
\(c=a_1\), and maximality of tangential runs gives \(d=b_1\).  Thus
\[
  [a_0,b_0],\quad [a_1,b_1],\quad [b_1+1,d']
\]
are consecutive locally short outward staircase-chain witnesses at the
levels \(u,u+1,u+2\).  All record, persistence, length, and endpoint-clearance
conditions are exactly those supplied by the two fixed-gap staircase
witnesses.

Now suppose \(h=2\).  With the same notation for the lower staircase and
with upper witnesses \([c,d]\), \([d+1,d']\) at levels \(u+2,u+3\), the
level-\(u+1\) run \([a_1,b_1]\) exits outward, so
\[
  d(x,v_{b_1+1})=u+2 .
\]
Before \(a_1\) the path has not visited level \(u+1\), and during
\([a_1,b_1]\) it is at level \(u+1\).  Since the radial distance changes by
at most one at each step, a previous visit to level \(u+2\) would force a
previous visit to level \(u+1\).  Hence \(b_1+1\) is the first visit to
level \(u+2\).  Since the upper lower run is record at level \(u+2\), we have
\(c=b_1+1\).  The four runs
\[
  [a_0,b_0],\quad [a_1,b_1],\quad [c,d],\quad [d+1,d']
\]
therefore satisfy the locally short staircase-chain conditions at the levels
\(u,u+1,u+2,u+3\).

Finally suppose \(h\ge3\), and write the lower staircase witnesses as
\([a,b]\), \([b+1,b']\) and the upper staircase witnesses as
\([c,d]\), \([d+1,d']\).  The upper lower run is record at level \(u+h\), so
\(c\) is the first time the path visits level \(u+h\).  A visit to level
\(u+h\) before \(b+1\) would force a visit to level \(u+1\) before \(b+1\),
while the times \(b+1,\ldots,b'\) themselves are at level \(u+1\).  Thus
\(b'<c\).  For \(b'<t<c\), persistence of the level-\(u+1\) run gives
\[
  d(x,v_t)>u+1 .
\]
The path has not yet visited level \(u+h\), and the radial distance sequence
cannot jump over level \(u+h\).  Hence
\[
  d(x,v_t)<u+h
  \qquad(b'<t<c).
\]
Thus every fixed-gap staircase-pair witness with \(h\ge3\) is a confined
staircase-bridge witness.  Each displayed profile inequality follows by
monotonicity of property-restricted profiles.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-gap locally short staircase-chain-pair profiles]
\label{def:bounded-gap-locally-short-staircase-chain-pair-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,\ell,B\ge1\) with
\(\ell\ge2\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,B,p}
(x,\gamma)\) be the property that the number of
\(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) for which there is a level
\(v\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) with
\[
  u<v\le u+B
\]
such that the locally short outward staircase-chain conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles} hold at
lower levels \(u\) and \(v\), with the same parameters \(K,L,\ell\), is
larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,B}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,B,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Staircase chains have bounded successor gaps]
\label{cor:staircase-chains-have-bounded-successor-gaps}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\), and put
\[
  B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1 .
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L,\ell,
    B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on locally short staircase-chain
profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on bounded-gap locally
short staircase-chain-pair profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,p}(x,\gamma)\)
holds, and sort the counted chain-start levels as
\[
  u_1<\cdots<u_{N_\star}.
\]
The same bounded-gap count as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:locally-short-staircases-have-bounded-successor-gaps}
shows that, for \(p\) close enough to \(\pc(H)\), more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(2K)}L_H
\]
successor pairs have gap at most \(B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\).  For each
such pair, the two chain witnesses satisfy the bounded-gap
staircase-chain-pair conditions with parameter \(2K\).  The endpoint
clearance assumptions are inherited because replacing \(K\) by \(2K\) weakens
the required depth.  This proves the property inclusion and hence the
profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-gap locally short staircase-chain-pair profiles]
\label{def:fixed-gap-locally-short-staircase-chain-pair-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,gap,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,h,p}
(x,\gamma)\) be the property that the number of
\(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) such that \(u+h\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) and
the locally short outward staircase-chain conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles} hold at
lower levels \(u\) and \(u+h\), with the same parameters \(K,L,\ell\), is
larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,gap,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,gap,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,h,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded-gap staircase-chain pairs have a fixed gap]
\label{cor:bounded-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-have-fixed-gap}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,\ell,B\ge1\) with
\(\ell\ge2\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,B}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,KB,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,gap,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on bounded-gap locally short
staircase-chain-pair profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on
the finite family of fixed-gap locally short staircase-chain-pair profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The proof is the same finite-gap pigeonhole used in
Corollary~\ref{cor:bounded-gap-staircase-pairs-have-fixed-gap}.  If the
bounded-gap staircase-chain-pair property holds, write \(N_h\) for the number
of counted starts whose successor chain starts at distance \(h\), still using
the stronger depth threshold \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\).
Then
\[
  \sum_{h=1}^B N_h>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
so some \(h\) has
\[
  N_h>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4KB}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(KB)}L_H .
\]
The depth assumptions with parameter \(K\) imply those with parameter \(KB\),
so the fixed-gap staircase-chain-pair property with parameters
\((KB,L,\ell,h)\) holds.  Taking the property-restricted union bound over
\(1\le h\le B\) gives the displayed inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Confined fixed-gap staircase-chain bridge profiles]
\label{def:confined-fixed-gap-staircase-chain-bridge-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L,h\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\).  Let
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,h,p}
(x,\gamma)\) be the property that the number of
\(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) satisfying the fixed-gap staircase-chain-pair
conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:fixed-gap-locally-short-staircase-chain-pair-profiles},
with lower-chain witnesses \([a_r,b_r]\), \(0\le r<\ell\), at levels
\(u+r\), and upper-chain witnesses \([c_r,d_r]\), \(0\le r<\ell\), at levels
\(u+h+r\), and such that
\[
  u+\ell-1<d(x,v_t)<u+h
  \qquad(b_{\ell-1}<t<c_0)
\]
is larger than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H .
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,h,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-gap staircase-chain pairs split]
\label{cor:fixed-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\),
\(\ell\ge2\), and \(h\ge1\).  If \(1\le h\le\ell\), then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,gap,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p).
\]
If \(h\ge\ell+1\), then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,gap,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on fixed-gap locally short
staircase-chain-pair profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on
longer locally short staircase chains and on confined fixed-gap
staircase-chain bridge profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Take a fixed-gap staircase-chain-pair witness with lower chain
\([a_r,b_r]\), \(0\le r<\ell\), and upper chain \([c_r,d_r]\),
\(0\le r<\ell\).

Suppose first that \(1\le h\le\ell\).  For \(0\le r<\ell-h\), the lower run
\([a_{h+r},b_{h+r}]\) and the upper run \([c_r,d_r]\) are both record
tangential runs at level \(u+h+r\).  Hence they have the same initial time,
and maximality gives
\[
  [c_r,d_r]=[a_{h+r},b_{h+r}]
  \qquad(0\le r<\ell-h).
\]
If \(h<\ell\), the identity at \(r=\ell-h-1\), together with the consecutive
condition in the upper chain, gives
\[
  c_{\ell-h}=d_{\ell-h-1}+1=b_{\ell-1}+1.
\]
If \(h=\ell\), the lower last run exits outward at time \(b_{\ell-1}+1\);
the radial distance cannot have visited level \(u+\ell\) earlier without a
previous visit to level \(u+\ell-1\), while
\([a_{\ell-1},b_{\ell-1}]\) is the first level-\(u+\ell-1\) run.  Thus
\(c_0=b_{\ell-1}+1\).  In both cases, concatenating the lower chain with the
non-overlapping tail of the upper chain gives a locally short outward
staircase chain of length \(\ell+h\), with all record, persistence, length,
and endpoint-clearance conditions inherited from the two witnesses.

Now suppose \(h\ge\ell+1\).  The upper first run is record at level \(u+h\),
so \(c_0\) is the first time the path visits level \(u+h\).  A visit to level
\(u+h\) before \(a_{\ell-1}\) would force a visit to level \(u+\ell-1\)
before \(a_{\ell-1}\), and the interval \([a_{\ell-1},b_{\ell-1}]\) itself
is at level \(u+\ell-1\).  Hence \(b_{\ell-1}<c_0\).  For
\(b_{\ell-1}<t<c_0\), persistence of the last lower-chain run gives
\[
  d(x,v_t)>u+\ell-1,
\]
while the record property of the upper first run and nearest-neighbour radial
motion give
\[
  d(x,v_t)<u+h .
\]
Thus the fixed-gap chain-pair witness is a confined staircase-chain bridge.
The two displayed profile inequalities follow by monotonicity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Staircase-chain bridges project to ordinary bridges]
\label{cor:staircase-chain-bridges-project-to-ordinary-bridges}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\),
\(\ell\ge2\), and \(h\ge\ell+1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,h-\ell+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on confined fixed-gap
staircase-chain bridge profiles follows from the corresponding exponent
hypothesis on ordinary confined fixed-gap bridge profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,h,p}
(x,\gamma)\) holds, and take a counted lower-chain start \(u\).  Let
\([a_r,b_r]\), \(0\le r<\ell\), be the lower-chain witnesses at levels
\(u+r\), and let \([c_r,d_r]\), \(0\le r<\ell\), be the upper-chain
witnesses at levels \(u+h+r\).  Put
\[
  U=u+\ell-1,
  \qquad
  g=h-\ell+1 .
\]
Then \(g\ge2\), \(U\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\), and
\[
  U+g=u+h\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N,
\]
because the lower and upper chain conditions require the starts \(u+\ell-1\)
and \(u+h\) to lie in the slab.

The last lower-chain run \([a_{\ell-1},b_{\ell-1}]\) is a record
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run at level \(U\), and the first upper-chain run
\([c_0,d_0]\) is a record \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run at level \(U+g\).  Their
length, persistence, and endpoint-clearance assumptions are exactly the
corresponding fixed-gap prefix-pair assumptions with gap \(g\).  The
chain-bridge confinement gives
\[
  U<d(x,v_t)<U+g
  \qquad(b_{\ell-1}<t<c_0),
\]
which is the ordinary confined bridge condition.  Thus every counted
chain-bridge start \(u\) yields the counted ordinary bridge level \(U\).  The
map \(u\mapsto U=u+\ell-1\) is injective, so the counted-level lower bound is
preserved with the same parameter \(K\).  This proves the property inclusion
and hence the profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-step staircase-chain amplification]
\label{cor:one-step-staircase-chain-amplification}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\).  Put
\[
  B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1,
  \qquad
  K^+=2K B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}.
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\min\{\ell,B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K^+,L,\ell+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{h=\ell+1}^{B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K^+,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second sum is absent if
\(B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\le\ell\).  More generally, if
\(\widetilde B\ge B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\) and
\(\widetilde K=2K\widetilde B\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\ell}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,\widetilde K,L,\ell+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{h=\ell+1}^{\widetilde B}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,\widetilde K,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on locally short staircase-chain
profiles follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the displayed
longer-chain and confined chain-bridge profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chains-have-bounded-successor-gaps} to
obtain a bounded-gap chain-pair profile with parameter \(2K\) and cutoff
\(B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\).  Then apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:bounded-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-have-fixed-gap}, which
replaces this by fixed-gap chain-pair profiles with parameter
\[
  K^+=2K B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}.
\]
Finally split each fixed gap using
Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-split}: gaps
\(1\le h\le\ell\) glue into chains of length \(\ell+h\), and gaps
\(h\ge\ell+1\) become confined chain bridges.  Combining the three displayed
profile inequalities gives the claim.
The more general displayed inequality follows from the first one by
monotonicity in the depth parameter and by adding finitely many nonnegative
chain and bridge terms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite staircase-chain amplification]
\label{cor:finite-staircase-chain-amplification}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\),
\(\ell\ge2\), and \(n\ge0\).  Put \(K_0=K\).  For
\(1\le r\le n\), choose integers \(B_r\) recursively so that
\[
  B_r\ge B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K_{r-1}}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K_{r-1}\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1,
  \qquad
  K_r=2K_{r-1}B_r .
\]
Let \(\mathcal A_0(\ell)=\{(\ell)\}\), and for \(r\ge1\) let
\(\mathcal A_r(\ell)\) be the set of sequences
\(\mathbf a=(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\) such that
\((a_0,\ldots,a_{r-1})\in\mathcal A_{r-1}(\ell)\) and
\[
  a_{r-1}+1\le a_r\le 2a_{r-1}.
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n(\ell)}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a_n}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_{r-1}(\ell)}
  \sum_{h=a_{r-1}+1}^{B_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,a_{r-1},h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here an inner bridge sum is interpreted as zero when
\(B_r\le a_{r-1}\), and the sums over \(\mathcal A_r(\ell)\) keep
multiplicity through the sequence \(\mathbf a\).  Consequently, the exponent
hypothesis on the initial chain profile follows from the same exponent
hypothesis on the terminal chain profiles and the accumulated confined
chain-bridge profiles displayed above.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The case \(n=0\) is the identity inequality.  Suppose the claim has been
proved for \(n-1\).  There are finitely many terminal sequences
\(\mathbf a=(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})\in\mathcal A_{n-1}(\ell)\), so
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-step-staircase-chain-amplification} may be applied
to each terminal chain profile with
\[
  (\widetilde B,\widetilde K)=(B_n,K_n)
\]
and with chain length \(a_{n-1}\).  This gives, for each such
\(\mathbf a\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{n-1},L,a_{n-1}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{a_n=a_{n-1}+1}^{2a_{n-1}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a_n}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{h=a_{n-1}+1}^{B_n}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a_{n-1},h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting these finitely many inequalities into the induction hypothesis
for \(n-1\) gives exactly the displayed bound for \(n\).  Since all index
sets are finite and independent of \(p\), the exponent implication follows
from the union-bound form of the displayed inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-free finite chain amplification]
\label{cor:multiplicity-free-finite-chain-amplification}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-staircase-chain-amplification}, define
\[
  I_r(\ell)=\{\ell+r,\ell+r+1,\ldots,2^r\ell\}
  \qquad(r\ge0),
\]
where \(I_0(\ell)=\{\ell\}\).  Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{a\in I_n(\ell)}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{a\in I_{r-1}(\ell)}
  \sum_{h=a+1}^{B_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,a,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
As usual, an inner bridge sum is zero when \(B_r\le a\).  Consequently, the
exponent hypothesis on the initial chain profile follows from the same
exponent hypothesis on these distinct terminal chain and accumulated
chain-bridge profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
We use the property inclusions underlying
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-step-staircase-chain-amplification}, rather than the
already-summed inequality.  For every \(a\ge2\), the one-step proof gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K_{r-1},L,a,p}
  \subseteq&
  \bigcup_{b=a+1}^{2a}
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K_r,L,b,p}
\\
  &\cup
  \bigcup_{h=a+1}^{B_r}
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}_{j,K_r,L,a,h,p}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The possible chain lengths after \(r\) chain continuations are exactly the
integer interval \(I_r(\ell)\), since
\[
  \bigcup_{a\in I_{r-1}(\ell)}\{a+1,\ldots,2a\}
  =
  I_r(\ell).
\]
Iterating the displayed property inclusion \(n\) times therefore gives a
single union over the distinct terminal lengths in \(I_n(\ell)\), together
with the distinct bridge profiles created at each intermediate step.  Taking
the property-restricted union bound gives the displayed profile inequality.
All displayed index sets are finite and independent of \(p\), so the exponent
implication follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-free chain amplification with ordinary bridges]
\label{cor:multiplicity-free-chain-amplification-with-ordinary-bridges}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:multiplicity-free-finite-chain-amplification}, for all
\(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{a\in I_n(\ell)}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{g=2}^{B_r-\ell-r+2}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,g}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
An inner ordinary-bridge sum is interpreted as zero when
\(B_r-\ell-r+2<2\).  Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial
chain profile follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the distinct
terminal chain profiles and the displayed ordinary confined fixed-gap bridge
profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Starting from
Corollary~\ref{cor:multiplicity-free-finite-chain-amplification}, each bridge
residual at step \(r\) has the form
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,a,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p),
\]
where \(a\in I_{r-1}(\ell)\) and \(h\ge a+1\).  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridges-project-to-ordinary-bridges}, this
term is bounded by the ordinary bridge profile with gap
\[
  g=h-a+1 .
\]
For \(a\in I_{r-1}(\ell)\), we have \(a\ge\ell+r-1\), so
\[
  2\le g\le B_r-a+1\le B_r-\ell-r+2 .
\]
Thus the union of all projected bridge residuals created at stage \(r\) is
contained in the union of the ordinary bridge properties with
\[
  2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2 .
\]
Taking the property-restricted union bound, with duplicate ordinary bridge
gaps counted only once, gives the displayed inequality.  The exponent
implication follows because the displayed index sets are finite for fixed
\(n\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Ordinary-bridge truncation in finite chain amplification]
\label{cor:ordinary-bridge-truncation-in-finite-chain-amplification}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:multiplicity-free-chain-amplification-with-ordinary-bridges},
for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{a\in I_n(\ell)}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\substack{2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2\\
        g< W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,g}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, the bridge sum at stage \(r\) may always be truncated to
gaps \(2\le g<W_{\beta,p}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Start from
Corollary~\ref{cor:multiplicity-free-chain-amplification-with-ordinary-bridges}.
For each stage \(r\), Lemma~\ref{lem:large-fixed-gaps-do-not-have-enough-slab-starts}
shows that every ordinary bridge term with
\[
  g\ge W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H
\]
is zero.  Removing these zero terms gives the displayed inequality.  The
last assertion is the weaker special case \(g<W_{\beta,p}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite chain amplification with inward-free bridges]
\label{cor:finite-chain-amplification-with-inward-free-bridges}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:ordinary-bridge-truncation-in-finite-chain-amplification},
for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{a\in I_n(\ell)}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\substack{2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2\\
        g< W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_r,L,g}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,free,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\substack{2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2\\
        g< W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H}}
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_r(g-1)}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, for fixed \(n\), the exponent hypothesis on the initial chain
profile follows from uniform exponent hypotheses on the displayed terminal
chain profiles, inward-free bridge profiles, and spread-return profiles over
the displayed gap ranges.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:confined-bridges-inward-free-or-returning} to each ordinary
bridge term in
Corollary~\ref{cor:ordinary-bridge-truncation-in-finite-chain-amplification}.
Since every displayed gap satisfies \(g\ge2\), the return-profile parameter is
\(2K_r(g-1)\).  This gives the displayed inequality.

For fixed \(n\), the number of displayed gaps at each stage is at most
\(W_{\beta,p}\), by
Corollary~\ref{cor:ordinary-bridge-truncation-in-finite-chain-amplification}.
Thus the total number of nonterminal summands is \(O_n(W_{\beta,p})\), and
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H} W_{\beta,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)).
\]
Uniform logarithmic exponent bounds over the displayed ranges therefore imply
the same bound for their finite union.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite chain amplification with chain-only bridge residuals]
\label{cor:finite-chain-amplification-with-chain-only-bridge-residuals}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-chain-amplification-with-inward-free-bridges}, for
all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{a\in I_n(\ell)}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\substack{2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2\\
        g< W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_r,L,g+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\substack{2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2\\
        g< W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H}}
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_r(g-1)}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  n\,W_{\beta,p}^2\,
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, for fixed \(n\), the bridge residuals in finite chain
amplification can be replaced by locally short chain profiles of lengths
\(g+1\), spread-return profiles, and the long-run profile, over the displayed
slab-truncated gap ranges.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:inward-free-bridges-are-chains-or-long-runs} to each
inward-free bridge term in
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-chain-amplification-with-inward-free-bridges}, with
\((K,h)=(2K_r,g)\).  This replaces that bridge term by a chain profile of
length \(g+1\) and a term
\[
  W_{\beta,p}\,
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p).
\]
At each stage \(r\), the gap range contains at most \(W_{\beta,p}\) integers
by Corollary~\ref{cor:ordinary-bridge-truncation-in-finite-chain-amplification}.
Summing the long-run contributions over \(1\le r\le n\) and all displayed
gaps gives the coefficient \(nW_{\beta,p}^2\).  The remaining terms are
exactly those displayed.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Long chains do not fit in one slab]
\label{lem:long-chains-do-not-fit-in-one-slab}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\).  If
\[
  \ell>W_{\beta,p},
\]
then
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
is false for every rooted path \((x,\gamma)\).  Consequently,
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)=0 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The slab
\[
  A_{j,p}=[jW_{\beta,p},(j+1)W_{\beta,p})
\]
contains at most \(W_{\beta,p}\) integer levels.  A locally short
staircase-chain witness of length \(\ell\) starting at \(u\) requires the
\(\ell\) distinct integer levels
\[
  u,u+1,\ldots,u+\ell-1
\]
all to belong to \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\).  This is impossible when
\(\ell>W_{\beta,p}\).  Hence the defining property is empty, and the
corresponding property-restricted profile is zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Long chains do not have enough slab starts]
\label{lem:long-chains-do-not-have-enough-slab-starts}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\).  If
\[
  W_{\beta,p}-\ell+1\le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
then
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
is false for every rooted path \((x,\gamma)\).  Consequently,
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)=0 .
\]
In particular, the profile is zero whenever \(\ell>W_{\beta,p}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A chain witness of length \(\ell\) starting at \(u\) requires all levels
\[
  u,u+1,\ldots,u+\ell-1
\]
to belong to \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\).  Since this slab contains at most
\(W_{\beta,p}\) integer levels, there are at most
\[
  \max\{W_{\beta,p}-\ell+1,0\}
\]
possible starts.  Under the displayed assumption this number is at most
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\), while the chain property requires
strictly more than that many counted starts.  Hence the defining property is
empty.  The final assertion is the special case in which the maximum is zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Start-count truncation of bridge-free finite chains]
\label{cor:start-count-truncation-bridge-free-finite-chains}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-chain-amplification-with-chain-only-bridge-residuals},
for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{\substack{a\in I_n(\ell)\\
        a< W_{\beta,p}+1-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_n}L_H}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_n,L,a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\substack{2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2\\
        g< W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_r,L,g+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{r=1}^n
  \sum_{\substack{2\le g\le B_r-\ell-r+2\\
        g< W_{\beta,p}-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_r}L_H}}
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_r(g-1)}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  n\,W_{\beta,p}^2\,
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, terminal chain lengths in the top
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K_n)\) portion of the slab do not
contribute to the bridge-free finite chain reduction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-chain-amplification-with-chain-only-bridge-residuals}.
For any terminal length \(a\in I_n(\ell)\) satisfying
\[
  a\ge W_{\beta,p}+1-
          \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_n}L_H,
\]
we have
\[
  W_{\beta,p}-a+1
  \le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_n}L_H .
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:long-chains-do-not-have-enough-slab-starts} therefore makes
the corresponding terminal chain profile zero.  Removing these zero terminal
terms gives the displayed inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The remaining iteration obstruction]
\label{rem:remaining-chain-iteration-obstruction}
Lemma~\ref{lem:long-chains-do-not-fit-in-one-slab} shows that terminal chain
profiles disappear once the amplified chain length exceeds the slab width.
Since \(W_{\beta,p}\asymp L_H\), reaching this deterministic cutoff through
the lower growth bound \(a\ge\ell+n\) requires an iteration depth of order
\(L_H\), not a fixed depth.  Thus the remaining obstruction is no longer a
local gluing issue: it is to control the accumulated bridge families under a
depth that grows with \(p\uparrow\pc(H)\), or to replace the linear-depth
iteration by a sharper amplification.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Counting range of the successor-gap step]
\label{lem:counting-range-successor-gap-step}
In the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chains-have-bounded-successor-gaps}, the
successor-gap conclusion follows from the counted-start lower bound only in
the range
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H>1 .
\]
More precisely, if
\[
  N_\star>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
\]
chain-start levels lie in one slab and
\[
  B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1,
\]
then the argument proves that more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
\]
successor pairs have gap at most \(B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\), provided
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(16K)>1\).  If instead
\[
  K\ge \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}4L_H,
\]
then the lower bound
\[
  N_\star>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H
\]
is compatible with \(N_\star=1\), and no successor-pair conclusion can be
deduced from this counting input alone.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(B=B_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K}\).  Since all counted starts lie in one
slab,
\[
  \sum_{q=1}^{N_\star-1}(u_{q+1}-u_q)\le W_{\beta,p}.
\]
For \(p\) close enough to \(\pc(H)\), \(W_{\beta,p}\le\beta L_H\), so the
number of successor gaps larger than \(B\) is at most
\[
  \frac{\beta}{B}L_H
  <
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H .
\]
Thus the number of successor gaps at most \(B\) is greater than
\[
  N_\star-1-\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H .
\]
Set
\[
  a=\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H .
\]
The hypothesis \(N_\star>4a\), together with \(a>1\), gives
\[
  N_\star-1-a>2a
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H .
\]
This is the claimed successor-pair lower bound.  The final assertion is just
the observation that, when \(K\ge\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/4\), the
defining lower bound on \(N_\star\) is at most \(1\).  A single counted start
has no successor pair, so the count alone cannot force a bounded-gap
successor.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Residual-width successor-gap count for chains]
\label{lem:residual-width-successor-gap-count-for-chains}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K,L\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge2\).  Put
\[
  R_{\ell,p}=\max\{W_{\beta,p}-\ell+1,0\}
\]
and
\[
  B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K R_{\ell,p}}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H}
  \right\rceil+1 .
\]
If
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H>1,
\]
then
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,short}_{j,K,L,\ell,p}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}_{
    j,2K,L,\ell,B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p},p}.
\]
Consequently, for such \(p\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L,\ell,
    B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Suppose that the chain property holds, and list the counted chain starts as
\[
  u_1<\cdots<u_{N_\star}.
\]
For every counted start \(u_q\), the whole interval
\[
  u_q,u_q+1,\ldots,u_q+\ell-1
\]
lies in \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\).  Hence the starts lie in an interval of
integer length at most \(R_{\ell,p}\), and therefore
\[
  \sum_{q=1}^{N_\star-1}(u_{q+1}-u_q)\le R_{\ell,p}.
\]
The number of successor gaps larger than \(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\) is at
most
\[
  \frac{R_{\ell,p}}{B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}}
  <
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H .
\]
Since the chain property gives
\[
  N_\star>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H,
\]
the same calculation as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:counting-range-successor-gap-step} shows that more than
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4(2K)}L_H
\]
successor pairs have gap at most \(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\).  Each such
successor pair gives the bounded-gap staircase-chain-pair property with
parameter \(2K\); endpoint-clearance conditions are inherited because the
depth requirement is weakened.  This proves the property inclusion, and the
profile inequality follows by the property-restricted union bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-top chains have bounded residual successor cutoffs]
\label{cor:near-top-chains-have-bounded-residual-successor-cutoffs}
In the setting of
Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-width-successor-gap-count-for-chains}, fix \(C>0\)
and put
\[
  B_C=
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16C}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1 .
\]
If
\[
  R_{\ell,p}\le \frac{C}{K}L_H
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H>1,
\]
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K,L,\ell,B_C}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,pair,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The residual bound gives
\[
  B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\le B_C .
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-width-successor-gap-count-for-chains} and then
use monotonicity of the bounded-gap chain-pair property in the gap cutoff.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Residual-width one-step amplification]
\label{cor:residual-width-one-step-staircase-chain-amplification}
In the setting of
Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-width-successor-gap-count-for-chains}, put
\[
  K^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}=2K B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}.
\]
If
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H>1,
\]
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\min\{\ell,B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p},L,\ell+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{h=\ell+1}^{B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p},L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second sum is absent if \(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\le\ell\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-width-successor-gap-count-for-chains} to obtain
a bounded-gap chain-pair profile with parameter \(2K\) and cutoff
\(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\).  Corollary~\ref{cor:bounded-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-have-fixed-gap}
then replaces this profile by fixed-gap chain-pair profiles with parameter
\[
  (2K)B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}=K^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}.
\]
Finally apply Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-split}: gaps
\(1\le h\le\ell\) glue into chains of length \(\ell+h\), and gaps
\(h\ge\ell+1\) become confined chain bridges.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-top one-step amplification has bounded cost]
\label{cor:near-top-one-step-amplification-has-bounded-cost}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-top-chains-have-bounded-residual-successor-cutoffs},
put
\[
  K_C=2K B_C .
\]
If
\[
  R_{\ell,p}\le \frac{C}{K}L_H
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K}L_H>1,
\]
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\min\{\ell,B_C\}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_C,L,\ell+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{h=\ell+1}^{B_C}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_C,L,\ell,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second sum is absent if \(B_C\le\ell\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-top-chains-have-bounded-residual-successor-cutoffs}
to get a bounded-gap chain-pair profile with parameter \(2K\) and cutoff
\(B_C\).  The fixed-gap pigeonhole and split steps are exactly those used in
the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:residual-width-one-step-staircase-chain-amplification},
with \(B_C\) in place of \(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bridge-free residual descent near the slab top]
\label{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:residual-width-one-step-staircase-chain-amplification},
suppose that
\[
  B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\le \ell .
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p},L,\ell+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, every displayed chain term has residual width
\[
  R_{\ell+h,p}=\max\{R_{\ell,p}-h,0\}\le \max\{R_{\ell,p}-1,0\}.
\]
The hypothesis \(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\le\ell\) is implied by
\[
  R_{\ell,p}\le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}(\ell-1)}{16K}L_H .
\]
In particular, if
\[
  R_{\ell,p}\le \frac{C}{K}L_H,\qquad
  C\le \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}(\ell-1)}{16},
\]
then the near-top one-step amplification of
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-top-one-step-amplification-has-bounded-cost} has no
confined chain-bridge residuals.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Under \(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\le\ell\), the bridge sum in
Corollary~\ref{cor:residual-width-one-step-staircase-chain-amplification} is
absent.  This gives the displayed inequality.  The residual identity follows
directly from the definition:
\[
  R_{\ell+h,p}
  =
  \max\{W_{\beta,p}-(\ell+h)+1,0\}
  =
  \max\{R_{\ell,p}-h,0\}.
\]
If
\[
  R_{\ell,p}\le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}(\ell-1)}{16K}L_H,
\]
then
\[
  \frac{16KR_{\ell,p}}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H}\le\ell-1,
\]
so \(B^{\rm res}_{K,\ell,p}\le\ell\).  The final assertion is the same
criterion after using the bound \(R_{\ell,p}\le C L_H/K\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite bridge-free residual descent iteration]
\label{cor:finite-bridge-free-residual-descent-iteration}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top}, fix
\(m\ge0\).  Let \(\mathcal H_0=\{\varnothing\}\), and set
\[
  \ell(\varnothing)=\ell,\qquad K(\varnothing)=K .
\]
For each word \(\mathbf h\in\mathcal H_r\), put
\[
  B(\mathbf h)=
  B^{\rm res}_{K(\mathbf h),\ell(\mathbf h),p}.
\]
Assume that, for every \(0\le r<m\) and every
\(\mathbf h\in\mathcal H_r\),
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K(\mathbf h)}L_H>1,
  \qquad
  B(\mathbf h)\le \ell(\mathbf h).
\]
Define \(\mathcal H_{r+1}\) to consist of all words
\(\mathbf h\frown h\), where \(\mathbf h\in\mathcal H_r\) and
\[
  1\le h\le B(\mathbf h),
\]
and set
\[
  \ell(\mathbf h\frown h)=\ell(\mathbf h)+h,\qquad
  K(\mathbf h\frown h)=2K(\mathbf h)B(\mathbf h).
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{\mathbf h\in\mathcal H_m}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K(\mathbf h),L,\ell(\mathbf h)}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, every terminal word \(\mathbf h\in\mathcal H_m\) satisfies
\[
  R_{\ell(\mathbf h),p}\le \max\{R_{\ell,p}-m,0\}.
\]
Consequently, if the displayed hypotheses hold through some
\(m\ge R_{\ell,p}\), then
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)=0 .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The case \(m=0\) is the identity inequality.  Suppose the inequality has
been proved at depth \(r<m\).  For each terminal word
\(\mathbf h\in\mathcal H_r\), the hypotheses allow
Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top} to be applied
with \((K,\ell)\) replaced by \((K(\mathbf h),\ell(\mathbf h))\).  This
replaces the terminal chain profile by the sum over children
\(\mathbf h\frown h\), \(1\le h\le B(\mathbf h)\), with the displayed
recursive parameters.  Substituting these finitely many inequalities gives
the depth \(r+1\) statement, and induction proves the displayed bound.

At each child step, Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top}
gives
\[
  R_{\ell(\mathbf h\frown h),p}
  =
  \max\{R_{\ell(\mathbf h),p}-h,0\}
  \le
  \max\{R_{\ell(\mathbf h),p}-1,0\}.
\]
Iterating this estimate along a word of length \(m\) gives the residual
bound.  If \(m\ge R_{\ell,p}\), then every terminal word has
\[
  R_{\ell(\mathbf h),p}=0,
\]
so
\[
  W_{\beta,p}-\ell(\mathbf h)+1\le0
  \le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K(\mathbf h)}L_H .
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:long-chains-do-not-have-enough-slab-starts} makes every
terminal profile in the displayed sum equal to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Bridge-free residual exhaustion has logarithmic depth obstruction]
\label{lem:bridge-free-residual-exhaustion-logarithmic-obstruction}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-bridge-free-residual-descent-iteration}, suppose
that \(R_{\ell,p}\ge1\) and that the hypotheses of that corollary hold
through some depth \(m\ge R_{\ell,p}\).  Then
\[
  4^{R_{\ell,p}-1}K
  <
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Equivalently,
\[
  R_{\ell,p}
  <
  1+
  \log_4\!\left(
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H}{16K}
  \right).
\]
Thus, under the current bridge-free descent recursion, residual exhaustion
from a fixed \(K\) can only be certified in this way when the initial
residual start width is \(O(\log L_H)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\mathbf 1_r\) denote the word of length \(r\) all of whose letters are
equal to \(1\).  Since \(1\le B(\mathbf h)\) for every node, the words
\(\mathbf 1_r\) belong to \(\mathcal H_r\) for all \(r\le R_{\ell,p}-1\).
Along this branch,
\[
  \ell(\mathbf 1_r)=\ell+r,
\]
and therefore
\[
  R_{\ell(\mathbf 1_r),p}
  =
  \max\{R_{\ell,p}-r,0\}
  =
  R_{\ell,p}-r
  \qquad(0\le r\le R_{\ell,p}-1).
\]
In particular, for \(0\le r\le R_{\ell,p}-2\), the residual width is
positive, so
\[
  B(\mathbf 1_r)
  =
  B^{\rm res}_{K(\mathbf 1_r),\ell(\mathbf 1_r),p}\ge2 .
\]
The recursive definition then gives
\[
  K(\mathbf 1_{r+1})
  =
  2K(\mathbf 1_r)B(\mathbf 1_r)
  \ge
  4K(\mathbf 1_r)
  \qquad(0\le r\le R_{\ell,p}-2),
\]
and hence
\[
  K(\mathbf 1_{R_{\ell,p}-1})\ge 4^{R_{\ell,p}-1}K .
\]
Because \(m\ge R_{\ell,p}\), the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-bridge-free-residual-descent-iteration} include the
counting-range condition at the node \(\mathbf 1_{R_{\ell,p}-1}\):
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16K(\mathbf 1_{R_{\ell,p}-1})}L_H>1.
\]
Combining the last two displays gives the claimed inequality.  The logarithmic
form is just its base-\(4\) logarithm.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Wide residual entry forces a first descent obstruction]
\label{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-bridge-free-residual-descent-iteration}, put
\(R=R_{\ell,p}\).  Suppose that \(R\ge1\) and
\[
  4^{R-1}K
  \ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Define the unit-branch parameters by
\[
  \ell_r=\ell+r,\qquad K_0=K,\qquad
  B_r=B^{\rm res}_{K_r,\ell_r,p}\qquad(0\le r\le R-1),
\]
and
\[
  K_{r+1}=2K_rB_r\qquad(0\le r\le R-1).
\]
Then there is a least \(r_*\in\{0,\ldots,R-1\}\) for which either
\[
  K_{r_*}\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H
  \qquad\text{or}\qquad
  B_{r_*}>\ell_{r_*}.
\]
For every \(r<r_*\), one has
\[
  K_r<
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H,
  \qquad
  B_r\le \ell_r,
\]
so the bridge-free residual one-step descent is valid at the corresponding
unit-branch node.  If
\[
  K_{r_*}<
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H,
\]
then \(B_{r_*}>\ell_{r_*}\), and the residual-width one-step amplification at
\((K_{r_*},\ell_{r_*})\) contains the non-empty confined chain-bridge sum
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*},L,\ell_{r_*}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\ell_{r_*}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*+1},L,\ell_{r_*}+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{h=\ell_{r_*}+1}^{B_{r_*}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*+1},L,\ell_{r_*},h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus a residual entry wider than the logarithmic threshold forces, along the
unit descent branch, either saturation of the counted-start range or the
appearance of a genuine chain-bridge packet before residual exhaustion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For \(0\le r\le R-1\),
\[
  R_{\ell_r,p}=\max\{W_{\beta,p}-(\ell+r)+1,0\}=R-r .
\]
In particular \(R_{\ell_r,p}>0\) for \(0\le r\le R-1\).  Hence
\[
  B_r=
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K_rR_{\ell_r,p}}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H}
  \right\rceil+1
  \ge2
  \qquad(0\le r\le R-1).
\]
It follows that
\[
  K_{r+1}=2K_rB_r\ge4K_r
  \qquad(0\le r\le R-1),
\]
and in particular
\[
  K_{R-1}\ge 4^{R-1}K
  \ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Therefore the displayed set of failing indices is non-empty, so the least
\(r_*\) exists.  Its minimality gives the two inequalities for every
\(r<r_*\).  Those inequalities are exactly the counting-range and
bridge-free hypotheses needed to apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top} at the
corresponding unit-branch node.

If
\[
  K_{r_*}<
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H,
\]
then the first alternative in the definition of \(r_*\) fails, so
\(B_{r_*}>\ell_{r_*}\).  The counting-range hypothesis still holds at
\((K_{r_*},\ell_{r_*})\), and
Corollary~\ref{cor:residual-width-one-step-staircase-chain-amplification}
applies.  Since \(B_{r_*}>\ell_{r_*}\), its bridge sum is non-empty, and
\[
  K^{\rm res}_{K_{r_*},\ell_{r_*},p}
  =
  2K_{r_*}B_{r_*}
  =
  K_{r_*+1}.
\]
Substituting these parameters gives the displayed inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[First bridge-active obstruction projects to ordinary bridges]
\label{cor:first-bridge-active-obstruction-projects-to-ordinary-bridges}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction},
suppose that the first obstruction is bridge-active rather than
counting-saturating, that is,
\[
  K_{r_*}<
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Then \(B_{r_*}>\ell_{r_*}\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*},L,\ell_{r_*}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\ell_{r_*}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*+1},L,\ell_{r_*}+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{g=2}^{B_{r_*}-\ell_{r_*}+1}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*+1},L,g}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, the bridge-active alternative implies the quantitative lower bound
\[
  R_{\ell_{r_*},p}>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}(\ell_{r_*}-1)}{16K_{r_*}}L_H .
\]
Thus any first obstruction of this type is an ordinary confined-bridge
packet occurring while the current residual width is still too large for the
bridge-free range.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The hypothesis rules out the counting-saturation alternative in
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction}, so
\(B_{r_*}>\ell_{r_*}\).  The same corollary gives the residual-width
one-step bound at \((K_{r_*},\ell_{r_*})\) with a non-empty chain-bridge sum.
For each \(h\in\{\ell_{r_*}+1,\ldots,B_{r_*}\}\),
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridges-project-to-ordinary-bridges}
gives
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*+1},L,\ell_{r_*},h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*+1},L,h-\ell_{r_*}+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Reindexing the bridge gaps by \(g=h-\ell_{r_*}+1\) gives the displayed
ordinary-bridge sum.

Finally,
\[
  B_{r_*}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K_{r_*}R_{\ell_{r_*},p}}
         {\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H}
  \right\rceil+1
  >
  \ell_{r_*}.
\]
Hence the ceiling is at least \(\ell_{r_*}\), which forces
\[
  \frac{16K_{r_*}R_{\ell_{r_*},p}}
       {\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H}
  >
  \ell_{r_*}-1.
\]
This is the claimed lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[First counting saturation has a last large bridge-free step]
\label{cor:first-counting-saturation-has-last-large-bridge-free-step}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction}, put
\[
  T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Suppose that the first obstruction index \(r_*\) is counting-saturating, in
the sense that
\[
  K_{r_*}\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}.
\]
If \(r_*=0\), then the initial chain profile is already outside the
successor-counting range.  If \(r_*\ge1\), put \(r_0=r_*-1\).  Then
\[
  K_{r_0}<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},\qquad
  B_{r_0}\le\ell_{r_0},
\]
and the predecessor step is bridge-free:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_0},L,\ell_{r_0}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_{r_0}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r_*},L,\ell_{r_0}+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover,
\[
  B_{r_0}
  \ge
  \frac{T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}}{2K_{r_0}}
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_{r_0}}L_H ,
\]
and every displayed child with increment \(h\) has residual width
\[
  R_{\ell_{r_0}+h,p}=\max\{R_{\ell_{r_0},p}-h,0\}.
\]
In particular the largest-increment child satisfies
\[
  R_{\ell_{r_0}+B_{r_0},p}
  \le
  \max\left\{
    R_{\ell_{r_0},p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_{r_0}}L_H,
    0
  \right\}.
\]
Thus a non-initial counting-saturation obstruction is preceded by a
bridge-free one-step packet with an \(L_H/K_{r_0}\)-scale successor window.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If \(r_*=0\), the displayed counting-saturation hypothesis says exactly that
the initial parameter \(K\) is not in the successor-counting range.

Assume \(r_*\ge1\), and set \(r_0=r_*-1\).  By minimality of \(r_*\) in
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction},
the two obstruction alternatives both fail at \(r_0\), so
\[
  K_{r_0}<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},
  \qquad
  B_{r_0}\le \ell_{r_0}.
\]
These are precisely the counting-range and bridge-free hypotheses for
Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top} at
\((K_{r_0},\ell_{r_0})\).  Applying that corollary gives the displayed
bridge-free inequality, and the recursive definition gives
\[
  K_{r_*}=K_{r_0+1}=2K_{r_0}B_{r_0}.
\]
Combining this identity with \(K_{r_*}\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}\)
proves
\[
  B_{r_0}\ge\frac{T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}}{2K_{r_0}}
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_{r_0}}L_H .
\]
The residual identity for the children is the residual identity in
Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top}.  Taking
\(h=B_{r_0}\) and using the lower bound on \(B_{r_0}\) gives the final
display.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Wide residual first-obstruction normal form]
\label{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction}, put
\[
  T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}
  =
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Assume \(R=R_{\ell,p}\ge1\) and
\[
  4^{R-1}K\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}.
\]
Then at least one of the following three alternatives holds.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Initial saturation:
\[
  K\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}.
\]

\item Ordinary bridge packet: there is \(r\in\{0,\ldots,R-1\}\) such that
\[
  K_r<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},\qquad B_r>\ell_r,
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\ell_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{g=2}^{B_r-\ell_r+1}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,g}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover
\[
  R_{\ell_r,p}>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}(\ell_r-1)}{16K_r}L_H .
\]

\item Last valid large-window step: there is an \(r\) with
\(0\le r\le R-2\) such
that
\[
  K_r<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},\qquad
  B_r\le\ell_r,\qquad
  K_{r+1}\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p),
\end{aligned}
\]
with
\[
  B_r\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_r}L_H .
\]
Consequently, the largest-increment child in this packet has residual width
at most
\[
  \max\left\{
    R_{\ell_r,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_r}L_H,
    0
  \right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

Thus every wide residual entry is reduced to initial loss of the counting
range, an ordinary confined-bridge packet, or the last bridge-free step
before the counting range is lost.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(r_*\) be the least obstruction index given by
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction}.
If \(K\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}\), then alternative (i) holds.  Assume
therefore that \(K<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}\).

If \(K_{r_*}<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}\), then the first obstruction is
bridge-active.  Alternative (ii), with \(r=r_*\), is exactly
Corollary~\ref{cor:first-bridge-active-obstruction-projects-to-ordinary-bridges}.

It remains to consider \(K_{r_*}\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}\).  Since
\(K_0=K<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}\), this forces \(r_*\ge1\).  Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:first-counting-saturation-has-last-large-bridge-free-step}
and setting \(r=r_*-1\) gives alternative (iii).  Since
\(r_*\le R-1\), this index satisfies \(r\le R-2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bridge-packet branch has truncated return form]
\label{cor:bridge-packet-branch-has-truncated-return-form}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}, suppose that
the ordinary bridge packet alternative holds at some index \(r\).  Define
\[
  \mathcal G_r
  =
  \left\{
    g\in\mathbb N:
    2\le g\le B_r-\ell_r+1,\quad
    g<
    W_{\beta,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H
  \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{\ell_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{g\in\mathcal G_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_{r+1},L,g}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,free,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{g\in\mathcal G_r}
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_{r+1}(g-1)}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the bridge-packet branch contains only ordinary bridge gaps
strictly below the slab-start cutoff, and those remaining gaps are reduced to
inward-free bridge profiles and spread-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The ordinary bridge packet alternative in
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form} gives the
same display with the ordinary bridge sum over
\[
  2\le g\le B_r-\ell_r+1 .
\]
If
\[
  g\ge
  W_{\beta,p}
  -
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H,
\]
then Lemma~\ref{lem:large-fixed-gaps-do-not-have-enough-slab-starts}, with
\(K=K_{r+1}\), makes the corresponding ordinary bridge profile equal to
zero.  Hence only \(g\in\mathcal G_r\) remain.

For every \(g\in\mathcal G_r\), apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:confined-bridges-inward-free-or-returning} with
\((K,h)=(K_{r+1},g)\).  Since \(g\ge2\), the spread-return parameter is
\(2K_{r+1}(g-1)\).  Substituting these inequalities into the truncated
ordinary bridge sum gives the displayed bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Large-window branch has subexponential child cost]
\label{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}, suppose that
the last valid large-window step alternative holds at some index \(r\).  Then
\[
  B_r\le \ell_r<W_{\beta,p},
\]
and hence the bridge-free child sum in that alternative contains at most
\(W_{\beta,p}\) terms.  Moreover,
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H} W_{\beta,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\]
follows from the same uniform exponent hypothesis on the child profiles
\[
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p),
  \qquad 1\le h\le B_r .
\]
The largest child in this subexponential family has residual width at most
\[
  \max\left\{
    R_{\ell_r,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_r}L_H,
    0
  \right\}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The large-window alternative gives \(0\le r\le R-2\) and \(B_r\le\ell_r\).
Since \(R=R_{\ell,p}\ge1\), we have
\[
  R=W_{\beta,p}-\ell+1 .
\]
Therefore
\[
  \ell_r=\ell+r\le \ell+R-2=W_{\beta,p}-1,
\]
and hence \(B_r\le\ell_r<W_{\beta,p}\).  The bridge-free sum in
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form} therefore has
at most \(W_{\beta,p}\) summands.

Since \(W_{\beta,p}=\max\{1,\lfloor\beta L_H\rfloor\}\), we have
\[
  \log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)).
\]
Thus multiplying a uniform logarithmic exponent bound by the displayed
number of child summands does not change the exponent.  This proves the
stated exponent implication.  The residual-width bound for the largest child
is the corresponding conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Few-start chain profiles]
\label{def:few-start-locally-short-staircase-chain-profiles}
In the setting of
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles}, fix
\(K,L\ge1\), \(\ell\ge2\), and \(q\ge1\).  Let
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}_{
    j,K,L,\ell,q,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
be the property obtained from
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles} by
replacing the final lower bound on the number of admissible chain starts by
the requirement that there are at least \(q\) such starts.  Equivalently,
there are at least \(q\) distinct
\(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) for which the length-\(\ell\) locally short
outward staircase-chain witnesses and the endpoint-clearance inequalities
with parameter \(K\) all hold.
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,q}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{n\ge0,\ |2n-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}_{
        j,K,L,\ell,q,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exact-start chain profiles]
\label{def:exact-start-locally-short-staircase-chain-profiles}
In the setting of
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles}, fix
\(K,L\ge1\), \(\ell\ge2\), and \(u\in\mathbb N\).  Let
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}_{
    j,K,L,\ell,u,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
be the property that \(u\) is an admissible chain start in
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles}: namely,
\(u+r\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) for every \(0\le r<\ell\), and there are
level-\(u+r\) \((-1,+1)\)-crossing runs \([a_r,b_r]\),
\(0\le r<\ell\), satisfying all consecutive-run, record, persistence,
shortness, and endpoint-clearance conditions in that definition.
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}
  \sup\Biggl\{
    \sum_{\substack{n\ge0,\ |2n-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{n,d}^{G,
      \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}_{
        j,K,L,\ell,u,p}}
\\
  &\hspace{5em}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \Biggr\},
\end{aligned}
\]
with value \(0\) if \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Few-start chains localize to exact starts]
\label{cor:few-start-chains-localize-to-exact-starts}
In the setting of
Definition~\ref{def:few-start-locally-short-staircase-chain-profiles}, for
every \(q\ge1\), put
\[
  R_{\ell,p}=\max\{W_{\beta,p}-\ell+1,0\}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,q}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  R_{\ell,p}\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the few-start chain profile follows
from the same exponent hypothesis on the exact-start chain profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If the few-start property holds, at least one admissible chain start
\(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) exists.  Hence
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}_{
    j,K,L,\ell,q,p}
  \subseteq
  \bigcup_{\substack{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\\
    u,u+1,\ldots,u+\ell-1\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}}
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}_{
    j,K,L,\ell,u,p}.
\]
The displayed union has at most \(R_{\ell,p}\) possible starts, since a
length-\(\ell\) chain must fit entirely inside a slab of integer width
\(W_{\beta,p}\).
Taking the property-restricted union bound in the weighted sums and then the
supremum in \(m\) gives the displayed inequality.  The exponent conclusion
follows
from
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)).
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Large-window children reduce to few-start chains]
\label{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}, suppose that
the last valid large-window step alternative holds at some index \(r\).  Put
\[
  q_{r,p}
  =
  \left\lfloor
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H
  \right\rfloor+1 .
\]
Then \(1\le q_{r,p}\le5\), and for every \(1\le h\le B_r\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h,q_{r,p}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{q=1}^{5}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h,q}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_r}
  \sum_{q=1}^{5}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h,q}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
The number of displayed summands is at most \(5W_{\beta,p}\).  Hence the
exponent hypothesis on the parent chain profile follows from a uniform
exponent hypothesis on these few-start child profiles.  The largest
increment \(h=B_r\) still has residual width at most
\[
  \max\left\{
    R_{\ell_r,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_r}L_H,
    0
  \right\}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The large-window alternative gives
\[
  K_{r+1}\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Therefore
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H\le4,
\]
and so \(1\le q_{r,p}\le5\).

For a fixed \(h\), the ordinary chain property with parameter \(K_{r+1}\)
requires the number of admissible chain starts to be strictly larger than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K_{r+1})\).  Since this number is an
integer, it is at least \(q_{r,p}\).  This is exactly the few-start property
with \(q=q_{r,p}\), giving the first displayed inequality.  The second
follows because \(q_{r,p}\in\{1,\ldots,5\}\).

Substituting these child bounds into the large-window inequality in
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form} gives the
parent inequality.  By
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost},
\(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\), so the total number of summands is at most
\(5W_{\beta,p}\), and
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}(5W_{\beta,p})}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)).
\]
Thus uniform few-start child exponent bounds pass to the parent.  The
residual-width bound for \(h=B_r\) is again the corresponding conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Large-window branch localizes to exact starts]
\label{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}, suppose that
the last valid large-window step alternative holds at some index \(r\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_r}
  5R_{\ell_r+h,p}\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here
\[
  R_{\ell_r+h,p}=\max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-h,0\}.
\]
Since \(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\), the total residual start cost is at most
\[
  5\sum_{h=1}^{B_r}R_{\ell_r+h,p}
  \le 5W_{\beta,p}^2,
\]
and hence its logarithm is \(o(L_H)\).
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the parent chain profile follows
from a uniform exponent hypothesis on the exact-start child profiles in the
displayed sum.  The child with \(h=B_r\) retains the residual-width bound
\[
  R_{\ell_r+B_r,p}
  \le
  \max\left\{
    R_{\ell_r,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_r}L_H,
    0
  \right\}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains}, and
then apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:few-start-chains-localize-to-exact-starts} to each
few-start child profile.  This gives the displayed inequality.  The bound
\[
  R_{\ell_r+h,p}=\max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-h,0\}
\]
is the residual identity for child length \(\ell_r+h\).  The bound
\(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\) is
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost}, and
also \(R_{\ell_r+h,p}\le W_{\beta,p}\).  Therefore the total residual start
cost is bounded by \(5W_{\beta,p}^2\).  Because
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}(5W_{\beta,p}^2)}{L_H}\to0,
\]
uniform exponent bounds over those exact-start children pass to the parent.
The residual-width statement is the largest-child conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Large-window exact-start branch has a low-residual tail]
\label{cor:large-window-exact-start-branch-has-low-residual-tail}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}, put
\[
  t_r=\left\lceil\frac{B_r}{2}\right\rceil .
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  5\sum_{h=1}^{t_r-1}
  R_{\ell_r+h,p}\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  5\max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-t_r,0\}
  \sum_{h=t_r}^{B_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p),
\end{aligned}
\]
