where the first sum is interpreted as zero when \(t_r=1\).  Every exact-start
child in the second sum has residual width at most
\[
  \max\left\{
    R_{\ell_r,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{64K_r}L_H,
    0
  \right\}.
\]
The total expanded union cost in the two sums is still at most
\(5W_{\beta,p}^2\), and hence is subexponential on the \(L_H\) scale.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Start from
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}.  Split its
sum over \(1\le h\le B_r\) into \(h<t_r\) and \(h\ge t_r\).  For the tail,
the residual identity gives
\[
  R_{\ell_r+h,p}
  =
  \max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-h,0\}
  \le
  \max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-t_r,0\}.
\]
Substituting this uniform tail bound gives the displayed inequality.

Since \(t_r\ge B_r/2\), the large-window lower bound
\[
  B_r\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_r}L_H
\]
from Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form} implies
\[
  t_r\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{64K_r}L_H .
\]
This proves the residual-width bound for every tail child.  Finally,
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost} gives
\(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\), and every displayed residual factor is at most
\(W_{\beta,p}\).  Thus the total expanded union cost is bounded by
\(5W_{\beta,p}^2\), whose logarithm is \(o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic residual layers for the exact-start branch]
\label{cor:dyadic-residual-layers-exact-start-branch}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}, put
\[
  M_r=\max\{1,\lceil\log_2 B_r\rceil\},\qquad
  s_{r,0}=B_r+1,\qquad
  s_{r,m}=\left\lceil\frac{B_r}{2^m}\right\rceil
  \quad(1\le m\le M_r).
\]
Then \(s_{r,M_r}=1\), and the intervals
\[
  I_{r,m}=\{s_{r,m},s_{r,m}+1,\ldots,s_{r,m-1}-1\},
  \qquad 1\le m\le M_r,
\]
partition \(\{1,\ldots,B_r\}\).  Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  5\sum_{m=1}^{M_r}
  \max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-s_{r,m},0\}
  \sum_{h\in I_{r,m}}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every exact-start child in the \(m\)-th layer has residual width at most
\[
  \max\left\{
    R_{\ell_r,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2^{m+5}K_r}L_H,
    0
  \right\}.
\]
The total expanded union cost over all dyadic layers is at most
\(5W_{\beta,p}^2\), and hence is subexponential on the \(L_H\) scale.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Since \(M_r\ge\lceil\log_2B_r\rceil\), we have
\[
  0<\frac{B_r}{2^{M_r}}\le1,
\]
and hence \(s_{r,M_r}=1\).  The displayed intervals are consecutive and
therefore partition \(\{1,\ldots,B_r\}\).

Start from
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}.  For
\(h\in I_{r,m}\), the residual identity gives
\[
  R_{\ell_r+h,p}
  =
  \max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-h,0\}
  \le
  \max\{R_{\ell_r,p}-s_{r,m},0\}.
\]
Replacing each residual factor by this layerwise upper bound gives the
displayed dyadic-layer inequality.

For the residual-width estimate, use \(s_{r,m}\ge B_r/2^m\) and the
large-window lower bound
\[
  B_r\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{32K_r}L_H
\]
from Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}.  Thus
\[
  s_{r,m}\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{2^{m+5}K_r}L_H,
\]
and every child in \(I_{r,m}\) has the stated residual-width bound.

Finally, the dyadic decomposition only repartitions the weighted exact-start
sum from Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}.
Since \(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\) and every residual factor is at most
\(W_{\beta,p}\), the expanded cost is at most \(5W_{\beta,p}^2\), whose
logarithm is \(o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-start chains with enough levels are record spread]
\label{lem:exact-start-chains-with-enough-levels-are-record-spread}
In the setting of
Definition~\ref{def:exact-start-locally-short-staircase-chain-profiles}, if
\[
  \ell>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H ,
\]
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, if
\[
  K\ge \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H ,
\]
then the displayed inequality holds for every \(\ell\ge5\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix an admissible exact start \(u\).  If
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}_{
    j,K,L,\ell,u,p}(x,\gamma)
\]
holds, then for each \(0\le r<\ell\) there is a level-\(u+r\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run satisfying the record, shortness, and
endpoint-clearance conditions from
Definition~\ref{def:short-prefix-record-outward-spread-profiles}.  The
levels \(u,u+1,\ldots,u+\ell-1\) are distinct and all lie in
\(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\).  Since their number is larger than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\), the property
\(\mathcal P^{\rm pre,rec,short}_{j,K,L,p}(x,\gamma)\) holds.  Thus, for
every \(u\),
\[
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}_{
    j,K,L,\ell,u,p}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal P^{\rm pre,rec,short}_{j,K,L,p}.
\]
Taking the corresponding property-restricted sums and then the suprema gives
the profile inequality.

If \(K\ge\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/16\), then
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H\le4,
\]
so every \(\ell\ge5\) satisfies the first displayed hypothesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Few-start chains with enough levels are record spread]
\label{cor:few-start-chains-with-enough-levels-are-record-spread}
In the setting of
Definition~\ref{def:few-start-locally-short-staircase-chain-profiles}, if
\[
  \ell>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H ,
\]
then, for every \(q\ge1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,q}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The few-start property with any \(q\ge1\) includes at least one admissible
exact start \(u\).  For that start, the exact-start chain property with
length \(\ell\) holds.  Since \(\ell\) is larger than the displayed
threshold, Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-start-chains-with-enough-levels-are-record-spread}
makes the corresponding path a prefix-record outward-spread path.  This
gives the property inclusion and hence the profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Large-window exact starts are record spread except short children]
\label{cor:large-window-exact-starts-are-record-spread-except-short-children}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}, put
\[
  \mathcal S_r=\{h\in\{1,\ldots,B_r\}:\ell_r+h\le4\}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  5\sum_{h\in\mathcal S_r}
  R_{\ell_r+h,p}\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  5\left(\sum_{h=1}^{B_r}R_{\ell_r+h,p}\right)
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal S_r\subseteq\{1,\ldots,4-\ell_r\}\), so
\(|\mathcal S_r|\le2\), and \(\mathcal S_r=\varnothing\) whenever
\(\ell_r\ge4\).  The total coefficient in the second line is at most
\(10W_{\beta,p}\), while the coefficient of the record-spread profile is at
most \(5W_{\beta,p}^2\).  Hence both costs are subexponential on the
\(L_H\) scale.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Start from
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}.  Split the
sum over \(1\le h\le B_r\) according to whether \(h\in\mathcal S_r\).  The
large-window alternative gives
\[
  K_{r+1}\ge\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H ,
\]
as used in
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains}.  For
every \(h\notin\mathcal S_r\), we have \(\ell_r+h\ge5\), and
Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-start-chains-with-enough-levels-are-record-spread}
therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting these bounds gives the displayed inequality.

Since Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles}
has \(\ell_r\ge2\), the set \(\mathcal S_r\) is contained in
\(\{1,\ldots,4-\ell_r\}\) and has at most two elements.  Each residual factor
is at most \(W_{\beta,p}\), so the total short-child coefficient is at most
\(10W_{\beta,p}\).  Also,
\[
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_r}R_{\ell_r+h,p}\le W_{\beta,p}^2
\]
by Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}.  Since
\(\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)\), both displayed costs are subexponential.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Threshold-tight short exact-start exceptions]
\label{cor:threshold-tight-short-exact-start-exceptions}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}, put
\[
  \mathcal E_r
  =
  \left\{
    h\in\{1,\ldots,B_r\}:
    \ell_r+h\le
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H
  \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  5\sum_{h\in\mathcal E_r}
  R_{\ell_r+h,p}\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,exact,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  5\left(\sum_{h=1}^{B_r}R_{\ell_r+h,p}\right)
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal E_r\subseteq\mathcal S_r\), where \(\mathcal S_r\) is
the set from
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-exact-starts-are-record-spread-except-short-children}.
In particular \(|\mathcal E_r|\le2\), and \(\mathcal E_r=\varnothing\) if
\[
  K_{r+1}>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{12}L_H .
\]
If \(h\in\mathcal E_r\) and \(\ell_r+h=4\), then
\[
  K_{r+1}= \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Thus length-four exceptions can occur only at exact saturation, and all
exceptions occur while
\[
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H
  \le K_{r+1}
  \le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{12}L_H .
\]
The exceptional exact-start coefficient is at most \(10W_{\beta,p}\), while
the record-spread coefficient is at most \(5W_{\beta,p}^2\); both are
subexponential on the \(L_H\) scale.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Start from
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}.  If
\(h\notin\mathcal E_r\), then
\[
  \ell_r+h>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H ,
\]
so
Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-start-chains-with-enough-levels-are-record-spread},
with \(K=K_{r+1}\) and \(\ell=\ell_r+h\), bounds the corresponding
exact-start child by the prefix-record outward-spread profile at parameter
\(K_{r+1}\).  Substituting this estimate for all \(h\notin\mathcal E_r\)
gives the displayed inequality.

The large-window branch has
\[
  K_{r+1}\ge
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Hence every \(h\in\mathcal E_r\) satisfies
\[
  \ell_r+h\le4,
\]
so \(\mathcal E_r\subseteq\mathcal S_r\).  The bound
\(|\mathcal E_r|\le2\) follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-exact-starts-are-record-spread-except-short-children}.
Since every child length satisfies \(\ell_r+h\ge3\), the inequality defining
\(\mathcal E_r\) is impossible when
\[
  3>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H ,
\]
which is equivalent to the displayed condition
\(K_{r+1}>\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/12\).

If \(h\in\mathcal E_r\) and \(\ell_r+h=4\), then the defining inequality
gives
\[
  K_{r+1}\le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Together with the large-window lower bound on \(K_{r+1}\), this gives the
claimed equality.  The final interval for possible exceptions follows by
combining the same lower bound with the emptiness criterion.

Finally, every residual coefficient is at most \(W_{\beta,p}\).  Since
\(|\mathcal E_r|\le2\), the exceptional coefficient is at most
\(10W_{\beta,p}\).  The record coefficient is bounded by
\[
  5\sum_{h=1}^{B_r}R_{\ell_r+h,p}\le5W_{\beta,p}^2
\]
as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts}.  The
subexponential statements follow from \(\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Large-window exceptions retain surplus starts]
\label{cor:large-window-exceptions-retain-surplus-starts}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains}, put
\[
  A_r=\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H,
  \qquad
  q_{r,p}=\lfloor A_r\rfloor+1,
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal E_r
  =
  \{h\in\{1,\ldots,B_r\}:\ell_r+h\le A_r\}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h\in\mathcal E_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h,q_{r,p}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  B_r\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, if \(h\in\mathcal E_r\), then
\[
  q_{r,p}>\ell_r+h,
\]
and \(q_{r,p}\in\{4,5\}\).  Thus the only exceptional few-start types are
\[
  (\ell_r+h,q_{r,p})\in\{(3,4),(3,5),(4,5)\}.
\]
The exceptional sum has at most two terms, while the record-spread
coefficient is at most \(W_{\beta,p}\); both costs are subexponential on the
\(L_H\) scale.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Start from the sharper first inequality in
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains}, namely
the child bound with the single value \(q=q_{r,p}\), and substitute it into
the large-window parent sum from
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}.  This gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h,q_{r,p}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(h\notin\mathcal E_r\), then \(\ell_r+h>A_r\).  Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:few-start-chains-with-enough-levels-are-record-spread}
with \(K=K_{r+1}\) and \(\ell=\ell_r+h\) bounds the corresponding summand by
the prefix-record outward-spread profile at parameter \(K_{r+1}\).  There
are at most \(B_r\) such summands, giving the displayed inequality.

For \(h\in\mathcal E_r\), the integer \(\ell_r+h\) satisfies
\[
  \ell_r+h\le A_r<\lfloor A_r\rfloor+1=q_{r,p},
\]
so \(q_{r,p}>\ell_r+h\).  The large-window branch also gives
\[
  K_{r+1}\ge\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H,
\]
and hence \(A_r\le4\), so \(q_{r,p}\le5\).  If \(\mathcal E_r\) is nonempty,
then some child length \(\ell_r+h\ge3\) is at most \(A_r\), so \(A_r\ge3\)
and \(q_{r,p}\ge4\).  This proves \(q_{r,p}\in\{4,5\}\), and the displayed
list of possible pairs follows from
\(\ell_r+h\in\{3,4\}\) and \(q_{r,p}>\ell_r+h\).

Finally, \(|\mathcal E_r|\le2\) follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:threshold-tight-short-exact-start-exceptions}, while
\(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\) follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost}.  Since
\(\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)\), both costs are subexponential.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Surplus-start chains are record spread]
\label{cor:surplus-start-chains-are-record-spread}
In the setting of
Definition~\ref{def:few-start-locally-short-staircase-chain-profiles}, if
\[
  q>
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H ,
\]
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell,q}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If the \(q\)-start chain property holds, there are at least \(q\) distinct
admissible start levels \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\).  For each such \(u\),
the first run in the length-\(\ell\) staircase-chain witness is a level-\(u\)
\((-1,+1)\)-crossing run satisfying the record, shortness, and
endpoint-clearance conditions in
Definition~\ref{def:short-prefix-record-outward-spread-profiles}.  Since the
number of these distinct start levels is larger than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\), the prefix-record outward-spread
property holds.  Taking the property-restricted union bound gives the
profile inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Large-window few-start branch collapses to record spread]
\label{cor:large-window-few-start-branch-collapses-to-record-spread}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains}, one has
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  B_r\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\), the coefficient is subexponential on the \(L_H\)
scale.  Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the large-window parent
chain profile follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the single
prefix-record outward-spread profile at parameter \(K_{r+1}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Put
\[
  A_r=\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H,
  \qquad
  q_{r,p}=\lfloor A_r\rfloor+1 .
\]
Then \(q_{r,p}>A_r\).  Start from the sharper first inequality in
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains}, and
substitute it into the large-window parent sum from
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}.  This gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L,\ell_r+h,q_{r,p}}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,qstart,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
For every \(h\), apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:surplus-start-chains-are-record-spread} with
\[
  K=K_{r+1},\qquad \ell=\ell_r+h,\qquad q=q_{r,p}.
\]
This bounds each child summand by the same prefix-record outward-spread
profile.  There are \(B_r\) summands, giving the displayed inequality.
Finally, \(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\) is
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost}, and
\(\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Locally short staircase chains are prefix-record spread]
\label{cor:locally-short-staircase-chains-are-prefix-record-spread}
In the setting of
Definition~\ref{def:locally-short-outward-staircase-chain-profiles}, for
every \(K,L\ge1\) and \(\ell\ge2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L,\ell}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K,L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If the locally short staircase-chain property holds, then the number of
admissible chain starts is larger than
\(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K)\).  For each such start \(u\), the
first run in the chain witness is a level-\(u\) \((-1,+1)\)-crossing run
satisfying the record, shortness, and endpoint-clearance conditions in
Definition~\ref{def:short-prefix-record-outward-spread-profiles}.  The
admissible starts are distinct levels in \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\), so these
first runs witness the prefix-record outward-spread property.  This gives a
property inclusion, and the displayed profile inequality follows by
monotonicity of property-restricted profiles.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Wide residual normal form with chain branches absorbed]
\label{cor:wide-residual-normal-form-with-chain-branches-absorbed}
In the setting and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}, assume
\(R=R_{\ell,p}\ge1\) and
\[
  4^{R-1}K\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}.
\]
Then at least one of the following alternatives holds.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Initial saturation:
\[
  K\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p}.
\]

\item Reduced bridge packet: there is \(r\in\{0,\ldots,R-1\}\) such that
\[
  K_r<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},\qquad B_r>\ell_r,
\]
and, with
\[
  \mathcal G_r
  =
  \left\{
    g\in\mathbb N:
    2\le g\le B_r-\ell_r+1,\quad
    g<
    W_{\beta,p}
    -
    \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K_{r+1}}L_H
  \right\},
\]
one has
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \ell_r\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{g\in\mathcal G_r}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_{r+1},L,g}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,free,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\qquad+
  \sum_{g\in\mathcal G_r}
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,2K_{r+1}(g-1)}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]

\item Reduced large-window packet: there is \(r\) with
\(0\le r\le R-2\) such that
\[
  K_r<T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},\qquad
  B_r\le\ell_r,\qquad
  K_{r+1}\ge T_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta,p},
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_r,L,\ell_r}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  B_r\,
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K_{r+1},L}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{enumerate}

In alternatives \((ii)\) and \((iii)\), all displayed index sets and
coefficients have logarithm \(o(L_H)\): indeed
\(\ell_r\le W_{\beta,p}\), \(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\), and
\(|\mathcal G_r|\le W_{\beta,p}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form}.  The
initial-saturation alternative is unchanged.

If the ordinary bridge-packet alternative holds, apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-packet-branch-has-truncated-return-form}.  Each
chain child in its first sum is bounded by the prefix-record outward-spread
profile at parameter \(K_{r+1}\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:locally-short-staircase-chains-are-prefix-record-spread}.
There are \(\ell_r\) such children, giving the reduced bridge-packet
display.

If the last valid large-window alternative holds, apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-few-start-branch-collapses-to-record-spread},
which gives the reduced large-window display.

It remains only to record the size bounds.  In the bridge-packet alternative
\(r\le R-1\), and hence
\[
  \ell_r=\ell+r\le\ell+R-1=W_{\beta,p}.
\]
The set \(\mathcal G_r\) is contained in \(\{2,\ldots,W_{\beta,p}-1\}\).
In the large-window alternative,
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost} gives
\(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\).  Since \(\log_{D_H}W_{\beta,p}=o(L_H)\), all displayed
finite costs are subexponential on the \(L_H\) scale.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why slab-exhausting depth is not automatic]
\label{rem:slab-exhausting-depth-not-automatic}
The recursive depth parameters in the finite chain amplification satisfy
\[
  K_r=2K_{r-1}B_r,\qquad
  B_r\ge
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K_{r-1}\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1 .
\]
Thus the current one-step mechanism increases \(K_r\) very rapidly.
Lemma~\ref{lem:counting-range-successor-gap-step} says that the bounded-successor
step is justified by the present counting argument only while
\[
  K_{r-1}<\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H .
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-width-successor-gap-count-for-chains} improves the
successor cutoff near the top of a slab by replacing the crude width
\(W_{\beta,p}\) with the residual start width
\(R_{\ell,p}=W_{\beta,p}-\ell+1\).  In particular, once a chain length is
already within \(O(L_H/K)\) of the top of the slab, the successor cutoff can
be bounded independently of \(p\), and
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-top-one-step-amplification-has-bounded-cost} gives a
bounded-cost one-step amplification in that regime.  In the still narrower
range of Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-free-residual-descent-near-slab-top}, this
step is bridge-free and decreases the residual chain-start width.  These
refinements do not by themselves give a route from a fixed initial \(\ell\)
into the near-top regime.  Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-bridge-free-residual-descent-iteration}
shows that, if the bridge-free hypotheses persisted until the residual
start-width was exhausted, the chain profile would vanish; the missing point
is to justify those hypotheses along such a descent from the chain profiles
produced by the earlier reductions.  Lemma~\ref{lem:bridge-free-residual-exhaustion-logarithmic-obstruction}
shows that the current \(K\)-recursion can certify such an exhaustion only
when the residual start-width at entry is already logarithmic in \(L_H\).
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-entry-forces-first-descent-obstruction}
packages the contrapositive as a first-obstruction alternative: outside that
logarithmic range, the unit descent branch must either leave the
counted-start range or create a confined chain-bridge packet.
Corollary~\ref{cor:first-bridge-active-obstruction-projects-to-ordinary-bridges}
then projects the latter alternative to the ordinary confined-bridge
families already used elsewhere in the reduction.
Corollary~\ref{cor:first-counting-saturation-has-last-large-bridge-free-step}
handles the remaining alternative: a non-initial counting saturation is
preceded by a bridge-free step with a successor window of order
\(L_H/K\).
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-first-obstruction-normal-form} combines
these observations into a single normal form for wide residual entries.
Corollary~\ref{cor:bridge-packet-branch-has-truncated-return-form} then
pushes the ordinary-bridge alternative through the existing bridge
truncation and inward-free-or-return split.
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-has-subexponential-child-cost} records
that the remaining large-window branch carries only a subexponential child
union, while one child has a residual drop of order \(L_H/K\).
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-children-reduce-to-few-start-chains} further
shows that, once this branch has saturated the counting range, each child can
be replaced by a bounded finite-start chain profile with \(q\le5\).
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-branch-localizes-to-exact-starts} removes the
remaining slab-level start choice at residual cost
\(\sum_{h=1}^{B_r}R_{\ell_r+h,p}\), reducing the branch to exact-start chain
profiles.
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-exact-start-branch-has-low-residual-tail}
then separates the upper half of this exact-start branch, where every child
has an \(L_H/K_r\)-scale residual-width drop.
Corollary~\ref{cor:dyadic-residual-layers-exact-start-branch} refines this
into dyadic residual layers, exposing the residual drop available at each
child-window scale.
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-exact-starts-are-record-spread-except-short-children}
gives a complementary escape from the exact-start branch: once the saturated
child parameter is in force, every exact-start child of total length at least
five is already one of the prefix-record outward-spread profiles treated by
the earlier reduction tree, leaving only exact-start children of total length
three or four as genuinely new finite exceptions.
Corollary~\ref{cor:threshold-tight-short-exact-start-exceptions} sharpens
this finite exception set further: the actual exceptional increments are
only those for which the short child length is still below the saturated
counting threshold \(\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/(4K_{r+1})\).  Thus
the exact-start exception set is empty once
\(K_{r+1}>\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}L_H/12\), and any length-four
exception can occur only at exact counting saturation.
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-exceptions-retain-surplus-starts} records the
same branch before the final exact-start localization is spent: all
non-exceptional children go directly to the prefix-record outward-spread
profile, while each exceptional child remains a few-start profile with more
admissible starts than chain levels.  The only remaining surplus-start types
are \((3,4)\), \((3,5)\), and \((4,5)\).
Corollary~\ref{cor:large-window-few-start-branch-collapses-to-record-spread}
then removes even this finite surplus-start family: the \(q_{r,p}\) distinct
start levels themselves already exceed the prefix-record counting threshold,
so every large-window few-start child is a prefix-record outward-spread
event.  Thus the large-window branch no longer leaves a new chain-type
residual; it returns to the existing prefix-record reduction tree with only a
single \(B_r<W_{\beta,p}\) coefficient.
Corollary~\ref{cor:locally-short-staircase-chains-are-prefix-record-spread}
then observes that the same start-level argument applies to every locally
short staircase-chain profile, not only to the saturated few-start children.
Consequently
Corollary~\ref{cor:wide-residual-normal-form-with-chain-branches-absorbed}
absorbs the remaining chain sums in the wide-residual normal form: outside
initial counting saturation, the two first-obstruction branches now reduce to
prefix-record outward-spread profiles, inward-free bridge profiles, and
spread-return profiles, all with subexponential coefficients.
Still, one cannot simply choose \(n\) of order
\(W_{\beta,p}\asymp L_H\) in
Corollary~\ref{cor:multiplicity-free-finite-chain-amplification} and invoke
Lemma~\ref{lem:long-chains-do-not-fit-in-one-slab}.  A valid growing-depth
argument must either keep the effective depth parameter below the counting
range, add a new source of many successor pairs after \(K_r\) becomes large,
or amplify chain length without the quadratic \(K\)-loss.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Counting-range-valid iterations stay subslab]
\label{lem:counting-range-valid-iterations-stay-subslab}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:multiplicity-free-finite-chain-amplification}, fix
\(K=K_0\ge1\) and \(\ell\ge2\), independent of \(p\).  Suppose that a
finite chain-amplification iteration of depth \(n=n(p)\) remains inside the
successor-counting range at every step, in the sense that
\[
  K_{r-1}<\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H
  \qquad(1\le r\le n).
\]
Then every terminal chain length \(a\in I_n(\ell)\) satisfies
\[
  a\le 2^n\ell
  \le
  \ell\sqrt{\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H}.
\]
Consequently, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\), every such
terminal length satisfies
\[
  a<W_{\beta,p}.
\]
Thus the slab-width vanishing criterion of
Lemma~\ref{lem:long-chains-do-not-fit-in-one-slab} cannot eliminate any
terminal chain length produced by a successor-counting-valid iteration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since
\[
  B_r\ge
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K_{r-1}\beta}{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}
  \right\rceil+1\ge2,
\]
the recursive depth parameters satisfy
\[
  K_r=2K_{r-1}B_r\ge4K_{r-1}.
\]
Hence, for \(n\ge1\),
\[
  K_{n-1}\ge4^{n-1}K .
\]
The counting-range assumption at step \(n\) gives
\[
  4^{n-1}K
  <
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H,
\]
and therefore
\[
  2^n
  <
  \sqrt{\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{4K}L_H}.
\]
The case \(n=0\) is trivial after enlarging the final \(p\)-neighbourhood.
Since \(I_n(\ell)\subseteq\{\ell+n,\ldots,2^n\ell\}\), the displayed bound on
terminal lengths follows.

Finally,
\[
  W_{\beta,p}=\max\{1,\lfloor\beta L_H\rfloor\}\ge\frac{\beta}{2}L_H
\]
for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\), while the terminal-length
bound is \(O(\sqrt{L_H})\) with constants fixed.  Thus
\[
  2^n\ell<W_{\beta,p}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(L_H\), proving the final assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Consequence for the present chain program]
\label{rem:present-chain-program-needs-new-ingredient}
Rounds 267--269 show that the present chain-amplification program has a
structural gap, not just a bookkeeping gap.  The slab support cutoff is at
linear scale \(W_{\beta,p}\asymp L_H\), but the terminal lengths reachable
before the successor-counting proof exits its range are only
\(O(\sqrt{L_H})\).  Closing the argument therefore requires a genuinely new
ingredient: either a bounded-successor extraction with much smaller
depth-parameter loss, a way to restart the counting lower bound after
renormalizing large \(K_r\), or a direct estimate for the bridge families
that accumulate before terminal chains can be exhausted.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Ideal doubled-count exhaustion has a constant obstruction]
\label{lem:ideal-doubling-loss-exhaustion-obstruction}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, fix \(K\ge1\) and
\(\ell\ge1\), independent of \(p\).  Suppose that, along a sequence
\(p\uparrow\pc(H)\), there are integers \(n=n(p)\ge0\) such that the
idealized doubled-count parameters remain in the successor-counting range,
namely
\[
  2^{r-1}K<\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H
  \qquad(1\le r\le n),
\]
and that the ideal terminal length reaches the slab cutoff,
\[
  2^n\ell>W_{\beta,p}.
\]
Then
\[
  K\beta\le \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8}\ell .
\]
Consequently, if
\[
  K\beta> \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8}\ell ,
\]
then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\), no such \(n\) exists.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For all sufficiently large \(L_H\), the second displayed condition forces
\(n\ge1\).  Applying the counting-range assumption at step \(n\) gives
\[
  2^{n-1}K<\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{16}L_H,
\]
and hence
\[
  2^n<\frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8K}L_H .
\]
Since \(W_{\beta,p}<2^n\ell\), we obtain
\[
  \frac{K W_{\beta,p}}{L_H}
  <
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda,\sigma,\beta}}{8}\ell .
\]
Taking \(p\uparrow\pc(H)\) along the chosen sequence and using
\(W_{\beta,p}/L_H\to\beta\) gives the asserted necessary condition.  The
final assertion is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What the ideal doubling test rules out]
\label{rem:ideal-doubling-test-rules-out}
Lemma~\ref{lem:ideal-doubling-loss-exhaustion-obstruction} tests the most
optimistic version of a lower-loss successor extraction that merely removes
the fixed-gap pigeonhole loss \(K\mapsto KB\), while retaining the unavoidable
halving of the counted successor starts.  For the raw chain terms in the
finite far-tail ladder, where \(q\in\{3,4\}\) and
\[
  K_{i,0}^{\rm ch}=512M_iB_iC_i,
\]
such an idealized route would still need
\[
  512M_iB_iC_i\,\beta_i
  \le
  \frac{\theta_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i}}{8}q .
\]
This constant inequality is not supplied by the present reductions.  Thus a
successful lower-loss route must do more than replace the step
\(K\mapsto 2KB\) by \(K\mapsto2K\): it must also improve the initial
depth-to-length ratio, restart the counted-start supply with a fresh ratio,
or estimate the bridge packets without waiting for terminal chains to exceed
the slab width.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Many tangential runs: adjacent crossing split]
\label{cor:many-tangential-runs-adjacent-crossing-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:horizontal-heavy-slab-spread-congestion}, let \(R\ge2\)
and put
\[
  P_R=\left\lfloor\frac{R-2}{4}\right\rfloor .
\]
Then
\[
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,R}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,tan,many}}(s,p)
  \le
  \sum_{\eta,\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}}
  \mathfrak C_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,P_R,\eta,\zeta}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,cross}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the many-run tangential profile
follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the four adjacent-crossing
tangential profile families.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(u\) and a rooted path \(\gamma=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\).  A level-\(u\)
tangential run that is not two-sided must contain time \(0\) or time
\(\ell\); hence there are at most two such runs.  Every two-sided level-\(u\)
tangential run is of exactly one of the four types
\((\eta,\zeta)\in\{-1,+1\}^2\), since maximality forces the adjacent
vertices just before and just after the run to lie outside \(S_u(x)\), while
adjacency to \(S_u(x)\) forces their distances from \(x\) to be \(u-1\) or
\(u+1\).  Therefore
\[
  R_x^u(\gamma)
  \le
  2+
  \sum_{\eta,\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}} R_{x,\eta,\zeta}^u(\gamma).
\]
If \(\mathcal T^{\rm many}_{u,R}\) holds and all four
\(\mathcal C^{\eta,\zeta}_{u,P_R}\) fail, then
\[
  R_x^u(\gamma)
  \le
  2+4P_R
  \le R,
\]
contradicting \(R_x^u(\gamma)>R\).  Thus
\[
  \mathcal T^{\rm many}_{u,R}
  \subseteq
  \bigcup_{\eta,\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}}
  \mathcal C^{\eta,\zeta}_{u,P_R}.
\]
Taking the corresponding union bound inside the property-restricted profiles
and then the supremum over \(u\) gives the displayed inequality.  The
exponent conclusion follows because there are only four terms.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Upper-shifted exterior-return profiles]
\label{def:upper-shifted-exterior-return-profiles}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for \(K\ge0\) define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
     {\rm rad,ret,up}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad=
  \sup_{u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N}
  \sup\left\{
    \sum_{\substack{r\ge0,\ |2r-m|\le2\\d>\lambda L_H}}
    Q^d\mathfrak R_{r,d}^{G,\mathcal X_{u+1,K}}:
    m\in\mathbb N,\ c_sL_H<m\le
      \left(\frac{1}{\alpha_\omega}+3s\right)L_H
  \right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
with value \(0\) if \(A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\) is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Upper-shifted returns move at most one slab]
\label{cor:upper-shifted-returns-move-at-most-one-slab}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:heavy-slab-token-dichotomy}, for every \(j\ge0\) and
\(K\ge0\),
\[
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,up}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret}}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j+1,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, the upper-shifted exterior-return exponent hypothesis follows
from the same exponent hypothesis on the same and next ordinary
exterior-return slabs.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(W=W_{\beta,p}\).  If \(u\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N\), then
\[
  u+1\in A_{j,p}\cap\mathbb N
  \quad\text{or}\quad
  u+1\in A_{j+1,p}\cap\mathbb N .
\]
Indeed, the only way \(u+1\) is not still in
\([jW,(j+1)W)\) is that \(u=(j+1)W-1\), in which case
\(u+1=(j+1)W\in A_{j+1,p}\).  Hence the supremum over
\(\mathcal X_{u+1,K}\) with \(u\in A_{j,p}\) is bounded by the sum of the
ordinary return-profile suprema over \(A_{j,p}\) and \(A_{j+1,p}\).  The
displayed inequality follows.  The exponent conclusion follows because the
right-hand side has two terms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Adjacent crossings localize to exterior returns]
\label{cor:adjacent-crossings-localize-to-exterior-returns}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:many-tangential-runs-adjacent-crossing-split}, let
\(R\ge1\) and set \(K=R-1\).  Then
\[
  \mathfrak C_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,R,\eta,\zeta}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,cross}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p)
\]
for
\[
  (\eta,\zeta)\in\{(-1,+1),(-1,-1),(+1,-1)\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathfrak C_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,R,+1,+1}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,cross}}(s,p)
  \le
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,up}}(s,p).
\]
Consequently, all adjacent-crossing exponent hypotheses follow from the
corresponding same-level and upper-shifted exterior-return exponent
hypotheses.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(u\) and write the relevant level-\(u\) crossing runs in increasing
order of their starting times.  If the exit type is \(\zeta=-1\), then every
such run ends with an inward level-\(u\) token.  Thus more than \(R\) runs
give more than \(R\) inward level-\(u\) tokens, and hence, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns}, the property
\(\mathcal X_{u,K}\).

It remains to consider type \((-1,+1)\).  If there are \(q>R\) such runs,
then between the end of each run and the start of the next one the path must
move from level \(u+1\) to level \(u-1\).  In each of the \(q-1\) intervening
time intervals there is therefore an inward level-\(u\) token.  Since
\(q-1\ge R>K\), Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns} again
gives \(\mathcal X_{u,K}\).

For type \((+1,+1)\), each run begins with an inward level-\(u+1\) token.
More than \(R\) such runs therefore imply \(\mathcal X_{u+1,K}\), again by
Lemma~\ref{lem:inward-level-tokens-exterior-returns}.  Taking the
corresponding property inclusions inside the profile definitions and then
the suprema gives the displayed inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-level same-sphere congestion: long run or many runs]
\label{cor:same-sphere-congestion-run-split}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:horizontal-heavy-slab-spread-congestion}, let \(K,L\ge1\)
and put
\[
  R_{K,L}=\left\lfloor\frac{K}{L}\right\rfloor.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,K}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor,lev}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,L}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda,\sigma,\beta,j,R_{K,L}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,tan,many}}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the exact-level same-sphere
congestion profile follows from the same exponent hypothesis on the long-run
and many-run tangential profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Fix an exact level \(u\).  The total number of same-sphere steps at level
\(u\) is the sum of the lengths of all level-\(u\) tangential runs.  If
\(\mathcal Z_{u,K}\) holds but \(\mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u,L}\) and
\(\mathcal T^{\rm many}_{u,R_{K,L}}\) both fail, then every level-\(u\)
tangential run has length at most \(L\), and there are at most
\(R_{K,L}\) such runs.  Hence
\[
  H_x(\gamma;\{u\})
  \le
  L R_{K,L}
  \le K,
\]
contradicting \(\mathcal Z_{u,K}\).  Thus
\[
  \mathcal Z_{u,K}
  \subseteq
  \mathcal T^{\rm long}_{u,L}\cup\mathcal T^{\rm many}_{u,R_{K,L}}.
\]
Taking the corresponding union bound inside the property-restricted profiles,
then summing with the same weights, gives the displayed profile inequality
after taking suprema.  The exponent conclusion follows because the sum has
two terms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fully localized finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:fully-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-spread-exterior-return-far-tail-ladder}, let
\(M_0,\ldots,M_{N-1}\ge1\) be integers and write
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,M_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor,spr}}(s,p),
\]
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm lev}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak Z_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,M_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,hor,lev}}(s,p),
\]
\[
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p),
\]
and
\[
  X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,Z_{i,j}^{\rm lev}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail and on the four
localized profile families appearing on the right-hand side.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-spread-exterior-return-far-tail-ladder}.  Each
horizontal-heavy slab term is bounded by
Corollary~\ref{cor:horizontal-heavy-slab-spread-congestion}, with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)=(\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,M_i).
\]
The displayed inequality follows after summing over \(i,j\).  All sums are
finite and independent of \(p\), and the slab-width factors are
exponent-negligible.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tangentially localized finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:tangentially-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:fully-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}, let
\(L_0,\ldots,L_{N-1}\ge1\) be integers and put
\[
  R_i=\left\lfloor\frac{M_i}{L_i}\right\rfloor
  \qquad(0\le i<N).
\]
Define \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:fully-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}, and write
\[
  T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,L_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,tan,long}}(s,p),
\]
\[
  T_{i,j}^{\rm many}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak T_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,R_i}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,tan,many}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm many}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the same-sphere spread
profiles, the two tangential run-profile families, and the two
exterior-return profile families.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:fully-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}.  Each
exact-level same-sphere congestion term
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm lev}
\]
is bounded by
Corollary~\ref{cor:same-sphere-congestion-run-split}, with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,M_i,L_i).
\]
Substituting these bounds gives the displayed inequality.  The exponent
conclusion is unchanged because all sums are finite and the only variable
multiplicative losses are slab-width factors \(W_{\beta_i,p}\), which have
logarithmic size \(o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Crossing finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:tangentially-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}, assume
that
\[
  R_i=\left\lfloor\frac{M_i}{L_i}\right\rfloor\ge2
  \qquad(0\le i<N),
\]
and put
\[
  P_i=\left\lfloor\frac{R_i-2}{4}\right\rfloor
  \qquad(0\le i<N).
\]
Define \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\),
\(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:tangentially-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}, and write
\[
  C_{i,j}^{\eta,\zeta}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak C_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,P_i,\eta,\zeta}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,cross}}(s,p)
  \qquad(\eta,\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}
  \sum_{\eta,\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}}C_{i,j}^{\eta,\zeta}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the same-sphere spread
profiles, the long-run profiles, the four adjacent-crossing tangential
profile families, and the two exterior-return profile families.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:tangentially-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), bound the many-run term
\[
  T_{i,j}^{\rm many}
\]
by Corollary~\ref{cor:many-tangential-runs-adjacent-crossing-split}, with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,R)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,R_i).
\]
Substitution gives the displayed inequality.  The exponent conclusion is
unchanged because the added crossing-type sum has four terms and the only
variable multiplicative losses remain the factors \(W_{\beta_i,p}\), whose
logarithmic size is \(o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Return-absorbed crossing finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:return-absorbed-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}, assume
that
\[
  P_i=\left\lfloor\frac{R_i-2}{4}\right\rfloor\ge1
  \qquad(0\le i<N),
\]
and put
\[
  K_i^\times=P_i-1
  \qquad(0\le i<N).
\]
Define \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\),
\(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}, and
write
\[
  X_{i,j}^{\times}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\times}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret}}(s,p),
\]
\[
  U_{i,j}^{\times}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\times}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,up}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(3X_{i,j}^{\times}(s,p)+U_{i,j}^{\times}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the same-sphere spread
profiles, the long-run profiles, the spread-return profiles, and the
same-level, upper-shifted, and repeated exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), use
Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-crossings-localize-to-exterior-returns} with
\[
  R=P_i,\qquad K=K_i^\times .
\]
The three crossing types other than \((+1,+1)\) are bounded by
\(X_{i,j}^{\times}\), while the \((+1,+1)\) type is bounded by
\(U_{i,j}^{\times}\).  Substitution gives the displayed inequality.  The
exponent conclusion is unchanged because all sums and the coefficient \(3\)
are fixed, and the only variable multiplicative losses remain the
exponent-negligible factors \(W_{\beta_i,p}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Return-only crossing finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:return-only-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-absorbed-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}, define
\(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\),
\(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and \(K_i^\times\) as there,
and for \(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\) write
\[
  B_{i,j}^{\times}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\times}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(4B_{i,j}^{\times}(s,p)+B_{i,j+1}^{\times}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the same-sphere spread
profiles, the long-run profiles, the spread-return profiles, and the two
ordinary exact-level exterior-return profile families \(B^\times\) and
\(X^{\rm ret}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:return-absorbed-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), use
Corollary~\ref{cor:upper-shifted-returns-move-at-most-one-slab} to bound
\[
  U_{i,j}^{\times}
  \le
  B_{i,j}^{\times}+B_{i,j+1}^{\times}.
\]
The term \(3X_{i,j}^{\times}+U_{i,j}^{\times}\) is therefore bounded by
\[
  4B_{i,j}^{\times}+B_{i,j+1}^{\times}.
\]
Substitution gives the displayed inequality.  The exponent conclusion is
unchanged because only one adjacent slab has been added for each fixed
\(i,j\), and all sums, coefficients, and numbers of slabs are independent of
\(p\), apart from the already exponent-negligible \(W_{\beta_i,p}\) factors.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Threshold-dominated return finite far-tail ladder]
\label{cor:threshold-dominated-return-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-only-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}, assume that
\[
  K_i^\times\ge K_i
  \qquad(0\le i<N).
\]
Define \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), and
\(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-only-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}, and for
\(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\) write
\[
  \widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the same-sphere spread
profiles, the long-run profiles, the spread-return profiles, and ordinary
exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:return-only-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}.  Since
\(K_i^\times\ge K_i\), monotonicity of the event
\(\mathcal X_{u,K}\) in \(K\) gives
\[
  B_{i,j}^{\times}(s,p)
  \le
  \widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
  \qquad(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}).
\]
For \(j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), the repeated-return term
\(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) in
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-only-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder} is exactly
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\).  Substituting the displayed monotonicity
bound gives the claimed inequality.  The exponent conclusion is unchanged
because all added coefficients and slab counts are fixed, while the factors
\(W_{\beta_i,p}\) are exponent-negligible.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Outward-through finite ladder]
\label{cor:outward-through-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:threshold-dominated-return-finite-far-tail-ladder}, define
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  For
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  U_{i,j}^{\rm out}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,spr}}(s,p),
\]
and for \(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,8M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  U_{i,j}^{\rm out}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)+R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, outward-through
tangential spread profiles, long-run profiles, spread-return profiles, and
ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:threshold-dominated-return-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), bound the same-sphere spread term
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}
\]
by Corollary~\ref{cor:same-sphere-spread-returns-or-outward-through}, with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,M_i).
\]
Substitution gives the displayed inequality.  The exponent conclusion is
unchanged because the added current/next spread-return sums have finitely
many terms independent of \(p\), and the only nonconstant multiplicative
losses are still the exponent-negligible factors \(W_{\beta_i,p}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Record-outward finite ladder]
\label{cor:record-outward-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:outward-through-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}, define
\(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  For
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm rec}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,2M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,rec}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  P_{i,j}^{\rm rec}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(2R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)+R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, record outward-through
spread profiles, long-run profiles, spread-return profiles, and ordinary
exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:outward-through-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.  For
each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:outward-through-spread-record-or-return} with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,M_i)
\]
gives
\[
  U_{i,j}^{\rm out}(s,p)
  \le
  P_{i,j}^{\rm rec}(s,p)
  +
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,2M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\]
The last profile is bounded by \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), by monotonicity in the
spread threshold and the definition of \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\) with parameter
\(8M_i\).  Substituting this bound in the outward-through ladder gives the
displayed inequality.  The exponent conclusion is unchanged because only a
fixed coefficient on an already listed spread-return family has changed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Subterminal record finite ladder]
\label{cor:subterminal-record-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:record-outward-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}, define
\(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  For
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm sub}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,4M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,sub}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  P_{i,j}^{\rm sub}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(3R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)+2R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, subterminal record
outward-through spread profiles, long-run profiles, spread-return profiles,
and ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:record-outward-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.  For
each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:record-outward-subterminal-or-return} with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,2M_i)
\]
gives
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm rec}(s,p)
  \le
  P_{i,j}^{\rm sub}(s,p)
  +
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)
  +
  R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr}(s,p).
\]
Substituting this in the record-outward ladder adds one more current
spread-return term and one more next-slab spread-return term, giving the
displayed coefficients \(3\) and \(2\).  The exponent conclusion is unchanged
because only fixed coefficients on already listed spread-return families have
changed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Persistent subterminal finite ladder]
\label{cor:persistent-subterminal-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:subterminal-record-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}, define
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  For
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm per}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,8M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,per}}(s,p),
\]
and for \(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,16M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  P_{i,j}^{\rm per}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(4R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p)
        +3R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, persistent subterminal
record profiles, long-run profiles, spread-return profiles, and ordinary
exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:subterminal-record-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:subterminal-record-persistent-or-return}
with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,4M_i)
\]
gives
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm sub}(s,p)
  \le
  P_{i,j}^{\rm per}(s,p)
  +
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p)
  +
  R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p).
\]
Also, by monotonicity in the spread threshold,
\[
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr}(s,p)\le R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p),
  \qquad 0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}.
\]
Substituting these inequalities into the subterminal record ladder gives the
displayed coefficients \(4\) and \(3\).  The exponent conclusion is unchanged
because only fixed coefficients and a fixed threshold choice for the same
spread-return family have changed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Deep persistent finite ladder]
\label{cor:deep-persistent-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-subterminal-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder},
define \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\),
\(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and \(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  For
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm deep}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak U_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,16M_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,out,deep}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  P_{i,j}^{\rm deep}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(4R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p)
        +3R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, deep persistent
subterminal record profiles, long-run profiles, spread-return profiles, and
ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-subterminal-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-levels-are-deeply-persistent}
with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,8M_i)
\]
gives
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm per}(s,p)\le P_{i,j}^{\rm deep}(s,p).
\]
Substitution gives the displayed inequality, and the exponent conclusion is
unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-prefix-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-prefix-spread-long-short-split}
with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L)

gives

Substitution gives the displayed inequality, with the existing long-run term
and the new long-run term combined into the factor \(2\).  The exponent

\begin{corollary}[Short outward-prefix finite ladder]

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:short-endpoint-prefix-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:short-endpoint-prefix-spread-outward-return-split}
with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,16M_i,L_i)
\]
gives
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,sh}(s,p)
  \le
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,out,sh}(s,p)
  +
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
  +
  R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p).
\]
Moreover,
\[
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}(s,p)\le R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
  \qquad(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i})
\]
by monotonicity in the spread-return threshold.  Substitution gives the
displayed coefficients \(5\) and \(4\).  The exponent conclusion is unchanged
because only fixed coefficients and fixed threshold choices for the same
spread-return family have changed.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:ordered-prefix-ladder-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\),
Corollary~\ref{cor:ordered-ladders-have-bounded-successor-gaps} with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,128M_i,L_i)
\]
gives
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,lad,sh}(s,p)
  \le
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,pair,sh}(s,p),
\]
because \(2K=256M_i\) and
\[
  B_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,128M_i}
  =
  \left\lceil\frac{2048M_i\beta_i}{\Theta_i}\right\rceil+1
  =
  B_i .
\]
Substitution gives the displayed inequality.  No coefficient changes occur in
this reduction, and the exponent conclusion is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\[

  =

\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le

\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,gap,sh}(s,p)

  &\quad+

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}

\\
  &\quad+

Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from

\begin{proof}

and independent of \(p\), so the exponent conclusion is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:locally-short-staircase-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:locally-short-staircases-have-bounded-successor-gaps}
with

  =

gives a bounded-gap staircase-pair profile with parameter \(512M_iB_i\) and

  =

Applying Corollary~\ref{cor:bounded-gap-staircase-pairs-have-fixed-gap} with
\[

then gives
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,sh}(s,p)

Substitution gives the displayed inequality.  The sums over \(h\) are finite

\end{proof}

\\

\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(7R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
        +5R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}

profiles with \(h\ge2\), long-run profiles, enlarged spread-return profiles,

\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-gap-staircase-pair-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\), Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-gap-staircase-pairs-split-into-chains-and-bridges}
with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,512M_iB_iC_i,L_i)
\]
gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\sum_{h=1}^{C_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,gap,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  P_{i,j,3}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chain,sh}(s,p)
  +
  P_{i,j,4}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chain,sh}(s,p)
  +
  \sum_{h=3}^{C_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitution gives the displayed inequality.  The number of new chain and
bridge profiles is finite and independent of \(p\), so the exponent
conclusion is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Chain-absorbed staircase-chain/bridge finite ladder]
\label{cor:chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder},
define \(B_i\), \(C_i\),
\(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}\),
\(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}\), \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}\),
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  For
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), write
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,rec,ch}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,512M_iB_iC_i,L_i}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,rec,short}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  2\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,rec,ch}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=3}^{C_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=2}^{B_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(7R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
        +5R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  3\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the chain-depth
prefix-record outward-spread profiles, confined fixed-gap locally short
staircase-bridge profiles with \(3\le h\le C_i\), confined fixed-gap bridge
profiles with \(h\ge2\), long-run profiles, enlarged spread-return profiles,
and ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}

Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\) and \(q\in\{3,4\}\), the chain profile
\[
  P_{i,j,q}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chain,sh}(s,p)
\]
is bounded by \(P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,rec,ch}(s,p)\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:locally-short-staircase-chains-are-prefix-record-spread},
with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L,\ell)

Substituting these two bounds for \(q=3\) and \(q=4\) gives the displayed
inequality.  The coefficient \(2\) is fixed, all other sums are those of
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder},
and the only nonconstant multiplicative losses remain the factors
\(W_{\beta_i,p}\), whose logarithms are \(o(L_H)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}

Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.

  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,ch}(s,p).

Substituting into the coefficient-\(2\) fixed-gap chain-depth prefix-pair

\begin{corollary}[Inward-free bridge persistent chain-absorbed finite ladder]
\label{cor:inward-free-bridge-persistent-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:confined-bridge-persistent-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder},
define \(B_i\), \(C_i\), \(B_i^{\rm ch}\), \(K_i^{\rm gap,ch}\),

\(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}\),

\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  For
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\) and
\(1\le h\le B_i^{\rm ch}\), write
\[
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,free,ch}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,2K_i^{\rm gap,ch},L_i,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,bridge,free,short}}(s,p)
\]
and
\[
  R_{i,j,h}^{\rm spr,br,ch}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak X_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,
    2K_i^{\rm gap,ch}\max\{h-1,1\}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad,ret,spr}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  2\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_i^{\rm ch}}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,free,ch}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  2\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=1}^{B_i^{\rm ch}}
  R_{i,j,h}^{\rm spr,br,ch}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,ch}(s,p)
        +R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,ch}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=3}^{C_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}(s,p)
\\

\\

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(7R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
        +5R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  3\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the finite family of
chain-depth inward-free confined bridge profiles, the chain-depth
bridge-return spread profiles, the earlier chain-depth spread-return

\end{corollary}

Corollary~\ref{cor:inward-free-bridges-are-chains-or-long-runs} with

Corollary~\ref{cor:locally-short-staircase-chains-are-prefix-record-spread}
with \(\ell=h+1\) bounds the chain profile by
\(P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,rec,br,recbr,recbr,ch}\).  Substituting these inequalities

coefficient
\(2B_i^{\rm ch}B_i^{\rm br,ch}+2B_i^{\rm ch}+3\) on the long-run term gives
the displayed inequality.

  R_{i,j,h}^{\rm spr,br,recbr,ch}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}

\\
  &\quad+

  \sum_{h=1}^{B_i^{\rm ch}}
  R_{i,j,h}^{\rm spr,br,ch}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+

  \sum_{h=2}^{B_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}(s,p)
\\

        +5R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  (2B_i^{\rm ch}B_i^{\rm br,ch}B_i^{\rm br,recbr,ch}
   +2B_i^{\rm ch}B_i^{\rm br,ch}+2B_i^{\rm ch}+3)
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+

  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}

\\
  &\quad+

        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).

\endgroup
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the finite family of
bridge-record-record-record confined fixed-gap bridge profiles, the retained
return-spread and bridge-return profiles named in the display, confined
fixed-gap staircase and bridge profiles, long-run profiles, enlarged
spread-return profiles, and ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
