\end{gathered}
$}
\]
This gives
\[
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{$
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm br19}(s,p)
  \le
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm ifr19}(s,p)
  +
  R_{i,j,h}^{\rm ret19}(s,p).
$}
\]
Substituting into the confined bridge sum with coefficient
\[
  D_i^{\rm rec,br,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,recbr,ch}
\]
gives the displayed replacement.  The added \(h\)-sum is finite and
independent of \(p\), and no new nonconstant multiplicative loss is introduced.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Staircase-chain-pair finite ladder]
\label{cor:staircase-chain-pair-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder},
define \(B_i\), \(C_i\), \(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}\),
\(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}\), \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}\),
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  Put
\[
  D_i
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{8192M_iB_iC_i\beta_i}
         {\theta_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i}}
  \right\rceil+5
\]
and
\[
  K_i^\sharp=1024M_iB_iC_iD_i .
\]
For \(q\in\{3,4\}\) and \(1\le h\le q\), write
\[
  P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,longchain,sh}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\sharp,L_i,q+h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p),
\]
and, for \(q\in\{3,4\}\) and \(q<h\le D_i\), write
\[
  P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chainbr,sh}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\sharp,L_i,q,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{q=3}^{4}
  \sum_{h=1}^{q}
  P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,longchain,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{q=3}^{4}
  \sum_{h=q+1}^{D_i}
  P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chainbr,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=3}^{C_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=2}^{B_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(7R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
        +5R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  3\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, longer locally short
staircase-chain profiles with lengths \(4,\ldots,8\), confined fixed-gap
staircase-chain bridge profiles, confined fixed-gap locally short
staircase-bridge profiles with \(3\le h\le C_i\), confined fixed-gap bridge
profiles with \(h\ge2\), long-run profiles, enlarged spread-return profiles,
and ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\) and \(q\in\{3,4\}\), apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chains-have-bounded-successor-gaps} with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L,\ell)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,512M_iB_iC_i,L_i,q).
\]
By the definition of \(D_i\),
\[
  D_i\ge B_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,512M_iB_iC_i}.
\]
Thus monotonicity in the bounded-gap cutoff gives a bounded-gap
staircase-chain-pair profile with parameter \(1024M_iB_iC_i\) and cutoff
\(D_i\).  Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:bounded-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-have-fixed-gap} with
this cutoff gives
\[
  P_{i,j,q}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chain,sh}(s,p)
  \le
  \sum_{h=1}^{D_i}
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\sharp,L_i,q,h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,gap,short}}(s,p).
\]
Now split each fixed gap using
Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-gap-staircase-chain-pairs-split}.  The terms with
\(1\le h\le q\) become the longer-chain profiles
\(P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,longchain,sh}\), and the terms with
\(q<h\le D_i\) become the confined chain-bridge profiles
\(P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chainbr,sh}\).  Substituting these two
bounds for the \(q=3\) and \(q=4\) chain terms in
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
gives the displayed inequality.  All new sums are finite and independent of
\(p\), so the exponent conclusion is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Second-stage staircase-chain finite ladder]
\label{cor:second-stage-staircase-chain-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-pair-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder},
define \(B_i\), \(C_i\), \(D_i\), \(K_i^\sharp\),
\(P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chainbr,sh}\),
\(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}\),
\(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}\), \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}\),
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  Put
\[
  E_i
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K_i^\sharp\beta_i}
         {\theta_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i}}
  \right\rceil+9,
  \qquad
  K_i^\flat=2K_i^\sharp E_i .
\]
For \(q\in\{3,4\}\), \(1\le h\le q\), write
\(\ell_{q,h}=q+h\).  For \(1\le a\le\ell_{q,h}\), define
\[
  P_{i,j,q,h,a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nextchain,sh}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\flat,L_i,\ell_{q,h}+a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p),
\]
and, for \(\ell_{q,h}<a\le E_i\), define
\[
  P_{i,j,q,h,a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nextchainbr,sh}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_i^\flat,L_i,\ell_{q,h},a}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{q=3}^{4}
  \sum_{h=1}^{q}
  \sum_{a=1}^{\ell_{q,h}}
  P_{i,j,q,h,a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nextchain,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{q=3}^{4}
  \sum_{h=1}^{q}
  \sum_{a=\ell_{q,h}+1}^{E_i}
  P_{i,j,q,h,a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nextchainbr,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{q=3}^{4}
  \sum_{h=q+1}^{D_i}
  P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chainbr,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=3}^{C_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=2}^{B_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(7R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
        +5R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  3\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, locally short
staircase-chain profiles with lengths \(5,\ldots,16\), confined fixed-gap
staircase-chain bridge profiles, confined fixed-gap locally short
staircase-bridge profiles with \(3\le h\le C_i\), confined fixed-gap bridge
profiles with \(h\ge2\), long-run profiles, enlarged spread-return profiles,
and ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-pair-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j,q,h\) with \(q\in\{3,4\}\) and \(1\le h\le q\), put
\(\ell=\ell_{q,h}\).
By the definition of \(E_i\),
\[
  E_i\ge B_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,K_i^\sharp}.
\]
Applying Corollary~\ref{cor:one-step-staircase-chain-amplification} with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L,\ell,\widetilde B)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,K_i^\sharp,L_i,\ell,E_i)
\]
gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &P_{i,j,q,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,longchain,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad\le
  \sum_{a=1}^{\ell_{q,h}}
  P_{i,j,q,h,a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nextchain,sh}(s,p)
  +
  \sum_{a=\ell_{q,h}+1}^{E_i}
  P_{i,j,q,h,a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nextchainbr,sh}(s,p).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting this bound for every longer-chain term in
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-pair-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder} gives
the displayed inequality.  All new sums are finite and independent of \(p\),
so the exponent conclusion is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-stage staircase-chain finite ladder]
\label{cor:finite-stage-staircase-chain-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder},
define \(B_i\), \(C_i\), \(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}\),
\(P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}\), \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}\),
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as there.  Fix \(n\ge0\).  For
\(0\le i<N\), put
\[
  K_{i,0}^{\rm ch}=512M_iB_iC_i .
\]
For \(1\le r\le n\), choose integers \(B_{i,r}^{\rm ch}\) so that
\[
  B_{i,r}^{\rm ch}\ge
  B_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,K_{i,r-1}^{\rm ch}}
  =
  \left\lceil
    \frac{16K_{i,r-1}^{\rm ch}\beta_i}
         {\theta_{\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i}}
  \right\rceil+1,
  \qquad
  K_{i,r}^{\rm ch}=2K_{i,r-1}^{\rm ch}B_{i,r}^{\rm ch}.
\]
For \(q\in\{3,4\}\) and
\(\mathbf a=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathcal A_n(q)\), write
\[
  P_{i,j,q,\mathbf a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nchain,sh}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_{i,n}^{\rm ch},L_i,a_n}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,short}}(s,p).
\]
For \(q\in\{3,4\}\), \(1\le r\le n\),
\(\mathbf a=(a_0,\ldots,a_{r-1})\in\mathcal A_{r-1}(q)\), and
\(a_{r-1}<h\le B_{i,r}^{\rm ch}\), write
\[
  P_{i,j,q,r,\mathbf a,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nchainbr,sh}(s,p)
  =
  \mathfrak P_{Q,\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,j,K_{i,r}^{\rm ch},L_i,a_{r-1},h}^{G\to H,
    {\rm rad,tan,pre,out,per,stair,loc,chain,bridge,short}}(s,p).
\]
Then, for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc(H)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
  &\le
  \mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{q=3}^{4}
  \sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_n(q)}
  P_{i,j,q,\mathbf a}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nchain,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{q=3}^{4}
  \sum_{r=1}^{n}
  \sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A_{r-1}(q)}
  \sum_{h=a_{r-1}+1}^{B_{i,r}^{\rm ch}}
  P_{i,j,q,r,\mathbf a,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,nchainbr,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=3}^{C_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,brdg,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \sum_{h=2}^{B_i}
  P_{i,j,h}^{\rm pre,br,sh}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  \bigl(7R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)
        +5R_{i,j+1}^{\rm spr,++}(s,p)\bigr)
\\
  &\quad+
  3\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,T_{i,j}^{\rm long}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
\\
  &\quad+
  \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
  \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}-1}
  W_{\beta_i,p}\,
  \bigl(5\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}(s,p)
        +\widehat X_{i,j+1}^{\rm ret}(s,p)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the exponent hypothesis on the initial far tail follows from
the same exponent hypothesis on the terminal far tail, the terminal
finite-stage staircase-chain profiles, the accumulated finite-stage confined
staircase-chain bridge profiles, confined fixed-gap locally short
staircase-bridge profiles with \(3\le h\le C_i\), confined fixed-gap bridge
profiles with \(h\ge2\), long-run profiles, enlarged spread-return profiles,
and ordinary exact-level exterior-return profiles.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
For each \(i,j\) and \(q\in\{3,4\}\), apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-staircase-chain-amplification} with
\[
  (\lambda,\sigma,\beta,K,L,\ell)
  =
  (\lambda_i,\sigma_i,\beta_i,K_{i,0}^{\rm ch},L_i,q)
\]
and with the chosen cutoffs \(B_1,\ldots,B_n\) equal to
\[
  B_{i,1}^{\rm ch},\ldots,B_{i,n}^{\rm ch}.
\]
This bounds the raw chain profile
\(P_{i,j,q}^{\rm pre,stair,loc,chain,sh}\) by the terminal chain profiles
indexed by \(\mathcal A_n(q)\) and the accumulated chain-bridge profiles
indexed by \(1\le r\le n\), \(\mathcal A_{r-1}(q)\), and
\(a_{r-1}<h\le B_{i,r}^{\rm ch}\).  Substituting these two bounds for the
\(q=3\) and \(q=4\) chain terms gives the displayed inequality.  All added
families are finite for fixed \(n\) and independent of \(p\), so the
exponent conclusion is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fully localized shifted original radial tail criterion]
\label{cor:fully-localized-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, let
\[
  \lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N
\]
with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\), let \(\delta>0\), let
\(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\), and let
\[
  K_0,\ldots,K_{N-1}\ge1,
  \qquad
  M_0,\ldots,M_{N-1}\ge1
\]
be integers.  Put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}2
  \qquad(0\le i<N)
\]
and define the localized profiles \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\),
\(Z_{i,j}^{\rm lev}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as
in Corollary~\ref{cor:fully-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
Assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\[
  0\le a<m_{\lambda_0,\delta}^{G\to H}
\]
one has
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak E_{a,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
and that, for every \(0\le i<N\) and
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr},\qquad
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm lev},\qquad
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret},\qquad
  X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak A(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\mathfrak A\) denotes the profile under consideration.  Then the
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) holds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:fully-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder} bounds
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) by the terminal far tail and
finite sums of the four localized profile families, with the only
nonconstant multiplicative losses equal to \(W_{\beta_i,p}\).  Since
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta_i,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H))
\]
for every fixed \(i\), the displayed exponent hypotheses imply the far-tail
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  Together with the
assumed near-tail bin estimates for
\(\mathfrak E_{a,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\), the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} hold with
\(\lambda=\lambda_0\).  Hence the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fully localized original radial subdivision criterion]
\label{cor:fully-localized-original-radial-subdivision-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}, suppose
that the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:fully-localized-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
hold for some choice of tail parameters.  Let \(\delta_{\rm fin}>0\), set
\[
  m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}
  =
  \left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{2\delta_{\rm fin}}\right\rfloor+1,
\]
and assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\(0\le a<m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak D_{a,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta_{\rm fin}\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s.
\]
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:fully-localized-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
gives the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  The displayed finite-bin
assumptions are exactly the finite-profile assumptions in
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-finite-radial-criterion}, with
\(\delta=\delta_{\rm fin}\).  That corollary therefore applies and gives
\(\pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tangentially localized shifted original radial tail criterion]
\label{cor:tangentially-localized-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, let
\[
  \lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N
\]
with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\), let \(\delta>0\), let
\(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\), and let
\[
  K_0,\ldots,K_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  M_0,\ldots,M_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  L_0,\ldots,L_{N-1}\ge1
\]
be integers.  Put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}2,
  \qquad
  R_i=\left\lfloor\frac{M_i}{L_i}\right\rfloor
  \qquad(0\le i<N),
\]
and define \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\),
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm many}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as
in Corollary~\ref{cor:tangentially-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
Assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\[
  0\le a<m_{\lambda_0,\delta}^{G\to H}
\]
one has
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak E_{a,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
and that, for every \(0\le i<N\) and
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr},\qquad
  T_{i,j}^{\rm long},\qquad
  T_{i,j}^{\rm many},\qquad
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret},\qquad
  X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound

       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\mathfrak A\) denotes the profile under consideration.  Then the
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) holds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:tangentially-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder} bounds
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) by the terminal far tail and
finite sums of the five tangentially localized profile families, with the
only nonconstant multiplicative losses equal to \(W_{\beta_i,p}\).  Since
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta_i,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H))
\]
for each fixed \(i\), the displayed assumptions imply the far-tail exponent
hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  Together with the
assumed near-tail bin estimates, the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} hold with
\(\lambda=\lambda_0\), giving the claimed tail exponent bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tangentially localized original radial subdivision criterion]
\label{cor:tangentially-localized-original-radial-subdivision-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}, suppose

\begin{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Adjacent-crossing localized shifted original radial tail criterion]
\label{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, let
\[
  \lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N
\]
with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\), let \(\delta>0\), let
\(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\), and let
\[
  K_0,\ldots,K_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  M_0,\ldots,M_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  L_0,\ldots,L_{N-1}\ge1
\]
be integers such that, with
\[
  R_i=\left\lfloor\frac{M_i}{L_i}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  P_i=\left\lfloor\frac{R_i-2}{4}\right\rfloor,
\]
one has \(R_i\ge2\) for every \(0\le i<N\).  Put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}2
  \qquad(0\le i<N),
\]
and define \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\),
\(C_{i,j}^{\eta,\zeta}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
Assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\[
  0\le a<m_{\lambda_0,\delta}^{G\to H}
\]
one has
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak E_{a,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
and that, for every \(0\le i<N\) and
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr},\qquad
  T_{i,j}^{\rm long},\qquad
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret},\qquad
  X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}
\]
and each of the four profiles
\[
  C_{i,j}^{\eta,\zeta}
  \qquad(\eta,\zeta\in\{-1,+1\})
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak A(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\mathfrak A\) denotes the profile under consideration.  Then the
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) holds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-finite-far-tail-ladder}
bounds \(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) by the terminal far
tail and finite sums of the same-sphere spread, long-run, adjacent-crossing,
spread-return, and repeated-return profile families.  The only nonconstant
multiplicative losses are the factors \(W_{\beta_i,p}\), and
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta_i,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H))
\]
for each fixed \(i\).  Hence the displayed assumptions imply the far-tail
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  Together with the
near-tail bin estimates, the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} hold with
\(\lambda=\lambda_0\), giving the claimed tail exponent bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Adjacent-crossing localized original radial subdivision criterion]
\label{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-original-radial-subdivision-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}, suppose
that the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-crossing-localized-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
hold for some choice of tail parameters.  Let \(\delta_{\rm fin}>0\), set
\[

\begin{corollary}[Return-absorbed shifted original radial tail criterion]
\label{cor:return-absorbed-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, let
\[
  \lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N
\]
with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\), let \(\delta>0\), let
\(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\), and let
\[
  K_0,\ldots,K_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  M_0,\ldots,M_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  L_0,\ldots,L_{N-1}\ge1
\]
be integers such that, with
\[
  R_i=\left\lfloor\frac{M_i}{L_i}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  P_i=\left\lfloor\frac{R_i-2}{4}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  K_i^\times=P_i-1,
\]
one has \(P_i\ge1\) for every \(0\le i<N\).  Put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}2
  \qquad(0\le i<N),
\]
and define \(Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr}\), \(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\),
\(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), \(X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\),
\(X_{i,j}^{\times}\), and \(U_{i,j}^{\times}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-absorbed-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
Assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\[
  0\le a<m_{\lambda_0,\delta}^{G\to H}
\]
one has
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak E_{a,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
and that, for every \(0\le i<N\) and
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  Z_{i,j}^{\rm spr},\qquad
  T_{i,j}^{\rm long},\qquad
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret},\qquad
  X_{i,j}^{\rm ret},\qquad
  X_{i,j}^{\times},\qquad
  U_{i,j}^{\times}
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak A(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\mathfrak A\) denotes the profile under consideration.  Then the
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) holds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:return-absorbed-crossing-finite-far-tail-ladder} bounds
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) by the terminal far tail and
finite sums of the same-sphere spread, long-run, spread-return,
same-level-return, upper-shifted-return, and repeated-return profile
families.  The only nonconstant multiplicative losses are the factors
\(W_{\beta_i,p}\), and
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta_i,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H))
\]
for each fixed \(i\).  Hence the displayed assumptions imply the far-tail
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  Together with the
near-tail bin estimates, the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} hold with
\(\lambda=\lambda_0\), giving the claimed tail exponent bound.
\end{proof}

\[

\begin{corollary}[Short endpoint-prefix radial tail criterion]
\label{cor:short-endpoint-prefix-reduced-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}, let
\[
  \lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N
\]
with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\), let \(\delta>0\), let
\(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\), and let
\[
  K_0,\ldots,K_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  M_0,\ldots,M_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  L_0,\ldots,L_{N-1}\ge1
\]
be integers such that, with
\[
  R_i=\left\lfloor\frac{M_i}{L_i}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  P_i=\left\lfloor\frac{R_i-2}{4}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  K_i^\times=P_i-1,
\]
one has \(K_i^\times\ge K_i\) for every \(0\le i<N\).  Put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}2
  \qquad(0\le i<N),
\]
and define \(P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,sh}\), \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+}\),
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:short-endpoint-prefix-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
Assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\[
  0\le a<m_{\lambda_0,\delta}^{G\to H}
\]
one has
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak E_{a,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that, for every \(0\le i<N\) and
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,sh},\qquad
  T_{i,j}^{\rm long},\qquad
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound, and that, for every
\(0\le i<N\) and \(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,+},\qquad
  \widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak A(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\mathfrak A\) denotes the profile under consideration.  Then the
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) holds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:short-endpoint-prefix-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
bounds \(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) by the terminal far
tail and finite sums of the short endpoint-prefix deep horizontal spread,
long-run, spread-return, and ordinary exact-level return profile families.
The only nonconstant multiplicative losses are the factors
\(W_{\beta_i,p}\), and the extra factor \(2\) on the long-run family is
fixed.  Since
\[
  \frac{\log_{D_H}W_{\beta_i,p}}{L_H}\to0
  \qquad(p\uparrow\pc(H)),
\]
the displayed assumptions imply the far-tail exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  Together with the
near-tail bin estimates, the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} hold with
\(\lambda=\lambda_0\), giving the claimed tail exponent bound.
\end{proof}

with \(\lambda_0>\rho/2\), let \(\delta>0\), let
\(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_{N-1}>0\), and let
\[
  K_0,\ldots,K_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  M_0,\ldots,M_{N-1}\ge1,\qquad
  L_0,\ldots,L_{N-1}\ge1
\]
be integers such that, with
\[
  R_i=\left\lfloor\frac{M_i}{L_i}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  P_i=\left\lfloor\frac{R_i-2}{4}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  K_i^\times=P_i-1,
\]
one has \(K_i^\times\ge K_i\) for every \(0\le i<N\).  Put
\[
  \sigma_i=\frac{\lambda_{i+1}}2
  \qquad(0\le i<N),
\]
and define \(P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,lad,sh}\), \(R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++}\),
\(T_{i,j}^{\rm long}\), \(S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\), and
\(\widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:ordered-prefix-ladder-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}.
Assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\[
  0\le a<m_{\lambda_0,\delta}^{G\to H}
\]
one has
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak E_{a,\delta}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_N}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
that, for every \(0\le i<N\) and
\(0\le j<J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  P_{i,j}^{\rm pre,lad,sh},\qquad
  T_{i,j}^{\rm long},\qquad
  S_{i,j}^{\rm ret}
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound, and that, for every
\(0\le i<N\) and \(0\le j\le J_{\sigma_i,\beta_i}\), each of
\[
  R_{i,j}^{\rm spr,++},\qquad
  \widehat X_{i,j}^{\rm ret}
\]
satisfies the same logarithmic exponent bound
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak A(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s,
\]
where \(\mathfrak A\) denotes the profile under consideration.  Then the
exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\) holds.

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:ordered-prefix-ladder-reduced-finite-far-tail-ladder}
bounds \(\mathfrak Y_{Q,\lambda_0}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}\) by the terminal far
tail and finite sums of the ordered short persistent prefix-ladder, long-run,
spread-return, and ordinary exact-level return profile families.  The only
nonconstant multiplicative losses are the factors \(W_{\beta_i,p}\), and the
extra factor \(2\) on the long-run family is fixed.  Since
\[

near-tail bin estimates, the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} hold with
\(\lambda=\lambda_0\), giving the claimed tail exponent bound.
\end{proof}

Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion} hold with

\begin{corollary}[Adjacent-stacked bridge subdivision criterion]
\label{cor:adjacent-stacked-bridge-reduced-original-radial-subdivision-criterion}

Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacent-stacked-bridge-reduced-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}

\[

  \left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{2\delta_{\rm fin}}\right\rfloor+1,

and assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\(0\le a<m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}\),

\]
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).

\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Seventh persistent subdivision criterion]
\label{cor:persistent-bridge-record-record-record-record-record-record-record-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-original-radial-subdivision-criterion}
In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}, suppose
that the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-bridge-record-record-record-record-record-record-record-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
hold for some choice of tail parameters.  Let \(\delta_{\rm fin}>0\), set
\[
  m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}
  =
  \left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{2\delta_{\rm fin}}\right\rfloor+1,
\]
and assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\(0\le a<m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak D_{a,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta_{\rm fin}\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s.
\]
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-bridge-record-record-record-record-record-record-record-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
gives the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  The displayed finite-bin
assumptions are the finite-profile assumptions in
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-finite-radial-criterion}, with
\(\delta=\delta_{\rm fin}\).  Applying that corollary gives the conclusion.
\end{proof}

In the setting of
Corollary~\ref{cor:original-radial-profile-subdivision-criterion}, suppose
that the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-bridge-record-record-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
hold for some choice of tail parameters.  Let \(\delta_{\rm fin}>0\), set
\[
  m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}
  =
  \left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{2\delta_{\rm fin}}\right\rfloor+1,
\]
and assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\(0\le a<m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak D_{a,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta_{\rm fin}\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s.
\]
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:persistent-bridge-record-record-chain-absorbed-staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
gives the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  The displayed finite-bin
assumptions are the finite-profile assumptions in
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-finite-radial-criterion}, with
\(\delta=\delta_{\rm fin}\).  Applying that corollary gives the conclusion.
\end{proof}

  m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}
  =
  \left\lfloor\frac{\rho}{2\delta_{\rm fin}}\right\rfloor+1,
\]
and assume, with \(\log_{D_H}0=-\infty\), that for every
\(0\le a<m_{\rho,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H}\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(H)}
  \frac{\log_{D_H}\mathfrak D_{a,\delta_{\rm fin}}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)}
       {\log_{D_H}\chiBar_p^H}
  +a\delta_{\rm fin}\log_{D_H}Q
  <
  -c_s\log_{D_H}\pc(H)-(2+7\alpha_\omega)s.
\]
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:staircase-chain-bridge-reduced-shifted-original-radial-tail-criterion}
gives the exponent hypothesis on
\(\mathfrak L_{Q,\rho}^{G\to H,{\rm rad}}(s,p)\).  The displayed finite-bin
assumptions are the finite-profile assumptions in
Corollary~\ref{cor:binned-shifted-original-finite-radial-criterion}, with
\(\delta=\delta_{\rm fin}\).  Applying that corollary gives the conclusion.
\end{proof}
