\begin{corollary}[Near-half-logarithmic pointwise root-annulus obstruction]
\label{cor:near-half-log-pointwise-root-annulus-obstruction}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-anchor-count-feasibility}, suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega>0\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that
for every \(\lambda>0\), every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\), every
\(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  U_\lambda=\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda,
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>U_\lambda L,
\]
or there is a vertex \(a\in V\) such that
\[
  d(x,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
\]
and
\[
  \tau_p(x,a)
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  Consequently,
if \(G\) is connected and \(\tau_p^{\max}\) is defined as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:pointwise-shell-decay}, then in the second alternative
there is an integer \(n\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\) such that
\[
  \tau_p^{\max}(n)
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-root-annulus-mass-obstruction}.  If the
super-half-logarithmic scale alternative fails, then the average of
\(\tau_p(x,\cdot)\) over the non-empty annulus
\(\{a:d(x,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}\) is at least the displayed threshold.
Some vertex in the annulus therefore attains at least this value.  The final
assertion follows by taking \(n=d(x,a)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Near-half-logarithmic pointwise root-annulus criterion]
\label{prop:near-half-log-pointwise-root-annulus-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1<\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\lambda>0\), \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\),
\(\theta>0\), integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
such that the following two exclusions hold.  First, no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\)
admits expanded gate-annulus data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Second, for every \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), every pair of vertices \(x,a\), and every
integer \(j>J+H\) with
\[
  B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p
  <
  2^j\le
  \left(\frac{1}{2\alpha_\omega}+\lambda\right)
  \log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
if
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  =
  \left(2^j-\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
        2^{j+1}+\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor\right],
\]
and \(d(x,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\), then
\[
  \tau_p(x,a)
  <
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\,
  L^{-3\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{-2\lambda\alpha_\omega-2\theta-5\theta\alpha_\omega},
\]
where \(D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\lambda,C_{\rm vol},\omega}\) is the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-anchor-density-obstruction}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We argue by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0 .
\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-pointwise-root-annulus-obstruction}, and
choose the parameters from the assumed criterion for this \(\epsilon\).  Take
\(p_0\ge p_1\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
Corollary~\ref{cor:near-half-log-pointwise-root-annulus-obstruction} applies.
The corollary gives expanded gate-annulus data satisfying either the
super-half-logarithmic scale condition, contradicting the first exclusion, or
a pointwise root-annulus lower bound.  In the latter case the inherited
weighted separated-fan conclusion gives \(2^j>B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), so the
second exclusion applies and gives the contradiction.  Hence
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The pointwise formulation above is only a diagnostic.  As
Proposition~\ref{prop:geodesic-lower-bound-pointwise-audit} shows, global
strict pointwise-supremum decay criteria can become vacuous because every
geodesic gives the lower bound \(\tau_p^{\max}(n)\ge p^n\).  The annular
average criterion in
Proposition~\ref{prop:near-half-log-root-annulus-density-criterion} retains
more information and is the stronger residual target.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Gate-annulus mass-to-operator lower bound]
\label{lem:gate-annulus-mass-to-operator-lower-bound}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite, let \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), and
let \(A,Y\subset V\) be finite non-empty sets.  Then
\[
  \norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  \frac{
    \sum_{a\in A}\sum_{\substack{y\in Y\\ d(y,a)\in I}}\tau_p(y,a)
  }{\sqrt{|A|\,|Y|}} .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\mathbf 1_A\) and \(\mathbf 1_Y\) be the indicator functions of \(A\)
and \(Y\).  Since \(T_p^I\) is a positive symmetric kernel,
\[
  \norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  \frac{\ip{\mathbf 1_Y}{T_p^I\mathbf 1_A}}
       {\norm{\mathbf 1_Y}_2\norm{\mathbf 1_A}_2}.
\]
The numerator is exactly the displayed double sum, and the denominator is
\(\sqrt{|A|\,|Y|}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive gate-annular operator dichotomy]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-annular-operator-dichotomy}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such
that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,
\]
every \(U>B\), every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and an interval
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  =
  \left(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p\right],
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
such that, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), either
\[
  2^j>UL,
\]
or
\[
  \norm{T_p^{I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-6\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{\beta(\theta,U,\omega)}
\]
where
\[
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{256C_{\rm vol}^7}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^6
  2^{6\eta J}U^{-6\eta}
\]
and
\[
  \beta(\theta,U,\omega)
  =
  2-4\theta-8\theta\alpha_\omega
  -3U\alpha_\omega-\frac32\theta\alpha_\omega .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Since
\(\pc>1/\Delta\), choose \(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that every selected
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\) and \(L\ge1\).  Choose the
expanded gate-annulus data from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  If
\(2^j>UL\), the first alternative holds, so assume that \(2^j\le UL\).

Let
\[
  A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}
\]
and let
\[
  Y=\{y\in K:\text{ there exists }z\in Z^\sharp
       \text{ with }d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}.
\]
The weighted separated-fan separation gives disjointness of the balls
\(B(z,r_p)\), and since \(d(a_z,z)=r_p\), the map \(z\mapsto a_z\) is
injective on \(Z^\sharp\).  Thus the root mass lower bound and
\(\tau_p\le1\) imply
\[
  |A|
  \ge
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  \ge
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
\]
where
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-4\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
For every \(z\in Z^\sharp\), the \(K\)-mass lower bound gives
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in Y\\d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \sum_{a\in A}\sum_{\substack{y\in Y\\d(y,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}
  \tau_p(y,a)
  \ge
  |A|\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \ge
  \left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^2 .
\]

The metric conclusions give \(A\subseteq B(x,2^{j+1}+r_p)\).  If
\(y\in Y\), then for some \(z\in Z^\sharp\),
\[
  d(x,y)
  \le d(x,a_z)+d(a_z,y)
  \le 2^{j+2}+2r_p,
\]
so \(Y\subseteq B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p)\).  Hence
\[
  |A|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+1}+r_p},
  \qquad
  |Y|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+2}+2r_p}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-annulus-mass-to-operator-lower-bound} therefore yields
\[
  \norm{T_p^{I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  \frac{\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^2}
       {C_{\rm vol}\omega^{3\cdot2^j+(3/2)r_p}} .
\]

Since \(p\ge1/\Delta\) and \(r_p\le\theta L\),
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Since \(2^j\le UL\), we also have \(j\le\log_2(UL)\), and hence
\[
  \sigma_j^6
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^6
  2^{6\eta J}U^{-6\eta}L^{-6\eta}.
\]
Finally,
\[
  \omega^{-3\cdot2^j-(3/2)r_p}
  \ge
  \chiBar_p^{-3U\alpha_\omega-(3/2)\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Combining the last three displays gives the stated lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gate support-profile product]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-support-profile-product}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such
that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,
\]
every \(U>B\), every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\) and
\[
  Y=\{y\in K:\text{ there exists }z\in Z^\sharp
       \text{ with }d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\},
\]
either
\[
  2^j>UL,
\]
or
\[
  |Y|\,\Theta_p(I_{j,p}^{\rm gate})
  \ge
  E_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-9\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{\zeta(\theta,\omega)}
\]
where
\[
  E_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{4096C_{\rm vol}^9}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}
\]
and
\[
  \zeta(\theta,\omega)
  =
  1-6\theta-12\theta\alpha_\omega .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Since
\(\pc>1/\Delta\), choose \(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that every selected
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\) and \(L\ge1\).  Choose the
expanded gate-annulus data.  If \(2^j>UL\), the first alternative holds, so
assume \(2^j\le UL\).

Let \(A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}\).  The weighted separated-fan separation gives
disjointness of the balls \(B(z,r_p)\), and since \(d(a_z,z)=r_p\), the map
\(z\mapsto a_z\) is injective on \(Z^\sharp\).  Hence
\[
  |A|
  \ge
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  \ge
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
Moreover, the \(K\)-mass lower bound gives
\[
  M:=
  \sum_{a\in A}\sum_{\substack{y\in Y\\d(y,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}
  \tau_p(y,a)
  \ge |A|\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
For \(y\in Y\), put
\[
  s_y=\sum_{\substack{a\in A\\d(y,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(y,a).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
  \sum_{y\in Y}s_y^2
  \ge
  \frac{M^2}{|Y|}
  \ge
  \frac{|A|^2\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^2}{|Y|}.
\]
Using \(K=A\) in Definition~\ref{def:annular-square-profile}, we get
\[
  \Theta_p(I_{j,p}^{\rm gate})
  \ge
  \frac1{\chiBar_p^2|A|}\sum_{y\in Y}s_y^2
  \ge
  \frac{\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^3}
       {\chiBar_p^2|Y|}.
\]

Since \(p\ge1/\Delta\) and \(r_p\le\theta L\),
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Since \(2^j\le UL\), we also have \(j\le\log_2(UL)\), and hence
\[
  \sigma_j^9
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}L^{-9\eta}.
\]
Combining the last three displays gives the support-profile product lower
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-support-profile-product} separates
the two losses in the square-profile route.  The expanded gate data force a
large product
\[
  |Y|\,\Theta_p(I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}).
\]
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-annular-square-profile-dichotomy}
then divides by the crude ball-volume bound on \(Y\).  Thus any improvement of
the square-profile threshold must either prove annular profile decay at the
gate scale or replace the ball-volume estimate for \(Y\) by a sharper
support-spread bound.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Support-profile escape]
\label{cor:support-volume-profile-branch-escape}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such
that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\), every \(U>B\), every \(\theta>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,
  \qquad
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
and
\[
  \delta(\theta,U,\omega)
  :=
  2-6\theta-15\theta\alpha_\omega-6U\alpha_\omega
  >0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Put
\[
  F_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{4096C_{\rm vol}^{10}}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}.
\]
Since \(\delta(\theta,U,\omega)>0\), choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\) that the expanded gate-annulus obstruction applies to every
\(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), every selected \(p\in[p_*,\pc)\) satisfies
\(p\ge1/\Delta\) and \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\ge1\), and
\[
  F_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}C_{\rm vol}^{-1}
  L^{-9\eta}\chiBar_p^{\delta(\theta,U,\omega)}
  >
  1 .
\]

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the expanded gate-annulus data.  Suppose,
for contradiction, that \(2^j\le UL\).  Let
\[
  A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}
\]
and
\[
  Y=\{y\in K:\text{ there exists }z\in Z^\sharp
       \text{ with }d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}.
\]
As in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-support-profile-product}, the
specific finite set \(A\) satisfies
\[
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}(A)}{\chiBar_p}
  \ge
  \frac{\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^3}
       {\chiBar_p^2|Y|}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:annular-profile-size-bounds}, applied to this same set \(A\),
gives
\[
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}(A)}{\chiBar_p}
  \le
  \frac{|A|}{\chiBar_p}.
\]
Therefore
\[
  |Y|\ge \frac{\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^3}
               {\chiBar_p|A|}.
\]

The metric conclusions give
\[
  A\subseteq B(x,2^{j+1}+r_p),
  \qquad
  Y\subseteq B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p).
\]
Under the cap \(2^j\le UL\), this yields
\[
  |A|\le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(2U+\theta)\alpha_\omega},
  \qquad
  |Y|\le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(4U+2\theta)\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Since \(p\ge1/\Delta\), \(r_p\le\theta L\), and \(j\le\log_2(UL)\), we also
have
\[
  \left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^3
  \ge
  \frac{1}{4096C_{\rm vol}^9}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}L^{-9\eta}
  \chiBar_p^{3-6\theta-12\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Combining the last four displays gives
\[
  |Y|
  \ge
  F_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-9\eta}
  \chiBar_p^{2-6\theta-13\theta\alpha_\omega-2U\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Together with the upper bound on \(|Y|\), this contradicts the choice of
\(p_*\), because the exponent difference is
\[
  2-6\theta-13\theta\alpha_\omega-2U\alpha_\omega
  -(4U+2\theta)\alpha_\omega
  =
  \delta(\theta,U,\omega).
\]
Hence \(2^j>UL\), as required.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The condition in
Corollary~\ref{cor:support-volume-profile-branch-escape} is non-empty
precisely in the same optimized range as the Schur-calibrated argument:
letting \(\theta\downarrow0\), it becomes \(6U\log_\Delta\omega<2\), i.e.
\[
  U<\frac{1}{3\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
This is weaker as a pure scale statement than
Corollary~\ref{cor:optimized-anchor-count-gate-escape}, which reaches
\(U<1/(2\log_\Delta\omega)\) using only the anchor count.  The support-profile
form is still useful because it records a two-replica support-volume
contradiction for the specific gate set \(A\), rather than only a cardinality
contradiction or a consequence of the annular Schur bound.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Capped support-profile feasibility]
\label{cor:capped-support-profile-feasibility}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\) and
\[
  \delta(\theta,U,\omega)
  =
  2-6\theta-15\theta\alpha_\omega-6U\alpha_\omega .
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\),
every \(U>B\), every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} such
that, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), either
\[
  2^j>UL,
\]
or
\[
  G_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-9\eta}\chiBar_p^{\delta(\theta,U,\omega)}
  \le 1,
\]
where
\[
  G_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{4096C_{\rm vol}^{11}}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}.
\]
Consequently, for fixed admissible parameters, a capped branch occurring
arbitrarily close to criticality forces \(\delta(\theta,U,\omega)\le0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Take
\(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that the expanded gate-annulus obstruction
applies, every selected \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\), and
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\ge1\).  Choose the expanded gate-annulus data.  If
\(2^j>UL\), the first alternative holds, so assume \(2^j\le UL\).

The proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:support-volume-profile-branch-escape} gives
\[
  |Y|
  \ge
  F_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-9\eta}
  \chiBar_p^{2-6\theta-13\theta\alpha_\omega-2U\alpha_\omega},
\]
where
\[
  F_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{4096C_{\rm vol}^{10}}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}.
\]
The metric containment \(Y\subseteq B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p)\) and the cap
\(2^j\le UL\) give
\[
  |Y|\le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(4U+2\theta)\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Combining the last two displays gives the stated feasibility inequality.

If the capped branch occurs for a sequence \(p\uparrow\pc\), then
\[
  G_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-9\eta}\chiBar_p^{\delta(\theta,U,\omega)}
  \le1
\]
along that sequence.  Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) and
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), this is impossible when
\(\delta(\theta,U,\omega)>0\).  Hence \(\delta(\theta,U,\omega)\le0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Optimized support-profile gate escape]
\label{cor:optimized-support-profile-gate-escape}
Under the graph and volume assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:support-volume-profile-branch-escape}, put
\[
  \alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega .
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that the following holds.  If
\(\alpha_\omega>0\), then for every
\[
  0<U<\frac{1}{3\alpha_\omega},
\]
every \(\eta>0\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), the same conclusion holds for every finite \(U>0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:support-volume-profile-branch-escape}.  First suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega>0\) and \(0<U<1/(3\alpha_\omega)\).  Choose \(B=U/2\), and
then choose \(\theta>0\) so small that
\[
  \theta<B,\qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
and
\[
  2-6\theta-15\theta\alpha_\omega-6U\alpha_\omega>0.
\]
This is possible because \(2-6U\alpha_\omega>0\).  Also
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega=U\alpha_\omega<\frac13<1 .
\]
Corollary~\ref{cor:support-volume-profile-branch-escape} applies with these
parameters and gives the desired data.

If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), fix any finite \(U>0\), choose \(B=U/2\), and choose
\[
  0<\theta<\min\{B,1/3\}.
\]
Then
\[
  2-6\theta-15\theta\alpha_\omega-6U\alpha_\omega
  =
  2-6\theta>0,
\]
while the other parameter inequalities are automatic.  Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:support-volume-profile-branch-escape} again proves the
claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive gate-annular square-profile dichotomy]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-annular-square-profile-dichotomy}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such
that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\) satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,
\]
every \(U>B\), every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and an interval
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  =
  \left(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p\right],
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
such that, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), either
\[
  2^j>UL,
\]
or
\[
  \Theta_p(I_{j,p}^{\rm gate})
  \ge
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L^{-9\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{\gamma(\theta,U,\omega)}
\]
where
\[
  D_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{4096C_{\rm vol}^{10}}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}
\]
and
\[
  \gamma(\theta,U,\omega)
  =
  1-6\theta-14\theta\alpha_\omega-4U\alpha_\omega .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Since
\(\pc>1/\Delta\), choose \(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that every selected
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\) and \(L\ge1\).  Choose the
expanded gate-annulus data from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  If
\(2^j>UL\), the first alternative holds, so assume that \(2^j\le UL\).

Let
\[
  A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\}
\]
and let
\[
  Y=\{y\in K:\text{ there exists }z\in Z^\sharp
       \text{ with }d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}.
\]
As in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-annular-operator-dichotomy}, the map
\(z\mapsto a_z\) is injective on \(Z^\sharp\), and hence
\[
  |A|\ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
Moreover,
\[
  M:=
  \sum_{a\in A}\sum_{\substack{y\in Y\\d(y,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}
  \tau_p(y,a)
  \ge |A|\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
For \(y\in Y\), put
\[
  s_y=\sum_{\substack{a\in A\\d(y,a)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(y,a).
\]
Then Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
  \sum_{y\in Y}s_y^2\ge\frac{M^2}{|Y|}
  \ge \frac{|A|^2\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^2}{|Y|}.
\]
Using \(K=A\) in Definition~\ref{def:annular-square-profile}, we obtain
\[
  \Theta_p(I_{j,p}^{\rm gate})
  \ge
  \frac1{\chiBar_p^2|A|}
  \sum_{y\in Y}s_y^2
  \ge
  \frac{|A|\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^2}
       {\chiBar_p^2|Y|}
  \ge
  \frac{\left(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right)^3}
       {\chiBar_p^2|Y|}.
\]

The metric conclusions give \(Y\subseteq B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p)\), and therefore
\[
  |Y|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+2}+2r_p}.
\]
Since \(p\ge1/\Delta\) and \(r_p\le\theta L\),
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Since \(2^j\le UL\), we also have \(j\le\log_2(UL)\), and hence
\[
  \sigma_j^9
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^9
  2^{9\eta J}U^{-9\eta}L^{-9\eta}.
\]
Finally,
\[
  \omega^{-2^{j+2}-2r_p}
  \ge
  \chiBar_p^{-4U\alpha_\omega-2\theta\alpha_\omega}.
\]
Combining the last four displays gives the stated lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Lemma~\ref{lem:annular-profile-size-bounds} gives
\(\Theta_p(I)\le1\) for every annulus \(I\).  Thus, whenever
\(\gamma(\theta,U,\omega)>0\), the second branch in
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-annular-square-profile-dichotomy}
is impossible sufficiently close to criticality.  Optimizing with
\(\theta\downarrow0\) gives the square-profile escape range
\(U<1/(4\log_\Delta\omega)\) when \(\omega>1\), weaker than the Schur-calibrated
operator range in
Corollary~\ref{cor:optimized-logarithmic-gate-scale-escape} but normalized in
the two-replica profile.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}
Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted-annular-mass-lower-bound} explains why a purely
weighted re-run of the square-profile argument does not improve the exponent
by itself.  Applying it with \(w=\mathbf 1_A\) gives the lower bound used
above.  Applying it instead with the root weights
\(w(a_z)=\tau_p(x,a_z)\) gives the same worst-case estimate, because the
available root-weight input is only
\(\sum_z\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\).  Any improvement of the
square-profile threshold must therefore prove either a larger selected gate
count or a larger total selected root weight; changing weights alone is
lossless but not stronger.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Capped gate-annular operator criterion]
\label{prop:capped-gate-annular-operator-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\), \(U>B\), \(\theta>0\),
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,
  \qquad
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
and the following two exclusions hold.

First, no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Second, for every \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) and every integer \(j>J+H\) such that
\[
  2^j\le U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
if
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  =
  \left(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p\right],
\]
then
\[
  \norm{T_p^{I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}_{2\to2}
  <
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L_p^{-6\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{\beta(\theta,U,\omega)},
  \qquad
  L_p=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
where
\[
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{256C_{\rm vol}^7}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^6
  2^{6\eta J}U^{-6\eta}
\]
and
\[
  \beta(\theta,U,\omega)
  =
  2-4\theta-8\theta\alpha_\omega
  -3U\alpha_\omega-\frac32\theta\alpha_\omega .
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We prove the first claim by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0.
\]
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}, and
choose the parameters from the assumed criterion for this \(\epsilon\).  Take
\(p_0\ge p_1\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that the expanded gate-annulus
obstruction applies, and choose its data.

If \(2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\), this data violates the first exclusion.
Thus \(2^j\le U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).  Repeating the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-annular-operator-dichotomy} with this
same data gives
\[
  \norm{T_p^{I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}\,
  L_p^{-6\eta}\,
  \chiBar_p^{\beta(\theta,U,\omega)},
\]
contradicting the second exclusion.  Hence
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The first exclusion in
Proposition~\ref{prop:capped-gate-annular-operator-criterion} is an exclusion
of large scales carrying the full expanded gate-annulus obstruction data.  It
is not the meaningless assertion that no large integer \(j\) exists.  This is
the point of keeping the gate-incidence data visible after the pointwise
audit.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Annular Schur bound]
\label{lem:annular-schur-bound}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite.  For every \(p<\pc\) and every
\(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\),
\[
  \norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}\le \chiBar_p .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The row sums of \(T_p^I\) are bounded above by the row sums of \(T_p\), hence
\[
  \sup_x\sum_y T_p^I(x,y)\le \chiBar_p .
\]
The kernel \(T_p^I\) is symmetric, so the same bound holds for column sums.
Schur's test gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Capped branch escape]
\label{cor:capped-operator-branch-escape}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Put \(\alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such
that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\), every \(U>B\), every \(\theta>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega<1,
  \qquad
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
and
\[
  \beta(\theta,U,\omega)
  =
  2-4\theta-8\theta\alpha_\omega
  -3U\alpha_\omega-\frac32\theta\alpha_\omega
  >1,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  Let
\[
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  =
  \frac{1}{256C_{\rm vol}^7}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^6
  2^{6\eta J}U^{-6\eta}.
\]
Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) and \(\beta(\theta,U,\omega)>1\), choose
\(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that the expanded gate-annulus
obstruction applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and whenever
\(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  L^{-6\eta}\chiBar_p^{\beta(\theta,U,\omega)}
  >
  \chiBar_p .
\]

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the expanded gate-annulus data.  Suppose,
for contradiction, that \(2^j\le U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).  The proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-annular-operator-dichotomy}, applied
to this same data, gives
\[
  \norm{T_p^{I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  C_{\epsilon,\eta,J,U,C_{\rm vol}}
  L^{-6\eta}\chiBar_p^{\beta(\theta,U,\omega)}
  >
  \chiBar_p .
\]
This contradicts Lemma~\ref{lem:annular-schur-bound}.  Hence
\(2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The exponent condition in
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-operator-branch-escape} is non-empty.  For example,
if
\[
  3U\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
then choosing \(0<\theta<B<U\) sufficiently small gives
\(\beta(\theta,U,\omega)>1\).
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Optimized logarithmic gate-scale escape]
\label{cor:optimized-logarithmic-gate-scale-escape}
Under the assumptions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-operator-branch-escape}, put
\[
  \alpha_\omega=\log_\Delta\omega .
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that the following holds.  If
\(\alpha_\omega>0\), then for every
\[
  0<U<\frac{1}{3\alpha_\omega},
\]
every \(\eta>0\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are data satisfying all conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>U\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), the same conclusion holds for every finite \(U>0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-operator-branch-escape}.  First suppose that
\(\alpha_\omega>0\) and \(0<U<1/(3\alpha_\omega)\).  Choose \(B=U/2\), and
then choose \(\theta>0\) so small that
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\alpha_\omega>0,
\]
and
\[
  2-4\theta-8\theta\alpha_\omega
  -3U\alpha_\omega-\frac32\theta\alpha_\omega
  >1 .
\]
This is possible because \(1-3U\alpha_\omega>0\).  Also
\[
  2B\alpha_\omega=U\alpha_\omega<\frac13<1 .
\]
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-operator-branch-escape} applies with these
parameters and gives the desired data.

If \(\alpha_\omega=0\), fix any finite \(U>0\), choose \(B=U/2\), and choose
\(0<\theta<\min\{B,1/4\}\).  Then
\[
  \beta(\theta,U,\omega)=2-4\theta>1,
\]
while the other parameter inequalities are automatic.  Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:capped-operator-branch-escape} again proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive root-weighted gate-incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-root-weighted-gate-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a finite non-empty set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset \(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a
map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
the tuple \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) satisfies the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan},
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the data by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  For
each \(z\in Z^\sharp\),
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \le
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \le
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|,
\]
since \(\tau_p(y,a_z)\le1\).  The other properties are inherited.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive deterministic anchored gate-incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a finite non-empty set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset \(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a
map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
the tuple \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) satisfies the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan},
\[
  |Z^\sharp|\ge\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
\]
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the data by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-root-weighted-gate-incidence-obstruction}.
Since \(\tau_p(x,a_z)\le1\),
\[
  |Z^\sharp|
  \ge
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
The remaining properties are inherited.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive uniform deterministic gate-incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-uniform-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a finite non-empty set
\(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset \(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a
map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
the tuple \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) satisfies the conclusions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-weighted-separated-fan},
\[
  |Z^\sharp|\ge\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
\]
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p_*\) close enough to \(\pc\) that the conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}
applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and also \(p_*\ge1/\Delta\).  This is
possible by Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-degree-pc-lower}.  Fix
\(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the deterministic gate-incidence data.  Since
\(p\ge p_0\ge1/\Delta\),
\[
  p^{2r_p}\ge \Delta^{-2r_p}\ge \chiBar_p^{-2\theta}.
\]
Hence the threshold \(\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}
satisfies
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega}
  \ge
  \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
The displayed lower bounds with \(\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\) follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive localized anchored incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-localized-anchored-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying
\[
  \theta<B,
  \qquad
  1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in V\),
finite non-empty sets \(A,Y,Z\subset V\), and a bijection \(a:Z\to A\) such
that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
\]
we have
\[
  2^j>BL,
  \qquad
  |A|\ge\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
  \qquad
  |Y|\ge\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p),
\]
\[
  d(x,z)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  \qquad(z\in Z),
\]
\[
  d(z,z')>2r_p\qquad(z,z'\in Z,\ z\ne z'),
\]
\[
  Y\subseteq B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in Y:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(K,x,j,Z_\theta,Z^\sharp\), and \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\), by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-uniform-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}.
Put
\[
  Z=Z^\sharp,\qquad A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\},
\]
and
\[
  Y=
  \bigcup_{z\in Z^\sharp}
  \{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}.
\]
If \(z,z'\in Z^\sharp\) and \(z\ne z'\), then \(a_z\ne a_{z'}\), since
\(a_z=a_{z'}\) would imply \(d(z,z')\le2r_p\), contradicting the separated fan
condition.  Thus \(a:Z\to A\) is a bijection and
\[
  |A|=|Z^\sharp|\ge\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
The same lower bound for \(|Y|\) follows from the pointwise incidence lower
bound for any fixed \(z\in Z^\sharp\).

For \(y\in Y\), choose \(z\in Z^\sharp\) with
\(d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\).  Since also
\(d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\),
\[
  d(x,y)\le d(x,a_z)+d(a_z,y)\le2^{j+2}+2r_p.
\]
The remaining displayed properties are inherited from the volume-sensitive
uniform deterministic gate-incidence obstruction and the separated fan
conditions.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive improved logarithmic gate scale]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-improved-logarithmic-gate-scale}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying \(\theta<B\), every \(a>0\) satisfying
\[
  (2a+\theta)\log_\Delta\omega
  <
  1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), the volume-sensitive localized anchored incidence obstruction of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-localized-anchored-incidence-obstruction}
can be chosen so that, with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  2^j\ge aL .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-localized-anchored-incidence-obstruction}.
Fix \(\eta,B,\theta,a,J,H\) as in the statement, and put
\[
  c_a=
  \frac{1}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}a^{-3\eta}.
\]
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that the volume-sensitive
localized anchored incidence obstruction applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\),
and whenever \(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  c_a L^{-3\eta}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega}
  >
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(2a+\theta)\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
This is possible by the strict exponent inequality in the statement.

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the localized anchored incidence data.
Suppose for contradiction that \(2^j<aL\).  Then \(j\le\log_2(aL)\), and the
definition of \(\sigma_j\) gives
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega}
  \ge
  c_a L^{-3\eta}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
On the other hand, \(A\subseteq B(x,2^{j+1}+r_p)\), so the volume-growth bound
gives
\[
  |A|
  \le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+1}+r_p}
  <
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{(2a+\theta)\log_\Delta\omega}.
\]
This contradicts \(|A|\ge\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\).  Hence
\(2^j\ge aL\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive matched anchored incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(B>0\)
satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,
\]
every \(\theta>0\) satisfying \(\theta<B\), every \(a>0\) satisfying
\[
  (2a+\theta)\log_\Delta\omega
  <
  1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex
\(x\in V\), and vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_m,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_m,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_m
\]
such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
  \qquad
  m=\left\lceil\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right\rceil,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge aL,
\]
the vertices \(z_1,\ldots,z_m\) are pairwise distinct and satisfy
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>2r_p\qquad(i\ne k),
\]
the vertices \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) are pairwise distinct, the vertices
\(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) are pairwise distinct, and, for every \(1\le i\le m\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the localized anchored incidence data from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-improved-logarithmic-gate-scale}.  Form the
finite bipartite graph \(\mathfrak B\) with left part \(A\), right part \(Y\),
and an edge between \(a_z\in A\) and \(y\in Y\) when
\[
  d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}.
\]
The corollary gives \(|A|\ge\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\), and the bijection
\(a:Z\to A\) gives, for every \(a_z\in A\),
\[
  \deg_{\mathfrak B}(a_z)
  =
  |\{y\in Y:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p).
\]
Since cardinalities and degrees are integers,
\[
  |A|\ge m,
  \qquad
  \deg_{\mathfrak B}(a)\ge m\quad(a\in A),
  \qquad
  m=\left\lceil\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right\rceil .
\]
Choose \(A_0\subseteq A\) with \(|A_0|=m\).  For every non-empty
\(S\subseteq A_0\), the neighbourhood \(N(S)\) contains the neighbourhood of
any vertex of \(S\), and hence \(|N(S)|\ge m\ge |S|\).  Hall's theorem gives a
matching saturating \(A_0\).  Write the matched left vertices as
\(a_1,\ldots,a_m\), the matched right vertices as \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\), and set
\(z_i=a^{-1}(a_i)\).  The matching gives the distinctness of the \(a_i\)'s and
\(y_i\)'s, the bijection \(a:Z\to A\) gives the distinctness of the \(z_i\)'s,
and all displayed metric properties are inherited from the localized anchored
incidence configuration.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Volume-sensitive matched anchored incidence criterion]
\label{prop:volume-sensitive-matched-anchored-incidence-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Suppose that for every \(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(B>0\),
\(\theta>0\), \(a>0\), integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega<1,\qquad
  \theta<B,
\]
\[
  (2a+\theta)\log_\Delta\omega
  <
  1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega,
\]
and no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in V\), and
vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_m,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_m,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_m
\]
with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,\qquad
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega},
  \qquad
  m=\left\lceil\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\right\rceil,
\]
such that all of the following hold:
\[
  2^j\ge aL,
\]
the vertices \(z_1,\ldots,z_m\) are pairwise distinct and satisfy
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>2r_p\qquad(i\ne k),
\]
the vertices \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) are pairwise distinct, the vertices
\(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) are pairwise distinct, and, for every \(1\le i\le m\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p).
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction},
with the \(L^2\)-gap conclusion supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Gate-energy exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:gate-energy-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/4\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan \((K,x,j,Z)\) at \(p\) satisfies
\[
  \mathcal G_{p,r_p}^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}(x,K,Z)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta}\chiBar_p^{2-2\theta}
\]
for any \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), where \(\sigma_j\) and \(r_p\) are the parameters
in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of Corollary~\ref{cor:gated-fan-obstruction}, with
the \(L^2\)-gap conclusion again supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Point-gated fan obstruction]
\label{cor:point-gated-fan-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/4\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a
finite non-empty set \(Z_\theta\subset V\), and maps
\(a,b:Z_\theta\to V\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\),
\[
  d(a_z,z)=d(b_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z_\theta),
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal H_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a,b)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{2-4\theta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:gated-fan-obstruction}.  Since \(d(x,z)\in I_j\) for
every \(z\in Z_\theta\) and \(r_p<2^j\), each sphere
\(\{v:d(v,z)=r_p\}\) is non-empty.  Let
\[
  M_{r_p}=\sup_{z\in V}|\{v:d(v,z)=r_p\}|.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-pair-selection} gives maps \(a,b:Z_\theta\to V\) with
\[
  \mathcal H_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a,b)
  \ge
  M_{r_p}^{-2}\mathcal G_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta).
\]
The maximum-degree bound gives
\[
  M_{r_p}\le \Delta^{r_p+1}\le\Delta\chiBar_p^\theta .
\]
Combining this with Corollary~\ref{cor:gated-fan-obstruction} proves the
displayed point-gated lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Point-gated exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:point-gated-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/4\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan \((K,x,j,Z)\) at \(p\) admits
maps \(a,b:Z\to V\), with \(d(a_z,z)=d(b_z,z)=r_p\), satisfying
\[
  \mathcal H_{p,r_p}^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}(x,K,Z,a,b)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{2-4\theta}
\]
for any \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), where \(\sigma_j\) and \(r_p\) are the parameters
in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:point-gated-fan-obstruction}, with the \(L^2\)-gap
conclusion supplied by Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-gate fan obstruction]
\label{cor:one-gate-fan-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/4\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a
finite non-empty set \(Z_\theta\subset V\), and a map \(a:Z_\theta\to V\)
such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\),
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z_\theta),
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal J_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a)
  \ge
  p^{2r_p}
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{2-4\theta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta,a,b\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:point-gated-fan-obstruction}.  Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-coalescence}
gives
\[
  \mathcal J_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a)
  \ge
  p^{2r_p}\mathcal H_{p,r_p}^{I_j}(x,K,Z_\theta,a,b),
\]
and the point-gated lower bound gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\label{prop:one-gate-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that

for any \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), where \(\sigma_j\) and \(r_p\) are the parameters

  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then

  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).

\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}

\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High one-gate obstruction]
\label{cor:high-one-gate-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/4\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a
finite non-empty set \(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset
\(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\),
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
and, putting
\[
  \kappa_j(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-4\theta},
\]
we have
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j(p)
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in I_j}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p,K,j,x,Z_\theta\) and a map \(a:Z_\theta\to V\) by
Corollary~\ref{cor:one-gate-fan-obstruction}, and set
\[
  L=
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{8\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{2-4\theta}.
\]
Since \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is separated, the balls \(B(z,r_p)\),
\(z\in Z_\theta\), are pairwise disjoint.  Hence the vertices \(a_z\) are
distinct, and
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z_\theta}\tau_p(x,a_z)\le\chiBar_p.
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:high-one-gate-layer-extraction} to this map \(a\).  The
resulting set \(Z^\sharp\) satisfies the two displayed lower bounds, since
\(L/(2\chiBar_p)=\kappa_j(p)\).  The root lower bound also makes
\(Z^\sharp\) non-empty.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[High one-gate exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:high-one-gate-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/4\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan \((K,x,j,Z)\) at \(p\) admits a
non-empty subset \(Z'\subseteq Z\) and a map \(a:Z'\to V\), with
\(d(a_z,z)=r_p\), satisfying
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z'}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j(p)
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,z)\in(2^j,2^{j+1}]}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z')
\]
for any \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), where \(\sigma_j\) and \(r_p\) are the parameters
in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans} and
\[
  \kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-4\theta}.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of Corollary~\ref{cor:high-one-gate-obstruction},
with the \(L^2\)-gap conclusion supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Expanded gate obstruction]
\label{cor:expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/4\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a
finite non-empty set \(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset
\(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and with \(\sigma_j,r_p,\kappa_j(p)\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:high-one-gate-obstruction}, the tuple
\((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\),
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
\[
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j(p),
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the data by Corollary~\ref{cor:high-one-gate-obstruction}.  If
\(z\in Z^\sharp\), then \(d(a_z,z)=r_p\), while the separated fan conditions
give \(d(x,z)\in I_j\).  The triangle inequality gives
\[
  d(x,a_z)\in(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p]=I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}.
\]
Similarly, every \(y\in K\) with \(d(y,z)\in I_j\) satisfies
\[
  d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}.
\]
Thus the pointwise \(K\)-mass lower bound from
Corollary~\ref{cor:high-one-gate-obstruction} remains valid when the summation
is enlarged to \(d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\).  The remaining displayed
properties are inherited.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Expanded gate-annulus exclusion criterion]
\label{prop:expanded-gate-annulus-exclusion-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/4\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan \((K,x,j,Z)\) at \(p\) admits a
non-empty subset \(Z'\subseteq Z\) and a map \(a:Z'\to V\), with
\(d(a_z,z)=r_p\), satisfying
\[
  d(x,a_z)\in(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p]\qquad(z\in Z'),
\]
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z'}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j(p),
\]
and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,a_z)\in(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p]}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z')
\]
for any \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), where \(\sigma_j,r_p\) are the parameters in
Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans} and
\[
  \kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-4\theta}.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}, with the \(L^2\)-gap
conclusion supplied by Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Root-weighted gate-incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:root-weighted-gate-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/4\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a
finite non-empty set \(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset
\(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and with \(\sigma_j,r_p,\kappa_j(p)\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:high-one-gate-obstruction}, the tuple
\((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\),
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
\[
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)\ge\kappa_j(p),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the data by Corollary~\ref{cor:expanded-gate-annulus-obstruction}.  For
each \(z\in Z^\sharp\),
\[
  \kappa_j(p)
  \le
  \sum_{\substack{y\in K\\d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}}}\tau_p(y,a_z)
  \le
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|,
\]
since \(\tau_p(y,a_z)\le1\).  The other properties are inherited.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of

\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Deterministic anchored gate-incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/4\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a
finite non-empty set \(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset
\(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
and with \(\sigma_j,r_p,\kappa_j(p)\) as in
Corollary~\ref{cor:high-one-gate-obstruction}, the tuple
\((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\),
\[
  |Z^\sharp|\ge\kappa_j(p),
\]
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the data by
Corollary~\ref{cor:root-weighted-gate-incidence-obstruction}.  Since
\(\tau_p(x,a_z)\le1\),
\[
  |Z^\sharp|
  \ge
  \sum_{z\in Z^\sharp}\tau_p(x,a_z)
  \ge \kappa_j(p).
\]
The remaining properties are inherited.
\end{proof}

\]
Then

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
