\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded-degree lower bound on criticality]
\label{lem:bounded-degree-pc-lower}
If \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), then
\[
  \pc(G)\ge \frac1{\Delta-1}\ge\frac1\Delta .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For \(p<1/(\Delta-1)\), the expected size of the open cluster of any vertex
\(x\) is at most the union bound over self-avoiding paths:
\[
  \chi_p(x)
  \le
  1+\sum_{n\ge1}\Delta(\Delta-1)^{n-1}p^n<\infty .
\]
Thus there is no infinite cluster at \(x\) almost surely.  Since \(x\) was
arbitrary, \(p\le\pc(G)\).  Letting \(p\uparrow1/(\Delta-1)\) gives the first
bound, and the second is immediate from \(\Delta\ge2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniform deterministic gate-incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:uniform-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/6\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite
non-empty \(K\subset V\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in K\), a
finite non-empty set \(Z_\theta\subset V\), a non-empty subset
\(Z^\sharp\subseteq Z_\theta\), and a map \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\) such that, with
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
with \(\sigma_j,r_p\) as in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}, and with
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta},
\]
the tuple \((K,x,j,Z_\theta)\) is an
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan at \(p\),
\[
  |Z^\sharp|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p),
\]
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\qquad(z\in Z^\sharp),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \widehat\kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z^\sharp).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(p_*\) close enough to \(\pc\) that the conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction} applies to every
\(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and also \(p_*\ge1/\Delta\).  This is possible by
Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-degree-pc-lower}.  Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose
the deterministic gate-incidence data.  Since \(p\ge p_0\ge1/\Delta\),
\[
  p^{2r_p}\ge \Delta^{-2r_p}\ge \chiBar_p^{-2\theta}.
\]
Hence the threshold \(\kappa_j(p)\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction} satisfies
\[
  \kappa_j(p)
  =
  \frac{p^{2r_p}\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-4\theta}
  \ge
  \widehat\kappa_j(p).
\]
The displayed lower bounds with \(\widehat\kappa_j(p)\) follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Uniform deterministic gate-incidence criterion]
\label{prop:uniform-deterministic-gate-incidence-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/6\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no
\((\epsilon,\eta,\theta,J,H)\)-separated fan \((K,x,j,Z)\) at \(p\) admits a
non-empty subset \(Z'\subseteq Z\) and a map \(a:Z'\to V\), with
\[
  |Z'|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p),
\]
\[
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p]\qquad(z\in Z'),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p]\}|
  \ge \widehat\kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z')
\]
for any \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\), where \(\sigma_j,r_p\) are the parameters in
Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans} and
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:uniform-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}, with the
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Localized anchored incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:localized-anchored-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/6\), every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\)
sufficiently close to \(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer
\(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in V\), finite non-empty sets \(A,Y,Z\subset V\), and
a bijection \(a:Z\to A\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
with \(\sigma_j,r_p\) as in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}, and with
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta},
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge\frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  |A|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p),
  \qquad
  |Y|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p),
\]
\[
  d(x,z)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  \qquad(z\in Z),
\]
\[
  d(z,z')>2r_p\qquad(z,z'\in Z,\ z\ne z'),
\]
\[
  Y\subseteq B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in Y:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \widehat\kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(K,x,j,Z_\theta,Z^\sharp\), and \(a:Z^\sharp\to V\), by
Corollary~\ref{cor:uniform-deterministic-gate-incidence-obstruction}.  Put
\[
  Z=Z^\sharp,\qquad A=\{a_z:z\in Z^\sharp\},
\]
and
\[
  Y=
  \bigcup_{z\in Z^\sharp}
  \{y\in K:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}.
\]
If \(z,z'\in Z^\sharp\) and \(z\ne z'\), then \(a_z\ne a_{z'}\), since
\(a_z=a_{z'}\) would imply \(d(z,z')\le2r_p\), contradicting the separated fan
condition.  Thus \(a:Z\to A\) is a bijection and
\[
  |A|=|Z^\sharp|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p).
\]
The same lower bound for \(|Y|\) follows from the pointwise incidence lower
bound for any fixed \(z\in Z^\sharp\).

For \(y\in Y\), choose \(z\in Z^\sharp\) with \(d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\).
Since also \(d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\),
\[
  d(x,y)\le d(x,a_z)+d(a_z,y)\le2^{j+2}+2r_p.
\]
The remaining displayed properties are inherited from the uniform deterministic
gate-incidence obstruction and the separated fan conditions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Localized anchored incidence criterion]
\label{prop:localized-anchored-incidence-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/6\), integers
\(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that for no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) do there exist
an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in V\), finite non-empty sets
\(A,Y,Z\subset V\), and a bijection \(a:Z\to A\) such that, writing
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
and
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta},
\]
all of the following hold:
\[
  2^j\ge\frac14\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  |A|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p),
  \qquad
  |Y|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p),
\]
\[
  d(x,z)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_z,z)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}
  \qquad(z\in Z),
\]
\[
  d(z,z')>2r_p\qquad(z,z'\in Z,\ z\ne z'),
\]
\[
  Y\subseteq B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
and
\[
  |\{y\in Y:d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}\}|
  \ge \widehat\kappa_j(p)
  \qquad(z\in Z).
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:localized-anchored-incidence-obstruction}, with the
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Improved logarithmic gate scale]
\label{cor:improved-logarithmic-gate-scale}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/7\),
every
\[
  0<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), the localized anchored incidence obstruction of
Corollary~\ref{cor:localized-anchored-incidence-obstruction} can be chosen so
that
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\epsilon\) be the constant from
Corollary~\ref{cor:localized-anchored-incidence-obstruction}.  Fix
\(\eta,\theta,a,J,H\) as in the statement, and put
\[
  c_a=
  \frac{1}{16\Delta^3}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}a^{-3\eta}.
\]
Choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that the localized anchored
incidence obstruction applies to every \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and whenever
\(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  c_a L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}
  >
  \Delta\chiBar_p^{2a+\theta}.
\]
This is possible because \(2a+\theta<1-6\theta\).

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the localized anchored incidence data.
Suppose for contradiction that \(2^j<aL\).  Then \(j\le\log_2(aL)\), and the
definition of \(\sigma_j\) gives
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}
  \ge
  c_a L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}.
\]
On the other hand, \(A\subseteq B(x,2^{j+1}+r_p)\), so bounded degree gives
\[
  |A|\le \Delta^{2^{j+1}+r_p+1}
  <
  \Delta\chiBar_p^{2a+\theta}.
\]
This contradicts \(|A|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p)\).  Hence
\(2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Improved gate-scale incidence criterion]
\label{prop:improved-gate-scale-incidence-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/7\),
\[
  0<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits a
localized anchored incidence configuration satisfying the conditions in
Proposition~\ref{prop:localized-anchored-incidence-criterion} and the
additional scale condition
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:improved-logarithmic-gate-scale}, with the \(L^2\)-gap
conclusion supplied by Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Left-degree matching extraction]
\label{lem:left-degree-matching-extraction}
Let \(\mathfrak B\) be a finite bipartite graph with left part \(A\) and right
part \(Y\).  Let \(m\ge1\) be an integer.  If \(|A|\ge m\) and every
\(a\in A\) has at least \(m\) neighbours in \(Y\), then \(\mathfrak B\)
contains a matching of size \(m\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(A_0\subseteq A\) with \(|A_0|=m\).  For every non-empty
\(S\subseteq A_0\), the neighbourhood \(N(S)\) contains the neighbourhood of
any one vertex of \(S\), and hence \(|N(S)|\ge m\ge |S|\).  Hall's theorem
therefore gives a matching saturating \(A_0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Matched anchored incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/7\),
every
\[
  0<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex
\(x\in V\), and vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_m,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_m,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_m
\]
such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
with \(\sigma_j,r_p\) as in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}, and with
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta},
  \qquad
  m=\left\lceil\widehat\kappa_j(p)\right\rceil,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
the vertices \(z_1,\ldots,z_m\) are pairwise distinct and satisfy
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>2r_p\qquad(i\ne k),
\]
the vertices \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) are pairwise distinct, the vertices
\(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) are pairwise distinct, and, for every \(1\le i\le m\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the localized anchored incidence data from
Corollary~\ref{cor:improved-logarithmic-gate-scale}.  Form the finite
bipartite graph \(\mathfrak B\) with left part \(A\), right part \(Y\), and an
edge between \(a_z\in A\) and \(y\in Y\) when
\[
  d(y,a_z)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}.
\]
Since \(|A|\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p)\) and each left degree is at least
\(\widehat\kappa_j(p)\), while cardinalities and degrees are integers, we have
\[
  |A|\ge m,\qquad \deg_{\mathfrak B}(a)\ge m\quad(a\in A),
  \qquad
  m=\left\lceil\widehat\kappa_j(p)\right\rceil .
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:left-degree-matching-extraction} gives a matching of size
\(m\).  Write the matched left vertices as \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\), the matched
right vertices as \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\), and set \(z_i=a^{-1}(a_i)\).  The
matching gives the distinctness of the \(a_i\)'s and \(y_i\)'s, the bijection
\(a:Z\to A\) gives the distinctness of the \(z_i\)'s, and all displayed
metric properties are inherited from the localized anchored incidence
configuration.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Matched anchored incidence criterion]
\label{prop:matched-anchored-incidence-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/7\),
\[
  0<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits an
integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex \(x\in V\), and vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_m,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_m,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_m
\]
with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta},
  \qquad
  m=\left\lceil\widehat\kappa_j(p)\right\rceil,
\]
such that all of the following hold:
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
the vertices \(z_1,\ldots,z_m\) are pairwise distinct and satisfy
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>2r_p\qquad(i\ne k),
\]
the vertices \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) are pairwise distinct, the vertices
\(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) are pairwise distinct, and, for every \(1\le i\le m\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p).
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction}, with the
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded-degree packing extraction]
\label{lem:bounded-degree-packing-extraction}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  If \(S\subseteq V\) is
finite and \(R\ge0\) is an integer, then there is \(S'\subseteq S\) such that
\[
  d(u,v)>R\qquad(u,v\in S',\ u\ne v)
\]
and
\[
  |S'|\ge |S|\Delta^{-R-1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose vertices greedily from \(S\), and after choosing \(u\) discard all
remaining vertices of \(S\cap B(u,R)\).  Each step discards at most
\(\Delta^{R+1}\) vertices, so the number of chosen vertices is at least
\(|S|\Delta^{-R-1}\).  The construction gives the displayed separation.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Separated matched incidence obstruction]
\label{cor:separated-matched-incidence-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/12\),
every
\[
  0<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex
\(x\in V\), and vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_n,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_n,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_n
\]
such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
with \(\sigma_j,r_p\) as in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}, and with
\[
  \widetilde\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^5}\chiBar_p^{1-12\theta},
  \qquad
  n=\left\lceil\widetilde\kappa_j(p)\right\rceil,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>4r_p,\qquad
  d(a_i,a_k)>2r_p,\qquad
  d(y_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(i\ne k),
\]
and, for every \(1\le i\le n\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the matched anchored incidence obstruction from
Corollary~\ref{cor:matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction}, with matched
triples indexed by a set \(M\) of size
\[
  m=\left\lceil\widehat\kappa_j(p)\right\rceil,
  \qquad
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}.
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-degree-packing-extraction} to the anchor set
\(\{z_i:i\in M\}\) with \(R=4r_p\).  This gives \(M_0\subseteq M\) such that
the anchors \(\{z_i:i\in M_0\}\) are \(4r_p\)-separated and
\[
  |M_0|\ge m\Delta^{-4r_p-1}.
\]
Apply the same lemma to the set \(\{y_i:i\in M_0\}\) with \(R=2r_p\).  This
gives \(M_1\subseteq M_0\) such that the vertices \(\{y_i:i\in M_1\}\) are
\(2r_p\)-separated and
\[
  |M_1|\ge m\Delta^{-6r_p-2}.
\]
Since \(m\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p)\) and
\(\Delta^{6r_p}\le\chiBar_p^{6\theta}\),
\[
  |M_1|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^5}\chiBar_p^{1-12\theta}
  =
  \widetilde\kappa_j(p).
\]
Thus \(|M_1|\ge n\), after replacing \(M_1\) by an arbitrary subset of size
\(n\).  Relabel this subset as \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

The \(z_i\)'s are \(4r_p\)-separated by construction, the \(y_i\)'s are
\(2r_p\)-separated by construction, and
\[
  d(a_i,a_k)\ge d(z_i,z_k)-d(a_i,z_i)-d(a_k,z_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(i\ne k).
\]
All remaining metric properties are inherited from
Corollary~\ref{cor:matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Disjoint gate-tube obstruction]
\label{cor:disjoint-gate-tube-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/12\),
every
\[
  0<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), the separated matched incidence obstruction of
Corollary~\ref{cor:separated-matched-incidence-obstruction} can be chosen
together with simple paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\) such that each
\(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\), runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), satisfies
\[
  \gamma_i\subseteq B(z_i,r_p),
\]
and the paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the separated matched incidence obstruction.  For each \(i\), choose a
geodesic \(\gamma_i\) from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), which has length \(r_p\) since
\(d(a_i,z_i)=r_p\).  Every vertex of \(\gamma_i\) lies in \(B(z_i,r_p)\).  If
\(\gamma_i\) and \(\gamma_k\) intersect for \(i\ne k\), then
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)\le2r_p,
\]
contradicting the separated matched obstruction, where \(d(z_i,z_k)>4r_p\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Disjoint gate-tube criterion]
\label{prop:disjoint-gate-tube-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/12\),
\[
  0<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits
vertices satisfying the metric and size conditions displayed in
Proposition~\ref{prop:separated-matched-incidence-criterion}, together with
simple paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\) such that each \(\gamma_i\) has
length \(r_p\), runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), satisfies
\[
  \gamma_i\subseteq B(z_i,r_p),
\]
and the paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:disjoint-gate-tube-obstruction}, with the \(L^2\)-gap
conclusion supplied by Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cross-separated tube obstruction]
\label{cor:cross-separated-gate-tube-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/14\),
every
\[
  3\theta<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex
\(x\in V\), vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_q,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_q,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_q,
\]
and simple paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_q\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
with \(\sigma_j,r_p\) as in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}, and with
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{48\Delta^6}\chiBar_p^{1-14\theta},
  \qquad
  q=\left\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)\right\rceil,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>4r_p,\qquad
  d(a_i,a_k)>2r_p,\qquad
  d(y_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(i\ne k),
\]
\[
  d(a_i,y_k)>2r_p\qquad(1\le i,k\le q),
\]
and, for every \(1\le i\le q\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
while \(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\), runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), satisfies
\[
  \gamma_i\subseteq B(z_i,r_p),
\]
and the paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_q\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the disjoint gate-tube obstruction from
Corollary~\ref{cor:disjoint-gate-tube-obstruction}, with triples indexed by a
set \(M\) of size
\[
  n=\left\lceil\widetilde\kappa_j(p)\right\rceil,
  \qquad
  \widetilde\kappa_j(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^5}\chiBar_p^{1-12\theta}.
\]
Form a graph \(\mathfrak C\) on the index set \(M\), joining distinct
\(i,k\in M\) if
\[
  d(a_i,y_k)\le2r_p
  \qquad\text{or}\qquad
  d(a_k,y_i)\le2r_p .
\]
For a fixed \(i\), there are at most \(\Delta^{2r_p+1}\) indices \(k\) with
\(d(a_i,y_k)\le2r_p\), and at most \(\Delta^{2r_p+1}\) indices \(k\) with
\(d(y_i,a_k)\le2r_p\).  Hence \(\mathfrak C\) has maximum degree at most
\(2\Delta^{2r_p+1}\).  A greedy independent-set extraction gives
\(M'\subseteq M\) such that no two distinct indices of \(M'\) are adjacent in
\(\mathfrak C\) and
\[
  |M'|\ge \frac{n}{2\Delta^{2r_p+1}+1}
  \ge \frac{n}{3\Delta^{2r_p+1}} .
\]
Since \(n\ge\widetilde\kappa_j(p)\) and
\(\Delta^{2r_p}\le\chiBar_p^{2\theta}\),
\[
  |M'|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{48\Delta^6}\chiBar_p^{1-14\theta}
  =
  \kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p).
\]
Replace \(M'\) by a subset of size
\(q=\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)\rceil\) and relabel it as
\(\{1,\ldots,q\}\).

For distinct indices \(i,k\), the independent-set property gives
\(d(a_i,y_k)>2r_p\).  For \(i=k\), put
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).  Since \(d(a_i,y_i)>2^j-r_p\),
\(2^j\ge aL\), \(r_p\le\theta L\), and \(a>3\theta\),
\[
  d(a_i,y_i)>(a-\theta)L>2\theta L\ge2r_p.
\]
All other displayed properties are inherited from the disjoint gate-tube
obstruction.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Cross-separated tube criterion]
\label{prop:cross-separated-gate-tube-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/14\),

\[

and simple paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_q\), with
\[

  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],

\[
  \sigma_j=
  \frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2 2^{-\eta(j-J)},
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{48\Delta^6}\chiBar_p^{1-14\theta},
  \qquad
  q=\left\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)\right\rceil,
\]
such that all of the following hold:
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>4r_p,\qquad
  d(a_i,a_k)>2r_p,\qquad
  d(y_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(i\ne k),
\]
\[
  d(a_i,y_k)>2r_p\qquad(1\le i,k\le q),
\]
and, for every \(1\le i\le q\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
while \(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\), runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), satisfies
\[
  \gamma_i\subseteq B(z_i,r_p),
\]
and the paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_q\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint.  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:cross-separated-gate-tube-obstruction}, with the
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Endpoint tube obstruction]
\label{cor:endpoint-separated-tube-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/16\),
every
\[
  4\theta<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex
\(x\in V\), vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_s,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_s,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_s,
\]
and simple paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
with \(\sigma_j,r_p\) as in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}, and with
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm end}(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{144\Delta^7}\chiBar_p^{1-16\theta},
  \qquad
  s=\left\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm end}(p)\right\rceil,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>4r_p,\qquad
  d(a_i,a_k)>2r_p,\qquad
  d(y_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(i\ne k),
\]
\[
  d(a_i,y_k)>2r_p,\qquad d(z_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(1\le i,k\le s),
\]
and, for every \(1\le i\le s\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
while \(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\), runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), satisfies
\[
  \gamma_i\subseteq B(z_i,r_p),
\]
and the paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the cross-separated tube obstruction from
Corollary~\ref{cor:cross-separated-gate-tube-obstruction}, with triples indexed
by a set \(M\) of size
\[
  q=\left\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)\right\rceil,
  \qquad
  \kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{48\Delta^6}\chiBar_p^{1-14\theta}.
\]
Form a graph \(\mathfrak D\) on the index set \(M\), joining distinct
\(i,k\in M\) if
\[
  d(z_i,y_k)\le2r_p
  \qquad\text{or}\qquad
  d(z_k,y_i)\le2r_p .
\]
For a fixed \(i\), there are at most \(\Delta^{2r_p+1}\) indices \(k\) with
\(d(z_i,y_k)\le2r_p\), and at most \(\Delta^{2r_p+1}\) indices \(k\) with
\(d(y_i,z_k)\le2r_p\).  Hence \(\mathfrak D\) has maximum degree at most
\(2\Delta^{2r_p+1}\), and a greedy independent-set extraction gives
\(M'\subseteq M\) with
\[
  |M'|\ge \frac{q}{2\Delta^{2r_p+1}+1}
  \ge \frac{q}{3\Delta^{2r_p+1}} .
\]
Since \(q\ge\kappa_j^{\rm xsep}(p)\) and
\(\Delta^{2r_p}\le\chiBar_p^{2\theta}\),
\[
  |M'|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{144\Delta^7}\chiBar_p^{1-16\theta}
  =
  \kappa_j^{\rm end}(p).
\]
Replace \(M'\) by a subset of size
\(s=\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm end}(p)\rceil\), and relabel it as
\(\{1,\ldots,s\}\).

For distinct indices \(i,k\), the independent-set property gives
\(d(z_i,y_k)>2r_p\).  For \(i=k\), put
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).  Since \(d(z_i,y_i)\ge d(a_i,y_i)-d(a_i,z_i)\),
\(d(a_i,y_i)>2^j-r_p\), \(2^j\ge aL\), \(r_p\le\theta L\), and
\(a>4\theta\),
\[
  d(z_i,y_i)>2^j-2r_p\ge(a-2\theta)L>2\theta L\ge2r_p.
\]
All other displayed properties are inherited from the cross-separated tube
obstruction.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Endpoint tube criterion]
\label{prop:endpoint-separated-tube-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Suppose that for every
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\), \(0<\theta<1/16\),
\[
  4\theta<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits an

\[

\]

  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm end}(p)=

\]
such that all of the following hold:

\[

  d(y_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(i\ne k),

\[
  d(a_i,y_k)>2r_p,\qquad d(z_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(1\le i,k\le s),
\]
and, for every \(1\le i\le s\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad

  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
while \(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\), runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), satisfies
\[
  \gamma_i\subseteq B(z_i,r_p),
\]
and the paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint.  Then

\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and

\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-separated-tube-obstruction}, with the \(L^2\)-gap
conclusion supplied by Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Buffered tube obstruction]
\label{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/19\),
every
\[
  5\theta<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), a vertex
\(x\in V\), vertices
\[
  z_1,\ldots,z_t,\qquad a_1,\ldots,a_t,\qquad y_1,\ldots,y_t,
\]
and simple paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_t\) such that, with
\[
  I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}],
  \qquad
  I_{j,p}^{\rm gate}=(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
\]
with \(\sigma_j,r_p\) as in Definition~\ref{def:separated-fans}, and with
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta},
  \qquad
  t=\left\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)\right\rceil,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  d(z_i,z_k)>4r_p,\qquad
  d(a_i,a_k)>2r_p,\qquad
  d(y_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(i\ne k),
\]
\[
  d(a_i,y_k)>2r_p,\qquad d(z_i,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(1\le i,k\le t),
\]
and, for every \(1\le i\le t\),
\[
  d(x,z_i)\in I_j,\qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,\qquad
  d(x,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
\]
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm gate},
  \qquad
  y_i\in B(x,2^{j+2}+2r_p),
\]
while \(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\), runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\), satisfies
\[
  \gamma_i\subseteq B(z_i,r_p),
\]
the paths \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_t\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint, and
\[
  d(v,y_k)>2r_p
  \qquad(1\le i,k\le t,\ v\in\gamma_i).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the endpoint tube obstruction from
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-separated-tube-obstruction}, with triples indexed
by a set \(M\) of size
\[
  s=\left\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm end}(p)\right\rceil,
  \qquad
  \kappa_j^{\rm end}(p)=
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{144\Delta^7}\chiBar_p^{1-16\theta}.
\]
Form a graph \(\mathfrak E\) on the index set \(M\), joining distinct
\(i,k\in M\) if
\[
  d(z_i,y_k)\le3r_p
  \qquad\text{or}\qquad
  d(z_k,y_i)\le3r_p .
\]
For a fixed \(i\), there are at most \(\Delta^{3r_p+1}\) indices \(k\) with
\(d(z_i,y_k)\le3r_p\), and at most \(\Delta^{3r_p+1}\) indices \(k\) with
\(d(y_i,z_k)\le3r_p\).  Hence \(\mathfrak E\) has maximum degree at most
\(2\Delta^{3r_p+1}\), and a greedy independent-set extraction gives
\(M'\subseteq M\) with
\[
  |M'|\ge \frac{s}{2\Delta^{3r_p+1}+1}
  \ge \frac{s}{3\Delta^{3r_p+1}} .
\]
Since \(s\ge\kappa_j^{\rm end}(p)\) and
\(\Delta^{3r_p}\le\chiBar_p^{3\theta}\),
\[
  |M'|
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta}
  =
  \kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p).
\]
Replace \(M'\) by a subset of size
\(t=\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)\rceil\), and relabel it as
\(\{1,\ldots,t\}\).

For distinct \(i,k\), the independent-set property gives
\(d(z_i,y_k)>3r_p\).  For \(i=k\), put
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).  Since
\[
  d(z_i,y_i)>2^j-2r_p,\qquad 2^j\ge aL,\qquad r_p\le\theta L,
\]
and \(a>5\theta\), we have
\[
  d(z_i,y_i)> (a-2\theta)L>3\theta L\ge3r_p.
\]
Thus \(d(z_i,y_k)>3r_p\) for all \(i,k\).  If \(v\in\gamma_i\), then
\(d(v,z_i)\le r_p\), and hence
\[
  d(v,y_k)\ge d(z_i,y_k)-r_p>2r_p .
\]
All other displayed properties are inherited from the endpoint tube
obstruction.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}, with the \(L^2\)-gap conclusion
supplied by Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Independent path-opening count]
\label{lem:independent-path-opening-count}
Let \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_t\) be pairwise edge-disjoint simple paths, each
of length \(r\).  In Bernoulli-\(p\) percolation, let
\[
  N=\#\{1\le i\le t:\text{ every edge of }\gamma_i\text{ is open}\}.
\]
Then \(N\) is binomial with mean \(\mu=t p^r\), and
\[
  \Pp\left(N<\frac{\mu}{2}\right)\le \exp\left[-\frac{\mu}{8}\right].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The path-opening events depend on disjoint edge sets and are therefore
independent.  Each has probability \(p^r\), so \(N\sim{\rm Bin}(t,p^r)\).
The displayed inequality is the standard Chernoff lower-tail bound for a
binomial random variable.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Open buffered tube obstruction]
\label{cor:open-buffered-tube-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/20\),
every
\[
  5\theta<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, with
\[
  N_{\rm open}
  =
  \#\{1\le i\le t:\text{ every edge of }\gamma_i\text{ is open}\}
\]
and
\[
  \lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{864\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta},
\]
we have
\[
  \Pp\left(N_{\rm open}\ge \lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)\right)
  \ge
  1-\exp\left[-\frac{\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)}{4}\right].
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-degree-pc-lower}, we have \(\pc>1/\Delta\); hence
we may take \(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that every selected
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\).  Choose the buffered tube
configuration from Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}.  The paths
\(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_t\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint, hence
edge-disjoint, and each has length \(r_p\).  Thus
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-path-opening-count} applies with
\[
  \mu=t p^{r_p}.
\]
Since \(t\ge\kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)\) and
\[
  p^{r_p}\ge \Delta^{-r_p}
  \ge
  \chiBar_p^{-\theta},
\]
we have
\[
  \mu\ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}
  =
  2\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p).
\]
Consequently
\[
  \Pp\left(N_{\rm open}<\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)\right)
  \le
  \Pp\left(N_{\rm open}<\frac{\mu}{2}\right)
  \le
  \exp\left[-\frac{\mu}{8}\right]
  \le
  \exp\left[-\frac{\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)}{4}\right],
\]
as claimed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Buffered tube mass obstruction]
\label{cor:buffered-tube-mass-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/20\),
every
\[
  5\theta<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^t \tau_p(a_i,z_i)
  \ge
  \kappa_j^{\rm tube}(p),
\]
where
\[
  \kappa_j^{\rm tube}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}.  As in
the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:open-buffered-tube-obstruction}, take \(p_0\)
close enough to \(\pc\) that the selected \(p\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\), and
choose the buffered tube configuration.  For each \(i\), the path
\(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\) and runs from \(a_i\) to \(z_i\).  Therefore
\[
  \tau_p(a_i,z_i)\ge p^{r_p}\ge\Delta^{-r_p}\ge\chiBar_p^{-\theta}.
\]
Since
\[
  t\ge
  \kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta},
\]
we obtain
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^t \tau_p(a_i,z_i)
  \ge
  t\chiBar_p^{-\theta}
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Buffered tube mass criterion]
\label{prop:buffered-tube-mass-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and suppose that

Proposition~\ref{prop:buffered-tube-criterion} and the additional mass bound
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^t \tau_p(a_i,z_i)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-mass-obstruction}, with the \(L^2\)-gap
conclusion supplied by Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Open-tube scale dichotomy]
\label{cor:open-tube-scale-dichotomy}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/20\),
every
\[
  5\theta<a<\frac{1-7\theta}{2},
\]
every \(b>0\) satisfying
\[
  \rho:=1-20\theta-3\eta b>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that
\[
  2^j\ge a\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
and at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>\chiBar_p^b,
\]
or, with
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}
  =
  \frac{1}{864\Delta^8}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J},
\]
\[
  \Pp\left(
    N_{\rm open}\ge c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}\chiBar_p^\rho
  \right)
  \ge
  1-\exp\left[
    -\frac{c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}}{4}\chiBar_p^\rho
  \right].
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the configuration supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:open-buffered-tube-obstruction}.  If
\(2^j>\chiBar_p^b\), then the first alternative holds.  Otherwise
\(j\le b\log_2\chiBar_p\), and therefore
\[
  \sigma_j^3
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}\chiBar_p^{-3\eta b}.
\]
Thus
\[
  \lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{864\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}
  \ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}\chiBar_p^\rho .
\]
The second alternative follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:open-buffered-tube-obstruction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Endpoint-anchor scale dichotomy]
\label{cor:endpoint-anchor-scale-dichotomy}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/31\),
every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, writing
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j\ge aL,
\]
and at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>BL,
\]
or
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^t \tau_p(y_i,z_i)
  \ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-21\theta-2B},
\]
where
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}
  =
  \frac{1}{432\Delta^8}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}B^{-3\eta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}.  As in
the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:open-buffered-tube-obstruction}, take \(p_0\)
close enough to \(\pc\) that the selected \(p\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\), and
choose the buffered tube configuration.  Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}
already gives \(2^j\ge aL\).  If \(2^j>BL\), then the first alternative holds.
Assume therefore that \(2^j\le BL\).

For every \(i\), choose a geodesic from \(y_i\) to \(a_i\) and concatenate it
with \(\gamma_i\).  Since
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\le2^{j+1}+r_p,
  \qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p,
\]
there is a path from \(y_i\) to \(z_i\) of length at most
\(2^{j+1}+2r_p\).  Hence
\[
  \tau_p(y_i,z_i)
  \ge
  p^{2^{j+1}+2r_p}
  \ge
  \Delta^{-2^{j+1}-2r_p}
  \ge
  \chiBar_p^{-2B-2\theta}.
\]
Moreover, \(2^j\le BL\) implies
\[
  \sigma_j^3
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}(BL)^{-3\eta}.
\]
Since
\[
  t\ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta},
\]
we get
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^t \tau_p(y_i,z_i)
  \ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-21\theta-2B}.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Buffered tube logarithmic scale amplification]
\label{cor:buffered-tube-log-scale-amplification}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/29\),
every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-19\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, writing
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j>BL .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}.  Put
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}^{\rm buf}
  =
  \frac{1}{432\Delta^8}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}B^{-3\eta}.
\]
Since \(2B<1-19\theta\), choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
whenever \(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}^{\rm buf}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta}
  >
  \Delta\chiBar_p^{2B}.
\]
This is possible because \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\).

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the buffered tube configuration from
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}.  Suppose for contradiction that
\(2^j\le BL\).  Then \(j\le\log_2(BL)\), and hence
\[
  \sigma_j^3
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}(BL)^{-3\eta}.
\]
Since \(t=\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)\rceil\), this gives
\[
  t\ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}^{\rm buf}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta}.
\]
On the other hand, the vertices \(z_1,\ldots,z_t\) are distinct and satisfy
\(d(x,z_i)\le2^{j+1}\).  Bounded degree therefore gives
\[
  t\le |B(x,2^{j+1})|
  \le\Delta^{2^{j+1}+1}
  \le \Delta\chiBar_p^{2B},
\]
contradicting the choice of \(p_*\).  Thus \(2^j>BL\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Matched-count buffered scale amplification]
\label{cor:matched-count-buffered-scale-amplification}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\).  There is
\(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/19\),
every
\[
  5\theta<B<\frac{1-6\theta}{2},
\]
every
\[
  5\theta<a<\min\left\{B,\frac{1-7\theta}{2}\right\},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, writing
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j>BL .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction}.  Put
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}^{\rm match}
  =
  \frac{1}{16\Delta^3}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}B^{-3\eta}.
\]
Since \(2B<1-6\theta\), choose \(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that
whenever \(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with \(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}^{\rm match}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}
  >
  \Delta\chiBar_p^{2B}.
\]

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the matched anchored incidence obstruction
with the auxiliary lower-scale parameter \(a\).  Suppose first that
\(2^j\le BL\).  Then \(j\le\log_2(BL)\), and hence
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16\Delta^3}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}
  \ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}^{\rm match}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-6\theta}.
\]
The matched anchors \(z_1,\ldots,z_m\) are distinct and satisfy
\(d(x,z_i)\le2^{j+1}\).  Therefore
\[
  m\le |B(x,2^{j+1})|
  \le \Delta^{2^{j+1}+1}
  \le \Delta\chiBar_p^{2B},
\]
contradicting \(m=\lceil\widehat\kappa_j(p)\rceil\ge\widehat\kappa_j(p)\) and
the choice of \(p_*\).  Thus the matched obstruction has \(2^j>BL\).

Starting from this fixed matched obstruction, run the deterministic thinning
and path-selection steps in the proofs of
Corollaries~\ref{cor:separated-matched-incidence-obstruction},
\ref{cor:disjoint-gate-tube-obstruction},
\ref{cor:cross-separated-gate-tube-obstruction},
\ref{cor:endpoint-separated-tube-obstruction}, and
\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}.  These steps keep the same \(p,x,j\) and
only pass to subsets of the matched triples, adding the geodesic tubes.  The
cardinality estimates are exactly those in the cited proofs, and the
same-index separation checks use the stronger bound \(2^j>BL\) together with
\(B>5\theta\).  The resulting buffered tube configuration therefore satisfies
all conditions of Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} and still has
\(2^j>BL\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive matched-count scale amplification]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-scale-amplification}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(\omega\ge1\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Assume also that \(\omega<\Delta\).  There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for
every \(\eta>0\), every \(0<\theta<1/19\), every \(B>5\theta\) satisfying
\[
  2B\log_\Delta\omega
  <
  1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega,
\]
every
\[
  5\theta<a<B
  \quad\text{satisfying}\quad
  (2a+\theta)\log_\Delta\omega
  <
  1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta\omega,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, writing
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j>BL .
\]
In particular, if \(\Delta\ge3\), one may take \(\omega=\Delta-1\), and the
condition on \(B\) becomes
\[
  B<
  \frac{1-2\theta-4\theta\log_\Delta(\Delta-1)}
       {2\log_\Delta(\Delta-1)} .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-anchored-incidence-obstruction}.
Write
\[
  \alpha=\log_\Delta\omega,
\]
and put
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,C_{\rm vol},B}^{\rm vmatch}
  =
  \frac{1}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}B^{-3\eta}.
\]
Since \(2B\alpha<1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha\) and \(\alpha<1\), choose
\(p_*<\pc\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\) that whenever \(p\in[p_*,\pc)\), with
\(L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\),
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,C_{\rm vol},B}^{\rm vmatch}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha}
  >
  C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2B\alpha}
\]
and
\[
  \frac{1}{432C_{\rm vol}^3\Delta^5}
  \chiBar_p^{1-15\theta-4\theta\alpha}
  >
  \frac{1}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta}.
\]

Fix \(p_0\in[p_*,\pc)\), and choose the volume-sensitive matched anchored
incidence obstruction with the lower-scale parameter \(a\).  If \(2^j\le BL\),
then \(j\le\log_2(BL)\), and hence
\[
  \widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)
  \ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,C_{\rm vol},B}^{\rm vmatch}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha}.
\]
The matched anchors are distinct and lie in \(B(x,2^{j+1})\), so the
volume-growth assumption gives
\[
  m\le |B(x,2^{j+1})|
  \le C_{\rm vol}\omega^{2^{j+1}}
  \le C_{\rm vol}\chiBar_p^{2B\alpha}.
\]
This contradicts
\(m\ge\widehat\kappa_j^{\rm vol}(p)\) and the choice of \(p_*\).  Thus the
matched obstruction has \(2^j>BL\).

Now run the same deterministic thinning and path-selection steps as in the
proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:matched-count-buffered-scale-amplification}.  These
steps preserve the same \(p,x,j\), and \(B>5\theta\) supplies the same-index
separation checks needed in the later buffered-tube extraction.  The total loss
from the packing and independent-set extractions after the matched stage is at
most a factor \(27\Delta^{13r_p+5}\).  Since
\[
  m\ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{16C_{\rm vol}^3}
  \chiBar_p^{1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha}
\]
and \(\Delta^{13r_p}\le\chiBar_p^{13\theta}\), the final thinned index set has
size at least
\[
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432C_{\rm vol}^3\Delta^5}
  \chiBar_p^{1-15\theta-4\theta\alpha}.
\]
By the second near-critical choice of \(p_*\), this is at least
\(\kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)\).  Passing to an arbitrary subset of size
\(\lceil\kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)\rceil\) gives a buffered tube configuration
satisfying the conditions of Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction}, and
it retains \(2^j>BL\).

For the final assertion, when \(\Delta\ge3\) and \(R\ge0\),
\[
  |B(u,R)|
  \le
  1+\Delta\sum_{k=1}^R(\Delta-1)^{k-1}
  \le
  \left(1+\frac{\Delta}{\Delta-2}\right)(\Delta-1)^R .
\]
Thus the preceding part applies with
\(C_{\rm vol}=1+\Delta/(\Delta-2)\) and \(\omega=\Delta-1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Endpoint-anchor logarithmic alternative collapse]
\label{cor:endpoint-anchor-logarithmic-collapse}
Under the assumptions and parameter range of
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-anchor-scale-dichotomy}, the buffered tube
configuration can be chosen so that
\[
  2^j>B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
In particular, within that parameter range the second alternative in
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-anchor-scale-dichotomy} is not needed.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The parameter assumptions in
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-anchor-scale-dichotomy} give
\[
  0<\theta<1/31<1/19,
  \qquad
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2}<\frac{1-6\theta}{2},
\]
and also \(a<\min\{B,(1-7\theta)/2\}\).  Hence
Corollary~\ref{cor:matched-count-buffered-scale-amplification} applies with
the same \(a\) and \(B\), giving a buffered tube configuration satisfying
\(2^j>B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive endpoint-anchor collapse]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/31\), every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j>BL .
\]
In particular, if \(\Delta\ge3\), one may take \(\omega=\Delta-1\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Put \(\alpha=\log_\Delta\omega\).  Since \(\omega<\Delta\), we have
\(\alpha<1\).  The endpoint-anchor parameter range gives
\[
  0<\theta<1/31<1/19,
  \qquad
  B>5\theta,
  \qquad
  5\theta<a<B.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  2B\alpha<2B<1-21\theta
  <
  1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha,
\]
where the last strict inequality follows from \(\alpha<1\).  Similarly,
\[
  (2a+\theta)\alpha<2a+\theta<2B+\theta<1-20\theta
  <
  1-2\theta-4\theta\alpha .
\]
Thus all hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-scale-amplification} are satisfied,
and that corollary gives the desired buffered tube configuration with
\(2^j>BL\).

For the final assertion, when \(\Delta\ge3\), the tree-volume estimate in
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-matched-scale-amplification} applies with
\(\omega=\Delta-1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Volume-sensitive large-scale buffered-tube criterion]
\label{prop:volume-sensitive-large-scale-buffered-tube-criterion}
Let \(G\) have maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and suppose that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Suppose that for every \(0<\epsilon\le1\) there exist \(\eta>0\),
\(0<\theta<1/31\),
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
integers \(J,H\ge0\), and \(p_1<\pc\) such that no \(p\in[p_1,\pc)\) admits an
integer \(j>J+H\) and a buffered tube configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} and
\[
  2^j>B\log_\Delta\chiBar_p .
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
This is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}, with the
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive large-scale open buffered tube obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-large-scale-open-buffered-tube-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/31\), every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  2^j>BL,
\]
and, with
\[
  N_{\rm open}
  =
  \#\{1\le i\le t:\text{ every edge of }\gamma_i\text{ is open}\}
\]
and
\[
  \lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{864\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta},
\]
we have
\[
  \Pp\left(N_{\rm open}\ge \lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)\right)
  \ge
  1-\exp\left[-\frac{\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)}{4}\right].
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-degree-pc-lower}, we have \(\pc>1/\Delta\); hence we may
take \(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\) that every selected \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\)
satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\).  Choose the large-scale buffered tube configuration
from Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}.  The paths
\(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_t\) are pairwise vertex-disjoint, hence edge-disjoint,
and each has length \(r_p\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-path-opening-count}
therefore applies with
\[
  \mu=t p^{r_p}.
\]
Since \(t\ge\kappa_j^{\rm buf}(p)\) and
\[
  p^{r_p}\ge\Delta^{-r_p}\ge\chiBar_p^{-\theta},
\]
we have
\[
  \mu
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}
  =
  2\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p).
\]
Consequently
\[
  \Pp\left(N_{\rm open}<\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)\right)
  \le
  \Pp\left(N_{\rm open}<\frac{\mu}{2}\right)
  \le
  \exp\left[-\frac{\mu}{8}\right]
  \le
  \exp\left[-\frac{\lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)}{4}\right].
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive large-scale open-tube dichotomy]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-large-scale-open-tube-dichotomy}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/31\), every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
every \(b>0\) satisfying
\[
  \rho:=1-20\theta-3\eta b>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  2^j>BL,
\]
and at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>\chiBar_p^b,
\]
or, with
\[
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}
  =
  \frac{1}{864\Delta^8}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J},
\]
\[
  \Pp\left(
    N_{\rm open}\ge c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}\chiBar_p^\rho
  \right)
  \ge
  1-\exp\left[
    -\frac{c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}}{4}\chiBar_p^\rho
  \right].
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the configuration supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-large-scale-open-buffered-tube-obstruction}.
It already satisfies \(2^j>BL\).  If \(2^j>\chiBar_p^b\), then the first
alternative holds.  Otherwise \(j\le b\log_2\chiBar_p\), and hence
\[
  \sigma_j^3
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}\chiBar_p^{-3\eta b}.
\]
Therefore
\[
  \lambda_j^{\rm open}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{864\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}
  \ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}\chiBar_p^\rho.
\]
The second alternative now follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-large-scale-open-buffered-tube-obstruction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive large-scale tube-mass dichotomy]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-large-scale-tube-mass-dichotomy}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/31\), every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
every \(b>0\) satisfying
\[
  \rho:=1-20\theta-3\eta b>0,
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
\]
\[
  2^j>BL,
\]
and at least one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
  2^j>\chiBar_p^b,
\]
or, with
\[
  d_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}
  =
  \frac{1}{432\Delta^8}
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J},
\]
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^t\tau_p(a_i,z_i)
  \ge
  d_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}\chiBar_p^\rho .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-degree-pc-lower}, take \(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\)
that every selected \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\).  Choose the
large-scale buffered tube configuration from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}.  It already
satisfies \(2^j>BL\).  If \(2^j>\chiBar_p^b\), then the first alternative
holds, so assume \(2^j\le\chiBar_p^b\).  Then
\[
  j\le b\log_2\chiBar_p
\]
and hence
\[
  \sigma_j^3
  \ge
  \left[\frac{\epsilon}{2}(1-2^{-\eta/2})^2\right]^3
  2^{3\eta J}\chiBar_p^{-3\eta b}.
\]
For every \(i\), the path \(\gamma_i\) has length \(r_p\) and joins \(a_i\) to
\(z_i\), so
\[
  \tau_p(a_i,z_i)\ge p^{r_p}\ge\Delta^{-r_p}\ge\chiBar_p^{-\theta}.
\]
Since the buffered tube configuration has
\[
  t\ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-19\theta},
\]
we get
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^t\tau_p(a_i,z_i)
  \ge
  \frac{\sigma_j^3}{432\Delta^8}\chiBar_p^{1-20\theta}
  \ge
  d_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta}\chiBar_p^\rho .
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Endpoint-anchor annular mass dichotomy]
\label{cor:endpoint-anchor-annular-mass-dichotomy}
Under the assumptions and notation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-anchor-scale-dichotomy}, the same conclusion
remains valid if the second alternative is replaced by the stronger
distance-localized alternative
\[
  \sum_{\substack{1\le i\le t\\ d(y_i,z_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm ea}}}
  \tau_p(y_i,z_i)
  =
  \sum_{i=1}^t \tau_p(y_i,z_i)
  \ge
  c_{\epsilon,\eta,J,\Delta,B}
  L^{-3\eta}\chiBar_p^{1-21\theta-2B},
\]
where
\[
  I_{j,p}^{\rm ea}=(2^j-2r_p,2^{j+1}+2r_p].
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the data supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-anchor-scale-dichotomy}.  If \(2^j>BL\), then
the first alternative holds, so assume the second alternative in that
corollary holds.  For every \(i\), the buffered tube configuration gives
\[
  d(y_i,a_i)\in(2^j-r_p,2^{j+1}+r_p],
  \qquad
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p.
\]
Therefore
\[
  d(y_i,z_i)\ge d(y_i,a_i)-d(a_i,z_i)>2^j-2r_p
\]
and
\[
  d(y_i,z_i)\le d(y_i,a_i)+d(a_i,z_i)\le2^{j+1}+2r_p.
\]
Thus \(d(y_i,z_i)\in I_{j,p}^{\rm ea}\) for every \(i\), and the
distance-localized lower bound is exactly the second lower bound from
Corollary~\ref{cor:endpoint-anchor-scale-dichotomy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Annular crossing mass]
\label{def:annular-crossing-mass}
For finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), a set \(Z\subseteq V\), and
\(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), define
\[
  \mathcal B_p^I(K,Z)
  =
  \frac1{|K|}
  \sum_{z\in Z}
  \sum_{\substack{x\in K\\d(x,z)\in I}}Q_p(x,z).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Weighted annular crossing obstruction]
\label{prop:weighted-crossing-obstruction}
Let \(G\) have bounded degree, and suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as
\(p\uparrow\pc\).  If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0,
\]
then there is \(\epsilon>0\) such that for every \(0<\alpha<\beta\), every
integer \(J\ge0\), and every \(p_0<\pc\), there are
\(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), and sets
\(Z_j\subset V\), \(j\ge J\), such that \(|K|>2\epsilon\chiBar_p\), and
\[
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{(\alpha+\beta)(j-J)}
  \mathcal B_p^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}(K,Z_j)
  \ge
  \frac{\epsilon^2}{4}(1-2^{-\alpha})^2(1-2^{\alpha-\beta}) .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Use the same \(\epsilon\), \(p\), \(K\), and thresholds \(\lambda_j\) as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:weighted-root-layer-obstruction}, and set
\[
  Z_j=Z_p^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}(K,\lambda_j).
\]
For every \(j\ge J\), the definition of \(Z_j\) gives
\[
  \mathcal B_p^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}(K,Z_j)
  \ge
  \lambda_j\frac{|Z_j|}{|K|}.
\]
Writing \(c=(1-2^{-\alpha})\epsilon\), we have
\[
  \lambda_j=\frac{c}{2}(1-2^{\alpha-\beta})2^{-\beta(j-J)}
\]
and Proposition~\ref{prop:weighted-root-layer-obstruction} gives
\[
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \frac{|Z_j|}{|K|}
  \ge \frac{c}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{(\alpha+\beta)(j-J)}
  \mathcal B_p^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}(K,Z_j)
  &\ge
  \frac{c}{2}(1-2^{\alpha-\beta})
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \frac{|Z_j|}{|K|}  \\
  &\ge
  \frac{c^2}{4}(1-2^{\alpha-\beta}),
\end{aligned}
\]
which is the desired bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Annular two-point operators]
\label{def:annular-two-point-operator}
For \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), define
\[
  T_p^I(x,y)=\tau_p(x,y)\mathbf 1\{d(x,y)\in I\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Separated pairs lower bound annular operators]
\label{lem:separated-pairs-annular-operator-lower-bound}
Let \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\), let \(p<\pc\), and let
\[
  u_1,\ldots,u_m,\qquad v_1,\ldots,v_m
\]
be vertices such that the \(u_i\)'s are distinct, the \(v_i\)'s are distinct,
and \(d(u_i,v_i)\in I\) for every \(1\le i\le m\).  Then
\[
  \norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  \frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\tau_p(u_i,v_i)
\]
and
\[
  \Theta_p(I)
  \ge
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p^2m}\sum_{i=1}^m\tau_p(u_i,v_i)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Put \(U=\{u_1,\ldots,u_m\}\) and \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\).  Since both sets
have size \(m\), the vectors \(\mathbf 1_U/\sqrt m\) and
\(\mathbf 1_V/\sqrt m\) have norm one.  Positivity gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}
  &\ge
  \frac1m\ip{\mathbf 1_V}{T_p^I\mathbf 1_U}  \\
  &=
  \frac1m
  \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{k=1}^m
  \tau_p(u_k,v_i)\mathbf 1\{d(u_k,v_i)\in I\}  \\
  &\ge
  \frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\tau_p(u_i,v_i).
\end{aligned}
\]
For the square-profile bound, use \(K=U\) in
Definition~\ref{def:annular-square-profile}.  At the distinct vertices
\(v_i\), the summand contains the diagonal contribution
\(\tau_p(u_i,v_i)\).  Hence
\[
  \mathcal R_p^I(U)
  \ge
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p m}
  \sum_{i=1}^m\tau_p(u_i,v_i)^2 .
\]
Dividing by \(\chiBar_p\) and taking the supremum over finite \(K\) gives the
displayed lower bound for \(\Theta_p(I)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive gate-shell operator obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-shell-operator-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are
constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and \(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/31\), every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  I_p^{\rm tube}=\{r_p\},
\]
we have
\[
  2^j>BL,
\]
\[
  \norm{T_p^{I_p^{\rm tube}}}_{2\to2}\ge\chiBar_p^{-\theta},
\]
and
\[
  \Theta_p(I_p^{\rm tube})\ge\chiBar_p^{-2-2\theta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the \(\epsilon\) from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded-degree-pc-lower}, take \(p_0\) close enough to \(\pc\)
that every selected \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) satisfies \(p\ge1/\Delta\).  Choose the
large-scale buffered tube configuration from
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse}.  It satisfies
\(2^j>BL\).  The vertices \(a_1,\ldots,a_t\) are distinct and
\(z_1,\ldots,z_t\) are distinct by the separation conditions, and
\[
  d(a_i,z_i)=r_p\qquad(1\le i\le t).
\]
Moreover each \(\gamma_i\) is a path of length \(r_p\) from \(a_i\) to
\(z_i\), so
\[
  \tau_p(a_i,z_i)\ge p^{r_p}\ge\Delta^{-r_p}\ge\chiBar_p^{-\theta}.
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:separated-pairs-annular-operator-lower-bound} with
\(u_i=a_i\), \(v_i=z_i\), and \(I=I_p^{\rm tube}\).  The operator lower bound
follows from the average lower bound on the \(\tau_p(a_i,z_i)\)'s, and the
square-profile lower bound follows from
\[
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p^2t}\sum_{i=1}^t\tau_p(a_i,z_i)^2
  \ge
  \chiBar_p^{-2-2\theta}.
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Annular operator control]
\label{lem:annular-operator-control}
For every \(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\) and every \(p<\pc\),
\[
  \Theta_p(I)
  \le
  \left(\frac{\norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}\right)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For every finite non-empty \(K\),
\[
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^I(K)}{\chiBar_p}
  =
  \frac{\norm{T_p^I\mathbf 1_K}_2^2}{\chiBar_p^2|K|}
  \le
  \left(\frac{\norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}\right)^2 .
\]
Taking the supremum over \(K\) gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic annular operator criterion]
\label{cor:dyadic-annular-operator}
Let \(G\) have bounded degree, and suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as
\(p\uparrow\pc\).  For \(j\ge J\), let \(I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}]\).  Suppose that
for some \(\alpha>0\),
\[
  \lim_{J\to\infty}
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \left(\frac{\norm{T_p^{I_j}}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}\right)^2
  =0.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The displayed assumption and Lemma~\ref{lem:annular-operator-control} imply
the hypothesis of Corollary~\ref{cor:dyadic-annular-far-leg}.  Hence
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).  Under the additional hypotheses, the
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Pointwise shell control of annular operators]
\label{lem:pointwise-annular-operator-control}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite.  For every
\(I\subseteq[0,\infty)\) and every \(p<\pc\),
\[
  \norm{T_p^I}_{2\to2}
  \le
  \sum_{n\in I\cap\mathbb N}\tau_p^{\max}(n)\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2},
\]
with the convention that the right-hand side may be infinite.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For \(n\ge0\), let
\[
  H_{p,n}(x,y)=\tau_p(x,y)\mathbf 1\{d(x,y)=n\}.
\]
Then \(0\le H_{p,n}\le \tau_p^{\max}(n)S_n^G\) entrywise.  Positivity gives
\[
  \norm{H_{p,n}}_{2\to2}
  \le
  \tau_p^{\max}(n)\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}.
\]
Since \(T_p^I=\sum_{n\in I\cap\mathbb N}H_{p,n}\) pointwise, the triangle
inequality in operator norm gives the claim, first for finite sums and then
by monotone convergence of positive kernels.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive logarithmic shell-growth obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-growth-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) is connected and locally finite, has maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
There is \(0<\epsilon\le1\) such that for every \(\eta>0\), every
\(0<\theta<1/31\), every
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
every pair of integers \(J,H\ge0\), and all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), there are \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\), an integer \(j>J+H\), and a buffered tube
configuration satisfying the conditions of
Corollary~\ref{cor:buffered-tube-obstruction} such that, with
\[
  L=\log_\Delta\chiBar_p,
  \qquad
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta L\right\rfloor,
\]
we have
\[
  2^j>BL
\]
and
\[
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \ge
  \chiBar_p^{-\theta}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose the configuration supplied by
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-gate-shell-operator-obstruction}.  It
satisfies \(2^j>BL\) and
\[
  \norm{T_p^{\{r_p\}}}_{2\to2}\ge\chiBar_p^{-\theta}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:pointwise-annular-operator-control}, applied to
\(I=\{r_p\}\), gives
\[
  \norm{T_p^{\{r_p\}}}_{2\to2}
  \le
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}.
\]
Combining the two inequalities proves the shell-growth lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Volume-sensitive logarithmic shell-growth criterion]
\label{prop:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-growth-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
If there exists \(0<\theta<1/31\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \chiBar_p^\theta
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  <1,
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We prove the first claim by contraposition.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0.
\]
Choose \(a,B\) with
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2},
\]
which is possible since \(\theta<1/31\), and fix arbitrary \(\eta>0\) and
integers \(J,H\ge0\).
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-growth-obstruction} then
gives, for every \(p_0\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), some \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\)
such that
\[
  \chiBar_p^\theta
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \ge 1 .
\]
Hence the displayed limsup is at least \(1\), contradicting the hypothesis.
Thus \(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

Under the additional quasi-transitivity and mean-field susceptibility
assumptions, the \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-sensitive logarithmic shell exponent obstruction]
\label{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-exponent-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) is connected and locally finite, has maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
For every \(0<\theta<1/31\), if
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
then
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \ge
  \Delta^{-1}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(0<\theta<1/31\), and choose \(a,B\) with
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2}.
\]
Apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-growth-obstruction} with
arbitrary \(\eta>0\) and \(J=H=0\).  For all \(p_0\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\), it gives some \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\) such that, with
\[
  A_p=\tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2},
\]
we have
\[
  A_p\ge\chiBar_p^{-\theta}.
\]
Letting \(p_0\uparrow\pc\) and choosing one such \(p\) for each \(p_0\) gives a
sequence \(p_n\uparrow\pc\).  Since \(\chiBar_{p_n}\to\infty\),
\[
  \frac{r_{p_n}}{\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_{p_n}}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Along this sequence,
\[
  A_{p_n}^{1/r_{p_n}}
  \ge
  \chiBar_{p_n}^{-\theta/r_{p_n}}
  \longrightarrow
  \Delta^{-1}.
\]
This proves the displayed limsup lower bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Volume-sensitive logarithmic shell exponent criterion]
\label{prop:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-exponent-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
If there exists \(0<\theta<1/31\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  <
  \Delta^{-1},
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We prove the first claim by contraposition.  If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0,
\]
then Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-exponent-obstruction}
gives
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \ge
  \Delta^{-1},
\]
contradicting the hypothesis.  Therefore
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

Under the additional quasi-transitivity and mean-field susceptibility
assumptions, the \(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Factored logarithmic shell exponent criterion]
\label{prop:factored-logarithmic-shell-exponent-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Suppose that there exist \(0<\theta<1/31\) and positive constants
\(\alpha,\rho\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}<\alpha,
  \qquad
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}^{1/r_p}<\rho,
\]
and
\[
  \alpha\rho<\Delta^{-1}.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\), the two displayed limsup assumptions
give
\[
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}\le\alpha,
  \qquad
  \norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}^{1/r_p}\le\rho .
\]
