Consequently
\[
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \le
  \alpha\rho
  <
  \Delta^{-1}.
\]
The first conclusion follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:volume-sensitive-logarithmic-shell-exponent-criterion}.
The \(L^2\)-gap conclusion again follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Volume-growth pointwise logarithmic decay criterion]
\label{cor:volume-growth-pointwise-logarithmic-decay-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
If there exists \(0<\theta<1/31\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}
  <
  \frac{1}{\Delta\omega},
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The sphere kernel \(S_n^G\) is symmetric and every row sum is
\[
  |\{v\in V:d(u,v)=n\}|
  \le
  |B(u,n)|
  \le C_{\rm vol}\omega^n .
\]
Schur's test therefore gives
\[
  \norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^n
  \qquad(n\ge0),
\]
and hence
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}^{1/r_p}
  \le
  \omega .
\]
Choose \(\alpha\) and \(\rho\) such that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}<\alpha,
  \qquad
  \omega<\rho,
  \qquad
  \alpha\rho<\Delta^{-1}.
\]
This is possible by the strict pointwise-decay hypothesis.  The result follows
from Proposition~\ref{prop:factored-logarithmic-shell-exponent-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Critical logarithmic shell exponent obstruction]
\label{cor:critical-logarithmic-shell-exponent-obstruction}
Under the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:single-remote-annulus-obstruction}, suppose in addition
that \(G\) is connected and locally finite, has maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), and that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
For every \(0<\theta<1/31\), if
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
then
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \ge
  \pc .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(0<\theta<1/31\) and \(q<\pc\).  Choose \(a,B\) with
\[
  5\theta<a<B<\frac{1-21\theta}{2}.
\]
Let \(p_0<\pc\) be close enough to \(\pc\) that \(p_0\ge q\) and that
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-sensitive-endpoint-anchor-collapse} applies with,
say, \(\eta=1\) and \(J=H=0\).  Choose the resulting large-scale buffered tube
configuration.  The vertices \(a_1,\ldots,a_t\) are distinct, the vertices
\(z_1,\ldots,z_t\) are distinct, and \(d(a_i,z_i)=r_p\).  Since
\(p\ge p_0\ge q\), each tube path gives
\[
  \tau_p(a_i,z_i)\ge p^{r_p}\ge q^{r_p}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:separated-pairs-annular-operator-lower-bound}, applied with
\(I=\{r_p\}\), gives
\[
  \norm{T_p^{\{r_p\}}}_{2\to2}\ge q^{r_p}.
\]
The pointwise shell-control lemma gives
\[
  \norm{T_p^{\{r_p\}}}_{2\to2}
  \le
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2},
\]
and hence
\[
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \ge q .
\]
Letting \(p_0\uparrow\pc\) produces a sequence \(p\uparrow\pc\), and then
letting \(q\uparrow\pc\) proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Critical logarithmic shell exponent criterion]
\label{prop:critical-logarithmic-shell-exponent-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
If there exists \(0<\theta<1/31\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  <
  \pc,
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first claim is the contrapositive of
Corollary~\ref{cor:critical-logarithmic-shell-exponent-obstruction}.  The
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Critical factored logarithmic shell criterion]
\label{prop:critical-factored-logarithmic-shell-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Suppose that there exist \(0<\theta<1/31\) and positive constants
\(\alpha,\rho\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}<\alpha,
  \qquad
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}^{1/r_p}<\rho,
\]
and
\[
  \alpha\rho<\pc.
\]
Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For \(p\) sufficiently close to \(\pc\),
\[
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \le \alpha\rho<\pc .
\]
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:critical-logarithmic-shell-exponent-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spherical obstruction]
\label{cor:critical-spherical-radius-pointwise-obstruction}
Assume the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:critical-logarithmic-shell-exponent-obstruction}.  Define
\[
  \rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)
  =
  \limsup_{n\to\infty}\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}^{1/n}.
\]
For every \(0<\theta<1/31\), if
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
then
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}
  \ge
  \frac{\pc}{\rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)} .
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(L\) denote the limsup on the left-hand side, and fix
\(\rho>\rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)\).  Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\), we have
\(r_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  Hence, for \(p\) sufficiently close to
\(\pc\),
\[
  \norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}\le \rho^{r_p}.
\]
Therefore
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \le
  \rho L .
\]
Corollary~\ref{cor:critical-logarithmic-shell-exponent-obstruction} gives the
opposite lower bound \(\pc\) for this product limsup, so \(L\ge \pc/\rho\).
Letting \(\rho\downarrow\rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)\) proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spherical logarithmic criterion]
\label{cor:critical-spherical-radius-pointwise-logarithmic-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
Define
\[
  \rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)
  =
  \limsup_{n\to\infty}\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}^{1/n}.
\]
If there exists \(0<\theta<1/31\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}
  <
  \frac{\pc}{\rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)},
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(\alpha,\rho>0\) such that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}<\alpha,
  \qquad
  \rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)<\rho,
  \qquad
  \alpha\rho<\pc .
\]
Since \(r_p\to\infty\),
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}^{1/r_p}
  \le
  \rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)
  <\rho .
\]
The result follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:critical-factored-logarithmic-shell-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Critical volume-growth pointwise logarithmic decay criterion]
\label{cor:critical-volume-growth-pointwise-logarithmic-decay-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite with maximum degree at most
\(\Delta\ge2\), suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), and
suppose that there are constants \(C_{\rm vol}<\infty\) and
\(1\le\omega<\Delta\) such that
\[
  |B(u,R)|\le C_{\rm vol}\omega^R
  \qquad(u\in V,\ R\ge0).
\]
If there exists \(0<\theta<1/31\) such that, with
\[
  r_p=\left\lfloor\theta\log_\Delta\chiBar_p\right\rfloor,
\]
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}
  <
  \frac{\pc}{\omega},
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
As in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:volume-growth-pointwise-logarithmic-decay-criterion},
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}^{1/r_p}
  \le \omega .
\]
Choose \(\alpha,\rho>0\) such that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}<\alpha,
  \qquad
  \omega<\rho,
  \qquad
  \alpha\rho<\pc .
\]
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:critical-factored-logarithmic-shell-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Geodesic lower-bound audit]
\label{prop:geodesic-lower-bound-pointwise-audit}
Let \(G\) be an infinite connected locally finite graph.  For every
\(n\ge0\) and every \(p\in[0,1]\),
\[
  \tau_p^{\max}(n)\ge p^n,
  \qquad
  \norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}\ge1.
\]
Consequently, if \(r_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), then
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}
  \ge \pc
\]
and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \ge \pc .
\]
In particular, the strict product hypothesis in
Proposition~\ref{prop:critical-logarithmic-shell-exponent-criterion} is never
satisfied on an infinite graph.  Since
\(\rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)\ge1\) and every admissible volume-growth constant
\(\omega\) in the criteria above satisfies \(\omega\ge1\), the strict
pointwise hypotheses in
Corollaries~\ref{cor:critical-spherical-radius-pointwise-logarithmic-criterion}
and~\ref{cor:critical-volume-growth-pointwise-logarithmic-decay-criterion} are
also never satisfied.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(n\).  Since \(G\) is infinite, connected, and locally finite, every
vertex has some vertex at distance \(n\).  If \(d(x,y)=n\), then any fixed
geodesic from \(x\) to \(y\) is open with probability \(p^n\), and this event
implies \(x\leftrightarrow y\).  Hence
\(\tau_p^{\max}(n)\ge p^n\).

For the sphere kernel, choose \(x\) with \(S_n(x)\ne\varnothing\).  Then
\[
  \norm{S_n^G\mathbf 1_{\{x\}}}_2
  =
  |S_n(x)|^{1/2}
  \ge1,
\]
so \(\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}\ge1\).  Applying these two bounds with
\(n=r_p\) gives
\[
  \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)^{1/r_p}\ge p,
  \qquad
  \left(
    \tau_p^{\max}(r_p)\norm{S_{r_p}^G}_{2\to2}
  \right)^{1/r_p}
  \ge p.
\]
Taking \(p\uparrow\pc\) proves the two limsup lower bounds.

The final assertions follow immediately.  The product criterion asks for a
strict upper bound below \(\pc\), contradicting the product lower bound.  The
spherical and volume-growth pointwise criteria ask for strict upper bounds
below \(\pc/\rho_{\mathrm{sph},2}(G)\) and \(\pc/\omega\), respectively; these
thresholds are at most \(\pc\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Proposition~\ref{prop:geodesic-lower-bound-pointwise-audit} is a warning about
loss of information in the pointwise supremum.  The preceding obstruction
statements remain true, but after replacing the structured endpoint
configuration by \(\tau_p^{\max}\), the resulting strict criteria are vacuous.
A viable proof must keep some averaged, localized, or matched-pair information
from the finite-set obstruction rather than trying to beat the open-geodesic
lower bound for the worst pair at distance \(r_p\).
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Pointwise dyadic annular criterion]
\label{cor:pointwise-dyadic-annular}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and of bounded
degree, and suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty .
\]
For \(j\ge J\), put \(I_j=(2^j,2^{j+1}]\).  If for some \(\alpha>0\),
\[
  \lim_{J\to\infty}
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \left(
    \frac{
      \sum_{n\in I_j\cap\mathbb N}
      \tau_p^{\max}(n)\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}
    }{\chiBar_p}
  \right)^2
  =0,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:pointwise-annular-operator-control} implies the hypothesis of
Corollary~\ref{cor:dyadic-annular-operator}.  Since quasi-transitivity gives
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), that corollary gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic operator obstruction]
\label{cor:dyadic-operator-obstruction}
Let \(G\) have bounded degree, and suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as
\(p\uparrow\pc\).  If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}>0,
\]
then there is \(\epsilon>0\) such that for every \(\alpha>0\),
\[
  \liminf_{J\to\infty}
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \left(\frac{\norm{T_p^{(2^j,2^{j+1}]}}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}\right)^2
  \ge (1-2^{-\alpha})\epsilon .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is connected and locally finite, then
\[
  \liminf_{J\to\infty}
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \sum_{j\ge J}2^{\alpha(j-J)}
  \left(
    \frac{
      \sum_{2^j<n\le 2^{j+1}}
      \tau_p^{\max}(n)\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}
    }{\chiBar_p}
  \right)^2
  \ge (1-2^{-\alpha})\epsilon
\]
for every \(\alpha>0\).  In particular, the two displayed obstructions hold
if \(G\) is connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and of bounded degree,
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
and \(\pc(G)=p_{2\to2}(G)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first lower bound follows by combining
Proposition~\ref{prop:dyadic-annular-obstruction} with
Lemma~\ref{lem:annular-operator-control}.  The pointwise shell lower bound
then follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:pointwise-annular-operator-control}.

For the final assertion, quasi-transitivity gives
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  If
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\), then
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion} gives
\(\pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)\), contradicting \(\pc(G)=p_{2\to2}(G)\).  Hence the
hypothesis of the first part holds.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Critical shell summability gives far-leg tightness]
\label{prop:critical-shell-gives-far-leg}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, and of bounded degree, and suppose
that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  If
\[
  \sum_{n\ge0}\tau_{\pc}^{\max}(n)\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
If, in addition, \(G\) is quasi-transitive and
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For \(p<\pc\), monotonicity gives
\(\tau_p^{\max}(n)\le\tau_{\pc}^{\max}(n)\).  Hence
Lemma~\ref{lem:pointwise-annular-operator-control}, applied to
\((R,\infty)\), gives
\[
  \norm{T_p^{(R,\infty)}}_{2\to2}
  \le
  \sum_{n>R}\tau_{\pc}^{\max}(n)\norm{S_n^G}_{2\to2}.
\]
The right-hand side tends to zero as \(R\to\infty\), uniformly in \(p<\pc\).
For every finite non-empty \(K\),
\[
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{>R}(K)}{\chiBar_p}
  =
  \frac{\norm{T_p^{(R,\infty)}\mathbf 1_K}_2^2}{\chiBar_p^2|K|}
  \le
  \left(
    \frac{\norm{T_p^{(R,\infty)}}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}
  \right)^2 .
\]
Since \(\chiBar_p\ge1\), it follows that
\(\lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\Theta_p(R)=0\).  The tail-limit
criterion, Corollary~\ref{cor:far-leg-tail-limit}, gives
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).

Under the additional quasi-transitivity and mean-field assumptions, the
\(L^2\)-gap conclusion follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sublinear two-replica finite-set criterion]
\label{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, and quasi-transitive.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty
\]
and
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\frac{\mathcal R_p^*}{\chiBar_p}=0 .
\]
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Proposition~\ref{prop:fe-iff-sublinear-two-replica} gives finite-set escape,
and the first assumption is the mean-field susceptibility input
\eqref{eq:mf}.  The conclusion follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:hutchcroft-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Far-leg tightness criterion for an \(L^2\) gap]
\label{cor:far-leg-tightness-l2-gap}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and of bounded
degree.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty
\]
and that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  For \(R<\infty\), let
\(\Theta_p(R)\) be as in Proposition~\ref{prop:far-leg-square-criterion}.
If for every \(\delta>0\) there are \(R<\infty\) and \(p_0<\pc\) such that
\[
  \Theta_p(R)\le\delta\qquad(p\in[p_0,\pc)),
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Proposition~\ref{prop:far-leg-square-criterion} gives
\(\mathcal R_p^*/\chiBar_p\to0\).  The conclusion then follows from
Corollary~\ref{cor:sublinear-two-replica-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Operator tail criterion]
\label{cor:operator-tail-l2-gap}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and of bounded
degree.  Suppose that
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty
\]
and that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  For \(R<\infty\), define
the truncated two-point operator
\[
  T_p^{>R}(x,y)=\tau_p(x,y)\mathbf 1\{d(x,y)>R\}.
\]
If
\[
  \lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{\norm{T_p^{>R}}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}=0,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For every finite non-empty \(K\),
\[
  \frac{\mathcal R_p^{>R}(K)}{\chiBar_p}
  =
  \frac{\norm{T_p^{>R}\mathbf 1_K}_2^2}{\chiBar_p^2|K|}
  \le
  \left(
    \frac{\norm{T_p^{>R}}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}
  \right)^2 .
\]
Taking the supremum over \(K\) gives the same bound on \(\Theta_p(R)\).  The
operator-tail assumption therefore implies the far-leg tightness hypothesis in
Corollary~\ref{cor:far-leg-tightness-l2-gap}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shell operator tail criterion]
\label{cor:shell-operator-tail-l2-gap}
Let \(G\) satisfy the assumptions of Corollary~\ref{cor:operator-tail-l2-gap}.
For \(n\ge0\), define the exact-distance two-point shell
\[
  H_{p,n}(x,y)=\tau_p(x,y)\mathbf 1\{d(x,y)=n\}.
\]
If
\[
  \lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p}
  \sum_{n>R}\norm{H_{p,n}}_{2\to2}=0,
\]
then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For every \(R\),
\[
  T_p^{>R}=\sum_{n>R}H_{p,n}
\]
pointwise.  Hence, by the triangle inequality in operator norm,
\[
  \norm{T_p^{>R}}_{2\to2}
  \le
  \sum_{n>R}\norm{H_{p,n}}_{2\to2},
\]
with the inequality understood as trivial if the right-hand side is infinite.
The assumed shell-tail estimate implies the hypothesis of
Corollary~\ref{cor:operator-tail-l2-gap}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Self-avoiding shell tails]
\label{prop:saw-shell-tail}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, and of bounded degree, and suppose
that
\[
  \gamma_{\mathrm{SAW},2}(G)<1/\pc(G).
\]
Then the exact-distance two-point shells from
Corollary~\ref{cor:shell-operator-tail-l2-gap} satisfy
\[
  \lim_{R\to\infty}
  \sup_{0\le p<\pc}
  \sum_{n>R}\norm{H_{p,n}}_{2\to2}=0.
\]
In particular, if \(G\) also satisfies the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:shell-operator-tail-l2-gap}, then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(\theta\) such that
\(\gamma_{\mathrm{SAW},2}<\theta<1/\pc\).  By the definition of
\(\gamma_{\mathrm{SAW},2}\), there is \(A<\infty\) such that
\[
  \norm{C_m}_{2\to2}\le A\theta^m
  \qquad(m\ge0),
\]
where \(C_m\) is the length-\(m\) self-avoiding endpoint kernel.

If \(d(x,y)=n\) and \(x\leftrightarrow y\), then the open cluster contains an
open self-avoiding path from \(x\) to \(y\) of some length \(m\ge n\).  The
union bound gives the entrywise estimate
\[
  H_{p,n}(x,y)
  \le
  \sum_{m\ge n}p^mC_m(x,y).
\]
Since all kernels are nonnegative, entrywise domination implies domination of
\(\ell^2\) operator norms.  Thus for \(p<\pc\),
\[
  \norm{H_{p,n}}_{2\to2}
  \le
  A\sum_{m\ge n}(p\theta)^m.
\]
Summing over \(n>R\) and using \(p\theta\le\pc\theta<1\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \sum_{n>R}\norm{H_{p,n}}_{2\to2}
  &\le
  A\sum_{n>R}\sum_{m\ge n}(p\theta)^m       \\
  &\le
  A\sum_{m>R}(m-R)(\pc\theta)^m .
\end{aligned}
\]
The final tail tends to zero as \(R\to\infty\), uniformly over \(p<\pc\).
Since \(\chiBar_p\ge1\), the shell-tail hypothesis of
Corollary~\ref{cor:shell-operator-tail-l2-gap} follows whenever its remaining
assumptions hold.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two-replica cluster interpretation]
\label{lem:two-replica-cluster-interpretation}
Let \(\omega_1,\omega_2\) be two independent Bernoulli-\(p\) percolation
configurations, and let \(C_i(z)\) be the open cluster of \(z\) in
\(\omega_i\).  Then, for every finite non-empty \(K\subset V\),
\[
  \chiBar_p|K|\,\mathcal R_p(K)
  =
  \sum_{z\in V}
  \mathbb E_p^{\otimes2}
  \bigl[
    |K\cap C_1(z)|\,|K\cap C_2(z)|
  \bigr],
\]
with equality in \([0,\infty]\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Expanding the square and using independence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \sum_{z\in V}
  \mathbb E_p^{\otimes2}
  \bigl[
    |K\cap C_1(z)|\,|K\cap C_2(z)|
  \bigr]
  &=
  \sum_{z\in V}\sum_{x,y\in K}
  \mathbb P_p(x\leftrightarrow z)\mathbb P_p(y\leftrightarrow z) \\
  &=
  \sum_{z\in V}\left(\sum_{x\in K}\tau_p(x,z)\right)^2 .
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the defining numerator of \(\mathcal R_p(K)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Far-leg cluster interpretation]
\label{lem:far-leg-cluster-interpretation}
Let \(\omega_1,\omega_2\) and \(C_i(z)\) be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:two-replica-cluster-interpretation}.  Then, for every
\(R<\infty\) and every finite non-empty \(K\subset V\),
\[
  \chiBar_p|K|\,\mathcal R_p^{>R}(K)
  =
  \sum_{z\in V}
  \mathbb E_p^{\otimes2}
  \bigl[
    |(K\setminus B(z,R))\cap C_1(z)|\,
    |(K\setminus B(z,R))\cap C_2(z)|
  \bigr],
\]
with equality in \([0,\infty]\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For fixed \(z\), independence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\mathbb E_p^{\otimes2}
  \bigl[
    |(K\setminus B(z,R))\cap C_1(z)|\,
    |(K\setminus B(z,R))\cap C_2(z)|
  \bigr]  \\
  &\qquad =
  \left(
    \sum_{\substack{x\in K\\ d(x,z)>R}}\tau_p(x,z)
  \right)^2 .
\end{aligned}
\]
Summing over \(z\) gives the defining numerator of
\(\mathcal R_p^{>R}(K)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Two-replica profile controls finite-set growth]
\label{prop:two-replica-differential}
Assume \(G\) has maximum degree at most \(\Delta<\infty\).  Let
\[
  S_p^{\mathrm{amb}}(K)=\sum_{x,y\in K}\tau_p(x,y).
\]
For every finite non-empty \(K\subset V\) and \(0\le p\le q<\pc\),
\[
  \frac{S_q^{\mathrm{amb}}(K)}{|K|}
  \le
  \frac{S_p^{\mathrm{amb}}(K)}{|K|}
  +
  \Delta\int_p^q \chiBar_s\,\mathcal R_s(K)\,ds .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
First work in a finite induced subgraph \(W\supseteq K\), and let \(T_s^W\)
be the two-point matrix for percolation restricted to \(W\).  As in the proof
of Proposition~\ref{prop:l2-open-right}, Russo's formula and BK give
\[
  \frac{d}{ds}T_s^W\le T_s^W A_W T_s^W
\]
entrywise, where \(A_W\) is the adjacency matrix of \(W\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \frac{d}{ds}\ip{\mathbf 1_K}{T_s^W\mathbf 1_K}
  &\le
  \ip{T_s^W\mathbf 1_K}{A_WT_s^W\mathbf 1_K}  \\
  &\le
  \Delta\norm{T_s^W\mathbf 1_K}_2^2
  \le
  \Delta\norm{T_s\mathbf 1_K}_2^2  \\
  &=
  \Delta\chiBar_s|K|\,\mathcal R_s(K).
\end{aligned}
\]
Integrating from \(p\) to \(q\), dividing by \(|K|\), and then letting
\(W\uparrow V\) gives the claimed inequality by monotone convergence.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Lemma~\ref{lem:two-replica-cluster-interpretation} explains the name: large
\(\mathcal R_p(K)\) means that, after summing over possible roots \(z\), two
independent clusters rooted at the same \(z\) both collect a large amount of
mass from \(K\).  Proposition~\ref{prop:two-replica-differential} shows that
this is also the quantity that appears naturally in the Russo--BK
differential growth of the finite-set two-point mass.  This makes
\(\mathcal R_p^*\) a percolation-specific target, not just an operator-norm
proxy.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Two-replica boundedness implies finite-set escape]
\label{prop:two-replica-implies-fe}
Let \(G\) be connected and locally finite, and suppose that
\[
  \chiBar_p\to\infty\qquad\text{as }p\uparrow\pc .
\]
If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\mathcal R_p^*<\infty,
\]
then finite-set escape holds.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(C<\infty\) and \(p_0<\pc\) be such that
\(\mathcal R_p^*\le C\) for \(p\in[p_0,\pc)\).  For every finite non-empty
\(K\subset V\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \sum_{x,y\in K}\tau_p(x,y)
  &=
  \frac{\ip{\mathbf 1_K}{T_p\mathbf 1_K}}{\chiBar_p|K|}  \\
  &\le
  \frac{|K|^{1/2}\norm{T_p\mathbf 1_K}_2}{\chiBar_p|K|}  \\
  &=
  \left(\frac{\mathcal R_p(K)}{\chiBar_p}\right)^{1/2}
  \le
  \left(\frac{C}{\chiBar_p}\right)^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The right-hand side tends to zero as \(p\uparrow\pc\), uniformly in \(K\).
This is finite-set escape.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two-replica intermediate theorem]
\label{thm:two-replica-intermediate}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, nonamenable, and of
bounded degree.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
  \item \(\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}\mathcal R_p^*<\infty\);
  \item \(\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty\).
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For quasi-transitive graphs, \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).
Proposition~\ref{prop:two-replica-implies-fe} gives finite-set escape.  The
second assumption is the mean-field susceptibility input \eqref{eq:mf}, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:hutchcroft-criterion} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A strict \texorpdfstring{\(L^2\)}{L2} gap forces the two-replica bound]
\label{prop:l2-gap-forces-two-replica}
Suppose that \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\).  If there exists
\(q>\pc\) such that \(T_q\) is bounded on \(\ell^2(V)\), then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc}\mathcal R_p^*=0 .
\]
In particular, \(p_c(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)\) implies the two-replica hypothesis in
Theorem~\ref{thm:two-replica-intermediate}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(q>\pc\) with \(M=\norm{T_q}_{2\to2}<\infty\).  By monotonicity of
connection probabilities, \(0\le T_p\le T_q\) pointwise for every
\(p<\pc\).  Hence, for every finite non-empty \(K\),
\[
  \mathcal R_p(K)
  =
  \frac{\norm{T_p\mathbf 1_K}_2^2}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \le
  \frac{M^2}{\chiBar_p}.
\]
Taking the supremum over finite \(K\) and letting \(p\uparrow\pc\) proves the
claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Proposition~\ref{prop:fe-iff-sublinear-two-replica} shows that the
finite-set escape scale is exactly
\(\mathcal R_p^*=o(\chiBar_p)\).  The bounded profile assumed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:two-replica-intermediate} is a stronger, more usable target:
it tests \(T_p\) only on indicators of finite sets and gives the layer-square
estimate needed in the separator-grid setup.  At the other end,
Proposition~\ref{prop:l2-gap-forces-two-replica} shows that any proof of
\(p_c<p_{2\to2}\) would force the still stronger conclusion
\(\mathcal R_p^*\to0\).  Thus the two-replica profile gives a calibrated
ladder: sublinear growth is equivalent to finite-set escape, bounded growth is
a plausible backscattering target, and vanishing growth is a necessary
consequence of the desired strict \(L^2\) gap.
\end{remark}

\section{A publishable intermediate target}

The global conjecture may be too hard to close in one jump.  A serious
intermediate result would still be valuable if it covers a natural class not
already handled by the known methods.  The following abstract theorem indicates
what such a result could look like.

\begin{definition}[Uniform critical scattering property]
A quasi-transitive graph \(G\) has the uniform critical scattering property if
for every sequence \(p_n\uparrow\pc\) and every sequence of finite sets
\(K_n\subset V\), there are partitions of \(K_n\) that are
\((o(1),o(1))\)-scattering for \(Q_{p_n}\).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform critical separator-convolution property]
A quasi-transitive graph \(G\) has the uniform critical separator-convolution
property if for every sequence \(p_n\uparrow\pc\) and every sequence of finite
sets \(K_n\subset V\), there are buffered partitions
\[
  K_n=K_{n,0}\sqcup K_{n,1}\sqcup\cdots\sqcup K_{n,m_n}
\]
and proper path separators \(W^{(n)}_{ij}\) between \(K_{n,i}\) and
\(K_{n,j}\), \(i,j\ge1\), \(i\ne j\), such that
\[
  \mathcal B_{p_n}(K_{n,0};K_n)\to0,
\]
\[
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_{p_n}|K_n|}
  \sum_{i=1}^{m_n}\sum_{x,y\in K_{n,i}}\tau_{p_n}(x,y)\to0
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal C_{p_n}(K_{n,1},\ldots,K_{n,m_n};W^{(n)})\to0 .
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Abstract intermediate theorem]
\label{thm:abstract-intermediate}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and nonamenable.
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
  \item \(G\) has the uniform critical scattering property;
  \item \(\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty\).
\end{enumerate}
Then \(\pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)\), and hence \(\pc(G)<\pu(G)\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The scattering property and Proposition~\ref{prop:scattering} give
finite-set escape.  The susceptibility assumption is exactly \eqref{eq:mf}.
The conclusion follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:hutchcroft-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Separator-convolution intermediate theorem]
\label{thm:separator-convolution-intermediate}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and nonamenable.
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
  \item \(G\) has the uniform critical separator-convolution property;
  \item \(\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}(\pc-p)\chiBar_p<\infty\).
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
  \pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The separator-convolution property and
Proposition~\ref{prop:separator-convolution-criterion} give finite-set escape.
The susceptibility assumption is \eqref{eq:mf}, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:hutchcroft-criterion} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
These intermediate theorems are not the final goal, because their assumptions
may hide most of the difficulty.  They are nevertheless useful targets: a
future paper could be publishable if it proves one of the uniform critical
separator properties for a previously untreated geometric or group-theoretic
class and verifies the susceptibility input.
\end{remark}

\section{From trapped mass to almost invariant sets}

This section formulates the desired contradiction mechanism.  It is not yet
proved in the required generality.

\begin{conjecture}[Trapped two-point mass creates graph almost-invariance]
\label{conj:trapped-to-folner}
Let \(G\) be connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive, and bounded degree.
If finite-set escape fails for \(Q_p=T_p/\chiBar_p\), then \(G\) has a Folner
sequence.  Equivalently, \(G\) is amenable.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:bridge-implies-main}
Assume Conjecture~\ref{conj:trapped-to-folner}.  Let \(G\) be connected,
locally finite, quasi-transitive, and nonamenable.  If \eqref{eq:mf} holds,
then \(\pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since \(G\) is nonamenable, it has no Folner sequence.  By the contrapositive
of Conjecture~\ref{conj:trapped-to-folner}, finite-set escape holds.  Together
with the assumed mean-field susceptibility bound \eqref{eq:mf},
Theorem~\ref{thm:hutchcroft-criterion} gives \(\pc(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Proposition~\ref{prop:bridge-implies-main} does not solve the open problem; it
isolates the missing bridge.  The bridge is plausible because failure of escape
gives finite sets retaining a positive fraction of a normalized, symmetric,
sub-Markov kernel.  A general principle of nonamenability says that finite
sets cannot retain random-walk mass uniformly.  The challenge is that \(Q_p\)
is not the random-walk kernel, and its relation to graph boundary is subtle.
\end{remark}

\section{A concrete spectral route}

Let \(P\) be the simple random walk operator on \(G\).  For bounded-degree
nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs, \(\norm{P}_{2\to2}<1\).  A direct proof of
finite-set escape would follow from an inequality of the following type.

\begin{conjecture}[Kernel-to-walk comparison]
\label{conj:comparison}
For every bounded-degree quasi-transitive graph \(G\), there are functions
\(\Phi_p:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) with \(\Phi_p(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), uniformly
as \(p\uparrow\pc\), such that for every finite non-empty \(K\subset V\),
\[
  \mathcal M_{Q_p}(K)
  \le
  \Phi_p\left(\frac{|\partial_EK|}{|K|}\right)
  + o_{p\uparrow\pc}(1).
\]
\end{conjecture}

This exact formulation is probably too optimistic: in a nonamenable graph,
the boundary ratio is bounded below, not small.  The useful direction would be
the contrapositive: if \(\mathcal M_{Q_p}(K)\) is large, then
\(|\partial_EK|/|K|\) must be small.  A more realistic form is therefore:

\begin{conjecture}[Mass-trapping isoperimetric inverse]
\label{conj:inverse}
There exists a function \(\Psi\) with \(\Psi(\epsilon)\downarrow0\) as
\(\epsilon\downarrow0\) such that the following holds.  If
\[
  \mathcal M_{Q_p}(K)\ge\epsilon
\]
for a sequence \(p\uparrow\pc\), then \(K\) contains a subset \(K'\) with
\[
  \frac{|\partial_EK'|}{|K'|}\le\Psi(\epsilon)+o_{p\uparrow\pc}(1).
\]
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proposition}
If Conjecture~\ref{conj:inverse} holds with \(\Psi(\epsilon)<h(G)\) for every
fixed \(\epsilon>0\) after passing sufficiently close to \(\pc\), then
finite-set escape holds on every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph \(G\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Suppose finite-set escape fails.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:failure-extraction}, there
are \(\epsilon>0\), \(p_n\uparrow\pc\), and finite sets \(K_n\) with
\(\mathcal M_{Q_{p_n}}(K_n)\ge\epsilon\).  Conjecture~\ref{conj:inverse} gives
subsets \(K'_n\) with boundary ratios eventually below \(h(G)\), contradicting
the definition of the Cheeger constant.
\end{proof}

The following elementary example shows why this inverse cannot be a theorem
about arbitrary symmetric adapted kernels on nonamenable graphs.

\begin{proposition}[Kernel-only nonamenability is insufficient]
\label{prop:kernel-only-insufficient}
Let \(\Gamma=F_2\times\mathbb Z\).  For every \(\delta>0\), there is a
finitely supported symmetric probability measure \(\mu\) whose support
generates \(\Gamma\), and a finite set \(K\subset\Gamma\), such that
\[
  \frac1{|K|}\sum_{x,y\in K}\mu(x^{-1}y)\ge1-\delta .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(a,b\) generate \(F_2\) and let \(t\) generate \(\mathbb Z\).  For
\(L\ge1\), let \(u_L\) be the uniform probability measure on
\(\{t^j:|j|\le L\}\), and let \(\nu\) be the uniform probability measure on
\(\{a,a^{-1},b,b^{-1},t,t^{-1}\}\).  Put
\[
  \mu=(1-\eta)u_L+\eta\nu .
\]
Then \(\mu\) is symmetric, finitely supported, and generating whenever
\(\eta>0\).

Let \(K_M=\{t^j:|j|\le M\}\), with \(M>L\).  If
\(|i|\le M-L\), then \(t^i\{t^j:|j|\le L\}\subseteq K_M\).  Hence
\[
  \frac1{|K_M|}\sum_{x,y\in K_M}\mu(x^{-1}y)
  =
  \frac1{|K_M|}\sum_{x\in K_M}\mu(x^{-1}K_M)
  \ge
  (1-\eta)\frac{2(M-L)+1}{2M+1}.
\]
Choosing \(\eta\) small and then \(M/L\) large makes the right-hand side at
least \(1-\delta\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Thus Kesten's theorem, property \(T\), or a spectral gap for a fixed simple
random walk cannot by themselves prove finite-set escape for \(Q_p\).  The
kernel \(Q_p\) must be used as a percolation two-point kernel, with its BK,
differential, or near-critical structure; otherwise mass can hide for a long
time inside a large amenable direction even when the ambient group is
nonamenable.
\end{remark}

\section{Known cases and stress tests}

Any proposed proof must recover the known positive cases without accidentally
proving a false amenable statement.

\subsection{Regular trees and killed growth}

The killed-growth condition is not vacuous.  On a regular tree, finite
subtrees have many boundary vertices, and the average number of long killed
self-avoiding paths grows like the square root of the ambient connective
constant.

\begin{proposition}[Killed growth on regular trees]
\label{prop:killed-tree}
Let \(T_d\) be the \(d\)-regular tree with \(d\ge3\).  Then
\[
  \kappa_{\mathrm{kill}}(T_d)=\sqrt{d-1}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \kappa_{\mathrm{kill}}(T_d)<1/\pc(T_d).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put \(q=d-1\).  Let \(R_n\) be the spherical operator on \(T_d\),
\[
  R_nf(x)=\sum_{y:\operatorname{dist}(x,y)=n}f(y).
\]
The standard spherical-polynomial estimate on the \(d\)-regular tree gives
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:tree-sphere-bound}
  \norm{R_n}_{2\to2}\le C_d(n+1)q^{n/2}.
\end{equation}
Indeed, \(R_n=P_n(A)\), where \(A\) is the adjacency operator, the spectrum of
\(A\) is contained in \([-2\sqrt q,2\sqrt q]\), and the polynomials \(P_n\)
are the tree-spherical Chebyshev polynomials.  The Chebyshev bound on this
interval yields \eqref{eq:tree-sphere-bound}.

For any finite \(K\subset T_d\), every killed self-avoiding path of length
\(n\) in \(K\) has endpoints at ambient distance \(n\).  Therefore
\[
  |K|A_n(K)
  \le
  \sum_{x,y\in K}\mathbf 1\{\operatorname{dist}(x,y)=n\}
  =
  \ip{\mathbf 1_K}{R_n\mathbf 1_K}
  \le
  C_d(n+1)q^{n/2}|K|.
\]
Taking the supremum over finite \(K\) and then the \(n\)th root gives
\(\kappa_{\mathrm{kill}}(T_d)\le\sqrt q\).

For the reverse inequality, let \(B_m\) be the ball of radius \(m\) around a
root \(o\).  If \(x\) and \(y\) lie at distance \(m\) from \(o\) in two
different principal branches, then the geodesic from \(x\) to \(y\) is a
killed self-avoiding path of length \(2m\) inside \(B_m\).  There are
\(d(d-1)q^{2m-2}\) ordered pairs of this type, while \(|B_m|\le C'_dq^m\).
Thus \(A_{2m}(B_m)\ge c_dq^m\), and hence
\(\kappa_{\mathrm{kill}}(T_d)\ge\sqrt q\).

Finally, \(\pc(T_d)=q^{-1}\), so \(\sqrt q<q=1/\pc(T_d)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Finite-set escape on regular trees]
\label{prop:tree-fe}
Let \(T_d\) be the \(d\)-regular tree with \(d\ge3\).  Then finite-set escape
holds on \(T_d\):
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc(T_d)}
  \sup_{K\subset V\text{ finite}}
  \frac{1}{|K|}\sum_{x,y\in K}Q_p(x,y)=0.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Again put \(q=d-1\).  On \(T_d\), the two-point function is exactly
\[
  \tau_p(x,y)=p^{\operatorname{dist}(x,y)}
\]
and
\[
  \chiBar_p=1+d\sum_{n\ge1}q^{n-1}p^n=\frac{1+p}{1-qp}.
\]
Using the spherical operators \(R_n\) from Proposition~\ref{prop:killed-tree},
we have, for every finite \(K\),
\[
  \frac{1}{|K|}\sum_{x,y\in K}Q_p(x,y)
  =
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \sum_{n\ge0}p^n\ip{\mathbf 1_K}{R_n\mathbf 1_K}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:tree-sphere-bound},
\[
  \frac{1}{|K|}\sum_{x,y\in K}Q_p(x,y)
  \le
  \frac{C_d}{\chiBar_p}
  \sum_{n\ge0}(n+1)(p\sqrt q)^n.
\]
As \(p\uparrow\pc=q^{-1}\), the series remains bounded because
\(p\sqrt q\le q^{-1/2}<1\), while \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\).  The bound is
uniform in \(K\), proving finite-set escape.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Two-replica profile on regular trees]
\label{prop:tree-two-replica-profile}
Let \(T_d\) be the \(d\)-regular tree with \(d\ge3\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc(T_d)}\mathcal R_p^*=0 .
\]
In particular, \(\sup_{p<\pc(T_d)}\mathcal R_p^*<\infty\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put \(q=d-1\), so \(\pc=q^{-1}\).  As in
Proposition~\ref{prop:tree-local-separator-convolution}, the tree spherical
bound \eqref{eq:tree-sphere-bound} gives
\[
  M_d:=\sup_{0\le p\le\pc}\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}<\infty .
\]
For every finite non-empty \(K\subset V(T_d)\),
\[
  \mathcal R_p(K)
  =
  \frac{\norm{T_p\mathbf 1_K}_2^2}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \le
  \frac{M_d^2}{\chiBar_p}.
\]
On the tree,
\[
  \chiBar_p=\frac{1+p}{1-qp}\to\infty
  \qquad (p\uparrow q^{-1}),
\]
so the displayed bound tends to zero uniformly over finite \(K\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Local separator-convolution on regular trees]
\label{prop:tree-local-separator-convolution}
Let \(T_d\) be the \(d\)-regular tree with \(d\ge3\).  Then \(T_d\) has the
local separator-convolution property near \(\pc(T_d)\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put \(q=d-1\), so \(\pc=1/q\).  Since
\(\tau_p(x,y)=p^{\operatorname{dist}(x,y)}\), we have
\[
  T_p=\sum_{n\ge0}p^nR_n,
\]
where \(R_n\) is the tree sphere kernel.  By \eqref{eq:tree-sphere-bound},
\[
  M_d:=\sup_{0\le p\le\pc}\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}<\infty .
\]

Fix \(\delta>0\).  Choose an integer \(L\) such that \(2/L\le\delta\), and put
\(R=2L\).  Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc\), choose
\(p_0<\pc\) such that
\[
  \frac{M_d^2}{\chiBar_p}\le\delta
  \qquad (p\in[p_0,\pc)).
\]
Root the tree at \(o\), and for \(r\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\) let
\[
  S_r=\{x:\operatorname{dist}(o,x)\equiv r\pmod L\}.
\]
Given a finite non-empty \(K\subset V\), choose \(r\) with
\(|K\cap S_r|\le |K|/L\), and set \(K_0=K\cap S_r\).  The non-buffer pieces are
the non-empty intersections of \(K\setminus K_0\) with the connected components
of \(T_d\setminus S_r\).  Each component is contained either in the initial
root slab before the first level of \(S_r\), or between two consecutive levels
of \(S_r\), so every such component has diameter at most \(2L\).  Hence the
pieces have diameter at most \(R\).

For any two distinct non-buffer pieces, take \(W_{ij}=S_r\).  This is a proper
path separator: it is disjoint from both pieces, and every path between
different components of \(T_d\setminus S_r\) hits \(S_r\).  The buffer mass is
bounded by the row sum:
\[
  \mathcal B_p(K_0;K)
  =
  \frac{2}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \sum_{x\in K_0,y\in K}\tau_p(x,y)
  \le
  \frac{2|K_0|}{|K|}
  \le
  \frac{2}{L}
  \le\delta .
\]
For the separator-convolution term, write \(f=\mathbf 1_{K\setminus K_0}\).
Since the kernels are nonnegative,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \chiBar_p|K|\,\mathcal C_p(K_1,\ldots,K_m;W)
  &=
  \sum_{i\ne j}\sum_{z\in S_r}U_i^p(z)U_j^p(z)  \\
  &\le
  \sum_{z\in S_r}\left(\sum_iU_i^p(z)\right)^2  \\
  &\le
  \norm{T_pf}_2^2
  \le
  M_d^2\norm{f}_2^2
  \le
  M_d^2|K|.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
  \mathcal C_p(K_1,\ldots,K_m;W)\le \frac{M_d^2}{\chiBar_p}\le\delta.
\]
This proves the local separator-convolution property.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Finite-fiber tree-grid separators]
\label{prop:finite-fiber-tree-grid-separators}
Let \(G\) be a connected bounded-degree graph, and let \(s\ge0\).  Suppose
that there are a bounded-degree tree \(\mathbb T\), a root
\(o\in V(\mathbb T)\), and a map
\[
  \pi:V(G)\to V(\mathbb T\square\mathbb Z^s)
\]
such that
\[
  b:=\sup_{u\in V(\mathbb T\square\mathbb Z^s)}|\pi^{-1}(u)|<\infty
\]
and, whenever \(x\sim y\) in \(G\),
\[
  \operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T\square\mathbb Z^s}(\pi(x),\pi(y))\le1 .
\]
If
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(G)}
  \frac{\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}^2}{\chiBar_p}<\infty,
\]
then \(G\) has the local separator-convolution property near \(\pc(G)\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\Delta_{\mathbb T}\) be a degree bound for \(\mathbb T\), and let
\[
  A=
  1+
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(G)}
  \frac{\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}^2}{\chiBar_p}.
\]
Fix \(\delta>0\).  Choose an integer \(L\) such that
\[
  \frac{(s+1)(2+A)}{L}\le\delta,
\]
and choose \(p_0<\pc(G)\) such that
\[
  \frac{\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}^2}{\chiBar_p}\le A
  \qquad (p\in[p_0,\pc(G))).
\]
Write a vertex of \(\mathbb T\square\mathbb Z^s\) as
\((t,n_1,\ldots,n_s)\), and define
\[
  \rho_0(t,n)=\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T}(o,t),
  \qquad
  \rho_j(t,n)=n_j \quad (1\le j\le s).
\]
For \(\mathbf a=(a_0,\ldots,a_s)\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^{s+1}\), put
\[
  \Sigma_{\mathbf a}
  =
  \{u\in V(\mathbb T\square\mathbb Z^s):
     \rho_j(u)\equiv a_j\pmod L
     \text{ for some }0\le j\le s\},
  \qquad
  S_{\mathbf a}=\pi^{-1}(\Sigma_{\mathbf a}).
\]
The connected components of
\((\mathbb T\square\mathbb Z^s)\setminus\Sigma_{\mathbf a}\) have at most
\[
  N_L=1+\Delta_{\mathbb T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L-1}
       (\Delta_{\mathbb T}-1)^\ell
\]
choices for the tree coordinate and at most \(L^s\) choices for the Euclidean
coordinates, with the evident interpretation when \(\Delta_{\mathbb T}=1\).
Thus each base component has at most \(N_LL^s\) vertices.  Since the fibers of
\(\pi\) have size at most \(b\), every component of
\(G\setminus S_{\mathbf a}\) has at most \(bN_LL^s\) vertices.  Indeed, the
projection of a connected set in \(G\setminus S_{\mathbf a}\) is connected in
\((\mathbb T\square\mathbb Z^s)\setminus\Sigma_{\mathbf a}\), because adjacent
vertices in \(G\) project to equal or adjacent vertices of the base graph.

Given a finite non-empty \(K\subset V(G)\), write
\(K_{\mathbf a}=K\cap S_{\mathbf a}\).  For each fixed vertex of \(G\), the
proportion of residue vectors \(\mathbf a\) for which it lies in
\(S_{\mathbf a}\) is at most \((s+1)/L\).  Hence
\[
  \frac{1}{L^{s+1}}
  \sum_{\mathbf a}\frac{2|K_{\mathbf a}|}{|K|}
  \le
  \frac{2(s+1)}{L}.
\]
Also, by positivity of \(T_p\),
\[
  \frac{1}{L^{s+1}}\sum_{\mathbf a}
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}\bigl(T_p\mathbf 1_K(z)\bigr)^2
  \le
  \frac{s+1}{L}
  \frac{\norm{T_p\mathbf 1_K}_2^2}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \le
  \frac{(s+1)A}{L}.
\]
Hence for some \(\mathbf a\),
\[
  \frac{2|K_{\mathbf a}|}{|K|}
  +
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}\bigl(T_p\mathbf 1_K(z)\bigr)^2
  \le \frac{(s+1)(2+A)}{L}\le\delta .
\]
Set \(K_0=K_{\mathbf a}\), and let the non-buffer pieces be the non-empty
intersections of \(K\setminus K_0\) with the connected components of
\(G\setminus S_{\mathbf a}\).
Each such piece has graph diameter at most
\[
  R=bN_LL^s-1.
\]
For two distinct non-buffer pieces, take \(W_{ij}=S_{\mathbf a}\).  This is a
proper path separator because the pieces lie in distinct components of
\(G\setminus S_{\mathbf a}\).

The buffer mass is bounded by
\[
  \mathcal B_p(K_0;K)
  \le \frac{2|K_0|}{|K|}.
\]
For the separator-convolution term, put \(f=\mathbf 1_{K\setminus K_0}\).
Since \(T_pf\le T_p\mathbf 1_K\) pointwise,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \chiBar_p|K|\,\mathcal C_p(K_1,\ldots,K_m;W)
  &=
  \sum_{i\ne j}\sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}U_i^p(z)U_j^p(z)  \\
  &\le
  \sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}\left(\sum_i U_i^p(z)\right)^2  \\
  &=
  \sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}\bigl(T_pf(z)\bigr)^2  \\
  &\le
  \sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}\bigl(T_p\mathbf 1_K(z)\bigr)^2 .
\end{aligned}
\]
The choice of \(\mathbf a\) therefore gives both
\[
  \mathcal B_p(K_0;K)\le\delta,
  \qquad
  \mathcal C_p(K_1,\ldots,K_m;W)\le\delta.
\]
Together with the diameter bound, this is the local
separator-convolution property.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Tree-grid separators from two-replica boundedness]
\label{prop:tree-grid-two-replica}
In the setup of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-fiber-tree-grid-separators},
replace the analytic hypothesis there by
\[
  \limsup_{p\uparrow\pc(G)}\mathcal R_p^*<\infty .
\]
Then \(G\) has the local separator-convolution property near \(\pc(G)\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(C<\infty\) and \(p_1<\pc(G)\) be such that
\(\mathcal R_p^*\le C\) for \(p\in[p_1,\pc(G))\).  Repeat the construction of
the periodic tree-Euclidean grids \(\Sigma_{\mathbf a}\), their lifts
\(S_{\mathbf a}\), and the constant \(N_L\) from the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-fiber-tree-grid-separators}.  Choose \(L\) so
large that
\[
  \frac{(s+1)(2+C)}{L}\le\delta .
\]
For a given finite non-empty \(K\), the buffer average is still at most
\(2(s+1)/L\).  Moreover, since each vertex of \(G\) belongs to at most an
\((s+1)/L\) fraction of the lifted grids,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \frac{1}{L^{s+1}}\sum_{\mathbf a}
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}\bigl(T_p\mathbf 1_K(z)\bigr)^2
  &\le
  \frac{s+1}{L}
  \frac{\norm{T_p\mathbf 1_K}_2^2}{\chiBar_p|K|}  \\
  &\le
  \frac{(s+1)C}{L}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus some \(\mathbf a\) has both buffer contribution and layer-square
contribution with total at most \(\delta\).  The components of
\(G\setminus S_{\mathbf a}\) have at most \(bN_LL^s\) vertices as before, so
the resulting pieces have uniformly bounded diameter.  The same separator
convolution estimate used in
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-fiber-tree-grid-separators} proves the local
separator-convolution property.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The two preceding finite-fiber tree-grid propositions are calibrations rather
than solutions of the general problem.  The global \(L^2\)-type hypothesis in
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-fiber-tree-grid-separators} is strong; when
\(\chiBar_p\to\infty\), it already implies finite-set escape by the elementary
spectral bound
\[
  \frac{\ip{\mathbf 1_K}{T_p\mathbf 1_K}}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \le
  \frac{\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}.
\]
The two-replica hypothesis in Proposition~\ref{prop:tree-grid-two-replica}
also implies finite-set escape directly by
Proposition~\ref{prop:two-replica-implies-fe}; its value here is that it
matches the exact square mass appearing in the separator-convolution term.
The point is geometric: finite fibers over periodic tree-Euclidean grids
automatically provide small buffers and uniformly local pieces.  In the
separator-convolution route, the genuinely missing estimate is control of
square two-point mass on the chosen separating grid without assuming the
conclusion-like global \(\ell^2\) bound.  In this setting it would be enough
to prove the layer-square estimate
\[
  \lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{p\uparrow\pc}
  \sup_{K\subset V\text{ finite}}
  \min_{\mathbf a\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^{s+1}}
  \frac{1}{\chiBar_p|K|}
  \sum_{z\in S_{\mathbf a}}
    \bigl(T_p\mathbf 1_K(z)\bigr)^2
  =0.
\]
The buffer term is already small on average over the shifts
\(\mathbf a\).  Thus, for product-like geometries, the separator program asks
for a two-replica backscattering estimate: two independent connections from
the same separating grid should not both carry a macroscopic amount of
near-critical mass into the same finite test set.
Proposition~\ref{prop:restricted-shell-layer-square} rewrites this target, for
graphs admitting a fibre decomposition over a base graph, as a restricted
base-sphere estimate.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Boundary energy on regular trees]
\label{prop:tree-boundary-energy}
Let \(T_d\) be the \(d\)-regular tree with \(d\ge3\).  Then
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow\pc(T_d)}
  \sup_{K\subset V\text{ finite}}\mathcal E_p(K)=0.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put \(q=d-1\).  The spherical estimate \eqref{eq:tree-sphere-bound} gives
\[
  \sup_{0\le p\le q^{-1}}\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}
  \le
  C_d\sum_{n\ge0}(n+1)q^{-n/2}
  <\infty .
\]
For a finite set \(K\), put
\[
  w(a)=\mathbf 1_{\partial_{\mathrm{in}}K}(a)\chi_p^K(a).
\]
Since \(\tau_p^K(a,x)\le\tau_p(a,x)\), we have
\[
  0\le w\le T_p\mathbf 1_K
\]
pointwise, and hence \(\norm{w}_2\le C_d\norm{\mathbf 1_K}_2\).  The exterior
boundary weight \(\mu_{p,K}\) is obtained from \(w\) by summing over at most
\(d\) neighbouring boundary vertices at each exterior vertex, so
\[
  \norm{\mu_{p,K}}_2^2\le d^2\norm{w}_2^2\le C'_d|K|.
\]
Moreover
\[
  \norm{Q_p}_{2\to2}=\frac{\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}}{\chiBar_p}
  \le \frac{C_d}{\chiBar_p}.
\]
Therefore
\[
  \mathcal E_p(K)
  =
  \frac{p^2}{|K|}\ip{\mu_{p,K}}{Q_p\mu_{p,K}}
  \le
  \frac{C''_d}{\chiBar_p}.
\]
Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\) as \(p\uparrow\pc(T_d)\), the bound tends to zero
uniformly in \(K\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The proof identifies the right obstruction for extending
\eqref{eq:kcg}.  The relevant comparison is not with the full number
\(d(d-1)^{n-1}\) of ambient self-avoiding paths from one vertex, but with the
spherical \(L^2\)-norm \(q^{n/2}\).  This suggests that a useful general
version of \eqref{eq:kcg} should be tied to Haagerup-type radial operator
bounds or to an \(L^2\) growth exponent, rather than to pointwise connective
constants.  Proposition~\ref{prop:tree-boundary-energy} also shows that the
boundary-energy condition is calibrated correctly on trees, although its proof
uses the already-known \(L^2\)-boundedness of \(T_p\) up to \(p_c\) and is
therefore not a general substitute for the missing argument.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Hyperbolic graphs}

Hutchcroft proved \(\pc<p_u\) and the stronger triangle-condition conclusions
for nonamenable Gromov hyperbolic quasi-transitive graphs
\cite{Hutchcroft2019Hyperbolic}.  In the language of this draft, hyperbolicity
provides enough large-scale separation to prove finite-set escape.

This case is the model for the separator program, but it also shows why the
general problem is hard.  Hyperbolicity supplies a canonical boundary and a
strong form of thin-triangle geometry.  General nonamenable Cayley graphs may
have no such boundary, may contain large flat or amenable-looking regions, and
may not admit any obvious half-space decomposition.  A general proof must
replace geometric boundary separation with an intrinsic probabilistic or
operator-theoretic mechanism.

\subsection{Nonunimodular transitive graphs}

Graphs admitting a nonunimodular quasitransitive automorphism group are also
not part of the remaining obstruction.  For such an action, let \(\Delta\) be
the modular function and define the tilted susceptibility threshold \(p_t\) by
finiteness of
\[
  \chi_{p,1/2}=\sum_x\tau_p(o,x)\Delta(o,x)^{1/2}.
\]
Hutchcroft proved \(p_c<p_t\) in this setting
\cite{Hutchcroft2020Nonunimodular}.  The general tilted-to-\(L^2\) comparison
gives \(p_t\le p_{2\to2}\) \cite{Hutchcroft2019Hyperbolic}.  Hence
\[
  p_c(G)<p_{2\to2}(G)
\]
for every graph in this nonunimodular class.

This matters for the project because nonunimodularity supplies an external
height function and a tilted mass-transport principle.  The unresolved
cases without a nonunimodular quasitransitive action do not have this structure
available globally.  The backscattering and Hammersley--Welsh mechanism of
Hutchcroft--Pan therefore needs a replacement for the tilt before it can apply
there.

\subsection{Products and uniqueness threshold phenomena}

For products such as \(T\times\mathbb Z^d\), the non-uniqueness phase and the
behavior at \(\pu\) are far better understood than in arbitrary graphs.
Recent work proves refined dimension-jump and \(p_{2\to2}\)-threshold
identifications in these product and lamplighter settings
\cite{HutchcroftPan2024Dimension}.  These examples are essential tests for
any proposed general proof: they contain large amenable directions but remain
nonamenable because of the tree factor.

They also test overly naive boundary arguments.  A box in the
\(\mathbb Z^d\)-direction has small boundary relative to its volume inside that
factor, while the product graph remains nonamenable because of expansion in
the tree direction.  Therefore a proof based only on local Euclidean-looking
boundary ratios will fail.  The normalized kernel \(Q_p\) must see the
nonamenable direction at the correct scale.

\subsection{Amenable graphs}

On amenable quasi-transitive graphs, \(\pc=\pu\).  Therefore no argument can
show finite-set escape from quasi-transitivity alone.  Any proof must use
nonamenability in a genuinely quantitative way.

This is a useful guard against false proofs.  If an argument uses only
bounded degree, transitivity, positivity, symmetry, BK-type inequalities, and
subcriticality, it is almost certainly proving too much.  Somewhere the proof
must use a spectral gap, a Cheeger lower bound, a cost/nonamenability input, or
an equivalent obstruction to Folner sequences.

\begin{proposition}[Two-replica profile diverges on the line]
\label{prop:line-two-replica-diverges}
For \(G=\mathbb Z\),
\[
  \lim_{p\uparrow1}\mathcal R_p^*=\infty .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On \(\mathbb Z\), \(\pc=1\),
\[
  \tau_p(x,y)=p^{|x-y|},
  \qquad
  \chiBar_p=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}p^{|m|}
  =
  \frac{1+p}{1-p}.
\]
Let \(K_N=\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and take
\[
  N=\left\lceil 4(1-p)^{-1}\right\rceil .
\]
If \(z\in\{N/4,\ldots,3N/4\}\cap\mathbb Z\), then \(z\) is at distance at
least \(N/4-1\) from both endpoints up to harmless rounding.  Thus, with
\(M=\lfloor N/4\rfloor-1\),
\[
  T_p\mathbf 1_{K_N}(z)
  =
  \sum_{x=1}^N p^{|x-z|}
  \ge
  \sum_{|m|\le M}p^{|m|}
  =
  \chiBar_p-\frac{2p^{M+1}}{1-p}.
\]
For \(p\) sufficiently close to \(1\), the choice of \(N\) gives
\[
  \frac{2p^{M+1}}{1-p}\le \frac12\chiBar_p,
\]
and hence \(T_p\mathbf 1_{K_N}(z)\ge\chiBar_p/2\) for all such \(z\).  There
are at least \(N/2\) such \(z\), so
\[
  \mathcal R_p(K_N)
  =
  \frac{\norm{T_p\mathbf 1_{K_N}}_2^2}{\chiBar_p N}
  \ge
  \frac18\,\chiBar_p
\]
for all \(p\) sufficiently close to \(1\).  Since \(\chiBar_p\to\infty\), the
supremum over finite \(K\) diverges.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Planar site conjectures}

Recent planar site-percolation work has resolved and refuted variants of
older Benjamini-Schramm planar questions in settings that are not the same as
Conjecture~\ref{conj:bs} \cite{Li2026Planar}.  These papers are relevant as
evidence that the area is active and that end-structure can be decisive.  They
do not remove the need to solve the quasi-transitive bond-percolation
nonamenability conjecture.

\section{Failed-proof guardrails}

The following tempting reductions should not be accepted without new input.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{F\arabic*.},leftmargin=2.5em]
  \item \emph{Row-sum normalization alone is insufficient.}
  Lemma~\ref{lem:q-basic} gives \(\norm{Q_p}_{2\to2}\le1\), but finite-set
  escape asks for a much stronger delocalization statement for normalized
  indicators.
  \item \emph{Nonamenability of \(G\) is not automatically nonamenability of
  \(Q_p\).}  The kernel \(Q_p\) is long range and depends on \(p\).  Its
  internal mass on finite sets need not be controlled directly by the
  edge-boundary of those sets without an additional comparison theorem.
  \item \emph{Mean-field susceptibility is not free.}  The condition
  \((\pc-p)\chiBar_p=O(1)\) is part of Hutchcroft's criterion.  A complete
  proof must establish it, bypass it, or replace the criterion.
  \item \emph{Known special cases should not be relabeled as the general
  theorem.}  Hyperbolic, nonunimodular, planar, product, and subgroup
  relativization results are major, but none is the full theorem targeted
  here.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Immediate technical tasks}

The next stages of the project are concrete.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{T\arabic*.},leftmargin=2.5em]
  \item Prove or disprove Conjecture~\ref{conj:inverse} in the stated form.
  The first check is whether products \(T\times\mathbb Z^d\) force a different
  inverse profile.
  \item Re-read the proof of Hutchcroft's hyperbolic case and rewrite the
  geometric half-space argument as an abstract separator lemma.
  \item Search for a class of nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs not covered
  by current results but satisfying the abstract separator lemma.
  \item Try to prove the mean-field susceptibility bound \eqref{eq:mf} from
  nonamenability alone, or find a replacement for Theorem~\ref{thm:hutchcroft-criterion}
  that avoids it.
  \item Keep an explicit failed-proof log so that recurring false reductions
  are not retried.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Conclusion}

The selected target is a real open problem in probability theory.  A complete
solution would be publishable and significant.  The working route is to prove
that nonamenability forces finite-set escape for the normalized subcritical
two-point kernel.  This draft proves only elementary reductions and identifies
the core missing bridge.  Subsequent work should focus on turning trapped
two-point mass into graph almost-invariance, or finding a different route to
\(\pc<p_{2\to2}\).
